text: The fourth installment of the American drama series *Chicago Fire* was green‑lit by NBC on February 5, 2015. It began airing on October 13, 2015 and wrapped up its run on May 17, 2016. This season comprised a total of 23 episodes.
title: Chicago Fire (season 4)

text: The Eagles’ song “Love Will Keep Us Alive,” penned by Jim Capaldi, Paul Carrack and Peter Vale and produced by the band together with Elliot Scheiner and Rob Jacobs, made its first appearance on the group’s 1994 Hell Freezes Over reunion tour. The lead vocal on the track was performed by bassist Timothy B. Schmit.
title: Love Will Keep Us Alive

text: Patrick Walter Brown, MPP (born May 26 1978), is a Canadian politician who presently holds the position of leader of the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario, making him Ontario’s Leader of the Official Opposition. He is commonly referred to as Patrick Brown.
title: Patrick Brown (politician)

text: Patrick Brown was chosen as the leader of the Ontario Progressive Conservative Party in May 2015, after which he resigned his seat in the federal parliament. He subsequently won a provincial by‑election on September 3, 2015, becoming the Member of Provincial Parliament for Simcoe North. Before entering federal politics, he worked as a lawyer in Barrie.
title: Patrick Brown (politician)

text: The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band recorded “Fishin’ in the Dark,” a song penned by Wendy Waldman and Jim Photoglo, and released it in June 1987 as the second single drawn from their album **Hold On**. The track went on to top both the U.S. and Canadian country charts, becoming the group’s third U.S. country‑music number‑one and second in Canada. After being made available for digital download, it surpassed one million sales by 2015 and earned a Platinum certification from the RIAA on September 12, 2014.
title: Fishin' in the Dark

text: Panning is the process of taking a sound signal—whether it is a single‑channel (monaural) track or a stereophonic pair—and routing it into a new stereo or multi‑channel sound field as determined by a pan control setting. This distribution operation includes the conversion of a stereo signal to a mono signal.
title: Panning (audio)

text: Panning is a technique employed on an audio mixer to narrow or even cancel the stereo width of a signal. By directing the left‑hand and right‑hand channels of a stereo source straight up—sending each channel equally to both the left and right mixer outputs—a dual mono signal is produced.
title: Panning (audio)

text: In a market‑based system, the determination of which goods and services will be produced is driven chiefly by the mechanisms of capital and financial markets, which allocate investment and producer resources in response to supply‑and‑demand signals.
title: Market economy

text: The pop ballad “Can’t Help Falling in Love” was first recorded by American singer Elvis Presley. Published through his own company, Gladys Music, the song was written by Hugo Peretti, Luigi Creatore, and George David Weiss, and its melody is based on Jean‑Paul‑Égide Martini’s 1784 romance “Plaisir d’amour.” Presley performed the track in his 1961 film *Blue Hawaii*, and although many other artists later covered it, the original recording was made by Elvis Presley.
title: Can't Help Falling in Love

text: Christopher Allen Lloyd (born October 22, 1938) is an American actor, voice actor, and comedian. He is most renowned for portraying Emmett “Doc” Brown in the Back to the Future film trilogy.
title: Christopher Lloyd

text: The Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (Save the Girl Child, Educate the Girl Child) initiative appointed Olympic bronze‑medallist Sakshi Malik as its brand ambassador on 26 August 2016.
title: Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana

text: The television series *Prison Break* has had its first five seasons released on DVD and Blu‑ray, and the show is also streamed on services like iTunes, Amazon Video, and Netflix. As a result, Netflix carries five seasons of *Prison Break*.
title: List of Prison Break episodes

text: In August 1945 the United States Army Air Forces’ 509th Composite Group, operating specially modified B‑29 Superfortress bombers from the island of Tinian, carried out the first combat use of atomic weapons. On 6 August a B‑29 released the uranium gun‑type bomb called **Little Boy** over Hiroshima. Three days later, on 9 August, another B‑29 dropped the plutonium implosion‑type bomb known as Fat Man on Nagasaki. Both explosions caused immediate, massive devastation and led to tens of thousands of deaths in the ensuing weeks and months.
title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

text: In mammalian sperm the cell is divided into a head, neck, midpiece and tail. The mitochondria are found in the midpiece, where they are wrapped in a spiral around a central filamentous core to generate the ATP needed for the sperm’s movement through the female reproductive tract.
title: Sperm

text: Sperm cells obtain most of the energy required for flagellar movement from the metabolism of fructose, and this metabolic activity takes place in the mitochondria that are positioned in the sperm’s midpiece, the region located at the base of the head.
title: Sperm

text: An equilateral triangle is the most symmetric type of triangle. It contains three distinct lines of reflection that pass through its center, giving it 3 lines of symmetry. In addition, the figure can be rotated by one‑third of a full turn and still coincide with itself, reflecting the dihedral symmetry group D₃ of order 6.
title: Equilateral triangle

text: By December 10 2017, a total of 205 original episodes of *Keeping Up with the Kardashians* had been broadcast, bringing the series to the end of its fourteen seasons.
title: List of Keeping Up with the Kardashians episodes

text: Sharecropping is an agricultural arrangement in which a landowner allows a tenant farmer to work a plot of his land, but the farmer keeps only a modest portion of the harvest and surrenders the larger share to the landowner. The practice has a long history and appears in various contractual forms, such as the Italian mezzadria, the French métayage, the Spanish mediero, and the Islamic muqasat.
title: Sharecropping

text: The domed stadium being built for the Las Vegas Raiders and the UNLV Rebels is located in Paradise, Nevada. It sits on about 62 acres west of Mandalay Bay, bounded by Russell Road, Hacienda Avenue, Polaris Avenue and Dean Martin Drive, just west of Interstate 15. Construction on the $1.9 billion project began in September 2017 and is planned to be finished in time for the 2020 NFL season.
title: Las Vegas Stadium

text: The name “Comanche” comes from the Ute word kÉ¨mantsi, which translates directly as “enemy.”
title: Comanche

text: The Duanwu Festival, widely known in the West as the Dragon Boat Festival, is a traditional Chinese holiday that takes place around the summer solstice. It is also called the Zhongxiao Festival (忠孝節), a title that signifies its purpose of commemorating fealty and filial piety. Observed on the fifth day of the fifth month of the lunisolar Chinese calendar—giving rise to the alternate name Double Fifth Festival—the exact Gregorian date changes each year; for instance, it occurred on June 9 in 2016 and on May 30 in 2017.
title: Dragon Boat Festival

text: In the “Susan Banks” storyline, Susan’s boyfriend Edmund Crumb is played by actor Adam Caine. After Kristen pretends to be Susan, she is compelled to marry Edmund, leading the couple to go on a honeymoon while the plot unravels around the mistaken identities and the death of Susan’s sister.
title: Susan Banks

text: The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds employs over 1,300 staff members, works alongside 18,000 volunteers, and counts **more than a million** members—including 195,000 youth members—making it the largest wildlife‑conservation charity in Europe.
title: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds

text: In Canada, the duration of a majority government is capped at four years. Under the amended Elections Act, an election must be held on the third Monday in October of the fourth calendar year following the previous polling date, effectively limiting the time a prime minister can remain in office to a four‑year term.
title: Prime Minister of Canada

text: The screenplay, penned by John Milius and Edward Anhalt, was filmed on location across the state of Utah, the place Redford had adopted as his home. The completed picture was subsequently entered into the 1972 Cannes Film Festival.
title: Jeremiah Johnson (film)

text: The movie was ultimately filmed on location in Utah. After Warner Bros. advanced Robert Redford $200,000 to secure his participation, the studio initially wanted to shoot on its backlot for budget reasons. Redford and director Sydney Pollack insisted that the picture be shot in Utah, convincing the studio that the cost would be comparable. To locate suitable spots, art director Ted Haworth drove more than 26,000 miles, and the production ended up using nearly one hundred Utah sites, including Mount Timpanogos, Ashley National Forest, Leeds, Snow Canyon State Park, St. George, Sundance Resort, Uinta National Forest, Wasatch‑Cache National Forest, and Zion National Park.
title: Jeremiah Johnson (film)

text: Dr. Jesse Bennett (born July 10, 1769; died July 13, 1842) is recorded as the first American doctor to carry out a successful Caesarean section. He performed the operation on his own wife at the delivery of their sole child on January 14, 1794.
title: Jesse Bennett

text: After departing from Carthage, Aeneas and the Trojan company set sail for Sicily. There, on the island, he organized funeral games to honor his father, who had died the previous year. The Trojans then continued their journey, eventually reaching the western coast of Italy, after which Aeneas descended into the underworld and encountered Dido and his father, who revealed the destiny of his descendants and the future of Rome.
title: Aeneas

text: The new season of *Lost in Space* premiered on Netflix on April 13, 2018. Earlier that year, on March 31, 2018, the pilot episode was screened exclusively at Awesome Con in Washington, D.C., followed by a Q&A with series executive producers Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless.
title: Lost in Space (2018 TV series)

text: General Armitage Hux is a fictional officer in the Star Wars saga, debuting in the 2015 film *Star Wars: The Force Awakens* and returning in its sequel *Star Wars: The Last Jedi* as a key player in the First Order’s leadership struggle. He is portrayed by Domhnall Gleeson.
title: General Hux

text: In a microscope the specimen slide is placed on the instrument’s stage, where it is held in position by slide clips, slide clamps, or a cross‑table that allows precise, remote movement of the slide on the microscope’s stage.
title: Microscope slide

text: The fourth installment of *Gotham* launched on Fox on September 21, 2017, with the series’ second half later returning on March 1, 2018.
title: Gotham (season 4)

text: The reggae‑inspired song “Man Gave Names to All the Animals” bases its verses on Genesis 2:19‑20, which recounts that the first human gave a name to every creature. In that biblical account, **Adam** is identified as the person who named each animal and bird, thereby providing names for all the animals in the world.
title: Man Gave Names to All the Animals

text: When an NHL player is placed on waivers, every one of the league’s 30 teams has the opportunity to submit a claim. The waiver period begins at noon Eastern Time and concludes 24 hours later. If a single team files a claim, that team acquires the player; if several teams submit claims, the player goes to the club with the lowest points percentage in the standings at the time of the request. Should no team place a claim, the player may be assigned to a minor‑league affiliate.
title: Waivers (NHL)

text: The Price Is Right debuted on NBC’s daytime schedule on November 26, 1956, marking its first broadcast year as 1956. Shortly thereafter, the show also launched a weekly primetime version.
title: The Price Is Right (1956 U.S. game show)

text: Thespis, originally a performer of dithyrambs—lyrical choral songs that retold mythic tales—breaks away from the traditional chorus by taking on the spoken words of single characters. In doing so, he distinguishes each role with a separate mask, thereby creating a new mode of presentation in which one singer acts as an individual character rather than remaining within the collective chorus. This innovation is credited with making Thespis the first actor in theatrical history.
title: Thespis

text: During Founder's Day, after Anna is incapacitated while trying to protect Jeremy, a police officer discovers her with the other tomb vampires. He injects Anna with vervain and transports her, along with the remaining vampires, to the Gilbert building, where they are burned together in accordance with the 1864 plan to eradicate their kind.
title: List of The Vampire Diaries characters

text: The Articles of Confederation were designed around a central principle: to keep the independence and sovereignty of the states intact. Accordingly, the national government was granted only the narrow powers that the former colonies had acknowledged as belonging to the king and parliament. Because the federal authority was so limited, the states retained the greater share of governmental power—**the states** held more power under the Articles of Confederation.
title: Articles of Confederation

text: The debating club in Almora was founded in 1871 A.D. when Pt. Buddhiballav Pant established it.
title: Almora

text: Throughout its history, the New England Patriots have taken the field in the Super Bowl ten times, a total that stands as the highest for any franchise. This record includes eight appearances that came after Bill Belichick became head coach and Tom Brady assumed the quarterback role in 2000. Since then, the team has also amassed 15 AFC East titles over 17 seasons beginning in 2001, never posting a losing record during that span. Their achievements feature a 126‑win stretch from 2003 to 2012, an unbeaten 16‑game regular season in 2007, and a 21‑game winning streak that spanned both regular‑season and playoff games from October 2003 to October 2004. Additionally, the Belichick‑Brady partnership holds the NFL record for the most Super Bowl appearances (eight) and victories (five) by a head‑coach/quarterback duo.
title: New England Patriots

text: By the year 1850 a submarine telegraph cable had been installed linking England and France, representing the first underwater line laid beneath the English Channel.
title: Transatlantic telegraph cable

text: In Rococo-era France, an enchantress who appears as a frail beggar woman comes to a castle during a grand ball and offers the cold‑hearted prince a rose in exchange for shelter. When he declines, she reveals her true nature, turning him into a beast and his attendants into household objects, erasing their existence from the memories of their loved ones, and casting a spell on the rose that can only be broken if he learns to love another and earns that love before the final petal falls.
title: Beauty and the Beast (2017 film)

text: Balaam, after receiving Balak’s invitation and God’s reluctant permission, departs with the Moabite princes. While traveling, an Angel of the Lord blocks the road, but only the donkey that Balaam is riding perceives the divine messenger and tries to avoid it. When Balaam strikes the animal for refusing to go forward, God miraculously endows the donkey with speech; the Scripture records that the donkey rebukes Balaam for his harshness in Numbers 22:28. At that instant Balaam also sees the Angel, who tells him that the donkey’s resistance prevented the Angel from killing him, prompting Balaam to repent and continue his mission.
title: Balaam

text: Guinness World Records recognized the Indian playback singer Asha Bhosle in 2011 as the most recorded artist in music history, noting that she has logged more song recordings than any other singer worldwide, surpassing even her sister Lata Mangeshkar.
title: Playback singer

text: The rite of placing ashes on the foreheads of Christians at Ash Wednesday is traced back to a decree of Pope Gregory I the Great (c. 540–604), who is credited with introducing the custom.
title: Ash Wednesday

text: The pop tune “It’s My Party,” which has been covered by numerous performers since the early 1960s, achieved its breakthrough in 1963 when the American vocalist Lesley Gore recorded it. Gore’s version rose to the top of both the United States pop and rhythm‑and‑blues charts, marking the first chart‑topping single produced by Quincy Jones.
title: It's My Party (Lesley Gore song)

text: The BBC first introduced the ending bass line of “The Chain” as its Formula One theme in 1978, and the piece continued to be used for the coverage until the network lost the television rights to ITV Sport in 1997.
title: The Chain

text: The show tune “You’ll Never Walk Alone” made its first appearance as part of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s musical *Carousel*, which opened in 1945.
title: You'll Never Walk Alone

text: The Deer Hunter takes place in the small, working‑class town of Clairton, Pennsylvania, in late 1967. During that time, steelworkers Mike Vronsky, Steven Pushkov and Nick Chevotarevich—along with their friends and co‑workers Stan, Peter “Axel” Axelrod and the local bar owner John Welsh—are preparing for two major rites of passage: marriage and military service.
title: The Deer Hunter

text: Since the 1983‑84 season, the NBA’s all‑time leader in the points‑rebounds double‑double category is Tim Duncan, who has logged a total of 840 such games. This makes Tim Duncan the record‑holder for the most double‑doubles in that statistical combination.
title: Double (basketball)

text: Panic! at the Disco issued their fourth live album, *All My Friends We're Glorious: Death of a Bachelor Live*, on December 15, 2017. The record was made available as a limited‑edition double‑vinyl set and as a digital download. Five days later the band released a non‑album Christmas song titled “Feels Like Christmas,” and on December 27 bassist Dallon Weekes announced his departure after more than eight years with the group.
title: Panic! at the Disco

text: Ashrita Furman (born Keith Furman on September 16, 1954) is a Guinness World Records record‑breaker. By 2017 he had set more than 600 official Guinness records and was listed as the holder of over 191 active records, giving him the distinction of possessing the greatest number of Guinness world records. He has been attempting and breaking records since 1979.
title: Ashrita Furman

text: The series was renewed for a third season, which ran from September 6 to November 1, 2016. Although its future remains unconfirmed, the show has thus far produced three seasons, with the latest being the third season.
title: From Dusk till Dawn: The Series

text: In the 2016 NBA draft, the Milwaukee Bucks used their tenth‑overall selection on Thon Maker. Maker entered the draft as a post‑graduate from Orangeville Prep, a high‑school program located in Orangeville, Ontario, Canada, making him the first player ever taken directly from a Canadian high school. His selection also marked the first time a high‑school player had been chosen in the first round since the 2005 draft.
title: NBA high school draftees

text: The Houston Astros are a Major League Baseball franchise based in Houston, Texas. After 51 seasons competing in the National League, the club transferred to the American League in 2013, becoming a member of the AL West division. Since 2000, the team has played its home games at Minute Maid Park.
title: Houston Astros

text: The Astros moved to the American League in 2013; their first game as an AL club was held on March 31, 2013, when they defeated the Texas Rangers 8–2.
title: Houston Astros

text: The Pennsylvania Railroad completed an uninterrupted rail line connecting Philadelphia and Pittsburgh by 1854, establishing the first passenger service between the two cities.
title: Pennsylvania Railroad

text: Sohrai is a cattle‑worship festival celebrated by the Santal and Oraon peoples of Jharkhand. In the state it is observed in October–November in Ranchi and again in December–January in Dumka.
title: Sohrai

text: The formal text of the Declaration of Independence was composed specifically to be delivered to the Second Continental Congress, which was meeting at the Pennsylvania State House in Philadelphia. When that Congress convened on July 4, 1776, it adopted the declaration, proclaiming the thirteen colonies to be independent sovereign states.
title: United States Declaration of Independence

text: The history of Hawaii records that the first immigrants reached the Hawaiian Islands around 1200, when Tahitian explorers discovered and began to settle the archipelago. This initial settlement marked the start of Hawaiian civilization, which would remain isolated from the wider world for several centuries.
title: History of Hawaii

text: The trademarked catch‑phrase “Let’s get ready to rumble!” was created by American ring announcer Michael Buffer, who was born on November 2, 1944 and is celebrated for his distinctive style of rolling letters and adding inflections when introducing fighters in boxing and professional wrestling.
title: Michael Buffer

text: The Pokémon Trading Card Game does not use the full set of eighteen Pokémon types found in the video games; it limits the game to only eleven distinct types. This reduced type system was created for the card game, with seven types appearing in the original Base Set and the remaining four added later as new sets were released. Consequently, the total number of different kinds of Pokémon cards in the TCG is **eleven**.
title: Pokémon Trading Card Game

text: American singer Cyndi Grecco (born May 19, 1952, in New York, New York) is the vocalist who performed the opening theme for the hit 1970s TV series *Laverne & Shirley*. The song, called “Making Our Dreams Come True” and backed by the Ron Hicklin Singers, was issued as a single that climbed to #25 on the charts on July 25, 1976.
title: Cyndi Grecco

text: The Lykan Hypersport, a limited‑production Lebanese supercar built by W Motors, is the first vehicle designed and manufactured in the Arab world. It appears in the film Fast & Furious 7, where the red Lykan is shown racing through the streets of Abu Dhabi.
title: Lykan HyperSport

text: The sixth installment of the FX horror anthology series American Horror Story is titled American Horror Story: Roanoke. This season, often called simply Roanoke, premiered on September 14, 2016—marking the franchise’s first debut outside of October—and concluded on November 16, 2016.
title: American Horror Story: Roanoke

text: What's My Line? was a panel‑style game show that aired on the CBS Television Network in the United States from 1950 until 1967, later inspiring international adaptations and later U.S. revivals. In its original run the program was moderated by John Daly, with regular panelists Dorothy Kilgallen, Arlene Francis and Bennett Cerf. Contestants were questioned by the celebrity panel to determine their “line of work,” and the panel sometimes had to identify a mystery guest. The series earned three Emmy Awards for Best Quiz or Audience Participation Show (1952, 1953, 1958) and won the Golden Globe for Best TV Show in 1962.
title: What's My Line?

text: Pat McCormick (June 30 1927 – July 29 2005) was an American actor and comedy writer. He is best known for portraying the character Big Enos Burdette in the film Smokey and the Bandit and its two sequels. In addition to his acting, McCormick wrote material for performers such as Red Skelton, Phyllis Diller and Johnny Carson, and contributed to television series like Get Smart. He was noted for his distinctive appearance—standing six feet, seven inches tall, weighing about 250 pounds, and sporting a walrus‑style mustache.
title: Pat McCormick (actor)

text: The track “You Can’t Always Get What You Want,” featured on the 1969 Let It Bleed album, is sung by the Rolling Stones. It was penned by Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, and Rolling Stone magazine ranked it as the 100th‑greatest song of all time in its 2004 “500 Greatest Songs” list.
title: You Can't Always Get What You Want

text: According to Mark Andreessen, product/market fit is achieved when a company is positioned in a favorable market and provides a product that is able to meet the demands of that market.
title: Product/market fit

text: The Golden State Warriors, an NBA franchise based in the San Francisco Bay Area, have captured five league titles. Their championship history began in 1947, when the team won its first NBA championship, followed by additional titles in 1956, 1975, 2015 and 2017.
title: Golden State Warriors

text: John B. Watson, working in the first half of the twentieth century, created methodological behaviorism, a framework that rejected introspective methods and focused exclusively on measuring observable actions and events. His approach laid the groundwork for what later became known as modern behaviorism.
title: Behaviorism

text: Canada, together with Mexico and the United States, was a party to the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). After NAFTA entered into force, commentators began to speculate that the three countries might eventually form a North American Union, modeled on the European Union created by the Maastricht Treaty.
title: North American Union

text: In Tolkien’s legendarium the western ships that carry the elves are bound for Valinor, the realm of the Valar situated in Aman and also called the Undying Lands. This blessed land, while not granting immortality to mortals, is the destination for the immortal peoples of Middle‑earth, and it is where the elf Legolas journeys with his companion.
title: Valinor

text: After Númenor’s ruin, the Undying Lands were withdrawn from the world so that mortals could no longer get there. The Elves are able to reach those realms only by taking the Straight Road and sailing in ships that can pass beyond the earth’s spheres, and they travel to Valinor.
title: Valinor

text: Felix Baumgartner, an Austrian skydiver and daredevil, became famous for leaping to Earth from a helium‑filled balloon in the stratosphere on 14 October 2012. During that descent he set world‑record figures, including a free‑fall distance of about 39 km (24 mi) and a peak speed of roughly 1 357.64 km/h (843.6 mph), which made him the first person to break the sound barrier without the aid of a powered vehicle. His jump also established new records for the altitude of exit, the vertical distance fallen without a drogue parachute, and the vertical speed achieved without a drogue.
title: Felix Baumgartner

text: In the United States, data collected for the year 2004 indicate that the typical hospice patient stayed in the program for an average of 57 days before passing away.
title: Hospice care in the United States

text: In Harper Lee’s *To Kill a Mockingbird*, Calpurnia – the African‑American housekeeper who looks after the Finch children – is also a mother; she brought up her son, Zeebo, to adulthood.
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: In the *To Kill a Mockingbird* character list, Calpurnia is identified as having a son named James Zeebo—often referred to simply as Zeebo. The African‑American woman Lula, who objects to Calpurnia bringing Atticus Finch’s children, Jem and Scout, to church, is described as a longstanding troublemaker with pretentious ideas, and Reverend Sykes warns her that she may be “churched” (subjected to church discipline).
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: In Harper Lee’s *To Kill a Mockingbird*, Calpurnia’s eldest son is Zeebo. He is one of the few members of the First Purchase Church who can read, often leading hymns by “lining” the verses for the congregation. Calpurnia taught him to read, and he also works as Maycomb’s garbage collector, even removing the dead rabid dog, Tim Johnson. When a church member tries to embarrass Scout and Jem for attending with their mother, Zeebo greets the children warmly, showing his quiet kindness.
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: In the 2017 American League Championship Series, the Houston Astros faced the New York Yankees in a best‑of‑seven contest for the league’s pennant and a spot in the World Series. After falling behind 3‑2 in the series, the Astros rallied to win the final two games, securing the American League pennant and advancing to meet the Los Angeles Dodgers in the 2017 World Series.
title: 2017 American League Championship Series

text: By 1912, major motion‑picture companies had established their production facilities near or within Los Angeles, and the city had become the capital of the film industry.
title: Hollywood

text: The vasomotor center, which cooperates with the cardiovascular and respiratory centers to regulate blood pressure and other homeostatic functions, is located in the medulla oblongata. Although the name implies a single “center,” its activity actually depends on a presympathetic network of interacting neurons. Input from cranial nerves IX (glossopharyngeal) and X (vagus) reaches this region, and when central chemoreceptors detect a rise in carbon‑dioxide levels, the center stimulates the sympathetic system to constrict blood vessels. The position of the vasomotor center within the medulla oblongata was first identified by Filipp Ovsyannikov in 1871.
title: Vasomotor center

text: Mexico’s involvement in the 2018 Winter Olympics, held in Pyeongchang, South Korea, spanned from 9 to 25 February 2018, with a delegation of four athletes competing in three different sports.
title: Mexico at the 2018 Winter Olympics

text: Ariana Clarice Richards (born September 11, 1979) is an American actress and painter. She portrayed Lex Murphy, the little girl in the blockbuster film Jurassic Park. Richards earned several Young Artist Awards for her performance before later turning her focus to a career in art.
title: Ariana Richards

text: The United States Constitution places all references to the executive branch in Article Two.  Article Two establishes the executive branch of the federal government and assigns it the responsibility to carry out and enforce federal laws.  It creates the offices of the President and Vice President, authorizes a Cabinet, and provides for executive departments, independent agencies, as well as various boards, commissions, and committees.
title: Article Two of the United States Constitution

text: Season five of *Vikings* was commissioned as a double season of twenty episodes, split into two ten‑episode blocks. The second half is slated to premiere in 2018.
title: Vikings (season 5)

text: In developing B cells the initial recombination step links a D gene segment with a J gene segment, deleting the intervening DNA and creating a DJ complex. The next step brings a V gene segment that lies upstream of this DJ complex into the rearrangement, joining the V segment to the pre‑formed DJ complex to generate a complete VDJ heavy‑chain gene. This V‑DJ joining follows the earlier D‑J recombination and results in the rearranged heavy‑chain locus that will be transcribed.
title: V(D)J recombination

text: Sri Lanka, along with Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, the Maldives, Nepal, India and Pakistan, makes up the region called South Asia. The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), founded in 1985, brings together all eight of these nations.
title: South Asia

text: Although the soundtrack credits Terry Reid for “Gimme Some Lovin’,” the track that actually plays in the film *Days of Thunder* is the original recording by **The Spencer Davis Group**. (Reid later included his own version on the 1991 solo album *The Driver*.)
title: Days of Thunder (soundtrack)

text: At the Ming tombs, a 7‑kilometer (4 mi) avenue leads into the burial complex; this road is called "Spirit Way". Lined with statues of guardian animals and officials, the avenue begins with a massive stone memorial archway erected in 1540, which remains one of the largest stone archways in China. The same thoroughfare, also known as the Sacred Way, terminates at the Great Red Gate—a three‑arch, red‑painted entrance.
title: Ming tombs

text: Publishers Clearing House, whose sweepstakes require no purchase, started in 1995 a tradition of revealing the winners of its $10 million prize just after the Super Bowl. This timing has become a hallmark of the company’s major prize announcements.
title: Publishers Clearing House

title: List of RWBY episodes

text: The franchise’s next championship after the 2004 campaign came in the 2017 season, when the Philadelphia Eagles secured the title by winning Super Bowl LII.
title: 2004 Philadelphia Eagles season

text: According to the Tanakh, the First Temple in Jerusalem was erected during the united monarchy under King Solomon. 1 Kings 6:1 records that building began in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, and scholars traditionally place his reign between roughly 970 and 931 BCE. Because of these conventional dates, the start of the temple’s construction falls in the mid-10th century BCE. The biblical account also notes that Hiram I of Tyre supplied architects, laborers, and cedar timber for Solomon’s project, and that the temple itself required seven years to complete, while the entire building program—including Solomon’s palace—took twenty years. During this period the temple was dedicated to Yahweh and housed the Ark of the Covenant.
title: Solomon's Temple

text: Earle Hyman (October 11 1926 – November 17 2017) was an American actor who performed on stage, television, and in films. In addition to voicing Panthro and other characters on the animated series *ThunderCats*, he appeared on the sitcom *The Cosby Show* as Russell Huxtable, the father of Cliff Huxtable, thereby serving as the series’ grandfather.
title: Earle Hyman

text: The Hebrew word shalom (שָׁלוֹם), which can also appear as sholom, sholem, sholoim, or shulem, translates into English as peace.
title: Shalom

text: In English, the Hebrew term shalom is understood to mean peace. It can describe peace between two parties—such as between a person and God or between nations—as well as the overall well‑being, welfare, or safety of an individual or a group. The word also appears in many related expressions and names, and its cognates include Arabic salaam, Maltese sliem, Syriac‑Assyrian Shlama, and Ethiopian Semitic sälam, all tracing back to the Proto‑Semitic root Š‑L‑M.
title: Shalom

text: In 1885, Hermann Ebbinghaus gathered experimental data that enabled him to draw one of the earliest forgetting curves, mapping how memory fades over time.
title: Forgetting curve

text: In the film’s concluding telethon sequence, the character’s solo whistling is performed by musician Andrew Bird. Earlier, Walter wrestles with the question of whether he is human or a Muppet, a conflict that resolves in the award‑winning number “Man or Muppet,” with the human version of Walter portrayed by Jim Parsons. After accepting his true nature, Walter adopts whistling as his signature skill and becomes the newest member of the Muppet ensemble.
title: Walter (Muppet)

text: Scotland’s most recent FIFA World Cup qualification occurred in 1998, when Craig Brown steered the side to the finals as the best runner‑up; the nation has not taken part in another World Cup since that tournament.
title: Scotland at the FIFA World Cup

text: The 2016 biographical war drama *Hacksaw Ridge* tells the World II story of Desmond Doss, a Seventh‑day Adventist combat medic who refused to bear arms and later became the first conscientious objector to receive the Medal of Honor for his actions at the Battle of Okinawa. The film was directed by Mel Gibson and written by Andrew Knight and Robert Schenkkan, adapting the 2004 documentary *The Conscientious Objector*. Andrew Garfield stars as Doss, portraying the film’s central character, while Sam Worthington, Luke Bracey, Teresa Palmer, Hugo Weaving, Rachel Griffiths and Vince Vaughn appear in supporting roles.
title: Hacksaw Ridge

text: The Bee Gees recorded the pop ballad “How Deep Is Your Love” in 1977, and the song was released as a single in September 1977.
title: How Deep Is Your Love (Bee Gees song)

text: When iron is exposed to oxygen together with water or atmospheric moisture, it undergoes a redox reaction that produces rust. Rust is the common name for the reddish iron oxide that forms under these conditions. Chemically, rust consists of hydrated iron(III) oxides, represented as Fe₂O₃·nH₂O, and iron(III) oxide‑hydroxide species such as FeO(OH) and Fe(OH)₃. Different visual appearances and spectroscopic signatures can be observed for the various forms of rust that develop in different environments.
title: Rust

text: When iron or an iron‑based alloy such as steel is left in the presence of oxygen and moisture for an extended time, the metal gradually transforms into rust. Rust is the common name for iron oxide, a compound that results from the atomic‑level combination of oxygen with the metal. This reaction creates a new oxide layer and weakens the original metallic bonds. Although the term “oxidation” describes many reactions of metals with oxygen, only iron and its alloys produce rust; other metals may corrode in different ways.
title: Rust

text: The Continental Congress cast its decisive vote on July 2, 1776, passing a resolution that declared the colonies independent. Two days after this vote, the formal Declaration of Independence was issued, announcing the creation of a new nation, the United States of America.
title: Continental Congress

text: The British ocean liner RMS Titanic went down in the North Atlantic Ocean in the early hours of 15 April 1912 after colliding with an iceberg during its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York.
title: RMS Titanic

text: Historians examining the origins of the American Civil War agree that the immediate catalyst to the conflict was slavery. While scholars debate whether ideological, economic, political, or social tensions were most decisive, they concur that disputes over slavery ultimately drove the Southern states to secede and sparked the war.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: The immediate trigger for the American Civil War was slavery. Southern political leaders opposed Northern antislavery attempts to block the spread of slavery into the western territories, and this resistance set off the secession movement that led to the formation of the Confederacy.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: After water enters the soil, it can either stay in the soil, travel downward to the groundwater table, or, if plant roots do not absorb it, become runoff.
title: Infiltration (hydrology)

text: Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi social entrepreneur, banker, and economist, is credited with pioneering the ideas of microcredit and microfinance through his establishment of the Grameen Bank, which offers small loans to entrepreneurs who are too poor to obtain traditional bank financing.
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: In 1976, Muhammad Yunus recognized that providing very small loans could have a disproportionate impact on impoverished households. While visiting the village of Jobra near Chittagong University, he saw that women who crafted bamboo furniture were forced to accept usurious credit to purchase raw material, only to surrender their earnings to the lenders. Conventional banks refused to offer such tiny loans at reasonable rates because they deemed the risk of default too high. Yunus, however, believed that given an opportunity, the poor would repay the money, making micro‑credit a viable business model. He tested this idea by lending US $27 of his own funds to 42 village women, each of whom earned a modest profit of BDT 0.50 (US $0.02) on the loan, thereby establishing the foundation of modern micro‑financing.
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: The compression‑release engine brake—commonly known as a Jake or Jacobs brake—is a device fitted to some diesel engines. When the driver activates it, the brake opens the exhaust valves right after the compression stroke, venting the compressed air from the cylinders and thereby slowing the vehicle.
title: Compression release engine brake

text: The song’s creators have consistently rejected any reading that links it to drug use. Leonard Lipton has explicitly said that “Puff the Magic Dragon is not about drugs,” and Peter Yarrow has repeatedly emphasized that the piece is meant to convey the hardships of growing older. Yarrow also notes that the song’s only meaning is the obvious one—its focus on the loss of innocence in children—and dismisses drug‑related interpretations as careless speculation.
title: Puff, the Magic Dragon

text: The engagement known as the First Battle of Bull Run—referred to as the First Battle of Manassas by the Southern side—occurred on July 21, 1861 in Prince William County, Virginia, about 25 miles west‑southwest of Washington, D.C. Each army fielded roughly 18,000 troops, many of whom were poorly trained and led. Union forces were slow to take up positions, giving Confederate reinforcements time to arrive by rail, and the fighting ended in a Confederate victory, followed by a disorganized retreat of the Union troops.
title: First Battle of Bull Run

text: The Ming dynasty (1368–1644) was governed by imperial rule, a system that, while dominant, gradually lost strength as the era progressed.
title: Economy of the Ming dynasty

text: Andreas Vesalius (31 December 1514 – 15 October 1564) was a Flemish physician of the sixteenth century who authored the landmark anatomical treatise *De humani corporis fabrica* (On the Fabric of the Human Body). His work established him as a pivotal figure in the development of modern human anatomy.
title: Andreas Vesalius

text: In 2015 Houston’s city charter was revised so that the mayor’s office shifted from two‑year terms to a single four‑year term, and the office is now limited to two four-year terms. This means a person elected mayor can serve a maximum of two consecutive four‑year periods before being barred from running again for that position.
title: Politics of Houston

text: The First Battle of Corinth, also referred to as the Siege of Corinth, was a Civil War engagement that spanned from April 29 to May 30, 1862. Union forces commanded by Major General Henry Halleck besieged the town, while Confederate troops under General P.G.T. Beauregard defended it. The fighting took place in Corinth, Mississippi, and concluded with the Federal capture of the city.
title: Siege of Corinth

text: Article One of the United States Constitution sets three qualifications for members of the House of Representatives. One of these is a minimum age: a candidate must be at least 25 years old. In addition, the individual must reside in the state they wish to represent and must have been a United States citizen for the seven years preceding the election.
title: Article One of the United States Constitution

text: During the Wild Card round of the postseason, the Kansas City Chiefs faced the Tennessee Titans, losing a tight 22‑21 contest in which Derrick Henry rushed for 156 yards. The defeat marked another disappointing season for Kansas City and extended their NFL record of consecutive home playoff losses to six.
title: Kansas City Chiefs

text: Charley was the third named storm and second hurricane of the 2004 Atlantic hurricane season, lasting from August 9 to August 15. At its peak it generated 150 mph (240 km/h) winds, which placed it in Category 4 on the Saffir‑Simpson Hurricane Scale. The system struck southwestern Florida while at that intensity, making it a Category 4 hurricane when it hit the state.
title: Hurricane Charley

text: When Hurricane Charley reached the southwest coast of Florida on August 13, it came ashore near Cayo Costa at about 19:45 UTC with sustained winds near 150 mph (240 km/h). At that moment the storm was rated as a Category 4 hurricane, making landfall with a central pressure of 941 mbar. The same classification—4—was recorded for the system as it moved inland toward Punta Gorda an hour later.
title: Hurricane Charley

text: The NBA’s All‑Star starters are chosen through a three‑part voting system that includes fans, players and members of the media. Since the 2017 revision, the fan component—referred to as fan voting—contributes half of the total vote tally, while player and media ballots each supply a quarter. Because fan voting supplies the greatest portion of the overall vote, it represents the source of the most votes for the All‑Star Game.
title: NBA All-Star Game

text: The adrenal glands secrete epinephrine, which stimulates beta‑2 adrenergic receptors in skeletal muscle, the heart, the lungs, and the brain during a sympathoadrenal response. This release works together with norepinephrine‑induced vasoconstriction of most blood vessels, enabling the sympathetic nervous system to redirect blood flow toward tissues needed for intense physical activity.
title: Sympathetic nervous system

text: In the track titled “People Are Crazy,” the narrator recounts a conversation in a bar that culminates in the old man’s refrain, “God is great, beer is good / And people are crazy.” The recording of this song is performed by Currington, whose vocal range on the track spans from B♭3 to D5.
title: People Are Crazy

text: In Islamic practice, the head‑covering garment worn by many Muslim women is called the hijab, also known as al‑khimar. This veil or scarf is intended to cover the head, breasts, neck and other parts of the body in accordance with modesty guidelines. The Qur’an instructs believing women to place their khimar over their bosoms, which has been interpreted by some scholars as an obligation for women to wear the hijab. While the Qur’an emphasizes modest dress and the covering of the breasts and genitals, it does not explicitly require every woman to cover her head, leaving the hijab’s status as a matter of interpretation.
title: Islam and clothing

text: The customary head covering worn by Muslim women is called the hijab, an Arabic noun that literally means “to cover.” This garment has become a visible marker of Islamic presence in Western Europe, and its use has sparked political debates and proposals for bans on face‑covering attire in several countries.
title: Islam and clothing

text: The Democratic Party took on its modern designation in the 1830s, when it arose from the disintegrated factions of the earlier Democratic‑Republican Party. This transformation was driven by Martin Van Buren, who organized a network of politicians across the states to support the war‑hero president Andrew Jackson of Tennessee.
title: History of the United States Democratic Party

text: The environmental impact of aviation includes its share of global anthropogenic CO₂ emissions. A 2007 report from the Environmental Change Institute at Oxford University estimates that aviation contributes a **4 percent cumulative effect** to human‑made climate change.
title: Environmental impact of aviation

text: The 2018 Elimination Chamber featured six contests, one of which took place on the pre‑show. In the headline bout, Roman Reigns won the first‑ever seven‑man Elimination Chamber match, earning the right to challenge Brock Lesnar for the Universal Championship at WrestleMania 34. The undercard included Alexa Bliss retaining the Raw Women’s Championship in the inaugural women’s Elimination Chamber, and Asuka defeating Nia Jax to extend her unbeaten streak while preventing Jax from joining her WrestleMania 34 title match. The event also highlighted Ronda Rousey’s signing of a Raw contract, during which she confronted COO Triple H and Raw Commissioner Stephanie McMahon in her first appearance since the night after Survivor Series.
title: Elimination Chamber (2018)

text: In the realms of publishing, art and communication, the word “content” denotes the information and experiences that are intended for a specific audience or end‑user. It is essentially the material that is expressed through various media—such as speech, writing, film, television, digital platforms, books, magazines, or live presentations—and delivered to convey meaning to listeners, readers, or viewers.
title: Content (media)

text: In communication, the element referred to as content is essentially the information that is delivered through a medium. This “information” constitutes the value that the end‑user receives, independent of the channel or any additional features of the medium.
title: Content (media)

text: Mercedes-Benz Stadium is a multi‑purpose retractable‑roof arena situated in Atlanta, Georgia. It serves as the home venue for the NFL’s Atlanta Falcons and Major League Soccer’s Atlanta United FC, taking the place of the nearby Georgia Dome that had hosted the Falcons for 25 years from 1992 until 2016.
title: Mercedes-Benz Stadium

text: The new football stadium in Atlanta, called Mercedes-Benz Stadium, is slated to be built on a large parking lot in the Vine City neighborhood, which lies less than a mile north of the former Georgia Dome site.  Reports from April 2012 indicated that the project’s cost had risen to roughly $947.7 million and that construction would begin in 2014, with the Falcons expected to start regular‑season play there in 2017.  Once the new venue is finished, the Georgia Dome will be demolished.
title: Mercedes-Benz Stadium

text: The San Jose Sharks are a professional ice‑hockey franchise that began play in the 1991‑92 NHL season. After their first season at the Cow Palace, the team relocated in 1993 to its current arena, the SAP Center, which is also referred to as the SAP Center at San Jose and is locally nicknamed the Shark Tank. Since that move, the Sharks have held all of their home games at this venue.
title: San Jose Sharks

text: An adult human has a total of 206 bones. They are split between the axial skeleton, which contains 94 bones (28 in the skull and 52 in the torso), and the appendicular skeleton, which holds the remaining 126 bones found in the limbs—32 in each arm and 31 in each leg. Because the appendicular skeleton accounts for 126 of the 206 bones, more than half of the bones are located in the appendicular skeleton.
title: List of bones of the human skeleton

text: The 1986 stage work The Phantom of the Opera is a musical whose score was composed by Andrew Lloyd Webber. Its lyrics were supplied by Charles Hart and Richard Stilgoe, who also collaborated with Lloyd Webber on the book. The production adapts Gaston Leroux’s French novel Le Fantôme de l’Opéra and centers on the celebrated soprano Christine Daaé, who becomes the object of obsession for a mysterious, disfigured musical genius hidden beneath the opera house.
title: The Phantom of the Opera (1986 musical)

text: In the Scopes trial, the state of Tennessee was represented by William Jennings Bryan, the three‑time presidential candidate who argued on behalf of the prosecution.
title: Scopes Trial

text: Rachel Kelly Tucker (born 29 May 1981) is a Northern Irish singer and actress who is perhaps best known for portraying Elphaba—the Wicked Witch of the West—in the musical Wicked, a role she performed both in the West End and on Broadway.
title: Rachel Tucker

text: During the Mauryan era, the ruler who pursued the annexation of Kalinga was Ashoka, the son of Bindusara. In 261 B.C. he launched a campaign against Kalinga, whose many sea ports and position on the main north‑south trade routes made it strategically valuable, and a battle was fought near the Daya River close to present‑day Bhubaneswar in Orissa.
title: Kalinga under the Mauryan

text: In the United States and Canada, a political action committee (PAC) is an organization that pools campaign contributions from members and then uses those funds to support or oppose candidates, ballot initiatives, or legislation. When a group spends or receives more than $1,000 to influence a federal election, it must register as a PAC with the Federal Election Commission under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended by the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act of 2002. State laws provide similar definitions for PAC status at the state level.
title: Political action committee

text: The Tiber, called Tiberis in Latin and Tevere in Italian, is a river that begins in the Apennine Mountains of Emilia‑Romagna and flows roughly 406 kilometres (252 mi) through Tuscany, Umbria and Lazio before emptying into the Tyrrhenian Sea between Ostia and Fiumicino. Its basin drains an area of about 17,375 km² (6,709 mi²). The Tiber has achieved lasting fame as the main watercourse of the city of Rome, which was founded on its eastern banks.
title: Tiber

text: Mount Whitney stands as the highest summit in the contiguous United States, reaching an elevation of 14,505 feet (4,421 m). Located on the border of Inyo and Tulare counties in California, the peak lies within the Sierra Nevada range, with its western slopes forming part of Sequoia National Park and its eastern side belonging to the Inyo National Forest. The mountain’s summit also marks the southern end of the John Muir Trail, which extends over 200 miles through the Sierra Nevada.
title: Mount Whitney

text: The television series The Walking Dead is primarily shot in the state of Georgia, where a long‑standing tax incentive program has encouraged large film productions to locate their filming there.
title: The Walking Dead (TV series)

text: After Bill reads a newspaper article describing a beauty‑queen who has died from a drug overdose, he goes to the morgue to view the corpse. There he confirms that the body belongs to a woman named Mandy. Later, Ziegler tells Bill that Mandy was a prostitute and drug addict whose death was the result of an accidental overdose, unrelated to the secret society’s machinations. Thus, the girl who dies in *Eyes Wide Shut* is identified as Mandy.
title: Eyes Wide Shut

text: The northernmost land engagement of the American Civil War occurred in St. Albans, Vermont. In this controversial operation, Confederate soldiers crossed from Canada on October 19, 1864, raiding the town to steal bank funds and to tempt the Union Army into diverting troops to protect the northern border against further incursions.
title: St. Albans Raid

text: Sudden chest pain is a common reason for emergency medical calls. Evidence indicates that giving **Aspirin** improves survival in acute coronary syndrome, and it is considered appropriate for EMS personnel to advise patients with sudden chest pain to take aspirin, provided they have not had any recent serious bleeding.
title: Chest pain

text: Principal exteriors were shot on location in the United Kingdom. A second unit filmed the medieval walls and towers of the Cité de Carcassonne in the town of Carcassonne, Aude, France, to represent Nottingham and its castle. Locksley Castle was portrayed by Wardour Castle in Wiltshire, enhanced in an early shot with a matte painting. Marian’s manor was filmed at Hulne Priory in Northumberland. Scenes set in Sherwood Forest were captured at various English sites: Burnham Beeches in Buckinghamshire served as the outlaws’ encampment, Aysgarth Falls in Yorkshire was used for the fight between Robin and Little John, and Hardraw Force in North Yorkshire was the spot where Marian sees Robin bathing. Sycamore Gap on Hadrian’s Wall provided the setting for Robin’s first confrontation with the sheriff’s men, while the chalk cliffs at Seven Sisters, Sussex, stood in for Robin’s return to England from the Crusades.
title: Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves

text: Executive orders issued by the President of the United States must be grounded in the Constitution; they must derive either from a specific constitutional clause—most often the powers enumerated in Article II—or from authority that Congress has delegated to the executive branch.
title: Executive order (United States)

text: Jenna Boyd, who relocated from Bedford, Texas to Los Angeles with her family to pursue acting, appeared in early projects such as *Dickie Roberts: Former Child Star* and later earned notice in *The Missing*. In 2005, Jenna Boyd portrayed the leukemia‑suffering Bailey Graffman in *The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants*. Subsequent work includes roles in the Lifetime miniseries *The Gathering* and an episode of *Ghost Whisperer*, as well as playing Paige Hardaway in the Netflix series *Atypical* (2017).
title: Jenna Boyd

text: By July 2017, India’s network of national parks numbered 103, together covering roughly 40,500 km² (about 15,600 sq mi), which is around 1.23 % of the country’s total land area. This count reflects the federal wildlife‑protection measures that were reinforced during the 1980s.
title: List of national parks of India

text: The Governor Edmund G. Brown California Aqueduct is a network of canals, tunnels and pipelines that moves water collected from the Sierra Nevada Mountains, along with water from valleys in Northern and Central California, to Southern California. Extending over 400 miles (approximately 640 km), it serves as the central element of the California State Water Project.
title: California Aqueduct

text: The Canadian Shield—also known as the Laurentian Plateau—is a vast expanse of exposed Precambrian igneous and high‑grade metamorphic rock that forms the ancient core of the North American continent. This geological shield stretches from the Great Lakes northward to the Arctic Ocean, covering more than half of Canada and reaching into the northern United States. Because the region is dominated by a thin veneer of soil over a deep, continuous bedrock, human settlement is sparse and overall industrial development is limited. Nevertheless, mining is prevalent throughout the Shield, making it the primary industry in the area.
title: Canadian Shield

text: The Canadian Shield holds some of the world’s richest mineral ore deposits, including nickel, gold, silver and copper, and it is dotted with numerous towns that extract these resources; consequently, mining is the dominant industry throughout the Shield.
title: Canadian Shield

text: A minibike, which may also be called a minimoto or pocketbike, is a miniature motorcycle. Most of these small bikes are powered by two‑stroke engines and use chain drive.
title: Minibike

text: Kathleen Erin Walsh (born October 13, 1967) is an American actress and businesswoman. She is known for portraying Dr. Addison Montgomery on the ABC television drama Grey’s Anatomy (as well as its spin‑off Private Practice).
title: Kate Walsh (actress)

text: In Israel, citizens who are Jewish, Druze or Circassian and who have reached the age of 18 are subject to conscription, while Arab Israelis are not drafted and other individuals may be exempt for religious, physical or psychological reasons. The standard period of mandatory military service is currently two years and eight months for men—some occupations require an additional four months—and two years for women. This means the service length is two years for women.
title: Conscription in Israel

text: Marvin is a masculine given name that originates from the Welsh name Mervyn. It also appears as a surname, and a related spelling variant is Marven.
title: Marvin (name)

text: The American sitcom Sabrina the Teenage Witch first aired on ABC on September 27, 1996, switched to The WB beginning with its fifth season, and wrapped up on April 24, 2003. Across its seven‑season lifespan, the series delivered a total of 163 episodes.
title: List of Sabrina the Teenage Witch episodes

text: Tami Roman was previously married to basketball player Kenny Anderson, and the couple had two children together.
title: Tami Roman

text: The heart’s electrical conduction system begins with a pacemaking impulse that triggers myocardial contraction. This impulse is generated in the sinoatrial node, after which it spreads across the right atrium, reaches the atrioventricular node, travels down the Bundle of His and its branches, and finally causes the right and left atria and ventricles to contract, allowing blood to be pumped throughout the body.
title: Electrical conduction system of the heart

text: The well‑known declaration “Ich bin ein Berliner” was spoken on 26 June 1963 in West Berlin by U.S. President John F. Kennedy. Delivered 22 months after the Berlin Wall’s construction, the speech was meant to affirm American support for West Germany and to confront Soviet policy. In the same address Kennedy also used the German sentence “Lasst sie nach Berlin kommen” (“Let them come to Berlin”).
title: Ich bin ein Berliner

text: Territorial losses for the Western Roman Empire became irreversible after the massive incursion of the Goths in 376. This wave of Gothic forces ultimately overcame the empire’s final standing field army in Europe, leaving the Western Roman state without any effective military power. The Goths defeated the last remaining Roman army in Europe.
title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

text: The Himadri Station, inaugurated on 1 July 2008 by India’s Minister of Earth Sciences, is the country’s first Arctic research outpost. It was established during India’s second Arctic expedition in June 2008 and is situated at the International Arctic Research Base in Ny‑Ålesund, Svalbard, Norway, roughly 1,200 km (750 mi) from the North Pole.
title: Himadri Station

text: The line where the Indian Plate meets the Eurasian Plate runs through Nepal, and the intense collision there has generated an orogenic belt. This belt is the same geological feature that gave rise to the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalaya Mountains.
title: Indian Plate

text: The Last Supper, a mural painted in the late 15th century, was created by Leonardo da Vinci and is displayed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. It is regarded as one of the most instantly recognizable works of art in the world.
title: The Last Supper (Leonardo da Vinci)

text: Gothic art first appeared in the early 12th century in the Île‑de‑France region of France, emerging at the Abbey Church of Saint‑Denis. This groundbreaking project was undertaken by Abbot Suger, whose patronage is credited with launching the new artistic movement. From that initial example the style rapidly expanded beyond architecture to encompass sculpture, textile work, and a range of painting techniques—including fresco, stained‑glass windows, illuminated manuscripts, and panel painting. Monastic orders such as the Cistercians and Carthusians were instrumental in disseminating the style throughout Europe and developing regional variations. By the late 14th century a more unified International Gothic style had taken shape, persisting into the late 15th century and beyond in many areas.
title: Gothic art

text: In The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the central theme is expressed as a violation of nature, a breach that produces intense psychological effects on the mariner himself and on every listener of his story. Scholars such as Jerome McGann have also read the work as a salvation narrative, noting its multi‑layered structure that mirrors Coleridge’s interest in higher criticism. Like the Iliad, Paradise Lost, or Dante’s Divine Comedy, the poem is considered a transhistorical piece rather than one of fixed universal significance.
title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

text: The overview of currencies used within the European Union notes that the single monetary unit shared by the member states that have joined the monetary union is called the euro. These states form the eurozone and operate under the European Central Bank, while other EU countries retain their own independent currencies.
title: Currencies of the European Union

text: The European Union’s common monetary unit is called the euro. It originated from the EU’s economic and monetary‑union project, which reached full implementation on 1 January 2002. Today the euro serves as the official currency of the majority of EU member states—only two are still exempt from mandatory adoption—and it is also the money used by EU institutions.
title: Currencies of the European Union

text: In the late nineteenth century, the European imperial powers carried out a massive scramble for African territory, establishing colonial holdings that ultimately set the borders of the continent’s present‑day countries.
title: Africa

text: The 1996‑set action film *Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man* follows two longtime friends as they battle corporate developers in a gritty Los Angeles future. The title character, Harley Davidson, is a biker‑clad anti‑hero who is portrayed by Mickey Rourke. Alongside him, Don Johnson appears as the Marlboro Man, while the story unfolds through bar fights, a daring armored‑car heist, and a final showdown in a skyscraper penthouse. The movie was largely shot around Tucson, Arizona, including scenes at the Davis‑Mountan Air Force Base “Boneyard.”
title: Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man

text: During the American Civil War, the land forces that fought for the Confederacy were organized as the Confederate States Army. This army served as the military land force of the Confederate States of America throughout the conflict, including at the Battle of Gettysburg.
title: Confederate States Army

text: The acetate ion, written as CH₃COO⁻ (also expressed as CH₃CO₂⁻), is the negatively charged species that results when acetic acid loses a proton. In chemical terminology this species is classified as a **polyatomic anion**. It functions as the conjugate base of acetic acid and can combine with various cations to form neutral acetate salts such as lead acetate or aluminum acetate.
title: Acetate

text: In the AMC horror drama *The Walking Dead*, the character Merle Dixon is introduced as the brother of Daryl Dixon. Merle Dixon appears early in the first season as a Southern‑style hunter whose abrasive, misogynistic and racist attitudes create friction with the other survivors. After a confrontation with group leader Rick Grimes, Merle disappears and later aligns himself with the Woodbury community, serving as the right‑hand man to its leader, the Governor, before becoming entangled in the ongoing conflict between the Governor and Rick’s group.
title: Merle Dixon

text: The forms IIII (for four) and VIIII (for nine) caused confusion, so they are normally written using subtractive notation. In this system the number four is represented as IV (one less than V), and nine as IX (one less than X).
title: Roman numerals

text: Malware, short for malicious software, is the collective name applied to any program that is intentionally created to damage, disable, or steal data. The term covers a wide range of harmful applications such as computer viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, scareware and other malicious programs, which may be delivered as executable code, scripts, active content, or other software forms. Its defining characteristic is the malicious intent to act against the user’s requirements, distinguishing it from software that causes accidental harm.
title: Malware

text: The United States entered World War I by formally declaring war on Austria-Hungary on December 7, 1917.
title: American entry into World War I

text: Milling is a machining process that removes material by making a series of small, separate cuts. In this operation a multi‑toothed cutter is rotated at high speed while the workpiece is either advanced slowly through the cutter or the cutter is fed into the workpiece. Because the cutter must run at such high rotational speeds, it is commonly fabricated from high‑speed tool steel. The speed at which the workpiece moves relative to one full revolution of the cutter is referred to as the feed rate.
title: Milling (machining)

text: In milling, the cutter’s cutting edges are usually fabricated from hard, temperature‑resistant materials so that they wear slowly. For low‑cost cutters, those cutting surfaces are often made of high‑speed steel, whereas more expensive tools may employ cemented carbide or be coated with thin films to further improve hardness and reduce friction.
title: Milling (machining)

text: In the Dragon Age series, the character Alistair was chiefly written by lead writer David Gaider, and his spoken performance is provided by Steve Valentine.
title: Alistair (Dragon Age)

text: Lionel Richie’s hit single “All Night Long (All Night)” was issued in 1983, appearing on his second solo album, Can’t Slow Down.
title: All Night Long (All Night)

text: American character actor Howard Caine (born Howard Cohen; January 2 1926 – December 28 1993) is best remembered for playing Gestapo Major Wolfgang Hochstetter in the television series Hogan’s Heroes, which ran from 1965 to 1971.
title: Howard Caine

text: In “Diamonds & Rust,” Baez describes an unexpected phone call from a former lover that throws her back to a rundown Greenwich Village hotel in the mid‑1960s, where she remembers giving him a pair of cuff‑links and reflects on the blend of treasured and tarnished memories she calls “diamonds and rust.” She has explicitly stated that the song’s subject is her relationship with Bob Dylan.
title: Diamonds & Rust (song)

text: In the television drama 7th Heaven, the eldest Camden child—Matthew “Matt” Camden, the firstborn of Annie and Eric—is portrayed by Barry Watson.
title: List of 7th Heaven characters

text: Henry James’s novella *The Turn of the Screw* made its debut in 1898, first appearing in serial form in Collier’s Weekly between 27 January and 16 April of that year, and later that October being published in the collection *The Two Magics*.
title: The Turn of the Screw

text: In governmental contexts, the word authority denotes the legitimate claim and right to exercise power, identifying having official power to act. While power describes the ability to influence someone’s behavior, authority specifically conveys the justification and recognized right to use that power, such as a court’s authority to impose legal punishments.
title: Authority

text: The Caucasus Mountains are a mountain system located in West Asia, extending from the Black Sea to the Caspian Sea within the Caucasus region.
title: Caucasus Mountains

text: The Ozarks consist of two main ranges—the Boston Mountains in Arkansas and the St. Francis Mountains in Missouri. The summit known as Lookout, which is also called Buffalo Lookout, rises within the Boston Mountains and represents the highest point of the entire Ozark highlands.
title: Ozarks

text: Carl Hiaasen’s 2002 young‑adult novel *Hoot* unfolds in Florida, where newcomer Roy befriends two eccentric characters, clashes with a hostile rival, and joins a campaign to stop a pancake‑house development that would destroy a colony of burrowing owls on the site. The book earned a Newbery Honor in 2003, and a film adaptation starring Logan Lerman, Brie Larson, and Cody Linley was released in May 2006, with Hiaasen and director‑writer Wil Shriner striving to keep the movie true to the original story.
title: Hoot (novel)

text: In the novel *Hoot*, the narrative follows Roy Eberhardt after he relocates to Florida, taking up residence in the small town of Coconut Cove. There, he encounters his classmate Dana Matherson, who begins to bully him, and he witnesses a mysterious boy running barefoot near the school bus. The story’s events—all from Roy’s perspective—unfold against the backdrop of this Florida setting.
title: Hoot (novel)

text: Japan’s system of government is a constitutional monarchy, meaning that the Emperor’s authority is largely symbolic and confined to ceremonial functions. The state’s political structure is organized into three separate branches: an executive branch, a legislative branch, and a judicial branch.
title: Government of Japan

text: The initial discharge in the episode known as the “shot heard round the world” occurred at the North Bridge, where the first shots were fired by **Americans acting under orders**. This engagement marked the first organized American volley, produced the first British casualties, and forced the British to retreat. Earlier gunfire at Lexington resulted in eight American deaths and a lightly wounded British soldier, but those incidents are described as a chaotic massacre rather than a formal battle.
title: Shot heard round the world

text: Crowne Plaza is an upscale, full‑service hotel chain that caters primarily to business travelers and the meetings‑and‑conventions market. The brand is owned by InterContinental Hotels Group, which also includes InterContinental Hotels & Resorts and Holiday Inn Hotels & Resorts in its portfolio. Crowne Plaza operates in more than 50 countries, with over 400 properties located in city centres, resort areas, coastal towns and near major airports.
title: Crowne Plaza

text: The lingam is a column‑like or oval (egg‑shaped) emblem of Shiva, crafted from stone, metal or clay. In Shaivite Hindu temples it appears as a smooth cylindrical mass positioned at the centre of the shrine, often set within a rimmed, disc‑shaped base that represents Shakti. This Shiva Linga is a mark that reminds of the Omnipotent Lord, symbolising the formless, all‑pervasive reality of Shiva.
title: Lingam

text: "Heroes and Villains" is the title of a BBC Only Fools and Horses episode that aired on 25 December 1996 as the first part of the 1996 Christmas trilogy and the thirteenth Christmas special. The broadcast drew a record UK audience of 21.3 million viewers. In this episode, Del and Rodney are invited to a fancy‑dress party and arrive dressed as Batman and Robin.
title: Heroes and Villains (Only Fools and Horses)

text: In the 1998 season, Mark O'Meara secured two of golf’s major titles, winning The Masters and later the British Open. His Masters triumph arrived on his 15th attempt, and that same year he also captured the Cisco World Match Play Championship while climbing to a career‑high second place in the Official World Golf Ranking.
title: Mark O'Meara

text: The debut volume of the Horrid Henry series, written by Francesca Simon and illustrated by Tony Ross, was published in 1994; it compiles a set of short stories about the same characters, in the tradition of the Just William books.
title: Horrid Henry (book)

text: A nod of the head—where the head moves in up‑and‑down arcs along the sagittal plane—constitutes a gesture. In many societies this movement is commonly employed, though not everywhere, to convey meanings such as agreement, acceptance, acknowledgment, or, when performed in the opposite direction, a refusal or “no.”
title: Nod (gesture)

text: The artificial sea‑level waterway called the Suez Canal is situated in Egypt, where it joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea across the Isthmus of Suez.
title: Suez Canal

text: In the National Basketball Association, a basketball court is specified to be 94 by 50 feet, which is the standard size used for professional games. This dimension distinguishes the NBA court from other variations, such as the slightly smaller FIBA court, but the NBA measurement remains fixed at 94 by 50 feet.
title: Basketball court

text: In the 2018 Sri Lankan local elections, about 70 % of eligible voters turned out, and the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna—headed by former president Mahinda Rajapaksa—won the largest share of seats and control of local authorities.
title: Sri Lankan local elections, 2018

text: The 1967 single “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” was issued under the name Frankie Valli, identifying him as the performer of the track. The record became one of his most successful releases, earning a gold certification and climbing to No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 for a week, held back by The Association’s “Windy.” It was co‑written with his Four Seasons bandmate Bob Gaudio and remained Valli’s biggest solo hit until he topped the chart in 1974 with “My Eyes Adored You.”
title: Can't Take My Eyes Off You

text: Lake Placid, New York, served as the host city for the Winter Olympic Games on two separate occasions—in 1932 and later in 1980—making it, together with St. Moritz and Innsbruck, one of the few sites that have hosted the Winter Olympics twice.
title: Lake Placid, New York

text: The expression “hot rod” is recorded as having emerged in the late 1930s in southern California, where enthusiasts began racing altered automobiles on the dry lake beds northeast of Los Angeles under the auspices of groups such as the Southern California Timing Association (SCTA). After World II the practice grew even more popular, especially in California, as many veterans returned with technical skills gained during their service. Earlier, bootleggers had also equipped cars to evade revenue agents during Prohibition, and some police departments modified vehicles for similar purposes.
title: Hot rod

text: Commander Kawas Manekshaw Nanavati’s murder trial against the State of Maharashtra began in 1959, when the Indian courts heard the case involving the death of Prem Ahuja, his wife’s lover. The proceedings, which drew unprecedented media coverage, were later dramatized in films such as the 1973 movie *Achanak* and the 2016 film *Rustom*. Although a jury initially returned a not‑guilty verdict, the Bombay High Court set aside that decision and ordered a bench trial, making it one of the last jury trials in India before the practice was largely abolished. Nanavati was eventually pardoned by Governor Vijayalakshmi Pandit.
title: K. M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra

text: In the original black‑and‑white television series *The Addams Family*, the role of Morticia Addams was performed by the American actress Carolyn Sue Jones. Jones, whose career began in the early 1950s, later earned an Academy Award nomination for *The Bachelor Party* (1957) and a Golden Globe as a promising newcomer in 1959, before taking on the iconic part of Morticia (as well as her sister Ophelia and the feminine counterpart of Thing, Lady Fingers) in 1964.
title: Carolyn Jones

text: The White Princess miniseries is composed of eight episodes. It follows the marriage of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York, a union that brings an end to the Wars of the Roses by joining the houses of Lancaster and York, while also exploring the couple’s mutual mistrust and the political machinations of their mothers that threaten both their marriage and the kingdom.
title: The White Princess (miniseries)

text: In the Supercars Championship every competitor runs a front‑mounted, rear‑wheel‑drive car that is equipped with a 5.0‑litre, naturally aspirated V8‑engine. The power unit, which features electronic fuel injection, delivers between 460 kW and 485 kW (approximately 620–650 bhp) and is limited to 7 500 rpm with a 10 : 1 compression ratio. While teams may choose a manufacturer‑derived block or a generic V8 Supercars unit, both Ford and Holden field US‑based racing engines that use push‑rod actuated valves and two valves per cylinder. Consequently, the Holden V8 Supercar is powered by a V8-engine.
title: Supercars Championship

text: The International Space Station, a habitable artificial satellite orbiting low Earth, began its construction when its inaugural component was launched into space in 1998. Subsequent modules, trusses, solar arrays and other hardware have been added using Russian Proton and Soyuz rockets together with American Space Shuttles, making the ISS the largest human‑made structure in orbit and often visible to the naked eye from Earth.
title: International Space Station
