text: Unsaturated fats are defined as fats or fatty acids whose hydrocarbon chains include at least one double bond. When a fatty‑acid chain has a single double bond it is called monounsaturated; if it has several, it is termed polyunsaturated.
title: Unsaturated fat

text: The 2009 American romantic‑comedy Ghosts of Girlfriends Past, directed by Mark Waters from a script by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, was filmed between February 19, 2008 and July 2008 in Massachusetts, featuring a cast that includes Matthew McConaughey, Breckin Meyer, Jennifer Garner, Lacey Chabert and Michael Douglas.
title: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past

text: The production of *Ghosts of Girlfriends Past* was shot mainly on location at Castle Hill, which lies in Ipswich, Massachusetts. This New England setting served as the primary filming site for the movie.
title: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past

text: Following Alexander Hamilton’s model for the First Bank, the Second Bank of the United States received its charter in 1816 when President James Madison authorized it. The bank opened its principal office in Philadelphia on January 7, 1817, and by 1832 it operated a network of twenty‑five branches nationwide.
title: Second Bank of the United States

text: In 1546 the Council of Trent issued its definition of the deuterocanonical books, a term the Roman Catholic Church had adopted in the sixteenth century. That council’s decree set these texts apart from the Hebrew canon (the protocanonical books) and from the apocryphal writings, thereby establishing the official list of books that were not to be regarded as part of the canonical Old Testament.
title: Deuterocanonical books

text: According to the list of Super Bowl champions, the Pittsburgh Steelers hold the record for the most titles, having captured six championships.
title: List of Super Bowl champions

text: The Chinese Immigration Act, which had been preceded by the 1885 head‑tax legislation, was finally enacted in 1923 after sustained pressure from federal officials and provincial interests, particularly in British Columbia. The law came into force on July 1, 1923, and effectively barred most Chinese immigrants from entering Canada, allowing entry only under a few narrowly defined categories.
title: Chinese Immigration Act, 1923

text: In the phloem of flowering plants, the elongated cells called sieve tube elements (also referred to as sieve tube members) are highly specialized. These cells join with adjacent members along their lateral sides, creating the continuous sieve tube that moves carbohydrates—principally sucrose—from leaves to fruits, roots, and other tissues. Unlike the water‑conducting xylem vessel elements, which become dead at maturity, sieve tube elements remain living cells, although they lose their nucleus as they mature.
title: Sieve tube element

text: The 80th edition of the NCAA Division I men’s basketball tournament began on March 13, 2018, and wrapped up on April 2 with the championship game taking place at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas.
title: 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament

text: In 2018, the Final Four will be staged at the Alamodome in San Antonio, representing the venue’s fourth time hosting the championship event.
title: 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament

text: On August 15, 1971 the Titans assembled and traveled to Gettysburg College, where they held their football training camp. The camp at Gettysburg College became the setting for the team’s intensive practices and the pivotal moments that eventually forged their unity.
title: Remember the Titans

text: American actress and voice artist Lauren Tom (born August 4, 1961) lends her voice to the character Amy Wong on the animated television series Futurama, also portraying Amy’s mother Inez in the show.
title: Lauren Tom

text: At the San Diego Comic‑Con panel on July 22 2017, IDW Entertainment’s president David Ozer revealed that Wynonna Earp had been renewed for a third season, and that the new season’s premiere was slated for 2018. On the same day, Space confirmed it had commissioned 12 episodes for that third season, in partnership with Syfy. The show’s dedicated fan community, known as “Earpers,” was credited with helping secure the renewal.
title: Wynonna Earp (TV series)

text: Season 3 of Wynonna Earp began production on January 15, 2018, indicating that the next season started in 2018.
title: Wynonna Earp (TV series)

text: Isaiah Amir Mustafa (born February 11, 1974) is an American actor and former NFL practice‑squad wide receiver. He is best known for playing the coach in the Old Spice television commercials that form the “The Man Your Man Could Smell Like” campaign.
title: Isaiah Mustafa

text: The Nobel Prize in Literature was first presented in 1901, marking the start of its annual awarding to authors from any nation whose body of work is deemed the most outstanding in an ideal direction, as stipulated in Alfred Nobel’s will. The Swedish Academy selects the laureate each year and announces the choice in early October. This prize is one of the five Nobel categories established by Nobel’s 1895 testament.
title: Nobel Prize in Literature

text: Mandalay Bay, a 43‑story luxury resort and casino on the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise, Nevada, is owned and operated by **MGM Resorts International**. The Four Seasons Hotel occupies the top five floors of the Mandalay Bay tower (floors 35‑39) and is run independently, but the property it resides in belongs to MGM Resorts International.
title: Mandalay Bay

text: The seismic event in central Mexico was produced along the boundary where the Cocos Plate dives beneath the North American Plate along the Pacific coast, a setting that constitutes a subduction zone. This type of plate interaction is responsible for many of the large earthquakes that occur in the region.
title: 2017 Central Mexico earthquake

text: In the United States, a standard drink—exemplified by a 12‑US‑fluid‑ounce (350 ml) serving of beer—contains about 14 grams of alcohol.
title: Standard drink

text: The United States Department of Homeland Security was created on November 25, 2002, when the Homeland Security Act of 2002 merged a collection of federal agencies into a single Cabinet-level department focused on homeland security.
title: United States Department of Homeland Security

text: Green algae are eukaryotic organisms that reproduce through a cycle known as alternation of generations.
title: Green algae

text: Brent Robert Barry, born on December 31, 1971, is a retired American professional basketball player and the son of former NBA star Rick Barry. Standing 6 feet 7 inches tall, he spent his NBA career as a shooting guard, winning two league championships with the San Antonio Spurs. In addition to his team successes, Barry captured the NBA Slam Dunk Contest title in 1996.
title: Brent Barry

text: Jyotirindra Basu (8 July 1914 – 17 January 2010) was an Indian politician of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) from West Bengal. He occupied the post of Chief Minister of West Bengal from 1977 to 2000, and this 23‑year tenure still stands as the longest service by any chief minister in India as of January 2015.
title: Jyoti Basu

text: The highest total of runs ever recorded by a team in a single inning is **18**, a milestone achieved by the Chicago White Stockings (now known as the Cubs) against the Detroit Wolverines on September 6, 1883.
title: Run (baseball)

text: The concept of castles was brought to England by the Norman invaders, who erected them for military, administrative, and domestic functions. These fortifications acted not only as defensive strongpoints but also as offensive bases that could be used in enemy territory. After his 1066 conquest, William the Conqueror secured his new realm by ordering the construction of many castles—such as Warwick Castle—to protect key positions and suppress potential rebellions.
title: Castle

text: Both the First Battle of El Alamein, which stopped the Axis push into Egypt, and the later Second Battle of El Alamein (23 October – 11 November 1942) were fought near the Egyptian railway halt of El Alamein, meaning the two battles took place in Egypt.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: The First and Second Battles of El Alamein were fought on the Egyptian coast. By 12 July 1942 the German‑Italian Panzer Army Africa had driven deep into Egypt, endangering the British Empire’s hold on the Suez Canal and Mandatory Palestine. In response, General Claude Auchinleck pulled the Eighth Army back to a line about 80 km (50 mi) west of Alexandria, where the Qattara Depression lay only 64 km (40 mi) from El Alamein, giving the defenders a short front and secure flanks. The Axis advance was halted there in early July during the First Battle of El Alamein, and the later Second Battle of El Alamein took place at the same location in Egypt.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: In the historical record of Alzheimer’s disease, the very first case was not identified until 1901, when German psychiatrist Alois Alzheimer described the condition in a fifty‑year‑old woman he called Auguste D. He monitored her progress until she died in 1906 and subsequently reported his observations publicly.
title: Alzheimer's disease

text: The phrase is said to be Scots in origin. The earliest known written occurrence of it appears in the 1719 “Epistle to Ramsay,” a poem by the Scottish writer William Hamilton.
title: To the nines

text: The opening credits of *Deadpool* play the song “Angel of the Morning” as performed by Juice Newton. Her rendition also appears in other movies and TV shows, such as Drew Barrymore’s introductory scene in *Charlie’s Angels*, the soundtrack of *Charlie Wilson’s War* (where it is also sung by Emily Blunt), the closing of *The Meddler*, and an episode of HBO’s *True Detective* season one.
title: Angel of the Morning

text: Kenny Rogers recorded a duet of “Mary, Did You Know?” with Wynonna Judd for his holiday album The Gift, and that version climbed to No. 55 on the Billboard Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart in 1997.
title: Mary, Did You Know?

text: The English‑language version of the new series of *Keeping Faith* debuted on BBC Wales on 13 February 2018. This launch followed the show's simultaneous filming in both Welsh and English, with the English edition airing first on the BBC platform.
title: Keeping Faith (TV series)

text: Ray Donovan is an American crime‑drama series created by Ann Biderman for Showtime. Its twelve‑episode first season debuted on June 30, 2013, and the show was subsequently renewed for additional installments. The fourth season premiered on June 26, 2016, and the fifth season began airing on August 6, 2017. To date, the series has aired **5** seasons.
title: Ray Donovan

text: When the war erupted in 1914, the United States adopted a policy of **neutrality**. Washington proclaimed that it would remain impartial, insisting on the rights of neutral nations while trying to broker a peace settlement. This stance allowed American businesses and banks to continue trading with either side, although the British blockade limited transactions with Germany. The neutral position was backed by various domestic groups, including Irish‑Americans, German‑Americans, women’s organizations, churches, and many educated Americans. President Woodrow Wilson publicly denounced violations of neutral rights by both the British and the Germans, maintaining the United States’ commitment to stay out of the fighting until later developments forced a change in policy.
title: History of U.S. foreign policy

text: The CW’s supernatural drama The Vampire Diaries—developed by Kevin Williamson and Julie Plec from L. J. Smith’s book series—premiered on September 10, 2009, and ended on March 10, 2017, delivering a total of 171 episodes over eight seasons.
title: The Vampire Diaries

text: The show was ultimately concluded after a total of 8 seasons. After lead actress Nina Dobrev announced her departure following the sixth season, the series was renewed on March 11 2016 for an eighth season, and on July 23 2016 the network confirmed that this final, 16‑episode run would be the last. The eighth season premiered on October 21 2016, marking the end of the series.
title: The Vampire Diaries

text: Under the Marriage Act 1961, the minimum age at which a person may legally marry in Australia is 18. This uniform age was established when the Sex Discrimination Amendment Act 1991 removed the earlier distinction that set the marriageable age at 16 for females and 18 for males, raising the female threshold to match the male one.
title: Marriage Act 1961 (Australia)

text: Jonathan Harris (born Jonathan Daniel Charasuchin; November 6, 1914 – November 3, 2002) was an American character actor. Among his most recognizable performances were the timid accountant Bradford Webster in the television adaptation of *The Third Man* and the irascible Dr. Zachary Smith in the 1960s science‑fiction series *Lost in Space*, a role he portrayed as Jonathan Harris. Near the end of his career he supplied voice work for animated films such as *A Bug’s Life* and *Toy Story 2*.
title: Jonathan Harris

text: In the Wurtz reaction, two alkyl halides are combined with sodium metal while the mixture is kept in a dry ether solution. The anhydrous ether acts as the reaction medium, allowing the sodium to engage the halides and couple them together. This coupling proceeds **to form a higher alkane** as the final product.
title: Wurtz reaction

text: The 2008 American comedy‑drama about the dog Marley is titled **Marley & Me**. Directed by David Frankel, its screenplay—written by Scott Frank and Don Roos—is adapted from John Grogan’s memoir of the same name. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston portray the couple who adopt Marley. The film debuted in the United States and Canada on December 25, 2008, setting a record for the biggest Christmas‑Day box‑office opening with $14.75 million in ticket sales. A direct‑to‑video prequel, *Marley & Me: The Puppy Years*, was released in 2011.
title: Marley & Me (film)

text: The Mayflower’s ship’s master was Master Christopher Jones, whose cabin was set aft on the main deck and measured roughly ten by seven feet. Directly forward of his cabin lay the steerage room, which held the ship’s compass, officer berths and a whipstaff for steering. Ahead of the steerage room was the capstan, and further forward, near the bow, was the forecastle where the cook prepared meals for the crew.
title: Mayflower

text: After a stretch of mediocrity that saw the franchise reach the postseason only once in eleven years, the Jets hired Bill Parcells in 1997. Parcells guided the team to a 12‑4 record in 1998, the best season since the AFL‑NFL merger, and New York advanced to the AFC Championship Game before falling to Denver. Throughout the 2000s the Jets made the playoffs five times, the most of any decade for the team. The franchise returned to the conference championship in consecutive seasons, first in 2009 and again in 2010. In the 2010 postseason the Jets won a playoff game to move on to the AFC Championship, where they were ultimately defeated.
title: History of the New York Jets

text: In 1885, Joseph F. Steinwand created a new cheese at his father’s dairy near the village of Colby, Wisconsin. He named the product after that community, which had been established three years earlier. Although Colby cheese is now produced elsewhere, the original town’s name remains part of its identity. Each mid‑July a local festival celebrates the cheese, offering free samples at the food booths. The historic factory was demolished on August 12, 2015, leaving only its foundations.
title: Colby cheese

text: Spanish actress Oona Castilla Chaplin (born 4 June 1986), who works under the name Oona Chaplin, portrayed Talisa Maegyr in the HBO television series *Game of Thrones*.
title: Oona Chaplin

text: In California, the historic U.S. Route 66 began on the Pacific Ocean at a point in Santa Monica, then traveled eastward through Los Angeles and San Bernardino before reaching Needles at the Arizona state line. The highway was shortened during the 1964 renumbering and its signage was removed in 1974; today most of its former path is covered by city streets, State Route 66, Interstate 15, and Interstate 40.
title: U.S. Route 66 in California

text: U.S. Route 66 was first established on the California coast in Santa Monica. The historic alignment began at the southwest terminus of Santa Monica Boulevard, which at that time ran from the Santa Monica–Los Angeles city line eastward to US 101. After the 1964 renumbering this stretch became part of State Route 2, but the original route still began in Santa Monica before continuing southeast as Sunset Boulevard toward SR 110.
title: U.S. Route 66 in California

text: Lori Grimes meets her death in the Walking Dead episode "Killer Within". Critics noted the impact of her final moments; HitFix’s Alan Sepinwall described the farewell between Lori and her son Carl as the most heartbreaking scene since the season‑two finale “Pretty Much Dead Already”. Los Angeles Times columnist Laura Hudson called the departure grim for a character who had endured prolonged grief, while Forbes writer Erik Kain said Lori’s “gut‑churning” demise was especially difficult to watch, even as he praised the heroic death of T‑Dog in the same episode.
title: Lori Grimes

text: American actress Sara Gilbert (born Sara Rebecca Abeles on January 29, 1975) played the character Darlene Conner on the ABC sitcom *Roseanne* from 1988 to 1997, a role that earned her two Primetime Emmy Award nominations. She later reprised Darlene in the 2018 eight‑episode revival of the series.
title: Sara Gilbert

text: Airtel Payments Bank, the first institution to receive a full licence from the Reserve Bank of India for operating a payments bank, uses Bharti Airtel’s extensive distribution network—covering about 87 percent of the country, more than 400 000 villages and 5 000 census towns—to reach customers. When a new account is opened, the bank assigns the account identifier directly from the customer’s mobile subscription. In fact, **Your Airtel mobile number** serves as the account number for the Airtel Payments Bank account. This arrangement is part of the bank’s introductory benefits, which also include a 7.25 % interest rate, a one‑lakh‑rupee deposit limit, free personal accident insurance, and a virtual debit card for online purchases. Withdrawals can be made at any Airtel Banking Point, and transfers to other banks incur a small fee, while transfers to another Airtel Payments Bank account are fee‑free.
title: Airtel Payments Bank Limited

text: Norman Greenbaum wrote and first recorded “Spirit in the Sky,” which was issued in late 1969. The single went on to sell two million copies between 1969 and 1970, peaking at number three on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 on April 18 1970 and remaining on the chart for fifteen weeks. It was later ranked the 22nd‑most successful song of 1970 by Billboard and reached the top position in the United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada that same year. The track also appears on the 1969 album titled *Spirit in the Sky* and has been covered by artists such as Doctor and the Medics and Gareth Gates, both of whom achieved UK chart‑topping success with their versions.
title: Spirit in the Sky

text: The upcoming edition of the World Cup of Hockey is slated to begin in 2020, at which point the tournament will move away from all‑star teams and instead feature qualifying teams.
title: World Cup of Hockey

text: In the anime series Dragon Ball GT, Goku attains the Super Saiyan 4 transformation. Chief character designer Katsuyoshi Nakatsuru explained that designing this form was difficult because Super Saiyan 4 emerges while a Saiyan is in the Ōzaru (Great Ape) state, prompting him to give Goku wilder hair and cover his body in red fur; he ultimately chose black hair to provide contrast with the fur.
title: Goku

text: During the seventeenth U.S. season of Dancing with the Stars, contestant Corbin Bleu was partnered with professional dancer Karina Smirnoff, and the duo finished the competition as the runners‑up.
title: Dancing with the Stars (U.S. season 17)

text: On Monday, July 10, 2017, at approximately 4 p.m., a United States Marine Corps Lockheed KC‑130T Hercules aircraft from Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron 452 crashed, and debris from the crash was later recovered in Leflore County, Mississippi, resulting in the deaths of all sixteen people on board.
title: 2017 United States Marine Corps KC-130 crash

text: The XXIII Olympic Winter Games—often called PyeongChang 2018—are slated to occur between 9 and 25 February 2018, with the events taking place in Pyeongchang County, South Korea.
title: 2018 Winter Olympics

text: In nuclear physics, beta decay (β‑decay) is a radioactive decay mode in which an atomic nucleus emits a fast electron or positron together with a neutrino. When a proton undergoes positron emission, the process—beta decay—converts the proton into a neutron, thereby changing the nuclide’s identity. The emitted particles are not present in the nucleus beforehand; they are created during the decay, allowing an unstable atom to achieve a more stable proton‑to‑neutron ratio.
title: Beta decay

text: Brisket is a portion of beef that comes from the breast or lower chest of a cow. It is one of the nine primary beef primal cuts and consists of the superficial and deep pectoral muscles, which support about 60 % of a standing or moving animal’s weight because cattle lack collar bones. The large amount of connective tissue in this area means the meat must be cooked properly to become tender.
title: Brisket

text: Harper Lee’s novel *To Kill a Mockingbird* was released in 1960, and it gained instant popularity—securing the Pulitzer Prize that year and rapidly establishing itself as a classic of modern American literature.
title: To Kill a Mockingbird

text: The music that U.S. television networks play as the Olympic Games theme—used for both the Summer and Winter Games—is the composition “Bugler’s Dream,” which was written by the French‑American film‑score composer Leo Arnaud.
title: Leo Arnaud

text: The melody most frequently associated with the Olympic Games—heard during broadcasts of both Summer and Winter editions—is the piece called “Bugler’s Dream.” That iconic theme was originally composed by Leo Arnaud.
title: Leo Arnaud

text: In the chronology of the world’s tallest buildings, the Great Pyramid of Giza—originally 146.5 metres (481 ft) high—held the title of the tallest human‑made structure for **over 3,800 years**, a reign that ended only with the construction of Lincoln Cathedral in 1300.
title: History of the world's tallest buildings

text: In the Jessie episode “Punch Dumped Love,” the guest cast features Isabella Palmieri, who appears as the character Rachel Kapowski.
title: List of Jessie episodes

text: Initially, Linus Torvalds applied the name “Linux” only to his kernel, but the kernel was commonly paired with software from the GNU project, creating a widely used GNU system. By June 1994, GNU’s bulletin was calling Linux a “free UNIX clone,” and the Debian project began branding its distribution as Debian GNU/Linux. In May 1996, Richard Stallman released Emacs 19.31 and briefly renamed the combined system “Lignux” to highlight the GNU‑Linux partnership. He soon abandoned the Lignux spelling and favored the designation **GNU/Linux**.
title: History of Linux

text: First Nations (French: Premières Nations) are the primary Indigenous peoples of Canada and are located south of the Arctic, while the Indigenous groups that inhabit the Arctic region are identified as Inuit. The Métis, another distinct ethnicity, arose from historic relationships between First Nations peoples and Europeans. Currently, Canada recognizes 634 First Nations governments or bands, roughly half of which are situated in the provinces of Ontario and British Columbia.
title: First Nations

text: Robinson is an English language patronymic surname that originated in England, meaning “son of Robin” (Robin being a diminutive of Robert). Variant spellings such as Robison and Robeson also exist. It ranks as the 15th most common surname in the United Kingdom, and according to the 1990 United States Census it was the twentieth most frequently encountered surname, accounting for 0.23 % of the population.
title: Robinson (name)

text: Cory Allan Michael Monteith (May 11 1982 – July 13 2013) was a Canadian actor and musician best known for portraying Finn Hudson on the Fox series Glee; he passed away on July 13 2013.
title: Cory Monteith

text: Keith Thibodeaux, born on December 1, 1950, is an American former child actor and musician who is best known for portraying Little Ricky on the television sitcom *I Love Lucy* and its continuation, *The Lucy‑Desi Comedy Hour*. His Cajun‑French surname was altered to “Keith” by co‑star Desi Arnaz because it was considered difficult to pronounce. Thibodeaux remains the last surviving regular cast member from the series.
title: Richard Keith (actor)

text: In the television drama *The Path*, the central family—Eddie Lane, his wife Sarah, and their children Hawk and Summer—make their home in Upstate New York. Their everyday life unfolds against this regional backdrop while they navigate the complexities of the Meyerist Movement and the personal crises that arise within it.
title: The Path (TV series)

text: Schadenfreude, literally “harm‑joy,” is the German term that describes the feeling of pleasure, joy, or self‑satisfaction that arises when a person learns of or watches another individual’s trouble, failure, or humiliation.
title: Schadenfreude

text: The NBA’s record of single‑game scoring leaders indicates that the highest point total ever recorded in a game belongs to Wilt Chamberlain, who amassed 100 points in a contest during the 1962 season. This 100‑point performance remains the league’s all‑time single‑game scoring record.
title: List of National Basketball Association single-game scoring leaders

text: Since the ATP began publishing rankings in 1973, twenty‑six men have reached the No. 1 spot, with seventeen of them ending a season as the year‑end leader. The current world number one is Rafael Nadal.
title: List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players

text: The CW confirmed that the series was renewed for a fifth season, which is scheduled to debut on April 24, 2018.
title: List of The 100 episodes

text: Dylan Massett eventually learns the truth about his parentage: his biological father is Norma's brother, Caleb. Norma reveals to Dylan that he was conceived through an incestuous rape, confirming that Caleb—not the man he had assumed—was his true father. This revelation forces Dylan to distance himself from the Bates family for a time.
title: List of Bates Motel characters

text: In 1922, after the Irish War of Independence and the signing of the Anglo‑Irish Treaty, most of the island withdrew from the United Kingdom and was established as the independent Irish Free State. The new state later adopted the name Ireland under the 1937 constitution, while the six northeastern counties remained within the United Kingdom as Northern Ireland.
title: History of Ireland

text: The 1974 single “Tell Me Something Good” was recorded by Rufus and Chaka Khan. Written by Stevie Wonder, the track became a hit in the United States, climbing to number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and spending a week at the top of the Cash Box Top 100. It is also noted for featuring an early use of a guitar talk box by Tony Maiden.
title: Tell Me Something Good

text: Charles Pathé, the French film pioneer, launched the newsreel format in the early 1910s, with the inaugural newsreel series being produced in 1911. The new form quickly became a regular feature of cinema programmes across North America, Britain, the Commonwealth and Europe, remaining popular until television news supplanted it in the 1960s.
title: Newsreel

text: Erosion carved the Grand Canyon, revealing one of the most complete geologic columns on the planet.
title: Grand Canyon

text: When the Gulf of California opened around 5.3 million years ago, the Colorado River’s base level fell, causing a marked increase in erosion. This intensified erosion removed nearly all of the canyon’s present depth by about 1.2 million years ago, and the terraced walls of the Grand Canyon were formed through differential erosion.
title: Grand Canyon

text: Since its debut on March 26, 1973, the soap opera The Young and the Restless has been taped at CBS Television City, utilizing studios 41 and 43 in Hollywood.
title: The Young and the Restless

text: World War II is commonly dated to 1 September 1939, when Nazi Germany launched its invasion of Poland; this aggressive act led France and the United Kingdom to issue formal declarations of war against Germany, marking the start of the global conflict.
title: World War II

text: Michael Rooker (born April 6, 1955) is an American actor who is best known for his breakout performance as Henry in *Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer* and for portraying Yondu Udonta in the *Guardians of the Galaxy* film series.
title: Michael Rooker

text: The West Wing suffered a serious incident on December 24, 1929, when an electrical fire caused extensive damage to the structure. President Herbert Hoover subsequently oversaw its reconstruction and added air‑conditioning.
title: West Wing

text: According to tradition, the Chaplet of Divine Mercy may be prayed at any time, yet when it is observed as a novena it is customarily recited each of the nine consecutive days that start on Good Friday and conclude on Divine Mercy Sunday.
title: Chaplet of the Divine Mercy

text: The Divine Mercy chaplet may be prayed repeatedly over nine days as a novena, and St. Faustina’s diary records that this novena is to be begun on Good Friday as a preparation for the Feast of Divine Mercy, celebrated each year on the first Sunday after Easter.
title: Chaplet of the Divine Mercy

text: Carol Ann Susi (February 2, 1952 – November 11, 2014) was an American actress who supplied the voice for the off‑screen character Mrs. Wolowitz, Howard Wolowitz’s mother, on the television sitcom *The Big Bang Theory*.
title: Carol Ann Susi

text: The Beast is not a single animal but a chimera—a creature assembled from many different species. Its form blends the head and horns of a buffalo, the torso and arms of a bear, the eyebrows of a gorilla, the jaws, teeth and mane of a lion, the tusks of a wild boar, and the legs and tail of a wolf, which would generally place it in the carnivore category. It also bears resemblances to mythic monsters such as the Minotaur or a werewolf, while its only unchanging physical trait is a pair of blue eyes.
title: Beast (Beauty and the Beast)

text: A touchdown awards the scoring team six points. Following the touchdown, the team can try for an extra point or a two‑point conversion, and then, provided there is still time left in the game, it kicks off to the opposing side.
title: Touchdown

text: After the 1964 Instruction on implementing the Constitution on Sacred Liturgy of the Second Vatican Council stipulated that, in normal circumstances, the epistle and gospel of the Mass should be read in the vernacular, the Church moved toward using local languages for the rest of the celebration. Permissions were thus granted from 1967 onwards to celebrate most of the Tridentine Mass in vernacular languages, including the Canon.
title: Latin Mass

text: After centuries of Native American habitation, Spanish colonization beginning in 1598, and a period of Mexican rule, the region became a U.S. territory following the Mexican‑American War. New Mexico was admitted to the Union as the 47th state on January 6, 1912.
title: New Mexico

text: In late 1946, full‑scale hostilities broke out between the Việt Minh and France, initiating the First Indochina War and establishing France as the first imperial power to fight in Vietnam.
title: History of Vietnam

text: In a formal dinner, each guest’s setting includes a bread roll that is normally served on a bread plate, and this bread plate is positioned at each place.
title: Table setting

text: Varsity Blues, the American comedy‑drama directed by Brian Robbins, was released in 1999. The story follows a small‑town 5A high‑school football team and its demanding coach as they navigate a turbulent season in the football‑obsessed community of the fictional West Canaan, Texas.
title: Varsity Blues (film)

text: Johannes Gutenberg, who worked as a goldsmith, created the first printing press in Europe during the 1430s, around 1439, by modifying existing technologies and introducing his own inventions. His key breakthrough was a hand‑mould that could rapidly produce metal movable‑type matrices, enabling a fully functional movable‑type printing system. This combination of a hand‑mould and a press dramatically lowered the cost of producing books and other documents, especially for short print runs.
title: Printing press

text: When the Earth’s spin is measured relative to the Sun, it completes one full turn in about 24 hours. This solar‑day length differs from the sidereal day, which is roughly 23 hours 56 minutes 4 seconds, but the key point for the Sun‑based measurement is the “about 24 hours” period.
title: Earth's rotation

text: After its early years as the Arizona Open, the event was called the Phoenix Open for the bulk of its history. In October 2003 the investment bank **Friedman Billings Ramsey** took over as title sponsor, and the tournament was renamed the FBR Open for the next six editions. Waste Management did not assume sponsorship until 2010.
title: Phoenix Open

text: In 1983, an Australian syndicate sailing under the Royal Perth Yacht Club secured a historic triumph when its yacht Australia II, commanded by skipper John Bertrand, defeated the defending challenger Liberty and captured the America’s Cup, bringing an end to the New York Yacht Club’s 132‑year reign.
title: 1983 America's Cup

text: The Toronto Maple Leafs, the professional ice‑hockey club based in Toronto, Ontario, now host their home games at the Air Canada Centre, a venue they moved into in February 1999 after earlier stints at the Mutual Street Arena and Maple Leaf Gardens.
title: Toronto Maple Leafs

text: Blue Bloods' eighth season debuted on CBS on September 29, 2017, and is planned to run for 22 episodes.
title: Blue Bloods (season 8)

text: During World War II, the United States government eventually assumed an active role in generating propaganda designed to bolster the war effort. Although it had been reluctant at first, pressure from the press, commercial interests, and advertisers convinced the government to launch a coordinated campaign, which it framed as the provision of information rather than overt propaganda.
title: American propaganda during World War II

text: The designation Moloch arose in the Second Temple period as a disparaging vocalisation of a divine name whose basic Semitic root is mlk, meaning “king.” Several Canaanite deities whose names incorporate this root—such as the Ammonite god Malkam (called Milcom in the KJV) and the Phoenician Melqart—were subsequently lumped together under the label Moloch.
title: Moloch

text: The tune that later became famous as “Fly Me to the Moon,” originally released under the title “In Other Words,” was composed in 1954 by the songwriter Bart Howard.
title: Fly Me to the Moon

text: Taxonomy is the scientific discipline that defines and names groups of living organisms based on shared traits, arranging them into hierarchical ranks such as domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. The discipline’s early development is credited to the Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus, who created the Linnaean system of classification and introduced the binomial nomenclature still used for naming species today. His work laid the foundation for modern taxonomic practice.
title: Taxonomy (biology)

text: Among the seven tracks from the album 17 that entered the Billboard Hot 100, “Everybody Dies in Their Nightmares” debuted at number 54. Because the album 17 is a release by XXXTentacion, the song “Everybody Dies in Their Nightmares” is performed by XXXTentacion.
title: 17 (XXXTentacion album)

text: The inaugural Twenty‑20 game to take place at Lord's was staged on 15 July 2004, featuring Middlesex against Surrey. This match drew a crowd of 27,509 spectators, marking the highest attendance for a county cricket fixture at the ground—apart from a one‑day final—since 1953.
title: Twenty20

text: The 2018 Major League Baseball regular season opened on March 29, 2018, and continued until the end of September.
title: 2018 Major League Baseball season

text: Malonyl‑CoA serves a central function in fatty acid biosynthesis by providing the substrate for the chain elongation phase, a role it also shares in polyketide biosynthesis.
title: Malonyl-CoA

text: In the sequel, the FBI leverages Gracie’s newfound fame by appointing her as the bureau’s public spokesperson. At the same time, Agent Eric Matthews—still reeling from a recent breakup—gets relocated to Miami, which accounts for his absence from the story.
title: Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous

text: The reigning monarch is Queen Elizabeth II. Under the established order of succession, her heir apparent—the first person entitled to inherit the throne—is her eldest son, Charles, Prince of Wales. Directly after him comes his elder son, Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, then William’s son Prince George, followed by his sister Princess Charlotte, and thereafter Prince Henry of Wales, the younger son of the Prince of Wales. The sixth position is held by Prince Andrew, Duke of York, the Queen’s second‑eldest son. Any of the first six in line who marry without the sovereign’s consent would be excluded from succession.
title: Succession to the British throne

text: Rick and Morty is an American adult‑animated science‑fiction comedy created by Justin Roiland and Dan Harmon. The series is scheduled for broadcast on Cartoon Network’s late-night programming block, Adult Swim. It follows the chaotic exploits of the cynical scientist Rick Sanchez and his easily‑influenced grandson Morty Smith as they toggle between ordinary family life and interdimensional adventures. The show debuted on December 2, 2013, and its third season wrapped up on October 1, 2017. A fourth season was hinted at in a September 2017 interview with Harmon and later referenced in the post‑credits scene of the third‑season finale, though its status remained uncertain as of April 2018.
title: Rick and Morty

text: A USB flash drive is a compact, removable storage device that uses flash memory accessed through a built‑in USB connector. Depending on the specific memory chip employed, such a drive can tolerate up to 100,000 write/erase cycles, which determines how many times data can be rewritten before the device begins to wear out. This endurance, together with its small size and low weight, makes the flash drive a common choice for portable data storage.
title: USB flash drive

text: According to the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum, a player may be inducted only through the vote of one of two groups. The first group is the Baseball Writers' Association of America, whose eligible members can select up to ten candidates from a ballot that usually lists between twenty‑five and forty names. The other group that can elect players is the Veterans Committee, which today operates as four separate subcommittees, each responsible for reviewing and voting on candidates from a particular era of baseball history.
title: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum

text: The word **acronym** is used for an abbreviation that is formed from the initial letters of a series of words. Some reference works draw a distinction, defining an acronym as an abbreviation that is spoken as a single word (for example, NATO, scuba, radar), while an initialism is an abbreviation pronounced letter by letter (such as FBI, CRT, HTML). Nevertheless, many dictionaries and style guides apply the term acronym to both kinds of initial‑letter abbreviations. Consequently, a set of initials that stand for a longer expression is called an acronym.
title: Acronym

text: In his writings, Bacon urged scholars to turn their investigations back toward nature, replacing the search for formal causes with a focus on the regular laws that govern physical phenomena. By emphasizing the efficient cause—what modern science calls the laws of nature—Bacon laid the groundwork for a scientific method that looks for consistent patterns in the natural world.
title: Nature (philosophy)

text: The State of the Union has evolved from a dialogue solely between the president and Congress into a nationwide address aimed at all Americans. With the rise of radio and later television, the speech is now broadcast live across major networks, often displacing regular programming. To capture the biggest possible viewership, the address, which was once delivered during daylight hours, is presently scheduled for the evening, after 9pm ET.
title: State of the Union

text: The designation “the West” stems from the geopolitical split first created during the Roman Empire, which divided Europe into an eastern, Greek‑speaking, urbanized zone and a western, Latin‑speaking, more rural region. This early Roman division laid the foundation for the later concept of “the West.”
title: Western world

text: Andrew Johnson became the first U.S. president ever impeached, the inaugural impeachment of a chief executive since the office was created in 1789. His removal attempt was the climax of a protracted political clash between Johnson—a lifelong Democrat—and the Republican‑controlled Congress over the proper handling of the defeated Southern states after the Civil War. The impeachment and the subsequent trial, which ended in acquittal, stand out as some of the most dramatic episodes of the Reconstruction Era, often viewed as driven by political expediency rather than necessity.
title: Impeachment of Andrew Johnson

text: Spanish moss (Tillandsia usneoides) is an epiphytic flowering plant that drapes from the branches of larger trees in tropical and subtropical regions. In the United States it is especially common in the low‑lying swamps, savannas, and bayous of the southeastern states, where it is frequently seen hanging from southern live oak (Quercus virginiana) and bald‑cypress (Taxodium distichum). This hanging growth habit gives the characteristic “beard‑like” appearance that is typical of Spanish moss.
title: Spanish moss

text: The Lord of the Rings film series comprises three high‑fantasy adventure movies directed by Peter Jackson. Adapted from J. R. R. Tolkien’s novel, the trilogy includes The Fellowship of the Ring (2001), The Two Towers (2002) and The Return of the King (2003). Produced as a New Zealand‑American collaboration by WingNut Films and The Saul Zaentz Company, the films were released through New Line Cinema.
title: The Lord of the Rings (film series)

text: Thaddeus Rowe Luckinbill (born April 24, 1975) is an American actor and producer who is best known for portraying J.T. Hellstrom on the CBS soap opera The Young and the Restless, a role he first took on in August 1999 and played until November 2010, before reviving the character again in December 2017.
title: Thad Luckinbill

text: The Ice Age franchise launched with its first feature, the film titled *Ice Age*, which debuted in 2002. Produced by Blue Sky Studios for 20th Century Fox, the series later expanded with four sequels released in 2006, 2009, 2012 and 2016.
title: Ice Age (franchise)

text: The GNU project, launched in 1984 to build a fully free operating system, is widely acknowledged as the work of its founder Richard Stallman. Stallman also established the Free Software Foundation, which promotes the combined designation GNU/Linux for systems that pair GNU’s software with the Linux kernel. Supporters of the GNU/Linux name argue that the original GNU effort must be explicitly credited, naming Richard Stallman as the principal contributor to the initiative.
title: GNU/Linux naming controversy

text: The GNU initiative is credited to **Richard Stallman**. In 1983, the founder of the Free Software Foundation laid out a plan for a fully free, Unix‑like operating system called GNU. He publicly detailed the project in a September manifesto published in *Dr. Dobb’s Journal*, and development work began the following January. By 1991 the mid‑level components of GNU were almost complete, while the lower‑level kernel—named GNU Hurd—remained largely unfinished.
title: GNU/Linux naming controversy

text: Collective Soul is an American rock band that began in Stockbridge, Georgia and later relocated to Atlanta. The group’s frontman is Ed Roland, who serves as the lead vocalist. Other members include rhythm guitarist Dean Roland, bassist Will Turpin, drummer Johnny Rabb, and lead guitarist Jesse Triplett.
title: Collective Soul

text: Dwyane Tyrone Wade Jr., born January 17 1982, is an American professional basketball player who currently suits up for the Miami Heat of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
title: Dwyane Wade

text: Johnny Manziel enrolled at Texas A&M and took the field for the Texas A&M Aggies as a redshirt freshman during the 2012 season.
title: Johnny Manziel

text: Johnny Manziel earned an athletic scholarship and enrolled at Texas A&M, where he played for the Aggies. He began his college career in 2011 under head coach Mike Sherman and then continued on the field for new head coach Kevin Sumlin during the 2012 and 2013 seasons.
title: Johnny Manziel

text: European folklore portrays the white stork as a messenger of new life, holding the role of bringing babies to new parents. The ancient legend, later popularized by Hans Christian Andersen’s 19th‑century tale “The Storks,” describes storks finding infants in caves or marshes and delivering them to households, either in a basket on their backs or clasped in their beaks. Families would signal their desire for children by leaving sweets on the windowsill for the stork, and the tradition has spread far beyond Europe to places such as the Philippines and parts of South America.
title: White stork

text: In bridge, a player may announce the holding of honors any time after the auction. While many players prefer to wait until the play is finished so as not to give the opponents clues about the distribution of cards, the rules permit the declaration at any point once bidding has ended. Honors can belong to any of the four hands, including dummy.
title: Bridge scoring

text: The doctrine of checks and balances holds that each branch of government can limit the others, preserving a balance among the three separate powers and protecting citizens from abuse. This system relies not only on separating powers but also on giving each branch constitutional tools to defend its own authority against encroachment. The idea that the powers of the state should be co‑equal and mutually restraining was first articulated during the Enlightenment, and the origin of checks and balances, like the separation of powers itself, is specifically credited to Montesquieu in the Enlightenment. Influenced by this theory, the United States incorporated the principle into its 1787 Constitution.
title: Separation of powers

text: According to the discussion of religious freedom in Nepal, the nation became a secular state when its Interim Constitution was formally promulgated on January 15, 2007. This constitution guarantees the right to practice any religion while expressly prohibiting attempts to convert others. Before that date, the 1990 constitution—effective until January 15, 2007—described Nepal as a “Hindu Kingdom,” though it did not establish Hinduism as a state religion.
title: Freedom of religion in Nepal

text: In the spring of 1609, John Smith addressed the Jamestown settlers with the maxim “He who does not work, neither shall he eat,” thereby instituting a rule that required every colonist to perform labor.
title: He who does not work, neither shall he eat

text: Montana lies in the northern portion of the Western United States. It is bounded on the east by North Dakota and South Dakota, on the south by Wyoming, and on the north by the Canadian provinces of British Columbia, Alberta, and Saskatchewan. The state that lies along Montana’s western and southwestern edge is Idaho.
title: Montana

text: In traditional Western notation a key signature at the start of a score indicates the scale that underlies the composition. As the work unfolds, the set of pitches may shift, introducing a different scale. When this shift is noticed, musicians describe the piece as having been **transposed** from its original key to a new one. This process raises or lowers the overall pitch range while keeping the interval relationships intact, allowing the music to accommodate different vocal or instrumental ranges.
title: Music theory

text: The Warriors novel series notes that its fifth volume, *River of Fire*, is slated to hit shelves on April 10, 2018.
title: Warriors (novel series)

text: The Sugarhill Gang’s hip‑hop single “Rapper’s Delight,” produced by Sylvia Robinson, was released in 1979. Although it was not the first record to feature rapped verses, the track is widely credited with bringing hip hop to a broad audience and establishing a template for later rap songs. Its composition incorporated samples from Chic’s “Good Times,” leading to a copyright settlement that added Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards as credited songwriters.
title: Rapper's Delight

text: Tiffany Adams Coyne, born on May 6, 1982, is an American model and dancer. She became the model on the game show *Let’s Make a Deal* after succeeding Alison Fiori in 2009.
title: Tiffany Coyne

text: The movie *It’s a Wonderful Life* did not achieve its classic status until many years after its original release; it turned into a regular television feature during the Christmas season in the late 1970s, becoming a beloved holiday staple. This unexpected resurgence delighted director Frank Capra and the film’s other creators, who later reflected on its newfound popularity.
title: It's a Wonderful Life

text: Cain and Abel, often shortened to Cain, is a password recovery tool for Microsoft Windows. It can retrieve many types of passwords by employing techniques such as network packet sniffing, dictionary attacks, brute‑force methods, and cryptanalysis using rainbow tables generated with the supplied winrtgen.exe utility. The software is maintained by Massimiliano Montoro and Sean Babcock.
title: Cain and Abel (software)

text: Claudia Grace Wells, an American actress born on July 5, 1966, is the performer who played Jennifer Parker in the 1985 film *Back to the Future*.
title: Claudia Wells

text: The 2012 Summer Olympics—officially the Games of the XXX Olympiad and popularly known as London 2012—were staged in London, United Kingdom, running from 27 July to 12 August 2012. The competition opened with the women's football group stage on 25 July at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, followed by the opening ceremonies two days later. A total of 10,768 athletes representing 204 National Olympic Committees took part.
title: 2012 Summer Olympics

text: Filming for the 2017 movie *Coming Home for Christmas* was carried out in British Columbia, using sites in Abbotsford, Vancouver and Langley during August 2017. The primary residence featured in the story was a mansion situated in the Aldergrove area of Langley.
title: Coming Home for Christmas (2017 film)

text: In the television series *Full House*, the Tanner family’s middle daughter, Stephanie Tanner—the child who sits between her older sister D.J. and younger sister Michelle—is portrayed by Jodie Sweetin.
title: List of Full House and Fuller House characters

text: The development at 301 Mission Street in San Francisco’s South of Market district includes a 58‑story condominium skyscraper known as Millennium Tower. Rising 645 feet (197 m), it is the city’s tallest residential building and contains the majority of the project’s 419 units. In May 2016 residents were notified that the main tower was both sinking and tilting, prompting a series of lawsuits over repair costs and disclosure of the tilt.
title: Millennium Tower (San Francisco)

text: The inaugural season of the Canadian‑American drama *When Calls the Heart* premiered on the Hallmark Channel in the United States on January 11, 2014.
title: When Calls the Heart

text: In the Supreme Court case Cohen v. California, Justice Harlan observed that “one man’s vulgarity is another’s lyric,” stressing that, without a more specific and compelling justification, the State could not, consistent with the First and Fourteenth Amendments, criminalize the simple public display of a single four‑letter expletive.
title: Cohen v. California

text: Tyrann Devine Mathieu (born May 13, 1992) is an American football safety who plays for the Houston Texans in the National Football League. During his collegiate career at Louisiana State University, he became known for generating turnovers, establishing an SEC record with eleven forced fumbles, and was popularly dubbed the “Honey Badger.”
title: Tyrann Mathieu

text: Following AMC’s cancellation of the series, Netflix commissioned a fourth and final season that comprised six episodes; this season was made available on Netflix on August 1, 2014.
title: List of The Killing episodes

text: Since its launch by the United States Committee for UNICEF (now the U.S. Fund for UNICEF) in 1953, the Trick‑or‑Treat for UNICEF campaign has expanded from orange collection boxes handed to millions of children in the 1960s to a nationwide fundraising effort that now includes text‑message donations and online fundraising pages. Over the decades, U.S. children and adults have raised more than US $175 million. Throughout its history, the money collected has been directed to UNICEF's global programing, although in 2005 half of the proceeds were temporarily earmarked for a domestic cause—assisting victims of Hurricane Katrina.
title: Trick-or-Treat for UNICEF

text: In an autocracy, supreme social and political authority is vested in a single individual, and that one person alone makes the key governmental decisions, free from external legal restraints or regular mechanisms of popular control.
title: Autocracy

text: When observed from a position directly above the north pole—whether that pole belongs to the Sun or to Earth—the planet’s path around the Sun is seen to move in a counterclockwise direction.
title: Earth's orbit

text: Gabbar Is Back, the 2015 Indian vigilante film directed by Krish, is a Hindi remake of the 2002 Tamil movie Ramanaa. The Tamil original was later adapted for Telugu audiences as the 2003 film Tagore, and Gabbar Is Back follows that Telugu version.
title: Gabbar Is Back

text: Apollo 11 was the mission that first placed people on the Moon. The spacecraft’s commander, Neil Armstrong, and lunar‑module pilot Buzz Aldrin touched down the Eagle on the lunar surface on 20 July 1969 at 20:18 UTC. Six hours after landing, at 02:56:15 UTC on 21 July 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first human to step onto the Moon, and about 20 minutes later Buzz Aldrin followed. The two astronauts spent roughly two and a quarter hours outside the module, gathering 47.5 lb (21.5 kg) of lunar material before returning to the command module Columbia, which Michael Collins had been piloting alone in lunar orbit.
title: Apollo 11

text: The 2005 movie *Capote*, which dramatizes Truman Capote’s experience writing *In Cold Blood*, casts Philip Seymour Hoffman in the lead role of the author. His performance earned him the Academy Award for Best Actor.
title: In Cold Blood

text: In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Nebula is portrayed by Karen Gillan. She debuted in this role with the 2014 movie *Guardians of the Galaxy* and returned for its 2017 sequel *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2*. Gillian is also scheduled to reprise the character in the 2018 film *Avengers: Infinity War* and the untitled Avengers installment planned for 2019.
title: Nebula (comics)

text: The formal writing system employed in ancient Egypt was Egyptian hieroglyphs. This script blended logographic, syllabic, and alphabetic elements and consisted of about a thousand distinct characters. Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious texts on papyrus and wood, and later the hieratic and demotic scripts developed from this original form; the Meroitic script eventually derived from demotic.
title: Egyptian hieroglyphs

Although that ruling was limited to males under the age of 21, Justice Langa observed in his dicta that there was a prevailing view that corporal punishment of adults was also unconstitutional.

text: In every Indian district the top criminal tribunal is the District and Sessions Court. The bench of this court is headed by a **District Judge**, who is appointed by the state Governor on the advice of the state’s chief justice. Although additional and assistant district judges may assist, the District Judge alone presides over the highest criminal court in the district.
title: District Courts of India

text: Historical records show that the last sustainable gray wolf pack was eliminated from Yellowstone National Park by 1926, after which the National Park Service continued its predator‑control policies until 1933.
title: History of wolves in Yellowstone

text: In U.S. federal courts, a case may be heard under diversity jurisdiction only if the dispute involves more than $75,000. Under 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a), Congress has set this dollar threshold as the minimum amount in controversy required for the court to have jurisdiction.
title: Amount in controversy

text: Bacteroides fragilis is an obligately anaerobic, Gram‑negative, rod‑shaped bacterium that normally inhabits the human colon as a component of the resident microbiota, although it may cause infection if it moves into the bloodstream or surrounding tissues after surgery, disease, or trauma.
title: Bacteroides fragilis

text: The lyric “I wanna rock’n’roll all night” comes from the song “Rock and Roll All Nite,” which was recorded by the American rock band Kiss. The track debuted on Kiss’s 1975 album *Dressed to Kill* and was later released as the A‑side of their fifth single, backed with “Getaway.” A live version issued in October 1975 climbed to No. 12 on the Billboard chart in early 1976, becoming the first of six Top 20 hits the group scored in the 1970s. Since 1976 the song has served as Kiss’s signature anthem and closing number at virtually every concert.
title: Rock and Roll All Nite

text: The name **Hellenism** identifies the modern Hellenic ethnic religion, which is also widely called **Hellenic Polytheism** (as well as Hellenismos, Dodekatheism, or Olympianism). It denotes a collection of religious movements that seek to revive or reconstruct the worship practices of ancient Greece, and these movements have been publicly emerging since the 1990s.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: The modern revival of worship of the Greek gods is most commonly identified by its followers as **Hellenism**.  This name, first employed by the Roman emperor Julian when he organized a systematic revival of Greek religion, now serves as the principal label for the contemporary polytheistic faith, though it can also refer to the ancient Greek religion and culture.  The expressions “Hellenic religion” and **Hellenic Polytheism** are used interchangeably with Hellenism, while smaller groups sometimes adopt alternative titles such as Dodekatheism or Olympianism.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is the name given to the religion that centers on belief in the Greek gods, and it is also described as Hellenic polytheism. In the United States, the Hellenic polytheist organization Hellenion identifies its practices as “Hellenic Pagan Reconstructionism” and explicitly uses the Greek term “Hellenismos” (Ἑλληνισμός, Hellēnismós) to refer to this faith. The group’s mission statement stresses historical accuracy, and it provides clergy training, adult religious‑education classes, and other courses for its members. By 2007 an unofficial estimate placed Hellenion’s membership at about 43 people, and in early 2010 the organization reported one fully chartered local congregation (a demos) and six emerging congregations (proto‑demoi) that hold rituals and public events.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: The contemporary religious tradition that venerates the ancient Greek deities—ranging from the Olympian gods to nature spirits, chthonic figures and heroic ancestors—is called **Hellenism**. Its adherents, often described as Hellenic polytheists, honor both divine and ancestral beings and practice a devotional system in which gifts and offerings are exchanged for the blessings of the gods. Their moral outlook is frequently shaped by classical Greek virtues such as reciprocity, hospitality, self‑control and moderation, drawing ethical guidance from sources like the Delphic maxims, the Tenets of Solon, the Golden Verses of Pythagoras, or Aristotle’s Ethics. Central to this worldview are the concepts of *kharis* (grace), which establishes reciprocal relationships among humans and the divine, and *eusebeia* (piety), reflecting a committed worship of the Hellenic gods.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: In the story *Gotham by Gaslight*, Batman confronts the serial killer known as the Ripper just as the murderer is about to seize his next victim. After a frantic pursuit through the streets of Gotham, the chase ends at the tomb of Thomas and Martha Wayne. There, the true identity of the Ripper is disclosed: **Jacob Packer** is the killer. Packer had previously studied medicine and law, financing his education with money taken from Thomas Wayne. However, after Martha Wayne rejected his romantic advances, he descended into madness. Driven by a delusional need to silence the imagined laughter of Martha in his mind, he began murdering women who resembled her.
title: Gotham by Gaslight

title: Stadion (running race)

Its enclosure contains a collection of palaces, cathedrals and towers, among which stands the Grand Kremlin Palace. The Grand Kremlin Palace was formerly the tsar's Moscow residence.
title: Moscow Kremlin

text: When an angle θ is measured, a circular arc is drawn with its center at the vertex of the angle. The magnitude of the angle is found by taking the ratio of the arc’s length s to the circle’s radius r, and this quotient gives the measure of the angle in radians.
title: Angle

text: John Hart, the American film and television actor born on December 13, 1917, is most remembered for taking over the title role in the television series *The Lone Ranger* after Clayton Moore’s departure; he played the Lone Ranger for a single season, serving from 1952 until 1953.

title: 2014 Winter Olympics medal table

text: Beijing, the capital of the People’s Republic of China, is situated in northern China. It is administered as a direct‑controlled municipality that includes 16 urban, suburban and rural districts, and it is surrounded by Hebei Province, with Tianjin Municipality lying to its southeast.
title: Beijing

text: Beijing is located in northern China, occupying the northernmost edge of the roughly triangular North China Plain. The city is bordered by mountains to the north, northwest and west, which separate the region’s agricultural heartland from the desert steppes beyond. In the municipality’s northwest, the Jundu Mountains dominate areas such as Yanqing County and Huairou District, while the western side is framed by the Xishan or Western Hills. The Great Wall runs across the northern sector of Beijing, following the rugged terrain that once protected the area from nomadic incursions. The highest point in the municipality is Mount Dongling in the Western Hills, rising to 2,303 metres (7,556 ft) on the border with Hebei.
title: Beijing

text: In basketball, a player who catches a pass while still facing the defender and has not yet begun to dribble is said to be in the **Triple threat** position. In this stance the player’s feet are set slightly wider than shoulder‑width, the knees are flexed, and one foot acts as a pivot while the other is placed a little ahead. From the Triple threat the offensive player can choose among three actions: take a jump shot, drive forward by dribbling, or deliver a pass to a teammate; the player may also use jab steps or pump fakes to disrupt the defender’s stance.
title: Basketball moves

text: Kerris Lilla Dorsey (born January 9, 1998) is an American actress and singer. In the 2011 baseball drama *Moneyball*, she appears as Casey Beane, the daughter of Billy Beane—the character portrayed by Brad Pitt.
title: Kerris Dorsey

text: The disorder later known as Huntington's disease received its eponym from the physician George Huntington, who gave a detailed description of the condition in 1872. An earlier, likely first description of the disease had been made in 1841 by Charles Oscar Waters. The genetic basis of the disorder was uncovered in 1993 by an international collaborative effort led by the Hereditary Disease Foundation. Beginning in the late 1960s, research and support organizations were formed to raise public awareness, assist affected individuals and families, and promote further study of the disease. Current research aims to clarify the disease mechanism, improve animal models, test medications that may alleviate symptoms or slow progression, and explore stem‑cell therapies to repair damage caused by the condition.
title: Huntington's disease

text: Bull shark dentition is characterized by needle-like teeth. text: The Gulf of Mexico, a basin that originated roughly 300 million years ago through plate‑tectonic processes, covers about 1.6 million km² (≈615,000 sq mi) and is bounded by the Florida Straits, the Yucatán Channel and the surrounding continental shelf. Its water volume is immense: the basin holds approximately 2,500 quadrillion liters of water, which is equivalent to **660 quadrillion US gallons** (about 550 quadrillion Imperial gallons, 2.5 million km³, or 600,000 cubic miles).
title: Gulf of Mexico

text: Vasoepididymostomy is a urologic procedure that creates an anastomosis between a single epididymal tubule (luminal diameter 0.15–0.25 mm) and the lumen of the vas deferens (diameter 0.3–0.4 mm). It is performed for patients who have congenital or acquired obstruction of the epididymis, or for those in whom previous attempts to reconstruct the vas deferens have failed. By directly attaching the vas deferens to the epididymis—the coiled tube on the posterior aspect of each testicle where sperm mature—the surgery bypasses blockages that may result from a vasectomy or other injury, providing an alternative when a vasovasostomy would be ineffective.
title: Vasoepididymostomy

title: Cozonac

text: The bald eagle is classified in the genus **Haliaeetus**, the group commonly known as sea eagles.
title: Bald eagle

text: An ICD‑10‑CM code is made up of seven characters. Positions 1‑3 designate the disease category, position 4 indicates the etiology, position 5 specifies the body part affected, position 6 reflects the severity of the illness, and position 7 serves as a placeholder for extensions that add further specificity.
title: ICD-10

text: The pia mater, whose Latin name means “tender mother,” is an extremely delicate membrane that serves as the innermost meningeal covering. This very thin fibrous sheet adheres tightly to the surface of the brain and spinal cord, following every contour of the gyri and sulci. Its outer surface is lined with a sheet of flat cells that are thought to be impermeable to fluid, and the membrane is pierced by blood vessels whose capillaries nourish the brain.
title: Meninges

text: Bohrium, symbol Bh, is the synthetic chemical element that carries atomic number 107. It was named in honor of the Danish physicist Niels Bohr. Because it does not occur naturally, it must be produced in a laboratory. The most stable confirmed isotope, ^270Bh, decays with a half‑life of roughly 61 seconds, while an unverified isotope, ^278Bh, may persist for about 690 seconds.
title: Bohrium

text: The element that carries atomic number 107 was officially assigned the IUPAC name **Bohrium**. In 1994 an IUPAC committee advised that the new element be called bohrium rather than nielsbohrium, arguing that using a scientist’s full name had no precedent. Although the discoverers raised concerns about possible confusion with boron, the Danish branch of IUPAC voted in favor of the recommendation, and the name Bohrium was internationally recognized in 1997.
title: Bohrium

text: The cash flow statement divides cash movements into operating, investing, and financing categories. text: The line of longitude situated 180 degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian is called the 180th meridian or antimeridian. This meridian, together with the Prime Meridian, creates a great‑circle division that separates the Earth into Western and Eastern Hemispheres. It serves as the reference for the International Date Line because most of its length runs through the open waters of the Pacific Ocean, although the line also cuts across parts of Russia, Fiji and Antarctica.
title: 180th meridian

text: Displacement is the vector that specifies both the straight‑line length separating two positions and the direction of that line. In contrast, distance is only a scalar magnitude and never decreases, while displacement includes a direction as well as a magnitude.
title: Distance

text: Displacement is the straight‑line length together with a direction that connects an initial position to a final position. It is distinct from the total distance traveled along a possibly curved path, such as the mileage recorded by an odometer. For example, if a vehicle moves from point A to point B and then returns to point A, the distance covered is non‑zero, but the displacement is zero because the starting and ending points coincide. In general, only motion that proceeds in a straight line has a displacement equal to the distance traveled.
title: Distance

title: Elizabeth Lail

text: In the television series *Game of Thrones*, the member of House Lannister who is a dwarf is Tyrion Lannister. He is the younger brother of Cersei and Jaime, the son of Tywin Lannister, and is frequently referred to by nicknames such as “The Imp” or “Halfman.” Despite his lack of physical strength, Tyrion’s sharp intellect and strategic mind allow him to navigate the political intrigues of Westeros throughout the show.
title: List of Game of Thrones characters

text: James "Jamie" Dornan, an Irish actor born on 1 May 1982, has appeared in films and television series such as Sofia Coppola’s *Marie Antoinette* and the ABC drama *Once Upon a Time*. In the Fifty Shades franchise, which launched in 2015, he portrays the character Christian Grey.
title: Jamie Dornan

text: Liam Cunningham, an Irish stage and screen actor born on 2 June 1961, is the performer who portrays Ser Davos Seaworth in HBO’s epic‑fantasy series *Game of Thrones*.
title: Liam Cunningham

text: The 2011 American dystopian science‑fiction action thriller **In Time** was written, directed and produced by Andrew Niccol. It follows a world in which people cease aging at twenty‑five and must spend the time displayed on a clock implanted in their arm as a form of currency. The film stars Justin Timberlake alongside Amanda Seyfried and Cillian Murphy, and it opened in theaters on October 28, 2011.
title: In Time

text: The notion of the unicorn did not stem from Greek mythology but from the works of Greek writers of natural history, who regarded the animal as real and said it inhabited the far‑off lands of India. The earliest surviving description is found in Ctesias’s *Indika*, where he portrays the beast as a swift wild ass with a horn about a cubit and a half long (roughly 700 mm) and a coat of white, red and black. Later authors such as Aristotle, Strabo and Pliny the Elder echo and elaborate on these reports, mentioning one‑horned creatures like the oryx, the “Indian ass,” and a monstrous monoceros with a single black horn two cubits in length. Aelian, in *On the Nature of Animals*, also quotes Ctesias and records that the Indian one‑horned horse was sometimes called “cartazonos,” a term linked to the Arabic word for rhinoceros.
title: Unicorn

text: The turning point arrived in the fall of 1862 with the Battle of Antietam. Lee’s offensive was repelled, and his army barely managed to retreat to Virginia, making it clear that a decisive Confederate triumph could not be expected. The waning of the Confederate tide was apparent in Britain, and as a result Prime Minister Palmerston and Foreign Secretary Russell abandoned any intention of presenting a mediation‑recognition scheme to the cabinet.
title: United Kingdom and the American Civil War

text: British officials had debated recognizing the Confederacy and even planned to mediate the conflict after the Second Battle of Manassas. Yet the Union’s triumph at the Battle of Antietam, combined with Lincoln’s Emancipation Proclamation and growing domestic opposition, caused the British government to withdraw its support for the South.
title: United Kingdom and the American Civil War

text: In the United States Electoral College, every state receives a number of electors equal to the sum of its senators and its representatives. When the three electors allotted to the District of Columbia by the Twenty‑third Amendment are included, the whole system comprises a total of 538 electors. This figure reflects the 435 members of the House of Representatives, the 100 senators, and the additional three electors for the capital.
title: Electoral College (United States)

text: Robert Gillespie Adamson IV (born July 11, 1985) is an American actor who has appeared as Phil Sanders on the series *Hollywood Heights* and as Charles Antoni on *Lincoln Heights*. He is presently cast in the role of Noah Newman on the daytime drama *The Young and the Restless*.
title: Robert Adamson (actor)

text: The Botswana pula entered circulation in 1976, when it was launched to replace the South African rand at par.
title: Botswana pula

text: Catherine Tramell, a fictional character created by writer Joe Eszterhas and portrayed by Sharon Stone, is the main antagonist in both the 1992 film *Basic Instinct* and its 2006 sequel *Basic Instinct 2*. In the sequel, she is the individual responsible for the murders, making her the real killer.
title: Catherine Tramell

text: The custom that later became known as the Easter Bunny began with German Lutherans, who told stories of an “Easter Hare” that acted as a judge of children’s conduct at the opening of Eastertide. In these early German tales the hare was depicted as a rabbit that delivered colored eggs, candy, and sometimes toys to the homes of well‑behaved youngsters, a role that later evolved into the familiar Easter Bunny figure.
title: Easter Bunny

text: Shirley Mae Jones (born March 31, 1934) is an American actress and singer. In the early 1970s she took on the lead role of Shirley Partridge—the widowed mother of five children—in the musical sitcom The Partridge Family, which ran from 1970 to 1974.
title: Shirley Jones

text: The animated educational short titled **Ek Anek Aur Ekta** was directed by **Vijaya Mulay**. Its visual design, animation and overall creation were handled by Bhimsain Khurana, while the song “Hind Desh ke Niwasi” featured lyrics by Pandit Vinay Chandra Maudgalya and the vocal performance of “Ek Chidiya, Anek Chidiyan” was given by Sadhna Sargam. The production team also included assistants S. M. Hasan, Mahesh Taavre and Girish Rao. The film earned the National Film Award for Best Educational Film and was the first release from the animation studios of the then Center for Education Technology, later receiving the Best Children’s Film award in Japan and becoming a celebrated example of Indian animation storytelling.
title: Ek Anek Aur Ekta

text: Under U.S. law, airsoft guns are not treated as firearms, so they are legally available to people of any age. However, retailers are prohibited from selling them over the counter to anyone younger than 18. State regulations follow the same pattern; for instance, California law permits the purchase of an airsoft gun only by a person who is **18** years old or older. While minors may still use these devices with parental permission, the age restriction applies specifically to the act of buying them.
title: Legal issues in airsoft

text: Most historians agree that jelly beans first became linked to Easter celebrations in the United States during the 1930s, a connection made because their shape resembles eggs. Earlier references to the candy include a claim that Boston confectioner William Schrafft suggested sending jelly beans to soldiers in 1861, and a July 5, 1905 mention in the Chicago Daily News advertising bulk jelly beans at nine cents per pound.
title: Jelly bean

text: The K'iche' constitute the largest Maya ethnic group in the region, surpassing all other Maya peoples in population size. In contrast, the Q’eqchi’ are the second‑largest Maya community, primarily found in lowland areas of Alta Verapaz, Petén, and western Belize, and later dispersed into other parts of Guatemala such as Izabal, Petén, and El Quiché. The prominence of the K'iche' as the most numerous Maya group is reflected across Central America.
title: Maya peoples

text: Human iron metabolism relies on the uptake of iron from food or supplements mainly in the duodenum. Enterocytes that line the duodenal wall contain specialized proteins that move iron into the body. For absorption, iron must be present either as part of a heme protein or in the ferrous (Fe²⁺) form. A brush‑border enzyme called duodenal cytochrome B (Dcytb) reduces ferric (Fe³⁺) iron to Fe²⁺, and the divalent metal transporter‑1 (DMT1) then transports the divalent iron across the enterocyte membrane.
title: Human iron metabolism

text: Starbucks went public with its initial public offering in June 1992. At that time the company operated 140 stores and posted revenue of US$73.5 million, a rise from US$1.3 million in 1987. The IPO sold a 12 % share for roughly US$25 million, valuing the business at about US$271 million.
title: Starbucks

text: In 2011 the Army altered its uniform rules, permitting sew‑on embroidered skill badges while keeping the five‑badge limit and prohibiting any mix of sew‑on and pin‑on devices. At the same time, soldiers could choose to have the Army tape, personal name tapes, and rank insignia sewn on rather than pinned. Skill tabs such as the President’s Hundred, Special Forces, Ranger and Sapper are placed on the left sleeve pocket flap and are limited to three tabs, unless the tab is part of a unit patch (for example “Mountain” or “Airborne”), which does not count toward the limit. The only branch insignia authorized for the Army Combat Uniform is the Chaplain emblem; it is positioned centered 1/8 inch above the name tape on the right side of the chest, i.e., above the right name tape. The emblem may be worn as a metal pin‑on or as a black embroidered patch with Velcro.
title: Army Combat Uniform

text: Plant hormones are signal molecules produced within the plant, present only in minute amounts.
