Every cell has the capacity to synthesize these compounds, which can act on nearby target cells or be translocated to distant parts of the organism. Once relocated, they regulate a wide range of developmental and physiological processes, including the initiation of flowers, the formation of stems and leaves, leaf abscission, seed growth, and the ripening of fruit. By directing which tissues expand upward or downward, influencing the timing of flowering, determining flower sex, and controlling senescence and even plant death, these growth factors shape the overall architecture and longevity of the plant. In the absence of plant hormones, a plant would remain largely an undifferentiated mass of cells.
title: Plant hormone

text: The authority of the Philippines’ highest court rests in its fifteen Justices, including the Chief Justice, who together exercise the constitutional power of administrative supervision over all lower courts and their personnel.
title: Supreme Court of the Philippines

text: In the 1996 live‑action adaptation titled *101 Dalmatians*, the notorious fashion designer Cruella de Vil is portrayed by actress Glenn Close. The film follows American video‑game designer Roger Dearly (Jeff Daniels) and his dalmatian Pongo as they meet Anita Campbell‑Green (Joely Richardson), a fashion designer at the House of de Vil. While Anita creates a coat with spotted fur inspired by her dog, her boss Cruella de Vil—played by Glenn Close—becomes obsessed with making garments from actual dalmatians, even arranging for a taxidermist to skin a white tiger for a rug.
title: 101 Dalmatians (1996 film)

text: In the HBO series *Game of Thrones*, the role of Jon Snow is performed by Kit Harington.
title: Jon Snow (character)

text: The series, released in the United States and Canada under the title *Where’s Waldo?*, is a collection of children’s puzzle books created by English illustrator Martin Handford. Each volume contains large, detailed double‑page illustrations crowded with dozens of people performing a variety of amusing activities, and readers are challenged to locate the hidden character Wally. In other words, it is a puzzle book.
title: Where's Wally?

text: Real Madrid holds the record for the most La Liga trophies, having secured the championship 33 times.
title: List of Spanish football champions

text: The Mall of America—often referred to locally as “MOA” or simply “the mall”—is a shopping mall situated in Bloomington, Minnesota, a suburb of the Twin Cities. Opened in 1992 near the junction of Interstate 494 and Minnesota State Highway 77, its chief purpose is shopping, offering extensive retail space that makes it the United States’ largest mall by total floor area.
title: Mall of America

text: The franchise was founded in 1993 by The Walt Disney Company as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and was sold to Henry and Susan Samueli in 2005, who renamed the team the Anaheim Ducks before the 2006–07 season. Since then the club has reached the playoffs repeatedly, earned six Pacific Division titles and two Western Conference championships, and its only Stanley Cup triumph occurred in (2006–07).
title: Anaheim Ducks

text: "I Wanna Be Sedated" is a track recorded by the American punk rock group the Ramones. Released on their fourth studio album, *Road to Ruin*, in September 1978, the song quickly became one of the band’s most recognizable pieces. It initially appeared as the B‑side to the UK single “She’s the One” on 21 September 1978, later saw a single release in the Netherlands that same year, and was issued in the United States in 1980 by RSO Records as part of the *Times Square* soundtrack album.
title: I Wanna Be Sedated

text: Before the Qin dynasty unified the region, the name Zhongguo was employed to designate the “Central States,” a term that highlighted the culturally distinct core area centered on the Yellow River valley, in contrast to the surrounding tribal periphery. The word combines the characters zhōng (中, “central” or “middle”) and guó (國/国, “state” or “states”).
title: Names of China

text: In the U.S. version of the game show Cash Cab, the host receives each trivia prompt from a support van that follows the taxi. The producers and camera crew in the van transmit the questions to him by way of a walkie-talkie and earpiece. The cab itself is fitted with ten cameras and additional recording equipment, while the support vehicle supplies the logistical information needed for the game.
title: Cash Cab (U.S. game show)

text: The plague moved northward throughout the first half of 1349, reaching York in May and sweeping across the northern counties during June, July and August. After surviving the winter of 1348‑49, the epidemic lost much of its vigor in the following cold season. By December 1349, the Black Death in England had largely given way, and life was beginning to return to relative normalcy. Overall, the disease required roughly 500 days to cross the whole country.
title: Black Death in England

text: The Ouija board made its commercial debut on July 1, 1890, when businessman Elijah Bond introduced it to the market. Initially it was treated as a harmless parlor amusement, but during World War I spiritualist Pearl Curran helped popularize it as a divining tool. Earlier, in 1886, spiritualists at camps in Ohio had already been using a talking board similar to the modern Ouija to try to communicate with the dead.
title: Ouija

text: The production began its principal photography on May 20, 2016, in Welch, West Virginia.
title: The Glass Castle (film)

text: Brazil is the country that grows the most coffee in the world, maintaining its position as the leading coffee producer globally. While other nations such as Vietnam have rapidly expanded their output and Indonesia ranks among the top exporters, Brazil’s coffee production remains unmatched.
title: Coffee

text: The upcoming Commonwealth Games are slated to occur from 27 July through 7 August 2022, with Birmingham confirmed as the host city during a press conference held on 21 December 2017.
title: 2022 Commonwealth Games

text: The pop group The Osmonds issued the single “One Bad Apple” on November 14, 1970. The song entered the Billboard Hot 100 on January 2, 1971, climbed to the top of the chart on February 13, 1971, and held the number‑one position for five consecutive weeks. It also reached No. 6 on the R&B chart and earned a Gold certification from the RIAA on February 4, 1971.
title: One Bad Apple

text: In American football the offense is required to position a minimum of **at least seven players** on the line of scrimmage before the snap. Only the two players at the ends of that line are eligible receivers; the remaining linemen are not. The other offensive players, including the quarterback and the backfield members, line up behind this group.
title: Eligible receiver

text: Super Bowl LII, the championship game for the 2017 NFL season, was contested on February 4, 2018, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota. This was the second time the league chose the city— the most northern venue ever to host the event— for a Super Bowl.
title: Super Bowl LII

text: At the 2018 Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel, who entered the race as the defending winner, again took the checkered flag, achieving the 48th victory of his Formula One career.
title: 2018 Australian Grand Prix

text: The Indian myna (Acridotheres tristis), also known as the common myna, belongs to the starling family Sturnidae. It is native to Asia. This omnivorous, open‑woodland bird shows a strong territorial instinct and has adapted extremely well to urban environments.
title: Common myna

text: The Indian myna (common myna) is a bird species native to Asia. Its original range extended across a wide swath of the continent, encompassing countries such as Iran, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Myanmar, Malaysia, Singapore, peninsular Thailand, Indo‑China and China.
title: Common myna

text: After graduating from Oxford in 1910, Henry Moseley accepted a post as a demonstrator in physics at the University of Manchester. There he joined the research laboratory that was overseen by the eminent physicist Sir Ernest Rutherford. During his initial year he carried a teaching load as a graduate teaching assistant, but was subsequently reassigned to work as a graduate research assistant under Rutherford’s supervision.
title: Henry Moseley

text: The manga begins in 2001, when the Diamond Is Unbreakable character Koichi Hirose travels to Naples at Jotaro Kujo’s request to locate a person named Haruno Shiobana and obtain a skin sample. The target turns out to be a middle‑school student called Giorno Giovanna, who is actually Dio Brando’s son. Giorno attempts to steal Koichi’s luggage but is halted by Koichi’s Stand, Echoes Act Three, which Giorno identifies as a Stand power akin to his own Gold Experience, capable of giving life to inanimate objects. From there the narrative follows Giorno’s goal of becoming a mafia boss to improve Naples, leading to his clash with gang member Leaky Eye Luka, his approach to the crime syndicate Passione, and his meeting with member Bruno Bucciarati, whose Stand Sticky Fingers can create and open zippers on any surface.
title: Vento Aureo

text: The octopus is a soft‑bodied mollusk with eight arms that belongs to the order Octopoda. This order, together with squids, cuttlefish and nautiloids, is placed within the class Cephalopoda. Like other members of this class, the octopus is bilaterally symmetric, has two eyes and a central beak at the base of its arms. Its flexible body lets it squeeze through narrow gaps, and it propels itself by expelling water through a siphon. Octopuses also have a sophisticated nervous system and sharp vision, ranking them among the most intelligent invertebrates.
title: Octopus

text: In biochemistry, the suffix **-ase** is attached to the end of an enzyme’s name. The most common convention is to take the name of the substrate and add this suffix, so an enzyme that breaks down peroxides is called peroxidase, while the enzyme that creates telomeres is named telomerase. Occasionally the name reflects the reaction rather than the substrate; for example, polymerase denotes the enzyme that assembles DNA strands, and reverse transcriptase refers to the enzyme that synthesizes DNA from an RNA template.
title: -ase

text: The library classification that later became known as the Dewey Decimal System was created by the American librarian **Melvil Dewey**. While working at the Amherst College library in 1873, Dewey formulated the ideas for his system and, by 1876, had produced a first version that he issued in a pamphlet called *A Classification and Subject Index for Cataloguing and Arranging the Books and Pamphlets of a Library*. This early edition, printed in a limited run, marked the origin of the classification method that would become the Dewey Decimal Classification.
title: Dewey Decimal Classification

text: Miller Lite is recognized as the United States’ first mainstream light beer. The brew originated in 1967 as “Gablinger’s Diet Beer,” a formulation developed by biochemist Joseph L. Owades while he was employed at New York’s Rheingold Brewery. Owades later passed the recipe to Peter Hand Brewing in Chicago; that company, after being purchased and renamed Meister Brau Brewing, introduced the drink as Meister Brau Lite. Financial problems forced Meister Brau to sell several labels to Miller in 1972, and the product was relaunched simply as “Lite.” After test marketing in Springfield, Illinois; Knoxville, Tennessee; and San Diego, California in 1973, Miller rolled the beer out nationally in 1975 under the brand name Miller Lite, establishing it as the first widely available light beer in the United States.
title: Miller Lite

text: "All I Want for Christmas Is You" is a holiday track recorded by the American vocalist Mariah Carey. She co‑wrote and co‑produced the song with Walter Afanasieff, and Columbia Records issued it on 1 November 1994 as the lead single from her fourth studio album, the holiday collection *Merry Christmas*. The upbeat love song features bell chimes, layered backing vocals, and synthesizer instrumentation.
title: All I Want for Christmas Is You

text: Clemson’s latest consensus Division I football national title was earned when the Tigers beat the Alabama Crimson Tide in the College Football Playoff championship game for the 2016 season, securing the championship in 2016.
title: Clemson Tigers football

text: The series spanned four seasons, during which a total of 49 episodes were produced and aired.
title: List of The Glades episodes

text: In the 1994 NCAA Division I men’s basketball championship, Arkansas emerged victorious, defeating Duke 76–72 to claim its first national title.
title: 1994 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament

text: The phrase “Jack Mormon” is believed to have originated in **Jackson County, Missouri** during the early 1830s.  At that time, Latter‑Day Saint settlers were expelled from Jackson County by an angry mob and many fled to nearby Clay County.  The residents of Clay County—mostly Democrats who welcomed the refugees—were derisively labeled “Jack” Mormons by the hostile citizens of Jackson County, giving rise to the term.
title: Jack Mormon

text: The expression “physiology” was originally coined by the French physician Jean Fernel (1497–1558).
title: Physiology

text: In Once Upon a Time, after Emma Swan and Captain Hook are pulled through Zelena’s time‑portal and return to Storybrooke, Emma regains her magic and decides to make the town her home. Following these events, she begins a romantic relationship with Hook.
title: Emma Swan

text: The National Invitation Tournament’s decline was evident by the mid-1980s, when it had fully transitioned into a secondary competition for lower‑profile teams, demonstrating that the NCAA tournament had become the premier event.
title: National Invitation Tournament

text: In the television series *Sister Wives*, Kody Brown’s original legal marriage was to his first wife, Meri. Their union remained the only legally recognized marriage until they obtained a legal divorce in September 2014. (Subsequent marriages were either spiritual unions or, in the case of his fourth wife Robyn, a legal marriage undertaken in December 2014 to facilitate the adoption of her three children.)
title: Sister Wives

text: Scholarly consensus holds that Buddhism first reached China in the first century CE, during the Han dynasty, when missionaries traveling from India introduced the faith to Chinese lands.
title: Chinese Buddhism

text: During the Han dynasty, the religion Buddhism first arrived in China by traveling along the Silk Road.  Historians have long debated whether the faith entered via maritime channels or overland passages, but both lines of inquiry agree that Buddhism reached Han China in the first century CE—evidenced by the founding of the White Horse Temple in 68 CE under Emperor Ming of Han.  This early introduction marks Buddhism as a major religious influence that entered China through the Silk Road during the Han period.
title: Chinese Buddhism

text: Buddhism entered China when Indian monks journeyed along the Silk Road to teach the faith, and by the early fifth century it was firmly established in southern China, receiving imperial and courtly patronage and becoming a focus of gentry‑supported religious practice.
title: Chinese Buddhism

text: “One of These Nights” was written by Don Henley and Glenn Frey and recorded by the American rock band Eagles. Serving as the title track on their One of These Nights album, the song was issued as a single that later topped the Billboard Hot 100. The released version trims the album cut by omitting most of the intro and the extended fade‑out. Henley sings the verses, while Randy Meisner provides the high‑harmony refrain, and Don Felder contributes a blues‑based guitar solo.
title: One of These Nights (song)

text: The flag of Vietnam is a solid red banner bearing a single gold (yellow) five‑pointed star at its centre. Designed in 1940, it first appeared during an uprising that year against French rule in the southern region of Vietnam. In the flag’s symbolism, the red field represents the revolutionary aspirations of the Vietnamese people, while the star stands for the five principal classes of society—intellectuals, farmers, workers, businesspeople and military personnel.
title: Flag of Vietnam

text: In Ernest Cline’s *Ready Player One*, the OASIS is presented as a virtual reality simulator that users enter through visors and haptic gloves. It operates both as a massive multiplayer online role‑playing game and as an entire virtual society, providing a stable in‑world currency and serving as an escape from the world’s 2040s energy crisis, climate effects, and overpopulation. The system was created by James Halliday, who later hid an Easter egg inside the OASIS that would grant the finder his fortune and control of the corporation.
title: Ready Player One

text: In the television series *Steptoe and Son*, the opening sequences frequently showed the family’s horse, named Hercules. This animal appeared regularly at the start of episodes, serving as a visual element of the show’s introductions.
title: Steptoe and Son

text: According to the records for the National Film Award for Best Actor, the very first honoree was Uttam Kumar, who was recognised at the 15th ceremony in 1968 for his performances in *Anthony Firingee* and *Chiriyakhana*. By 2017, the actor Amitabh Bachchan had become the most celebrated, having secured the award four times—more than any other performer. Kamal Haasan and Mammootty follow with three wins each, while Sanjeev Kumar, Mithun Chakraborty, Om Puri, Naseeruddin Shah, Mohanlal and Ajay Devgn have each received it twice. A few actors, notably Mithun Chakraborty and Mammootty, have been honoured for work in two different languages. The most recent recipient noted is Riddhi Sen, who was awarded at the 65th National Film Awards for his role in the Bengali film *Nagarkirtan*.
title: National Film Award for Best Actor

text: Soft iron, characterized by its low coercivity, is commonly used for the cores of electromagnets. The low coercivity diminishes the energy loss that occurs during a hysteresis cycle. This reduction in energy loss is also the reason soft iron is selected for transformer cores and electric motors.
title: Hysteresis

text: The United States Secretary of State is appointed by the President and, after a confirmation hearing before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, must be approved by the Senate. Because the role is classified as a Level I position in the Executive Schedule, the officeholder’s salary is $205,700.
title: United States Secretary of State

text: Patrick Walshe (July 26, 1900 – December 11, 1991) was an American dwarf character actor and circus performer noted for his animal impersonations. In the classic film *The Wizard of Oz*, he took on the role of Nikko, the chief of the Winged Monkeys. While his screen appearances were limited, the bulk of his career was spent in theater, vaudeville, and circus performances.
title: Pat Walshe

text: President Ferdinand Marcos told a gathering of his University of the Philippines College of Law alumni that he intended to terminate martial law by the end of January 1981.
title: History of the Philippines (1965–86)

text: During the last Ice Age the Solent was not a sea channel but a river that ran southeast from the area of present‑day Poole Harbour toward the middle of the English Channel. As sea levels rose, the river valley was inundated, and the chalk ridge west of the Needles was breached, giving rise to the island now known as the Isle of Wight.
title: Isle of Wight

text: The New York Giants have captured four Super Bowl titles, the most recent of which was earned in Super Bowl XLVI. That championship was secured in 2011, marking the latest year the franchise won a Super Bowl. Earlier victories came in Super Bowls XXI (1986), XXV (1990) and XLII (2007).
title: New York Giants

text: Later, the zoo animals gather to discuss how they can help Griffin win Stephanie’s heart. Jerome the Bear proposes teaching Griffin their mating techniques, but Joe the Lion, played by Sylvester Stallone, objects, reminding everyone that the animal code forbids talking to humans.
title: Zookeeper (film)

text: In NASCAR, the pace car leads the field around the track at pit road speed during the warm‑up laps, since the series does not permit speedometers or electronic speed‑limiting devices. This practice lets drivers observe the engine RPM that matches the required pit road speed, and any driver who exceeds that speed on pit road is penalized.
title: Safety car

text: Sheev Palpatine—better known by his Sith title Darth Sidious—is the figure who sits on the throne of the Galactic Empire in the Star Wars saga. In the original trilogy he appears as the aged, pallid‑faced Emperor who commands the Empire and oversees Darth Vader, while the prequel films show his rise from a charismatic Naboo senator to Supreme Chancellor, ultimately reshaping the Republic into an empire with himself as its ruler.
title: Palpatine

text: The track titled “Fool (If You Think It’s Over)” was initially released to the public in 1978 and was performed by British singer‑songwriter Chris Rea, who also wrote its lyrics and composed the music. The song is featured on his 1978 debut album, Whatever Happened to Benny Santini?.
title: Fool (If You Think It's Over)

text: After the turmoil surrounding her relationships and the loss of her pregnancy, Hope decides to leave Los Angeles. She travels abroad and spends time with her friend Brooke, meeting her in Milan, Italy. While in the city, Hope remains there and does not return to L.A. with Brooke.
title: Hope Logan

text: The vibranium that was forged into Captain America’s famous circular shield originated in Wakanda. In a 2001 retcon, King T’Chaka of the African nation gave Captain America a second sample of the alien metal—found only in Wakanda and the Savage Land—in early 1941, and that sample was used to create the new shield, retiring his earlier triangular one.
title: Captain America's shield

text: On April 26, 2005, Circuit City announced that its Canadian locations would be rebranded as The Source by Circuit City (known in Quebec as La Source par Circuit City). The name change was rolled out across most stores by early July of that year, and the retailer introduced its own house brands—Nexxtech and Centrios—replacing the former RadioShack brands.
title: The Source (retailer)

text: The show slowly reveals the Smoking Man’s history—his real name C.G.B. Spender, his ties to the secretive Syndicate, and his family connections—but the hint that he is actually the biological father of FBI Special Agent Fox Mulder does not emerge until later in the sixth season, when new evidence points to that relationship.
title: Cigarette Smoking Man

text: In the sixteenth series of the television drama Silent Witness, forensic pathologist Leo Dalton meets his end when a blast occurs, dying in an explosion.
title: Silent Witness

text: The public sector, also known as the state sector, represents the portion of the economy that includes both public services and public enterprises.
title: Public sector

text: Jeff East, an American actor born on October 27, 1957, began working professionally at the age of fourteen. He is especially remembered for playing the teenage Clark Kent in Alexander Salkind’s 1978 film *Superman: The Movie*.
title: Jeff East

text: Born on 7 August 1871, Abanindranath Tagore CIE (অবনীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর) emerged as the leading artist who founded the Indian Society of Oriental Art. As its principal creator, he also spearheaded the Bengal school of art, championing Swadeshi values in Indian painting. In addition to his visual contributions, he authored several celebrated children’s books, including Rajkahini and Khirer Putul.
title: Abanindranath Tagore

text: In the Indian botanical tradition, the scholar Parashara (c. 400 – c. 500 AD), who authored the Vṛksayurveda (the science of tree life), carried out detailed examinations of plant structure. His close observations of cells and leaves led him to recognize that plants are composed of cells, a insight that preceded later classifications of dicotyledons and monocotyledons.
title: History of botany

text: During the autumn and winter seasons, the United States’ earliest sunrise is recorded at the summit of Cadillac Mountain, because the sun rises to the south of due east at that time. By contrast, in most of spring and summer the first sunrise occurs at other locations.
title: Cadillac Mountain

text: The national flag of Hungary is a horizontal tricolour composed of red, white and green bands. This exact arrangement has been the official flag of Hungary since 23 May 1957. Its design stems from republican movements of the 18th and 19th centuries, while the colours themselves originate in the Middle Ages. The current Hungarian tricolour mirrors the republican‑movement flag that was first employed in the United Kingdom in 1816.
title: Flag of Hungary

text: Hungary’s national flag is composed of three horizontal bands of red, white and green. The tricolour design was inspired by the French flag as a nod to the ideas of the French Revolution, while the three colours themselves come from the historic Hungarian coat of arms that have been in use in essentially the same form since the mid‑15th century. These hues were originally taken from the arms of the Árpád dynasty, which first appeared in the late 12th and early 13th centuries. The stripes are arranged horizontally rather than vertically to avoid confusion with Italy’s similar‑looking flag, which also adopted a French‑style tricolour. Records also indicate that a version of the present‑day Hungarian tricolour was already displayed at the coronation of Matthias II of Hungary in 1608.
title: Flag of Hungary

text: The New Day’s tag‑team championship reign carried on into 2016; on December 14, 2016 they were acknowledged as the longest‑reigning WWE tag‑team champions, a distinction they held while possessing the titles.
title: The New Day (wrestling)

text: In 2016, The New Day captured the WWE Tag Team Championship. When the 2016 WWE draft occurred, the duo was moved to the Raw brand, which turned the tag titles into a Raw‑exclusive championship. Their reign continued with successful defenses against Gallows and Anderson at events such as SummerSlam on August 21 and Clash of Champions on September 25, ultimately establishing them as the longest‑reigning champions in the title’s history.
title: The New Day (wrestling)

text: “White Wedding” is a track performed by Billy Idol; it was released on his self‑titled 1982 album. The single originally reached No. 108 on Billboard’s Bubbling Under the Hot 100, and after a 1983 re‑issue it climbed to No. 36 on the Hot 100. In the United Kingdom, the song later peaked at No. 6 on the UK Singles Chart following re‑releases in 1985 and 1988.
title: White Wedding (song)

text: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) functions as a ministry of the Indian government, charged with administering corporate legislation such as the Companies Acts and the Limited Liability Partnership Act and overseeing the regulation of Indian enterprises.
title: Ministry of Corporate Affairs

text: The United States moved forward with the canal project after President Theodore Roosevelt backed the Panamanian rebels’ bid to break away from Colombia.  Roosevelt altered American policy, endorsed the separation, and shortly after Panama’s declaration of independence he signed a treaty with the new government that secured the rights needed for the canal’s construction.
title: Panama Canal

text: During the construction of the Panama Canal, the United States was led by President Theodore Roosevelt. On May 6 1904 he appointed John Findley Wallace—formerly chief engineer and later general manager of the Illinois Central Railroad—as chief engineer of the canal project. Overwhelmed by the disease‑ridden environment, the dilapidated French infrastructure, and the cumbersome bureaucracy of the Isthmian Canal Commission, Wallace resigned abruptly in June 1905. He was succeeded by John Frank Stevens, a self‑educated engineer who had built the Great Northern Railroad and who began bypassing the commission, sending his requests directly to the Roosevelt administration in Washington.
title: Panama Canal

text: The halftime entertainment for Super Bowl LII, staged on February 4, 2018 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, was headlined by Justin Timberlake, who had been confirmed as the performer by the NFL on October 22, 2017. The broadcast of the show was carried nationally by NBC.
title: Super Bowl LII halftime show

text: Prime rib—also referred to as a standing rib roast—is cut from the primal rib, one of the nine primary sections of beef. The rib portion of a cow spans ribs six through twelve, and a standing rib roast may include anywhere from two to seven of those ribs.
title: Standing rib roast

text: Heath Ledger, who died on 22 January 2008 from an accidental intoxication of prescription drugs, had finished filming his performance as The Joker in *The Dark Knight* a few months before his death. Ledger played the Joker in *The Dark Knight*, and his passing occurred while the film was still being edited and during the production of his final role as Tony in *The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus*. His untimely death cast a shadow over the promotion of the $185 million Batman production, but his critically acclaimed portrayal earned numerous posthumous accolades, including the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.
title: Heath Ledger

text: In Christopher Nolan’s 2008 movie *The Dark Knight*, the role of the Joker is performed by Ledger. This was his penultimate screen appearance, with the film debuting roughly half a year after his death. While shooting in London, Ledger described his interpretation of the character as a “psychopathic, mass‑murdering, schizophrenic clown with zero empathy.” His portrayal earned him a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, accepted by his family, as well as a Golden Globe in the same category.
title: Heath Ledger

text: Gravity, sometimes called gravitation, is the natural attraction that pulls any objects with mass toward one another. This force operates on scales ranging from individual atoms and photons up to entire planets and stars. Because mass and energy are interchangeable, all forms of energy—including light—both generate and are affected by gravity. On Earth, gravity gives physical objects weight, and the Moon’s gravity creates the ocean tides. The original gaseous matter in the universe was drawn together by gravity, leading to the formation of stars and the clustering of those stars into galaxies, so gravity shapes many of the large‑scale structures we observe. Its reach is infinite, although its strength diminishes with increasing distance.
title: Gravity

text: Judith Cynthia Aline Keppel (born 18 August 1942) achieved a historic milestone when she became the first contestant to claim the £1 million top prize on the United Kingdom version of the television quiz show *Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?*. Her victory also made her the inaugural winner of a million‑pound prize on any British television game programme and, to date, the only woman in the UK to have reached that level. Since 2003 she has been a regular panelist on the BBC Two quiz series *Eggheads*.
title: Judith Keppel

text: The 2018 Pro Bowl, which served as the National Football League’s all‑star contest for the 2017 season, was held at Camping World Stadium in Orlando, Florida on January 28, 2018. This marked the second consecutive year the event was staged in Orlando.
title: 2018 Pro Bowl

text: The Pro Bowl’s three‑year agreement, which began in 2017, designates Camping World Stadium in Orlando as the venue for the upcoming game.
title: 2018 Pro Bowl

text: "Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head" was written by lyricist Hal David and composer Burt Bacharach for the 1969 film *Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid*. The song won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, and its creators also received the Oscar for Best Original Score. The recording was performed by B. J. Thomas, who completed it after seven takes after Bacharach expressed dissatisfaction with the first six. In the film version, Thomas sang while recovering from laryngitis, giving his voice a hoarser quality than the commercial 7‑inch release, and the movie featured a separate vaudeville‑style instrumental break in double time while Paul Newman performed bicycle stunts.
title: Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head

text: Since the 1947 partition of British India that gave rise to the modern states of India and Pakistan, the two nations have engaged in four wars—including one that was never formally declared—alongside a series of border skirmishes and military stand‑offs.
title: Indo-Pakistani wars and conflicts

text: The geocentric system, whose astronomical calculations were used to construct both astrological and astronomical charts for over fifteen hundred years, was formulated by the ancient astronomer Ptolemy. This model remained dominant until the early modern period, when it was eventually replaced by the heliocentric theories of Copernicus, Galileo and Kepler.
title: Geocentric model

text: In 1973 the soul vocalist Ronnie Dyson released the original recording of the Bobby Eli‑co‑written track “Just Don’t Want to Be Lonely.” Dyson’s version climbed to No. 60 on the U.S. pop chart, No. 30 on the Adult Contemporary chart, and No. 29 on the R&B chart. Its B‑side was the song “Point of No Return,” penned by Tom Bell and Linda Creed.
title: Just Don't Want to Be Lonely

text: Stephen Sondheim composed “Send In the Clowns” expressly for the actress Glynis Johns, who introduced the song when she originated the role of Desirée in the Broadway production. The composition features four verses and a bridge set in a complex compound meter. After its debut, the tune became Sondheim’s most famous work, especially following Frank Sinatra’s 1973 recording and Judy Collins’ chart‑topping versions in 1975 and 1977, after which many other artists recorded it and it entered the jazz‑standard repertoire.
title: Send In the Clowns

text: The picture offers a fictionalized look at the rise and fall of Charles Foster Kane, a media mogul whose character was modeled in part on the real‑world newspaper tycoon William Randolph Hearst, alongside inspirations such as Chicago businessmen Samuel Insull and Harold McCormick and elements of Orson Welles’s own life.
title: Citizen Kane

text: Antigonon leptopus is a fast‑growing climbing vine that ascends by means of tendrils and can reach lengths of 25 feet or more. Its foliage consists of cordate (heart‑shaped) leaves, sometimes taking a triangular form, each leaf measuring roughly 2½ to 7½ cm long. The plant bears its blossoms in panicles that line the rachis, producing pink or white flowers from spring through autumn. In addition, Antigonon leptopus develops underground tubers and substantial rootstocks, generates abundant seeds that float on water, and its fruit and seeds are eaten and dispersed by a variety of animals such as pigs, raccoons and birds. The tubers are capable of resprouting if the vine is cut back or damaged by frost.
title: Antigonon leptopus

text: When the original proposal collapsed, the James Bond film *Licence to Kill* selected Gladys Knight to sing its title theme. Her recording—written by Narada Michael Walden, Jeffrey Cohen and Walter Afanasieff and built around the “horn line” from *Goldfinger*—later reached the United Kingdom’s Top 10. At five minutes twelve seconds, the song is the longest Bond theme, and its music video was directed by Daniel Kleinman.
title: Licence to Kill (soundtrack)

text: The 2017 Grand National was claimed by One For Arthur, becoming only the second horse trained in Scotland to secure victory in the race after Rubstic in 1979. The winning horse was ridden by jockey Derek Fox, trained by Lucinda Russell, and started the contest at odds of 14/1.
title: 2017 Grand National

text: In the 2016 World Series—played from October 25 through November 2—the National League champion Chicago Cubs met the American League champion Cleveland Indians. The Cubs emerged as the winners, beating the Indians to capture the championship.
title: 2016 World Series

text: In the 2016 World Series, the Cubs defeated the Indians, winning the best‑of‑seven contest 4 games to 3 to claim their first championship since 1908. The decisive Game 7 ended with an 8–7 victory in extra innings, becoming the fifth Game 7 ever to go beyond nine innings and the first such instance since 1997, which also involved the Indians. A rain delay occurred just as the tenth inning was about to begin. By rallying from a 3‑1 series deficit, Chicago joined a short list of teams that have reversed a World Series after trailing early in the matchup.
title: 2016 World Series

text: Although the Rocky and Bullwinkle Show continued to be syndicated through The Program Exchange into the 2010s, the franchise’s ownership has since shifted. The underlying rights are now owned by Universal Pictures, which also controls the libraries of former owners DreamWorks Animation and Classic Media. In partnership with Ward Productions, Universal Pictures operates the joint venture Bullwinkle Studios, the entity that manages the Rocky and Bullwinkle properties.
title: The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends (TV series)

text: In December 1878, British official Bartle Frere—acting without his government’s approval—presented an ultimatum to the Zulu monarch Cetshwayo that required, among other demands, the disbanding of the Zulu army and the abandonment of key cultural traditions. Unable to meet these terms, Cetshwayo’s refusal led Frere to send Lord Chelmsford to invade Zululand, igniting the Anglo‑Zulu War in which the Zulu king Cetshwayo led his people in combat against the British forces.
title: Anglo-Zulu War

text: The Anglo‑Zulu War began after a border dispute involving the Zulu kingdom and the Boers. The Zulu king Cetshwayo was the leader who confronted the British ultimatum presented by Sir Henry Bartle Frere following a commission report in July 1878. When Cetshwayo gave no reply by the extended deadline of 11 January 1879, a British force commanded by Lieutenant‑General Frederick Augustus Thesiger, 2nd Baron Chelmsford, invaded Zululand in January 1879, initiating the conflict.
title: Anglo-Zulu War

text: The light hair and eye colors that are common in northern Europe, such as blonde hair and green eyes, are tied to the same physiological adaptation that produces lighter skin.  Lighter skin results from a low concentration in pigmentation, which permits more ultraviolet light to reach the skin and stimulate vitamin D synthesis in regions with limited sunlight.  Because the overall amount of pigment is reduced, the hair and the iris also contain less melanin, giving rise to the characteristic blonde hair and green eye coloration.
title: Blond

text: Vertebrates first emerged about 525 million years ago during the Cambrian explosion, a time of rapid diversification of life. The earliest known member of this group is believed to be the Myllokunmingia. Other early Cambrian vertebrates, such as Haikouichthys ercaicunensis, already possessed the basic vertebrate body plan—a notochord, rudimentary vertebrae, and a well‑defined head and tail—though they lacked true jaws and relied on filter feeding near the seabed. Small eel‑like conodonts, known from paired tooth‑segment microfossils, appear later in the record from the late Cambrian through the Triassic, but their exact phylogenetic placement remains uncertain.
title: Vertebrate

text: The American television series Wonder Woman, which aired from 1975 to 1979, featured Lynda Carter in the title role as Wonder Woman/Diana Prince. The show began on ABC with a World‑War‑II setting and later moved to CBS, where it was retitled The New Adventures of Wonder Woman. Alongside Carter, Lyle Waggoner played the character of Steve Trevor.
title: Wonder Woman (TV series)

text: The treaty finalizing the Louisiana Purchase was executed on 30 April 1803 by Robert Livingston, James Monroe, and Barbé Marbois in Paris. President Thomas Jefferson announced the agreement to the American public on July 4, and after the signing Livingston declared, “We have lived long, but this is the noblest work of our whole lives… From this day the United States take their place among the powers of the first rank.”
title: Louisiana Purchase

text: In 1945, the presidents of the eight schools came together and signed the inaugural Ivy Group Agreement, which set academic, financial, and athletic standards for their football teams. This agreement laid the foundation for the policies that would later define the Ivy League.
title: Ivy League

text: Jack London’s adventure novel *The Call of the Wild* takes place in the Yukon, Canada, during the 1890s Klondike Gold Rush, a period when sled dogs were in great demand. The narrative follows Buck, a dog who is taken from his California ranch and sold into Alaskan sled‑dog service, where he must adapt to the harsh, primitive conditions of that decade.
title: The Call of the Wild

text: In the film *Rio Bravo*, the youthful gunslinger known as Colorado Ryan is portrayed by Ricky Nelson. He appears alongside Pat Wheeler (Ward Bond), whose supply wagon arrives in town, and the other characters such as Stumpy (Walter Brennan) and the jail’s inmates.
title: Rio Bravo (film)

text: John Joseph Patrick Ryan (December 30, 1920 – January 21, 1998), who worked under the stage name Jack Lord, was an American actor, director and producer. He is best known for originating the character Steve McGarrett in the CBS television series *Hawaii Five‑O*, which ran from 1968 to 1980.
title: Jack Lord

text: In the 1965 amendments to the Social Security Act, Title XIX created the program known as Medicaid, authorizing federal matching assistance to states so they could fund health‑care services for individuals whose incomes were at or near the public‑assistance level.
title: Social Security Amendments of 1965

text: The Mike O’Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge, an arch span crossing the Colorado River at the Hoover Dam site, was completed as the centerpiece of the Hoover Dam Bypass project. Situated within the Lake Mead National Recreation Area about 30 miles (48 km) southeast of Las Vegas, the bridge carries U.S. Route 93 between Arizona and Nevada. It opened in 2010, replacing the former routing of US 93 that ran atop the dam and eliminating the hazardous hairpin turns and blind curves that had previously been required. The structure is named for former Nevada Governor Mike O’Callaghan and former Arizona Cardinals player‑turned‑soldier Pat Tillman.
title: Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge

text: At the Constitutional Convention the delegates first settled on the meeting’s guiding principles, and then turned their attention to the Virginia Plan— a proposal that had been introduced by Madison, which they subsequently began to modify.
title: Constitutional Convention (United States)

text: When the 1787 Constitutional Convention finally gathered, James Madison was the first delegate to arrive, followed shortly by the rest of Virginia’s representatives. While they waited for the other states’ delegates, the Virginian group prepared the Virginia Plan—a proposal that was both designed and written by James Madison.
title: Constitutional Convention (United States)

text: In 2017, the permanent population of the Bora Bora archipelago was recorded as 10,605.
title: Bora Bora

text: The IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) relies on standard IETF protocols whenever possible, and one of the key protocols it employs is SIP, which stands for Session Initiation Protocol. This use of SIP helps IMS integrate smoothly with Internet services while providing a common control layer that separates the access network from the service layer.
title: IP Multimedia Subsystem

text: Celebrity Big Brother, the celebrity edition of the U.S. version of Big Brother, was aired on CBS during the winter of the 2017‑18 network television season. The series premiered on February 7, 2018, with Julie Chen returning as host and executive producers Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan overseeing production for Fly on the Wall Entertainment in partnership with Endemol Shine North America.
title: Celebrity Big Brother (U.S. TV series)

text: The U.S. version of Celebrity Big Brother was broadcast on CBS during the winter of the 2017‑18 network television season. CBS placed the spin‑off in the February 2018 sweeps period, airing episodes on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, with special Thursday and Saturday broadcasts. Each show ran for one hour from 8:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. EST, while the Friday episodes and the season finale were two‑hour events. The live Internet feeds were also available through CBS All Access, and a companion series, Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark, aired nightly on Pop.
title: Celebrity Big Brother (U.S. TV series)

text: The Mongol‑led Yuan dynasty collapsed amid widespread peasant revolts, and among the insurgent groups the Red Turbans—affiliated with the White Lotus Buddhist secret society—rose in 1351. Zhu Yuanzhang, a formerly penniless peasant and Buddhist monk, entered the Red Turbans in 1352 and soon earned a reputation, especially after marrying the foster daughter of a rebel commander. In 1356 his rebel forces captured the city of Nanjing, which he later designated as the capital of a new regime. Zhu Yuanzhang ultimately overthrew the Mongol Yuan and established the Ming dynasty.
title: Ming dynasty

text: When the Yuan dynasty began to collapse, rival rebel factions vied for control of China. In 1363 Zhu Yuanzhang defeated his chief rival, Chen Youliang, in the massive naval Battle of Lake Poyang, eliminating the last major opposition in the Yangtze River valley. With no other capable challengers after the Red Turban leader’s suspicious death in 1367, Zhu Yuanzhang advanced his forces toward the Yuan capital Dadu (now Beijing) in 1368. The Yuan emperor fled northward, and Zhu Yuanzhang razed the Yuan palaces in Dadu, declared the founding of a new regime, and thus overthrew the Mongol Yuan and established the Ming dynasty. He adopted the era name Hongwu, meaning “Vastly Martial.”
title: Ming dynasty

text: The ancient Chinese military treatise titled *The Art of War*, which originated in the Spring and Autumn period of the 5th century BC, is credited to the strategist Sun Tzu. The text is organized into thirteen chapters, each addressing a different facet of warfare and its application to strategy and tactics. For roughly fifteen centuries it served as the principal work in the collection later formalized as the Seven Military Classics by Emperor Shenzong of Song in 1080, and it continues to be a highly influential source on military, business, and legal strategy throughout East Asia and beyond.
title: The Art of War

text: The inaugural Star Trek vessel bearing the name Enterprise is the USS Enterprise, which carries the registry designation **NCC-1701**. This original starship serves as the primary setting for the series and is identified by that hull number throughout the franchise.
title: USS Enterprise (NCC-1701)

text: The episode titled "Ménage à Troi" is the twenty‑fourth installment of the third season of Star Trek: The Next Generation, and it also marks the seventy‑second episode of the series overall.
title: Ménage à Troi

text: When Ed Sheeran talked about the origins of “Love Yourself” on the Howard Stern Show on March 7 2017, he explained that the track was initially intended for Rihanna, even noting that the original lyric was “fuck yourself.”
title: Love Yourself

text: During World War I, the Ottoman Empire fought alongside the Central Powers. It entered the conflict by launching a surprise attack on Russia’s Black Sea coast on 29 October 1914, which led Russia to declare war on 5 November 1914. Ottoman forces then battled the Entente in both the Balkans and the Middle Eastern theatre. The empire’s defeat occurred in 1918, a pivotal event that paved the way for its eventual dissolution in 1921.
title: History of the Ottoman Empire during World War I

text: The Ottoman Empire’s participation in World War I came to an end on 30 October 1918, when the Armistice of Mudros was signed, marking its surrender. This armistice, concluded in 1918, terminated Ottoman involvement in the conflict.
title: History of the Ottoman Empire during World War I

text: The retinal blood supply runs within the optic nerve; this nerve not only transmits the ganglion‑cell axons to the brain but also houses the vessels that provide circulation to the retina.
title: Retina

text: Maia Harumi Shibutani, born on July 20, 1994, in New York City, is the daughter of Chris Shibutani and Naomi Uyemura. Both of her parents are of Japanese descent, a fact that gives Maia and her older brother Alex Shibutani a Japanese ethnic background. The siblings grew up in the United States, with Maia beginning figure skating at age four while attending Greenwich Academy in Connecticut.
title: Maia Shibutani

text: The Rivingtons followed their 1962 Billboard Hot 100 hit “Papa‑Oom‑Mow‑Mow” with a similarly styled song titled “The Bird’s the Word,” which was released in 1963. This later inspired the Trashmen’s version that became known as “Surfin’ Bird.”
title: Surfin' Bird

text: The remake’s principal photography was carried out in Broken Hill and Sydney, beginning on 5 March 2017 and continuing for five weeks.
title: Wake in Fright (miniseries)

text: Jack Gleeson (born 20 May 1992) is an Irish former actor who is most recognized for his role as King Joffrey Baratheon in the HBO television series *Game of Thrones*.
title: Jack Gleeson

text: A turlough, or turlach, is a disappearing lake that occurs chiefly in the limestone (karst) landscapes of western Ireland, situated to the west of the River Shannon. Its name derives from the Irish word *tuar* meaning “dry,” combined with the suffix *‑lach*, which denotes “a place” in an abstract sense. These seasonal water bodies are characteristic of Irish karst terrain, where the underlying exposed limestone allows water to fill and then drain away periodically.
title: Turlough (lake)

text: The United States Pledge of Allegiance, a statement of loyalty to the national flag and republic, has undergone only a handful of revisions. Its most recent wording change occurred on Flag Day in 1954, when the phrase “under God” was added to the text.
title: Pledge of Allegiance (United States)

text: In 1911 the United States House of Representatives adopted House Joint Resolution 39, a proposal to amend the Constitution so that senators would be selected by direct popular vote.
title: Seventeenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

text: The musical fantasy picture The Wizard of Oz was released in 1939. Produced by Metro‑Goldwyn‑Mayer, the American film features Judy Garland as Dorothy Gale and was directed primarily by Victor Fleming.
title: The Wizard of Oz (1939 film)

text: The third installment of *The Trials of Apollo*, titled **The Burning Maze**, is slated for publication on **May 1, 2018**.
title: The Trials of Apollo

text: In the film *Snow Dogs*, the protagonist Ted goes to Tolketna to claim the dogs left to him by Lucy. He discovers that the inheritance consists of a pack of seven Siberian Huskies together with a single companion named Nana, who is described as a Border Collie. This detail identifies Nana’s breed as a Border Collie.
title: Snow Dogs

text: Sauron secretly forged the One Ring in the volcanic Mount Doom of Mordor, making it the supreme Ring of Power. This single ring was intended to dominate the other Rings and bind their bearers to his will, and while Sauron wore it his power on earth was amplified.
title: Sauron

text: According to the Hebrew calendar, the year identified as AM 5778 commenced at sunset on 20 September 2017 and will conclude at sunset on 9 September 2018.
title: Hebrew calendar

text: The Gupta Empire minted extensive series of gold coins that portrayed Gupta kings performing various rituals, making it the dynasty associated with the earliest Indian gold coinage.
title: Coinage of India

text: Carlos Alan Autry Jr. (born July 31, 1952) is an American actor who portrayed Captain Bubba Skinner on the NBC television series *In the Heat of the Night*.
title: Alan Autry

text: The crown‑of‑thorns starfish (Acanthaster planci) is native to the Indo-Pacific. Its distribution stretches from the Red Sea and the east African coast, across the Indian Ocean, and through the tropical and subtropical Pacific as far west as the coast of Central America, with a particular abundance around Australian reefs. The species is found wherever coral reefs or hard‑coral communities occur within this region.
title: Crown-of-thorns starfish

text: In “Sorry, Wrong Number,” the drama takes place in a Manhattan apartment. The story follows Leona Stevenson, the spoiled, bedridden daughter of wealthy businessman James Cotterell, who finds herself alone after her husband’s delayed return and the servants’ night off. While there, she overhears a crossed telephone call that reveals a plot to murder a woman, setting the suspenseful events against the backdrop of Manhattan.
title: Sorry, Wrong Number

text: In the movie *Sorry, Wrong Number*, the action is anchored in New York City: the heroine’s bedroom window frames the night‑time skyline of Manhattan, establishing the urban setting for the story. The film follows noir conventions, unfolding in real time with flashbacks, and is shot in a dark, shadow‑filled style that heightens suspense.
title: Sorry, Wrong Number

text: The Outback denotes the extensive, remote interior region of Australia, distinguishing it from the “bush,” which colloquially describes any land outside the major urban centers.
title: Outback

text: The track, written by will.i.am, apl.de.ap, Taboo, Justin Timberlake, Ron Fair, Printz Board, George Pajon, Fiona Davies, M. Fratantuno, and J. Curtis and co‑produced by will.i.am and Ron Fair, serves as a commentary on global issues. In this song, The Black Eyed Peas lament on various worldwide problems, addressing topics such as terrorism, governmental hypocrisy, racism, gang violence, environmental pollution, war and intolerance.
title: Where Is the Love?

text: India’s national cricket side made its Test debut at Lord’s on 25 June 1932, becoming the sixth nation to be granted Test status. In the first fifty years of international play the team was relatively weak, winning just 35 of its first 196 Tests. It was not until 1952, almost twenty years after its debut, that India achieved its first Test victory. The team later grew stronger in the 1970s with the emergence of players such as Sunil Gavaskar, Gundappa Viswanath, Kapil Dev and the spin quartet of Erapalli Prasanna, Srinivas Venkataraghavan, Bhagwat Chandrasekhar and Bishen Singh Bedi.
title: India national cricket team

text: The India national cricket team secured its first ever Test victory in 1952, beating England at Madras during the side’s 24th Test match.
title: India national cricket team

text: The balance sheet is the financial statement that presents a company’s assets, liabilities and equity at a specific point in time, usually the end of the fiscal year. By definition, the total dollar amount of assets always equals the combined total of liabilities and equity, thereby illustrating the fundamental accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
title: Financial accounting

text: On July 9 1958, an earthquake‑triggered landslide at the head of Lituya Bay in Alaska generated a megatsunami that climbed to a maximum height of 520 metres (1,710 ft) at the entrance to Gilbert Inlet. The wave surged over the headland, stripping trees and soil down to the bedrock, then raced along the fjord that forms Lituya Bay, destroying a fishing boat anchored there and killing two people. Howard Ulrich and his son managed to stay in their boat as the wave passed and both survived.
title: Megatsunami

text: Red‑eared slider females search the shoreline during the final weeks before they lay eggs, spending increasing time out of the water and repeatedly scratching at the ground. When they find a suitable spot, they use their hind legs to dig a cavity. The female then deposits her clutch of eggs into **a hole** that she has excavated.
title: Red-eared slider

text: Published in 2006, *The Miraculous Journey of Edward Tulane* is a novel by Kate DiCamillo. The story, which follows the life of a china rabbit, also earned the Boston Globe‑Horn Book Award for Fiction that same year.
title: The Miraculous Journey of Edward Tulane

text: Lord Banquo, the Thane of Lochaber, is a figure in William Shakespeare’s 1606 tragedy *Macbeth*. He starts out as a fellow general and ally of Macbeth, and the two men encounter the three witches together. The witches predict that Macbeth will become king while Banquo will not, though his descendants will inherit the throne. Because of this prophecy, Macbeth arranges for Banquo’s murder, hiring two assassins who kill him, though his son Fleance escapes. In a later banquet scene Banquo’s ghost appears, startling Macbeth and revealing the slain noble’s lingering presence.
title: Banquo

text: The inaugural Nobel Prize in Physics was presented in 1901 to Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen of Germany; he received a cash award of 150,782 Swedish kronor, which corresponded to 7,731,004 SEK when adjusted to December 2007 values.
title: List of Nobel laureates in Physics

text: In Nigeria the maritime‑tropical south‑westerly winds that usher the monsoon arrive in central areas around July and remain active till September, at which point the monsoon system starts to withdraw southward.
title: Geography of Nigeria

text: The artifact known as the Cyrus Cylinder, issued by Cyrus, has been cited by the last Shah of Iran, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, as the world’s first declaration of universal human rights—a claim that some historians regard as anachronistic.
title: Cyrus Cylinder

text: Dragon Ball Z, the anime continuation of the original Dragon Ball series, was broadcast on Japan’s Fuji Television from April 26 1989 through January 31 1996. Over the course of its Japanese run the show accumulated a total of **291 episodes**.
title: List of Dragon Ball Z episodes

text: The gallbladder is a small hollow organ that stores and concentrates bile before it enters the small intestine. In humans the pear‑shaped organ is located in the upper right abdomen, lying **beneath the liver**. It receives bile from the common hepatic duct and releases it via the common bile duct into the duodenum, where the bile aids fat digestion.
title: Gallbladder

text: The Constitution’s treatment of the right to property has been altered several times. Although the Forty‑Fourth Amendment of 1978 removed it from the catalogue of fundamental rights, a new clause—Article 300‑A—was inserted, stating that “no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.” Consequently, the right to property is no longer classified as a fundamental right; however, it continues to exist as a **constitutional right**.
title: Fundamental rights in India

text: Donald Trump, who assumed office as the 45th President of the United States on January 20, 2017, continues to serve as the nation’s current president.
title: President of the United States

text: The novel’s action is set in Tulsa, Oklahoma, in 1965, although the city’s name is never directly mentioned in the narrative.
title: The Outsiders (novel)

text: The series‑finale of Grey’s Anatomy’s eighth season, titled “Flight,” aired on May 17, 2012 and centers on an aviation disaster that leaves six Seattle Grace Mercy West physicians fighting for survival. In the crash’s aftermath, Dr. Lexie Grey (Chyler Leigh) is the only one who does not make it, ultimately dying from her injuries.
title: Flight (Grey's Anatomy)

text: When the aircraft crashes in the forest, the surviving doctors—Meredith Grey, Cristina Yang, Arizona Robbins, Derek Shepherd, and Mark Sloan—sustain serious injuries, but none are as badly hurt as Dr. Lexie Grey. Lexie is pinned beneath a large piece of wreckage and, despite Yang and Sloan’s attempts to lift it, they realize she cannot be rescued. Sloan stays with her, holding her hand as she passes away, smiling at the end.
title: Flight (Grey's Anatomy)

text: In the *Tom and Jerry* cartoons the irritable American bulldog who constantly threatens Tom is called Spike. He makes his debut in the 1942 short “Dog Trouble,” and later gains a speaking role in the 1944 episode “The Bodyguard.” Spike is characterized by his stern attitude toward cats, a soft spot for mice, and fierce protectiveness of his son Tyke, often punishing Tom whenever the pup is disturbed. His personality includes a possessive streak over his bone and a notable ticklishness that Tom sometimes tries to exploit.
title: List of Tom and Jerry characters

text: Pearls have been collected from the Indian Ocean for millennia; divers have harvested seawater pearls in Indian waters such as the Gulf of Mannar, as well as in other parts of the ocean. The Indian Ocean remains the sea where pearl gathering has historically taken place in India.
title: Pearl

text: Manchester United Football Club, the professional side based in the Old Trafford area of Greater Manchester, England, has played its home games at a stadium named Old Trafford since moving there in 1910. The club was originally founded as Newton Heath LYR Football Club in 1878, adopted the name Manchester United in 1902, and has competed in the Premier League, the top tier of English football.
title: Manchester United F.C.

text: The Great Gatsby unfolds against the backdrop of the prosperous Long Island of 1922. Fitzgerald situates his narrative in this affluent suburb during the Roaring Twenties, a period marked by economic boom, jazz, new media, and the rise of organized crime that underpins Gatsby’s wealth. By embedding the plot in the historical setting of 1922 Long Island, the novel offers a vivid social portrait of the era.
title: The Great Gatsby

text: Under the framework of IRS penalties, Taxpayers in the United States can incur monetary sanctions when they fail to comply with federal tax obligations. The Internal Revenue Service is the agency that imposes these penalties at the federal level, and it may only levy those penalties that are authorized by federal tax law. While state and local jurisdictions have their own rules, this passage focuses solely on the federal penalties administered by the IRS.
title: IRS penalties

text: In the sitcom *How I Met Your Mother*, the character known as “The Mother” is named Tracy McConnell. The series, narrated by Future Ted, chronicles Ted Mosby’s quest to meet her. Tracy McConnell appears across eight episodes—from “Lucky Penny” through “The Time Travelers”—first becoming visible in the episode “Something New” and later being promoted to a main‑cast role in season 9. The part is performed by Cristin Milioti.
title: The Mother (How I Met Your Mother)

text: In the United Kingdom, corporation tax was lowered from the earlier 28% level that applied between 2008 and 2010 and, as of April 2015, the single main rate was set to a flat **20%**. This rate applies to company profits across Great Britain.
title: United Kingdom corporation tax

text: The Divergent franchise began with Divergent in 2014, followed by The Divergent Series: Insurgent in 2015 and The Divergent Series: Allegiant in 2016, together earning more than $765 million worldwide. Although a fourth installment titled The Divergent Series: Ascendant was planned, it was never made because Allegiant performed poorly at the box office.
title: The Divergent Series

text: In *Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie*, the Rangers come back equipped with their new animal-themed Ninja Zords. Using these animal-themed Ninja Zords, they are able to destroy one of Ivan’s Ecto‑Morphicons and continue the battle against the remaining threat.
title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie

text: According to the Indian High Courts Act of 1861, the President of India determines the number of judges that may serve in each High Court, alongside the Chief Justice.
title: Indian High Courts Act 1861

text: Human fertilization is the joining of a human egg with a sperm cell, an event that normally occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube. This union produces a zygote, also referred to as a fertilized egg, thereby initiating prenatal development. The dynamics of fertilization in humans were first described by scientists during the nineteenth century.
title: Human fertilization

text: Human fertilization involves the fusion of a sperm cell with an ovum. In the typical sequence, copulation is followed by ejaculation, then ovulation, after which a sperm encounters the secondary oocyte. The sperm’s acrosome releases enzymes that enable it to bore through the egg’s outer jelly coat; subsequently the sperm plasma membrane merges with the egg’s plasma membrane, the sperm head detaches from its flagellum, and the resulting zygote travels down the Fallopian tube toward the uterus. Various alternatives—such as artificial insemination, in‑vitro fertilization, external ejaculation without copulation, or copulation shortly after ovulation—can also lead to fertilization.
title: Human fertilization

text: The earliest recorded use of tool‑mark analysis to connect a projectile with a particular mold dates to 1835. In that year a Bow Street Runner in London examined a bullet recovered from a murder victim and matched the markings on it to a mold discovered in a suspect’s home, showing that the suspect had produced the bullet. Further items found at the suspect’s residence confirmed his involvement, and he was subsequently convicted.
title: Forensic firearm examination

text: Roger Federer captured the Australian Open men’s singles championship, successfully defending his title by defeating Marin Čilić in the final 6–2, 6–7 (5–7), 6–3, 3–6, 6–1. The victory marked his record‑tying sixth Australian Open men’s singles crown.
title: 2018 Australian Open – Men's Singles

text: During the 12th century, beds started to become widely popular in both France and Germany.  Luxury furniture expanded at this time, and wooden bedsteads were produced with elaborate inlaid, carved and painted ornamentation.  Folding beds were also used, serving as daytime couches with silk‑covered cushions on leather, while at night a linen sheet, pillows and silk‑covered skins were added.  The period’s manuscripts show increasingly rich designs, including embroidered coverlets, curtains hung above the bed and small hanging lamps, all reflecting the growing prominence of the bed in medieval domestic life.
title: Bed

text: "The Glory of Love," a song that became a number‑one pop hit after Benny Goodman recorded it in 1936, was written by Billy Hill. The tune later enjoyed renewed success when the R&B group The Five Keys released their version in 1951, topping the R&B chart for four non‑consecutive weeks and reportedly selling a million copies, although original pressings are now scarce.
title: The Glory of Love (song)

text: The scientific work titled *On the Origin of Species*—fully known as *On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life*—was published on 24 November 1859. It was authored by Charles Darwin, whose research and observations from the 1830s Beagle expedition, along with later correspondence and experiments, formed the basis for the book’s argument that populations evolve over generations through natural selection. This publication is widely regarded as the cornerstone of evolutionary biology.
title: On the Origin of Species

text: “Rip It Up” was released in 1983 as a single by the Scottish post‑punk band Orange Juice. It served as the second single taken from their 1982 album of the same title and became the group’s only UK Top 40 hit, climbing to No. 8 on the chart. The track marked a shift from the band’s earlier material, featuring Chic‑style guitar work and a synthesiser‑driven, disco‑leaning sound.
title: Rip It Up (Orange Juice song)

text: Maryse Ouellet and her husband, The Miz, are slated to lead their own reality television series titled Miz & Mrs., which is scheduled to premiere in 2018.
title: Maryse Ouellet

text: In 2018, Maryse Ouellet and her husband, professional wrestler The Miz, launched the reality‑television series titled **Miz & Mrs.**.
title: Maryse Ouellet

text: The language family called the Uralic languages comprises roughly 38 languages spoken by around 25 million people, mainly in Northern Eurasia. Its most widely spoken members are Finnish and Hungarian, both official languages of their respective countries (Finland and Hungary) and recognized within the European Union. Other Uralic languages with significant speaker numbers include Estonian, Erzya, Moksha, Mari, Udmurt, and Komi.
title: Uralic languages

text: The theory of unbalanced economic growth is generally associated with Hirschman. He offered a comprehensive theoretical formulation of this strategy. In less‑developed nations, typical features include very low GNI per capita and sluggish growth of GNI per capita, pronounced income inequality and widespread poverty, limited productivity, heavy reliance on agriculture, an under‑developed industrial base, a high share of consumption relative to savings, rapid population growth and large dependency burdens, elevated unemployment and underemployment, technological lag, and a dual economy that contains both traditional and modern sectors. These conditions often result in scarce resources and inadequate infrastructure, making it difficult to mobilize investors and entrepreneurs and to channel cash flows into the various sectors needed for balanced economic development.
title: Strategy of unbalanced growth

text: The word “spirit” used to describe alcoholic drinks originates in Middle Eastern alchemy. In those early alchemical experiments the practitioners were chiefly concerned with creating medicinal elixirs rather than attempting to turn lead into gold. When they distilled fermented material, the vapor that rose and was then condensed was labeled the spirit of the original substance.
title: Distilled beverage

text: Disney's Art of Animation Resort— the first new property added to the Disney Vacation Club complex in over seven years and the fifth value‑priced resort joining All‑Star Sports, All‑Star Music, All‑Star Movies, and Pop Century—opened its family suites on May 31, 2012, with the standard rooms becoming available later on September 15, 2012.
title: Disney's Art of Animation Resort

text: The small intestine is the segment of the gastrointestinal tract that lies between the stomach and the large intestine, and it is the location where most nutrients are absorbed. It consists of three regions—the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum. The duodenum, the shortest portion, begins the absorption process and receives bile and pancreatic juice via the pancreatic duct, regulated by the sphincter of Oddi. Throughout the small intestine, finger‑like villi increase surface area to facilitate the uptake of nutrients and minerals from digested food.
title: Small intestine

text: Primary ossification centers are the first regions of a bone where ossification begins. These centers typically emerge during prenatal development, forming in the central portion of each growing bone. In long bones, the primary center is located in the diaphysis (shaft), whereas in irregular bones it is usually situated within the body of the bone. Most bones possess a single primary center—such as all long bones—though certain irregular bones like the os coxa (hip) and vertebrae may have several.
title: Ossification center

text: In the sequel, Kevin’s family plans a vacation to Florida. While they board a flight bound for the Sunshine State, Kevin mistakenly ends up on a different aircraft that lands in New York City, setting the stage for his new adventure.
title: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York

text: The eighth season, announced by HBO in July 2016, is the concluding chapter of the fantasy drama series Game of Thrones. Unlike the earlier installments, this final season contains only six episodes and adapts material that George R. R. Martin has shared with the showrunners for his upcoming novels.
title: Game of Thrones (season 8)

text: The Vikram Samvat, also known by its abbreviations V.S. or B.S., is a historic Hindu calendar that originated in the Indian subcontinent and is observed in both India and Nepal. It follows a system of lunar months combined with a solar sidereal year. Importantly, it is used as the official calendar in Nepal.
title: Vikram Samvat

text: In 1901 CE the Rana rulers of Nepal declared the Vikram Samvat to be the official Hindu calendar of the country, starting with Samvat 1958. As a result, Nepal’s new year commences on the first day of the month of Baishakh, which usually occurs in April–May of the Gregorian calendar, and the occasion is celebrated with the historic Bisket Jatra carnival in Bhaktapur. From 2007 onward, Nepal also recognizes Nepal Sambat as its national calendar.
title: Vikram Samvat

text: During the 49th Academy Awards ceremony, the Academy presented the Best Picture Oscar to the movie Rocky.
title: 49th Academy Awards

text: Dollree Mapp, an employee of the illegal gambling operations run by Cleveland racketeer Shon Birns, became the central figure in the incident that gave rise to the Mapp v. Ohio case. On May 23, 1957, Cleveland police received an anonymous telephone tip that a numbers operator named Virgil Ogletree—wanted for questioning in a recent bombing—might be staying at Mapp’s residence, along with betting slips and equipment used in the “California Gold” numbers racket organized by her boyfriend, Edward Keeling. When three officers arrived at the house and asked to come inside, Mapp consulted her lawyer by phone and refused entry without a search warrant. Two officers left, while the third remained outside to monitor the property.
title: Mapp v. Ohio

text: In the 2017 film *Wonder Woman*, the villainous Doctor Poison—originally the Princess Maru incarnation—makes her cinematic debut, portrayed by Spanish actress Elena Anaya.
title: Doctor Poison

text: Elton John’s ballad “Sacrifice,” for which Bernie Taupin supplied the lyrics and John composed the music, appears on his 1989 album Sleeping with the Past. The song was initially issued in October 1989, then re‑released in 1990 as the second single from that record, and it went on to enjoy major chart success in France and the United Kingdom, becoming his first solo number‑one hit and staying at the top for five weeks.
title: Sacrifice (song)

text: In the mid‑1500s a large, exceptionally pure vein of solid graphite was uncovered near Grey Knotts in Borrowdale, Cumbria. Because chemistry was still rudimentary, the mineral was mistakenly identified as a form of lead and was given the Latin name plumbago (“lead ore”). This misidentification led to the enduring habit of calling the pencil’s black core “lead” in many languages, even though the material is actually graphite. Nevertheless, the black core of pencils never contained the element lead.
title: Pencil

text: Downton Abbey is a British period‑drama created by Julian Fellowes and produced by Carnival Films and Masterpiece. The series debuted on ITV in the United Kingdom on 26 September 2010 and later on PBS in the United States on 9 January 2011 as part of the Masterpiece Classic anthology. A total of six series were produced; the sixth aired in the autumn of 2015 in the UK and Ireland and reached U.S. audiences in January 2016. On 26 March 2015, the sixth series was confirmed to be the final series, with its concluding episode broadcast in the United Kingdom on 25 December 2015. Over the course of the programme, 52 episodes were shown across the six series.
title: List of Downton Abbey episodes

text: The portion of an enzyme that binds an allosteric regulator is called the regulatory site. This ligand‑binding region is separate from the active site, and when a modulator attaches to it the enzyme undergoes conformational changes that can either enhance or suppress its catalytic activity.
title: Regulatory site

text: The Democratic‑Republican Party fell apart after the disputed 1824 presidential election, when the party’s internal factions began to act as separate political groups. Supporters of John Quincy Adams, allied with Henry Clay, pushed for modernization, a national banking system, industrial growth, and federal funding for roads and other internal improvements—positions that the Old Republicans and the Jacksonian wing typically opposed. This split, rooted in the contested 1824 contest, marked the party’s ultimate fragmentation.
title: Democratic-Republican Party

text: The 1976 track “You’ll Never Find Another Love Like Mine,” written by Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff, was recorded by R&B vocalist Lou Rawls for his album *All Things in Time*. Rawls’ rendition became his breakout single, topping both the R&B and Easy Listening charts, reaching number four on the dance chart, and climbing to number two on the Billboard Hot 100—held off the summit for two weeks by the Bee Gees’ “You Should Be Dancing” and KC and the Sunshine Band’s “(Shake, Shake, Shake) Shake Your Booty.” This achievement marked the only occasion a Rawls record entered Billboard’s pop top ten and was the first major hit for Philadelphia International featuring the re‑formed MFSB lineup after several original members departed. Beginning in 1977, the song opened Rawls’ live performances.
title: You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine

text: Philippe Petit, a French high‑wire artist born on 13 August 1949, earned worldwide fame when he illegally walked a tightrope between the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City on the morning of 7 August 1974. He rigged a 200‑kilogram cable and used a custom‑made 8‑metre balancing pole to suspend himself roughly 400 metres (1,000 feet) above the ground, where he performed for 45 minutes, making eight passes along the wire. The following week he celebrated his 25th birthday, and the legal charges were later dismissed after he gave a free performance for children in Central Park.
title: Philippe Petit

text: Alan Shearer, who notched his 100th Premier League goal in the 1995–96 season, remains the competition’s all‑time leading scorer. He reached the century of goals in just 124 appearances—the fewest games required—and still holds the record for the most Premier League goals overall. The next quickest player to 100 goals was Harry Kane, who needed 141 matches.
title: List of Premier League players with 100 or more goals

text: Within the cell nucleus, transcription occurs, converting the DNA template into messenger RNA. Because transcription is the first stage of protein biosynthesis, the initial creation of the protein’s genetic blueprint takes place in the cell nucleus.
