The DNA, composed of two sugar‑phosphate helices held together by phosphodiester bonds, is unwound by the enzyme helicase, exposing a single‑strand template. RNA polymerase then reads this template from the 3′ end toward the 5′ end and synthesizes a complementary mRNA strand in the 5′‑to‑3′ direction. The completed mRNA molecule passes out of the nucleus through nuclear pores and proceeds to the cytoplasm for the next steps of protein production.
title: Protein biosynthesis

text: During the Second Great Awakening, revival meetings served as the period’s most effective means of evangelizing, drawing participants from across regional boundaries and helping the movement spread rapidly through Kentucky, Tennessee, and southern Ohio.
title: Second Great Awakening

text: Catch Me If You Can is an American biographical crime picture that debuted in 2002. The film was directed and co‑produced by Steven Spielberg, with a screenplay written by Jeff Nathanson. It dramatizes the early life of Frank Abagnale, who, before turning nineteen, carried out multimillion‑dollar scams by impersonating a Pan American pilot, a Georgia physician, and a Louisiana parish prosecutor. Leonardo DiCaprio and Tom Hanks headline the cast, supported by Christopher Walken, Martin Sheen, and Nathalie Baye.
title: Catch Me If You Can

text: Development on the film started in 1980, but progress stalled until the book’s rights were acquired in 1997. After several directors were considered, Spielberg took on the project and principal photography was conducted from February through May of 2002. The movie was finished and released in that year, 2002.
title: Catch Me If You Can

text: Catch Me If You Can began its production in January 2002, although the start of principal photography was later moved to February 7 in Los Angeles, California.
title: Catch Me If You Can

text: The Quebec Winter Carnival (Carnaval de Québec) is a pre‑Lenten celebration held each year in Quebec City. While the festivities were held intermittently from as early as 1894, they have been organized on an annual basis since 1955. In that inaugural year the festival introduced its official emblem—a mascot named **Bonhomme Carnaval**, which serves as the recognized symbol of the carnival.
title: Quebec Winter Carnival

text: The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, chartered in 1964, is situated in Nashville, Tennessee, and ranks among the world’s largest institutions devoted to preserving and interpreting American vernacular music. Its holdings constitute one of the most extensive musical collections globally.
title: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum

text: In the motion picture 8 Mile, the story and its characters are loosely on Eminem, mirroring the rapper’s own upbringing and his effort to launch a career in a hip‑hop world that is predominantly African‑American. The film follows the white protagonist B‑Rabbit, a stand‑in for Eminem, as he navigates this environment.
title: 8 Mile (film)

text: The Jamaican reggae group Inner Circle released the song “Bad Boys” in 1987; after a 1993 re‑release it climbed to the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100. That track is widely known for serving as the opening theme of the U.S. television series *Cops*.
title: Bad Boys (Inner Circle song)

text: Regina Spektor composed and performed the opening theme “You’ve Got Time” for Netflix’s series *Orange Is the New Black*, which debuted in July 2013. The song earned a nomination for Best Song Written for Visual Media at the 56th Annual Grammy Awards.
title: Regina Spektor

text: Regina Spektor wrote and recorded the song “You’ve Got Time,” which is used as the opening theme for Netflix’s series *Orange Is the New Black* that premiered in 2013. The show’s creator, Jenji Kohan, approached Spektor to create the opening number, and Spektor performed the theme tune.
title: Regina Spektor

text: The track “Lord Have Mercy on the Working Man” was written by Kostas. It was recorded by American country singer Travis Tritt and issued in August 1992 as the lead single from his third album, T‑R‑O‑U‑B‑L‑E. The song climbed to number 5 on Billboard’s Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, becoming Tritt’s tenth entry on that list.
title: Lord Have Mercy on the Working Man

text: In the United States, any act that Congress adopts and that is subsequently signed by the President—or, if the President vetoes it, passed again by Congress over that veto—is categorized as statutory law.
title: List of United States federal legislation

text: Although the United States Treasury formerly circulated banknotes larger than $100, those high‑denomination notes were withdrawn in 1969. In the present day, the Federal Reserve issues just seven denominations of U.S. currency—$1, $2, $5, $10, $20, $50, and $100—so the $100 bill is the largest bill currently in American money.
title: Large denominations of United States currency

text: Pseudounipolar neurons have their cell bodies situated in dorsal‑root ganglia. Their axons exit the ganglion and enter the dorsal root, where they bifurcate. The peripheral branch runs through the distal dorsal root, continuing into the spinal nerve and onward to skin, joints, and muscle.
title: Pseudounipolar neuron

text: On the November 19, 1999 broadcast of *Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?*, contestant Carpenter reached the final, million‑dollar question without having employed any of the standard lifelines. When he finally used the Phone‑A‑Friend option, he dialed his father not to ask for assistance but simply to inform him that he was about to win the top prize. After answering correctly, Carpenter became the program’s first millionaire, a victory that brought him nationwide attention and subsequent appearances on talk shows and later episodes of the game itself.
title: John Carpenter (game show contestant)

text: The Sahara, whose Arabic name translates to “the Great Desert,” is the largest hot desert and ranks as the third‑largest desert on Earth after Antarctica and the Arctic. Spanning roughly 9.2 million square kilometres—an area comparable to that of China or the United States—the desert’s name derives from the Arabic word ṣaḥra, meaning “desert.”
title: Sahara

text: In 1488 the Portuguese explorer Bartolomeu Dias captained the first European ship to navigate around the southern tip of Africa. By rounding the point now known as the Cape of Good Hope—originally named Cabo das Tormentas—his voyage marked the moment when a vessel following the western African coast shifted from a primarily southerly to an easterly course. This achievement was a key milestone in Portugal’s efforts to reach the Far East by sea.
title: Cape of Good Hope

text: Excavations at the prehistoric Burzahom settlement have uncovered roofing material made from birch, confirming that the houses there were topped with this tree species. The presence of birch in the building remains aligns with the site’s name—'Burzahom' means “birch” in Kashmiri—and demonstrates that the tree was utilized for roof construction during the Neolithic period.
title: Burzahom archaeological site

text: The classic kitchen brigade system was created by the French chef Georges Auguste Escoffier, who organized the kitchen into a hierarchical team that assigns specific duties to each member.
title: Brigade de cuisine

text: The track titled “For What It’s Worth (Stop, Hey What’s That Sound)” was written by Stephen Stills and recorded on December 5, 1966. It was issued as a single in January 1967, and the performance was delivered by Buffalo Springfield. The record reached number seven on the Billboard Hot 100 and later earned spots on Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Songs list and Acclaimed Music’s ranking for 1967.
title: For What It's Worth

text: John Ernest Crawford (born March 26, 1946) is an American actor, singer, and musician. At the age of twelve he gained fame by portraying Mark McCain—the son of Lucas McCain, played by Chuck Connors—in the ABC Western series *The Rifleman*, which aired from 1958 to 1963. Earlier, Crawford had appeared before a national audience as a Mouseketeer.
title: Johnny Crawford

text: Daren Maxwell Kagasoff (born September 16, 1987) is the American actor who portrayed Ricky Underwood on the ABC Family teen drama series *The Secret Life of the American Teenager*, which ran from 2008 to 2013.
title: Daren Kagasoff

text: Tim Russert assumed the role of moderator of Meet the Press on December 8, 1991. He continued in that capacity until his death on June 13, 2008, making him the longest‑serving moderator in the program’s history.
title: Meet the Press

text: The song “Where Have All the Flowers Gone?” originated as a modern folk‑style piece whose melody and initial three verses were composed by Pete Seeger in 1955 and appeared in Sing Out! magazine. Subsequent verses were later added in May 1960 by Joe Hickerson, extending the work into a circular form.
title: Where Have All the Flowers Gone?

text: One concrete example of an Atwood‑type arrangement in everyday life is an elevator that employs a counterweight. **An elevator with a counterbalance approximates an ideal Atwood machine and thereby relieves the driving motor from the load of holding the elevator cab — it must only counteract the net weight difference and the inertia of the two masses.** By pairing the cab with a counterweight, the motor need not support the full weight of the car, making the system function much like the classic two‑mass pulley experiment. This principle is also used in other transport devices such as funicular railways, ski lifts, and boat lifts, but the elevator counterweight system is the most direct real‑world application.
title: Atwood machine

text: The Tin Woodman, once an ordinary man named Nick Chopper, was transformed into a being of pure tin after his enchanted axe severed each of his limbs and the tinsmith Ku‑Kl​ip replaced them with metal prostheses. In the process Ku‑Kl​ip failed to give him a new heart, leaving the Tin Woodman without the capacity to love the woman he adored. Because of this loss, the Tin Woodman longs to obtain a heart so he can feel love again.
title: Tin Woodman

text: In L. Frank Baum’s *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz*, Dorothy Gale encounters the Tin Woodman when she and her friends free him from rust after a rainstorm in the forest. He accompanies Dorothy to the Emerald City because he hopes to receive a heart from the Wizard. This desire to obtain a heart drives the Tin Woodman’s participation in the adventure alongside the Scarecrow and the Cowardly Lion.
title: Tin Woodman

text: The Tin Woodman in *The Wizard of Oz* is noted for his longing to obtain a heart, a wish that stands in contrast to the Scarecrow’s yearning for brains. He openly admits that he possesses neither a heart nor a brain, yet his desire for a heart remains a central part of his character’s journey.
title: Tin Woodman

text: Rigor mortis is a critical factor in meat technology because the timing of its onset and its eventual resolution are among the elements that affect the tenderness of meat. If carcasses are chilled immediately after slaughter to roughly 15 °C (59 °F), a cold‑shortening reaction can take place, causing the muscle sarcomeres to contract to about one‑third of their original length.
title: Rigor mortis

text: Steve Miller Band’s song “The Joker” was released as part of their album The Joker, which came out in 1973. The track later reached the top of the US Billboard Hot 100 in early 1974.
title: The Joker (Steve Miller Band song)

text: In Yann Martel’s 2001 novel *Life of Pi*, the young protagonist Pi Patel endures a 227‑day ordeal after a shipwreck, stranded on a Pacific lifeboat together with a Bengal tiger named **Richard Parker**.
title: Life of Pi

text: The United States’ compulsory military service that supplied troops for the Vietnam conflict continued until the early 1970s, ending in 1973. During this era, the Selective Service System held lotteries—such as the one on December 1, 1969—to rank men born between 1944 and 1950 for possible induction, but the overall draft program was terminated in 1973.
title: Draft lottery (1969)

text: The final draft call was made on December 7, 1972, and the legal authority to conscript men ended on June 30, 1973, after which no further inductions were made.
title: Draft lottery (1969)

text: In the essay titled “Shooting an Elephant,” the English narrator is Orwell, who recounts being summoned to kill an aggressive elephant while he was serving as a police officer in Burma. Pressured by the expectations of the local people, he carries out the shooting despite his personal reservations, and the animal’s slow, painful death deepens his anguish. The work is widely read as a metaphor for British imperialism and expresses Orwell’s view that when a white man becomes a tyrant, he ultimately destroys his own freedom.
title: Shooting an Elephant

text: The United States two‑dollar bill ($2) is a current denomination of U.S. currency. The obverse of the note features the third President, Thomas Jefferson, while the reverse displays John Trumbull’s painting *The Declaration of Independence*. Prior to 1929, when the bill was issued in a large size, it appeared as a United States Note, National Bank Note, silver certificate, Treasury or “Coin” Note, and Federal Reserve Bank Note. After the 1929 reduction to the modern size, it was produced only as a United States Note until production ceased in 1966. Ten years later the bill was reissued as a Federal Reserve Note with a new reverse design. Because banks often retain the bill and demand is low, two‑dollar notes are seldom encountered in everyday circulation, a scarcity that has given rise to urban legends and occasional difficulties when trying to use the bill for purchases.
title: United States two-dollar bill

text: "It Ain't Me" is a 2017 single that pairs Norwegian DJ Kygo with American singer Selena Gomez. The track was issued on 17 February 2017 by Interscope Records, Sony and Ultra as the lead single from Kygo’s debut EP, *Stargazing*. Written by Kygo, Gomez, Andrew Watt, Brian Lee and Ali Tamposi and produced by Kygo, Watt, Ben Rice and Louis Bell, the song blends dance‑pop, electropop and tropical‑house elements. In the recording, Selena Gomez delivers the verses in a husky tone, while her chorus vocals are reduced to recurring syllables, set against an acoustic‑guitar‑driven arrangement that builds into a drop featuring piano, bass, synths, finger‑snap claps and pan‑flute melodies. The lyrics reminisce about a past relationship that was damaged by alcoholism and frequent partying.
title: It Ain't Me

text: Ford took part in the Boy Scouts of America and earned the organization’s highest honor, the Eagle Scout rank. He remains the sole Eagle Scout who has ever risen to the office of President of the United States.
title: Gerald Ford

text: Geoffrey Dyson Palmer, OBE (born 4 June 1927) is an English actor best known for playing Lionel Hardcastle in the long‑running TV sitcom *As Time Goes By* (1992–2005).
title: Geoffrey Palmer (actor)

text: The location where the optic nerves meet and partially cross the midline is known as the optic chiasm. This structure sits at the base of the brain, immediately beneath the hypothalamus, and functions as the crossing point for optic fibers in all vertebrate species.
title: Optic chiasm

text: In the Idaho setting of *Where the Red Fern Grows*, the boy named Billy is identified by the surname Colman. While heading home from his job in the Snake River Valley, Billy Colman watches a pack of dogs attack a stray coonhound. He takes the wounded dog inside, feeds it, allows it to recover, and then releases it, trusting that it will return to its home.
title: Where the Red Fern Grows

text: “Too Much Time on My Hands,” the second single taken from Styx’s 1981 triple‑platinum album *Paradise Theatre*, was both written and performed vocally by Tommy Shaw, who also delivers the lead‑guitar solo during the song’s bridge.
title: Too Much Time on My Hands

text: During the 2002 season that ended with the Buccaneers’ Super Bowl XXXVII victory, the team’s quarterback was Brad Johnson. That year the offense ranked 25th in the league in total yards (5,222), and Johnson earned a Pro Bowl nod after completing 281 of 451 attempts for 3,049 yards, 22 touchdowns and only six interceptions. Running back Michael Pittman led the rushing attack with 718 yards and also caught 59 passes for 477 yards. Fullback Mike Alstott contributed 548 rushing yards and five touchdowns, plus 35 receptions for 242 yards and two scores. Wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson topped the receiving list with 76 catches for 1,088 yards and five touchdowns, while Keenan McCardell added 61 receptions for 670 yards and six touchdowns.
title: Super Bowl XXXVII

text: In the spring of 1915, Field Marshal August von Mackensen led a combined German and Austro‑Hungarian force in the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive. The operation proved a highly successful and victorious campaign for the Central Powers against the Russian army on the Eastern Front.
title: Bulgaria during World War I

text: Because the Salton Sea’s water is extremely salty, only a few fish are able to survive in it. The introduced tilapia are the principal species that can tolerate the high salinity and pollution levels of the lake. Other freshwater fish are found in the rivers and canals that feed the sea, but they do not live in its waters.
title: Salton Sea

text: Southend Pier, a prominent landmark in Southend‑on‑Sea, extends 1.34 miles (2.16 km) into the Thames Estuary, which makes it the longest pier in the United Kingdom. The structure is recognised as a Grade II listed building.
title: Southend Pier

text: Cora ultimately chooses to honor her engagement and will wed the prince, Henry, instead of fleeing with Rumplestiltskin.
title: The Miller's Daughter (Once Upon a Time)

text: Robert Lee Griffin III (born February 12, 1990), nicknamed RG3 or RGIII, is an American football quarterback who is currently a free agent. He played college football at Baylor, where he won the 2011 Heisman Trophy, and was selected second overall by the Washington Redskins in the first round of the 2012 NFL Draft.
title: Robert Griffin III

text: “That Ain’t No Way to Go” is a country track co‑written and performed by the American duo Brooks & Dunn. Issued in March 1994 as the fifth and final single from their album *Hard Workin’ Man*, the song climbed to the top of Billboard’s Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart. The writing credits include Kix Brooks, Ronnie Dunn and Don Cook.
title: That Ain't No Way to Go

text: On his 1979 album *Joe’s Garage Act I*, Frank Zappa released the single “Joe’s Garage,” which follows the introductory track “The Central Scrutinizer” and launches the story of the titular garage. Although the single only reached the top‑20 in Norway and Sweden, it became one of Zappa’s most‑played songs on American FM radio at the time. From 1980 to 1988 Zappa performed “Joe’s Garage” in concert alongside the companion piece “Why Does it Hurt When I Pee?” on every tour after the single’s release. Consequently, Frank Zappa sang “Why Does it Hurt When I Pee?” during those live performances.
title: Joe's Garage (song)

text: The Panic! at the Disco track that portrays a wedding scene—featuring lines like “The poor groom’s bride is a whore”—is the song I Write Sins Not Tragedies. In response to that language, many U.S. radio stations asked for an edited version, swapping the word “whore” for a shhh sound and omitting “god” from “goddamn.” Nevertheless, several modern‑rock stations still play the original recording.
title: I Write Sins Not Tragedies

text: Panic! at the Disco’s track “I Write Sins Not Tragedies,” the band’s first single to be accompanied by a music video, portrays a bizarre, circus‑themed wedding in its visual narrative, featuring a performance by the Lucent Dossier Vaudeville Cirque.
title: I Write Sins Not Tragedies

text: The Panic! at the Disco track titled **I Write Sins Not Tragedies** portrays a wedding that quickly descends into disorder. In the video, the bride—acted by Jessie Preston—and the groom, Daniel Isaac McGuffey, stand at the altar ready to exchange vows. While the bride’s relatives appear formally attired, they are later shown to have fallen asleep, their eyelids painted with eyes. In contrast, the groom’s side consists of low‑brow entertainers and carnival performers who interrupt the ceremony. Brendon Urie, the band’s vocalist, appears as the ringmaster and narrator, repeatedly disrupting the proceedings. After a clash between the two families, the bride flees the church, pursued by a guest, and the ringmaster drags the bewildered groom outside by his tie as the bride is seen kissing the trailing guest. The groom looks shocked, and both he and Urie bow to the camera, with the ringmaster ultimately revealed to be the groom’s alter ego.
title: I Write Sins Not Tragedies

text: German verbs are divided into two main classes: weak verbs, which take a dental‑consonant ending, and strong verbs, which are distinguished by a vowel gradation (ablaut). Most verbs in each class follow regular patterns, though various subgroups and occasional anomalies occur, and the only completely irregular verb in the language is sein (to be). Textbooks for learners often treat all strong verbs as irregular, and the language contains **more than 200** strong verbs, even though there is a gradual tendency for strong verbs to become weak over time.
title: German verbs

text: The saying “Patience is a virtue” is traced to the fifth‑century epic poem "Psychomachia," which first recorded the expression.
title: Patience is a virtue

text: In the Storybrooke episode, Elsa’s aunt shows up as the Snow Queen. When Robin Hood, Marian and Roland stop at the local ice‑cream shop, the Snow Queen—portrayed by Elizabeth Mitchell—serves them a cone and quietly enchants it with a spell.
title: Rocky Road (Once Upon a Time)

text: In the novel *Eragon*, the young farmhand discovers that the mysterious stone he has found is in fact a dragon egg. When the creature hatches, he gives the dragon the name **Saphira**, and the two become inseparable companions as they flee their village and join the rebel Varden.
title: Eragon

text: Any location that falls on the production‑possibility frontier or anywhere to its left can be achieved with the resources and technology that are presently available; such points are described as attainable. In contrast, positions that lie to the right of the frontier are **unattainable**, because the existing stock of resources does not permit the economy to produce those combinations of goods. Points situated strictly left of the curve indicate inefficiency, since more of at least one good could be produced without reducing output of another. A point on the curve itself is efficient, meaning that increasing the output of one good would require decreasing the output of the other.
title: Production–possibility frontier

text: The 1700 Cascadia earthquake is the megathrust event that struck the Cascadia subduction zone on January 26, with scientists estimating its moment magnitude in the range of 8.7 to 9.2. The rupture involved the Juan de Fuca Plate, extending from mid‑Vancouver Island southward along the Pacific Northwest coast to northern California. About 1,000 km (620 mi) of fault broke, producing an average slip of roughly 20 m (66 ft).
title: 1700 Cascadia earthquake

text: After Mona Vanderwaal is exposed as the original “A,” she begins receiving visits from a mysterious figure called Red Coat, who proposes a partnership and together they assemble the “A‑Team.” Although the group later fragments, the role of the second “A” and the leader of the A‑Team is eventually disclosed: **CeCe Drake** is identified as the individual behind the Red Coat persona and the head of the new “A” operation.
title: A (Pretty Little Liars)

text: The phrase began to be widely employed in 1987, when the United Nations World Commission on Environment and Development—known as the Brundtland Commission—issued its landmark report *Our Common Future*. In that document the commission argued that development could be acceptable only if it was “sustainable development,” a concept intended to satisfy present needs without worsening environmental problems.
title: History of sustainability

text: Principal photography for *The Killing of a Sacred Deer* began on August 23, 2016 in Cincinnati, with early shooting taking place at The Christ Hospital. Additional scenes were captured in the city’s Hyde Park and Northside neighborhoods, while the school sequences were filmed at Roger Bacon High School.
title: The Killing of a Sacred Deer

text: In the story, Julie discovers a newspaper article that identifies Susie's father, **Ben Willis**, as the man they accidentally ran over. The article also reveals that Ben Willis had already killed David in retaliation for his daughter's death, making him the murderer they have been trying to evade. This realization drives Julie to the docks, where the events surrounding Ben Willis’s pursuit of the group unfold.
title: I Know What You Did Last Summer

text: Tessa Peake-Jones, an English actress born on 9 May 1957, portrayed the character Raquel in the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses, appearing in that role from December 1988 until the series ended in 2003.
title: Tessa Peake-Jones

text: The sacroiliac joint, also known as the SI joint, is the articulation between the sacrum and the ilium, one of the coxal bones of the pelvis. Strong ligaments bind the two bones, forming a robust, weight‑bearing synovial plane joint whose irregular elevations and depressions interlock the surfaces. Humans have a pair of these joints—one on the left and one on the right—and although they usually correspond, their exact morphology varies from person to person.
title: Sacroiliac joint

text: Among the music featured in *Red Dead Redemption* is the track “Far Away,” performed by José González. The song earned the Best Song in a Game honor at the Spike Video Game Awards and was later performed live on BBC Radio 1’s Zane Lowe show in June 2010, at Rockstar’s New York office in July 2010, and during the Spike awards ceremony in December 2010.
title: Music of Red Dead Redemption

text: In the United States, tomato purée is a processed food made mainly from tomatoes and may be sold plain or seasoned. It is set apart from tomato paste by its consistency as well as by its ingredient makeup; the purée is less thick than paste and generally contains fewer additives.
title: Tomato purée

text: In Indian state legislatures, the Legislative Council is led by a presiding officer called the Chairman. The Chairman, together with a Deputy Chairman, is elected from among the council’s members.
title: Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)

text: Dusty Springfield’s recording of “Son of a Preacher Man” was issued in late 1968, and it quickly became an international hit, climbing to No. 10 on the U.S. charts and No. 9 in the United Kingdom. The single was produced by Jerry Wexler, Tom Dowd, and Arif Mardin for Springfield’s first Atlantic Records album, Dusty in Memphis. It marked her final Top‑Ten appearance in the U.S. until her 1987 collaboration with the Pet Shop Boys on “What Have I Done to Deserve This?”
title: Son of a Preacher Man

text: The United Kingdom became a combatant in the Second World War in 1939; after Germany’s invasion of Poland on 1 September, Britain issued an ultimatum that was ignored and then formally declared war on Germany on 3 September, thereby entering the conflict.
title: British Empire in World War II

text: The Cornell note‑taking system, sometimes called the Cornell method or Cornell way, was created in the 1940s by Walter Pauk, who was an education professor at Cornell University. Pauk promoted the technique in his popular textbook *How to Study in College*.
title: Cornell Notes

text: In the opening of his letter Paul plainly states that it is addressed “to the churches of Galatia” (Galatians 1:2).  The exact setting of those congregations is contested: a minority of scholars interpret “Galatia” as an ethnic label for a Celtic people living in northern Asia Minor, whereas most view it as a geographic reference to the Roman province of central Asia Minor—an area settled by Celtic immigrants in the 270s BC that still bore Gaulish cultural and linguistic features in Paul’s day.  The Acts of the Apostles likewise records Paul traveling to the “region of Galatia and Phrygia,” which lies immediately west of that province.
title: Epistle to the Galatians

text: The 1995 Hindi romance Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge was filmed in a series of 5‑, 10‑ and 20‑day schedules between September 1994 and August 1995. Its cinematographer, Manmohan Singh, shot the iconic song “Tujhe Dekha To,” featuring Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol standing amid the mustard fields on the outskirts of Gurgaon, near Delhi.
title: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge

text: The White Witch’s residence in Narnia is a fortress known as her castle. When Edmund arrives there alone, he is met with a hostile reception from the White Witch after arriving at her castle, indicating that this is the place where she lives.
title: White Witch

text: Within Luke–Acts the author frames the narrative as a response to a theological dilemma concerning the spread of the Messiah beyond the Jewish people. The work functions as an apology for the Jesus movement, and most of the speeches and sermons recorded in Acts are directed to Jewish audiences, with Roman officials appearing only as neutral judges in disputes over Jewish law. By presenting Christians as a Jewish sect, the author seeks legal recognition while also highlighting the Jews' rejection of the promised Messiah.
title: Acts of the Apostles

text: The surname Gómez is derived from the personal name Gomes, which itself is a borrowing of the Visigothic term guma. In that language, guma means “man”. This same root appears in several Germanic languages—Old English guma, Middle English gome, High Old German gomo, Middle High German gome—and is cognate with the Latin word homo, all of which also denote “man”.
title: Gómez

text: The 1964 single “A Change Is Gonna Come” by Sam Cooke was issued on December 22, 1964, through RCA Victor. The recording was produced by Hugo & Luigi, and it was arranged and conducted by René Hall. It was released as the B‑side to “Shake.”
title: A Change Is Gonna Come

text: The track “Knockin’ on Heaven’s Door” was written and performed by Bob Dylan, created for the soundtrack of the 1973 movie *Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid*. It was issued as a single and climbed to No. 12 on the Billboard Hot 100. Dylan biographer Clinton Heylin has called the piece “an exercise in splendid simplicity,” and it has become one of Dylan’s most frequently covered songs from his post‑1960s catalog.
title: Knockin' on Heaven's Door

text: The annual Army–Navy football contest is now staged chiefly at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, the home stadium of the Philadelphia Eagles. Although the game has occasionally been moved to other neutral venues—such as the Rose Bowl, Giants Stadium (later MetLife Stadium), M&T Bank Stadium, and FedExField—its primary location remains Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia.
title: Army–Navy Game

text: Grey matter (also written as gray) is a principal component of the central nervous system. It is composed of neuronal cell bodies together with their dendritic processes, alongside glial cells, synapses and a network of capillaries. In contrast to white matter, which is dominated by long‑range myelinated axon tracts, grey matter contains a high density of cell bodies and relatively few myelinated fibers. In living tissue it appears as a light gray hue, the coloration being influenced by the blood vessels and neuronal cell bodies within it.
title: Grey matter

text: The story’s opening takes place in an unnamed village that, as revealed in the sequel *An Acceptable Time*, is situated in Connecticut. This setting is reflected in the description of the centuries‑old Murry farmhouse, which echoes both the Austin family series and Madeleine L’Engle’s own Connecticut home, Crosswicks.
title: A Wrinkle in Time

text: The outermost layer of human skin, the epidermis, contains no blood vessels. Cells in the deepest parts of this layer are nourished almost entirely by oxygen that diffuses from the surrounding air, with only a minimal contribution from capillaries that extend into the outer dermis. Consequently, the epidermis relies on diffusion rather than a direct blood supply for its metabolic needs.
title: Human skin

text: "Seven Nation Army," the song by the American rock duo the White Stripes, was issued as the lead single from their fourth studio album, *Elephant*, in March 2003, marking its release in that year.
title: Seven Nation Army

text: Students for a Democratic Society (SDS) emerged in early 1960 when the Student League for Industrial Democracy renamed itself. The group’s very first meeting was held that same year on the University of Michigan campus in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where Alan Haber was elected president.
title: Students for a Democratic Society

text: In January 2004, NASA successfully landed its twin Mars Exploration Rovers—Spirit (MER‑A) and Opportunity (MER‑B)—on the surface of Mars, marking the first time a rover was placed on the Red Planet. Both vehicles went on to exceed their mission objectives, providing key scientific findings such as definitive proof that liquid water once existed at their respective landing sites. Their solar panels were occasionally cleared by Martian dust devils and windstorms, extending their operational lifespans; Spirit remained active until 2010, when it ceased communications after becoming stuck in a sand dune.
title: Exploration of Mars

text: Nawab Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum asked the celebrated Pashtun religious figure Haji Sahib of Turangzai to set the foundation stone of Islamia College. Although Haji Sahib had been declared a proclaimed offender by the British for his anti‑colonial activities and was barred from entering British‑administered areas, the Nawab appealed to Sir George Roos‑Keppel. The British authorities consented to a one‑day entry for Haji Sahib, on the condition that he would return to tribal lands afterward. On the day of the ceremony Haji Sahib stayed overnight in the Pokh Mosque of Tehkal, was escorted by Sheikh Muhammad Ibrahim, and, while British officials including Sir Roos‑Keppel watched, he placed the foundation stone. Afterward he went back to Tehkal and then left the British‑controlled territory for the tribal region.
title: Islamia College University

text: The term **Acid rain** designates the deposition of acidic material that reaches the ground in wet forms—including rain, snow, sleet, fog, cloud water, and dew—as well as in dry form as particles and gases that can later combine with moisture. This mixture of acidic components results in precipitation that contains a high concentration of acids.
title: Acid rain

text: In the United States, the contributions of Filipino Americans are honored each October through Filipino American History Month. The Filipino American National Historical Society founded the observance in 1988, and it is especially prominent in California and Hawaii, where large Filipino American communities reside. Local organizations in those states often stage their own celebrations throughout the month.
title: Filipino American History Month

text: Kryptonite is a radioactive mineral that comes from the shattered remains of Krypton, the fictional planet that is Superman’s home world. The green variety of Kryptonite, which was first introduced in 1943 as a plot device, emits radiation that neutralizes Superman’s powers, inflicts pain and nausea, and can ultimately be fatal with prolonged exposure. Lead is the only known substance on Earth that can block Kryptonite radiation, and it is also the only material Superman cannot see through with his x‑ray vision. Over the years writers have added other colors—red, gold, blue, white and black—each producing its own distinct effects.
title: Superman

text: Principal photography for *I Am Number Four* began on May 17, 2010, employing twenty locations, all situated within the Pittsburgh metropolitan area. DreamWorks selected the region chiefly for the Pennsylvania Film Production Tax Credit, and the shoot was slated to run for roughly twelve to thirteen weeks.
title: I Am Number Four (film)

text: In human anatomy the combined area that includes the thoracic, mammary, abdominal, naval, and coxal regions is called the trunk.
title: List of human anatomical regions

text: In the world of Harry Potter, the Defence Against the Dark Arts (often abbreviated D.A.D.A.) is the class that trains pupils in defensive techniques against dark magic and dangerous creatures. Throughout the series the position changes each year, and by the seventh book—when Death‑Eaters have taken control of Hogwarts—the curriculum is even renamed simply “the Dark Arts.” During this final year, the class is taught by Amycus Carrow.
title: Magic in Harry Potter

text: In NCIS: Los Angeles the agent called G. Callen was originally named Grisha Alekandrovich Nikolaev, so the “G.” in his name stands for Grisha.
title: G. Callen

text: CLS, originally named Continuous Linked Settlement, is a U.S.‑based specialist financial institution that offers its members settlement services for transactions that arise in the foreign exchange market. By routing their FX trades through CLS, participants can lower the settlement risk that typically accompanies such trades, even though the foreign exchange market operates without a central exchange or clearing facility.
title: CLS Group

text: On May 6 1937 the German passenger airship LZ 129 Hindenburg was on a scheduled flight to Naval Air Station Lakehurst in Manchester Township, New Jersey, when it ignited while attempting to moor to the station’s mast. The vessel was carrying 97 people in total—36 passengers and 61 crew members.
title: Hindenburg disaster

text: Born in 1942 in the Gert Town neighborhood of New Orleans, Louisiana, Tami Lynn is an American soul vocalist. In 1971 she achieved a UK Singles Chart Top Ten placement with her recording of “I’m Gonna Run Away From You,” a song that she performed herself.
title: Tami Lynn

text: During production of the 2015 crime drama *Black Mass*, actress Dakota Johnson appears in the film as Lindsey Cyr, the longtime former girlfriend of Whitey Bulger.
title: Black Mass (film)

text: In the late 1930s, when theater owners were initially reluctant to allow snacks because they feared the noise would distract audiences, a change occurred. In 1938 a Midwestern cinema proprietor named **Glen W. Dickson** placed popcorn‑making machines in the foyers of his theatres. The move proved profitable, prompting other exhibitors to follow suit and establishing popcorn as a staple of movie‑going. During the Great Depression the snack was already cheap—selling for about five to ten cents per bag—and its popularity grew further during World War II when sugar rationing reduced candy consumption, leading Americans to eat roughly three times more popcorn than before.
title: Popcorn

text: After the Thermidorian Reaction, the French state was governed by the Directory, an executive council established in 1795 that struggled with financial instability, corruption accusations, and contested military ventures abroad. Burdened by these problems, the Directory’s authority came to an end in 1799 when a coup led by Napoleon Bonaparte toppled the government.
title: French Revolution

text: Touching Evil is a British television drama serial that premiered in 1997 on ITV, produced by United Productions for Anglia Television. Created by Paul Abbott and co‑written with Russell T. Davies for the first season, the series began with six hour‑long episodes and was followed by two sequel serials in 1998 and 1999. The entire three‑season run ended on 6 June 1999 after a total of 16 episodes.
title: Touching Evil

text: The 1957 country‑and‑western song “A White Sport Coat (and a Pink Carnation)” was both written and performed by Marty Robbins. It was recorded on January 25, 1957 and released by Columbia Records on March 4, 1957, with the session conducted and arranged by Ray Conniff.
title: A White Sport Coat

text: In 1954 the pioneering high‑level language FORTRAN was developed at IBM by a team led by John Backus. This breakthrough gave rise to the first operating system written in a high‑level language, which was also created at IBM.
title: History of programming languages

text: Matthew Lyn Lillard, an American actor born on January 24, 1970, is known for a variety of film roles, including his portrayal of Shaggy Rogers in the live‑action Scooby‑Doo productions. He appeared as Shaggy in the 2002 Scooby‑Doo film and its 2004 sequel, Scooby‑Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed.
title: Matthew Lillard

text: Real Madrid possess the record for the longest streak of Champions League (formerly European Cup) triumphs, having secured the trophy five times in succession from 1956 through 1960. This run of consecutive victories is unmatched by any other club.
title: List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League finals

text: A cashier’s check is issued by a bank, which draws the check on its own funds and signs it, thereby guaranteeing the payment.
title: Cashier's check

text: To obtain a cashier’s check, a person must request one from a bank; the institution then immediately debits the requested amount from the customer’s account and assumes responsibility for covering the check.
title: Cashier's check

text: The FaZe Clan began on YouTube in 2010, initially sharing Call of Duty trick‑shot videos. As the members’ personalities evolved, they shifted to vlogs and creative skits, and the group’s YouTubers—including FaZe Banks, FaZe Apex, FaZe Blaze, FaZe Rug, FaZe Adapt, FaZe Censor, and FaZe Rain—each now have over one million subscribers, with several ranging between three and five million. The official FaZe Clan channel itself has about 4.8 million subscribers, but FaZe Rug has the most subscribers of all the FaZe members, with roughly eight million followers.
title: FaZe Clan

text: Fluoride that enters the mouth from fluoridated water becomes incorporated into saliva and plaque fluid, where it can interact with the mineral phase of teeth. When the plaque pH stays above about 4.5, fluoride ions combine with dissolved hydroxyapatite to produce a fluorapatite‑like layer that rapidly covers the exposed tooth. This newly formed veneer is far more resistant to acid attack than the underlying hydroxyapatite and accumulates the greatest amount of fluoride in the tooth, being stored at the surface of the enamel.
title: Water fluoridation

text: In the early 1800s, California society was largely dominated by Spanish missionaries, ranchers, and troops. Their presence stretched along a chain of missions that ran from Loreto northward to just beyond today’s San Francisco Bay Area and reached inland roughly 25–50 miles (40–80 km) from each mission.
title: History of California before 1900

text: When the National Recovery Administration was established, its leadership was assigned to retired United States Army general and successful businessman Hugh S. Johnson, who became the agency’s first director. Johnson later earned Time magazine’s 1933 “Man of the Year” distinction and regarded the NRA as a nationwide crusade to restore employment and revitalize industry.
title: National Recovery Administration

text: The Paraguay River originates in the state of Mato Grosso in Brazil, where its headwaters arise, and after flowing roughly 2,621 km (1,629 mi) through Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay and Argentina it empties into the Paraná River just north of the Argentine cities of Corrientes and Resistencia.
title: Paraguay River

text: Although the International Olympic Committee does not mandate a specific language for the Olympic anthem, it has been performed in Greek. For example, at the 2008 Olympic opening and closing ceremonies in Beijing, China, the anthem was sung in Greek rather than the host nation’s official language, Mandarin.
title: Olympic Hymn

text: On 23 September 1779 the American squadron that included the Bonhomme Richard encountered the British Baltic Fleet—41 ships under the escort of HMS Serapis and the hired armed vessel Countess of Scarborough—**near Flamborough Head**. The two flagships, Bonhomme Richard and Serapis, then fought a fierce battle that lasted several hours, ultimately forcing the British captain to surrender.
title: USS Bonhomme Richard (1765)

text: Michael Moriarty, born on April 5, 1941, is an American‑Canadian stage and screen actor who also performs as a jazz musician. He won both an Emmy Award and a Golden Globe for his first television role as a Nazi SS officer in the 1978 miniseries *Holocaust*. From 1990 through 1994, Michael Moriarty played Executive Assistant District Attorney Benjamin Stone during the first four seasons of the television series *Law & Order*. His film work includes titles such as *Bang the Drum Slowly*, *Who’ll Stop the Rain*, *Q: The Winged Serpent*, *The Stuff*, *Pale Rider*, *Troll*, *Courage Under Fire*, and *Shiloh*.
title: Michael Moriarty

text: In the 1983 film **Return of the Jedi**, the story finally discloses that Princess Leia is not only Darth Vader’s daughter but also the twin sister of Luke Skywalker, confirming the siblings’ relationship.
title: Princess Leia

text: The University of Miami, a private, non‑sectarian research university situated in Coral Gables, Florida, reported that its total student body numbered 16,801 in the 2016 academic year. This enrollment figure encompasses students across its twelve colleges and schools, including the Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine, the on‑campus law school, and the Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science located on Virginia Key.
title: University of Miami

text: A concave mirror generates a real image only when the object lies farther from the mirror than its focal point; under these circumstances the image produced is inverted. As the object is moved nearer to the focal point, the image recedes toward infinity, and once the object crosses the focal point the image switches to a virtual one that is no longer inverted.
title: Real image

text: Beats Electronics introduced its inaugural self‑designed products in October 2012, launching the Beats Executive headphones together with the Beats Pill wireless speaker. This marked the company's first foray into wireless audio equipment.
title: Beats Electronics

text: The Crossing is an American science‑fiction thriller that premiered on ABC and CTV on April 2 2018, with its pilot episode made available online by ABC on March 20 2018. Production for the series was carried out in British Columbia, Canada.
title: The Crossing (TV series)

text: Cool Hand Luke is an American prison drama film released in 1967; it was directed by Stuart Rosenberg and stars Paul Newman in the title role, with George Kennedy delivering an Oscar‑winning performance.
title: Cool Hand Luke

text: Starting in 2015, the Hero World Challenge was scheduled to take place at the Albany development in the Bahamas, a venue arrangement set to last for a minimum of three years.
title: Hero World Challenge

text: By November 1971 the conflict seemed inevitable, and the Soviet Union is reported to have warned Pakistan that a war would be a “suicidal course for Pakistan’s unity.” Throughout that month, thousands of conservative Pakistani politicians staged marches in Lahore and across the country, urging Pakistan to crush India. In reaction, India began a massive buildup of its army on the western border, waiting until December when drier ground would aid operations and Himalayan passes would be snow‑bound, limiting any Chinese intervention. On 23 November, **President Yahya Khan** declared a state of emergency throughout Pakistan and told the nation to prepare for war.
title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971

text: The Romantic era is dated differently across regions and artistic fields, yet a frequently cited timeframe places it from 1780–1830. This range is often referenced as a concise summary of the period’s beginning and end, even though other scholars suggest slightly earlier or later dates depending on the medium or country.
title: Romanticism

text: Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian born on 8 October 1881 in Dumenza, Varese, is the thief who stole the Mona Lisa from the Louvre on 21 August 1911. He died on 8 October 1925 in Saint‑Maur‑des‑Fossés, France.
title: Vincenzo Peruggia

text: In the musical Fiddler on the Roof, the character Hodel performs the song “Far From the Home I Love.” While at the railway station she tells her father that her true home is wherever her beloved is, even though she will always cherish her family.
title: Fiddler on the Roof

text: “Billy Don’t Be a Hero” is a pop song that debuted in 1974. It first became a hit in the United Kingdom for Paper Lace and, a few months later, achieved success in the United States with Bo Donaldson and The Heywoods. The track was written and composed by British songwriters Mitch Murray and Peter Callander.
title: Billy Don't Be a Hero

text: Since FTP does not incorporate encryption, every piece of data it sends—usernames, passwords, commands, and file contents—is transmitted in clear text; in other words, **all transmissions** can be read by anyone who captures the network packets.
title: File Transfer Protocol

text: According to the Srimad Bhagavatam, the divine couple Krishna and Rukmini are said to have a son called Pradyumna. This character is regarded as an incarnation of Kamadeva, the god of love, and is listed among the four vyuha avatars of Vishnu.
title: Pradyumna

text: "I Wanna Be the Only One" is a track by the British R&B girl group Eternal, issued as the third single from their album *Before the Rain*. The song topped the UK Singles Chart and features a guest vocal from BeBe Winans, representing the trio’s third partnership with him following his work on the 1994 single “Crazy” and the 1995 single “It Will Never End.”
title: I Wanna Be the Only One

text: The term diastema (plural diastemata) denotes a space or gap that can occur between two teeth, including the two front incisors. This feature is found in many mammalian species and is especially common in children, though it may also be present in adults. It usually arises from an imbalance between the size of the jaw and the teeth, and the pulling action of the labial frenulum can further separate the front teeth, creating a diastema.
title: Diastema

text: The CN Tower contains a metal staircase that extends all the way to the SkyPod, which sits 100 m (328 ft) above the main deck. Reaching this observation level requires climbing **2,579 steps**, the longest continuous metal stairway on the planet. These stairs are intended solely for emergency use and are normally closed to the public, opening only twice a year for charity stair‑climb events.
title: CN Tower

text: South Sudan’s admission process began with its approval for membership in March 2016, and the country finalized its entry by signing the accession treaty in April 2016. Following the signing, it was given a six‑month period to ratify the agreement, which it completed on 5 September, at which point South Sudan formally became a member of the East African Community.
title: East African Community

text: Since the 1979/80 season, all Test cricket has been played with six‑ball overs. Earlier in the game’s history Test overs were shorter—originally four balls each—and the number of balls per over varied in different countries, generally matching the standards used in other first‑class cricket at the time.
title: Over (cricket)

text: The House of Representatives elects the Speaker of the House at the opening of each new Congress and whenever an incumbent Speaker dies, resigns, or is removed. After the Clerk of the House solicits nominations—typically one from each major party—the Clerk calls the roll of the Representatives. Each Representative then states the surname of the candidate they support; members may also vote for someone who is not a House member or cast a “present” vote to abstain.
title: Speaker of the United States House of Representatives

text: In the series’ tenth season (1969‑1970), Steve Douglas takes a second wife. He marries Barbara Harper, a widowed schoolteacher who arrives with her five‑year‑old daughter, Dorothy “Dodie.” The role of Barbara Harper is portrayed by actress Beverly Garland.
title: My Three Sons

text: In Chinese mythology, dragons act as guardians of the Four Seas, with each of the four major Dragon Kings presiding over one of these seas.
title: Chinese dragon

text: Naz Khialvi, the Pakistani lyricist and radio broadcaster, wrote the Sufi verse titled “Tum Ek Gorakh Dhanda Ho.” In Urdu, the phrase “Gorakh Dhanda” is rendered in English as “You are a Puzzle.”
title: Naz Khialvi

text: John Hancock (January 23, 1737 – October 8, 1793) was an American merchant, statesman and leading Patriot of the Revolution. He presided over the Second Continental Congress and later served as the first and third Governor of Massachusetts. He is especially remembered for the unusually large and stylish signature he placed on the United States Declaration of Independence, a mark so famous that “John Hancock” has become a common U.S. term for one’s signature.
title: John Hancock

text: Two years after being released from Camp Green Lake, Theodore “Armpit” Johnson attempts to create a stable life in Austin, Texas, where he works digging deep holes and cares for his neighbor, ten‑year‑old Ginny McDonald, who has cerebral palsy. While employed at the mayor’s residence in that city, he is approached by his former Camp Green Lake friend Rex “X‑Ray” Washburn, who asks him to fund a ticket‑scalping scheme for an upcoming concert.
title: Small Steps (novel)

text: The season consisted of 20 episodes. Ten of those installments aired in the summer of 2016, with the other ten broadcast beginning in April 2017. The premiere premiered on June 21, 2016, on Freeform. Production and filming kicked off at the end of March 2016, a detail confirmed by showrunner I. Marlene King. The opening episode was written by King and directed by Ron Lagomarsino, and its title was disclosed on King’s Twitter account on March 17, 2016. On August 29, 2016, it was announced that this would be the series’ final season.
title: Pretty Little Liars (season 7)

text: The Geographic South Pole lies on the continent of Antarctica. It rests atop a flat, barren, windswept ice plateau at an elevation of 2,835 m (9,301 ft) above sea level and is situated roughly 1,300 km (800 mi) inland from the nearest open water at the Bay of Whales. The ice sheet at the pole is estimated to be about 2,700 m (9,000 ft) thick, meaning the land beneath the ice is essentially at sea level.
title: South Pole

text: Before 1948, the territories that would later become North and South Vietnam were still under French control. France created a semi‑independent State of Vietnam within the French Union, showing that the region remained a part of France at that time.
title: History of Vietnam since 1945

text: Walmart, formally known as Wal‑Mart Stores, Inc. and doing business as Walmart, is an American multinational retail corporation that operates a vast chain of hypermarkets, discount department stores and grocery outlets. The company is headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas; it was founded by Sam Walton in 1962 and incorporated on 31 October 1969. In addition to its core stores, Walmart owns and runs Sam’s Club warehouse clubs. As of 31 October 2017, the corporation had 11,703 stores and clubs in 28 countries, marketed under 59 different names, including Walmart in the United States and Canada, Walmart de México y Centroamérica in Mexico and Central America, Asda in the United Kingdom, the Seiyu Group in Japan, and Best Price in India, with wholly owned operations in Argentina, Chile, Brazil and Canada.
title: Walmart

text: The Miami Marlins hold their spring training each year at Roger Dean Stadium, one of only two venues in Florida that host two Major League Baseball teams for spring‑training activities. In this complex the Marlins share the main field with the St. Louis Cardinals, while each club uses its own practice fields, outdoor batting cages, multiple pitching mounds, and modern conditioning facilities.
title: Roger Dean Stadium

text: The phrase “social justice” was not employed as a distinct term until the mid‑nineteenth century; it entered explicit usage in the 1840s, a period during which Jesuit priest Luigi Taparelli is generally credited with coining the expression.
title: Social justice

text: The specific expression “social justice” first appears in modern discourse in the 1840s, when Catholic scholars such as the Jesuit Luigi Taparelli introduced it in articles for *Civiltà Cattolica* based on the philosophy of St. Thomas Aquinas. Their usage marked the earliest known application of the term.
title: Social justice

text: The National Anthem was initially codified in 1932 without any prescribed behavior. A later amendment, effective on June 22, 1942, stipulated that people who were not in uniform must stand at attention—men removing their hats—while the anthem was performed, and that those in uniform were to salute.
title: The Star-Spangled Banner

text: Dolley Madison popularized the office of First Lady by championing causes such as aid for orphans and women, presenting herself in elegant attire that drew newspaper attention, and, most famously, risking her own safety to rescue iconic national treasures during the War of 1812. Through these actions she established the standard for the role, a model that guided nearly every First Lady until the 1930s.
title: First Lady of the United States

text: In Middle‑Eastern cooking, the traditional fats include butter and its clarified counterpart, which is called smen. Olive oil is also widely used in coastal Mediterranean areas, while religious practices influence the choice of fat during specific observances.
title: Middle-Eastern cuisine

text: Phosphorus pentoxide, a white crystalline solid, is the chemical compound whose molecular formula is P₄O₁₀ (its common name comes from the empirical formula P₂O₅). It serves as the anhydride of phosphoric acid and is widely used as a strong desiccant and dehydrating agent.
title: Phosphorus pentoxide

text: The Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park is owned by the Cornett family, who have been carrying out upgrades to boost its entertainment, hiking, canoeing, camping and other recreational offerings. The park provides a range of camping choices, from primitive sites and RV spots to furnished park‑model units, and even features a tree house that can be used for special occasions and events.
title: Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park

text: In the original version of *Return of the Jedi*, Sebastian Shaw appears in the film’s concluding scenes as the unmasked, redeemed Anakin Skywalker, revealing that the figure hidden beneath Darth Vader’s mask is indeed Anakin Skywalker.
title: Sebastian Shaw (actor)

text: In the emotional climax of *Return of the Jedi*, the scene in which Luke Skywalker removes the helmet reveals the man beneath Darth Vader’s mask: Anakin Skywalker, shown as the redeemed, unmasked and dying figure.
title: Sebastian Shaw (actor)

text: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, the debut fantasy novel by British author J. K. Rowling and the first installment of the Harry Potter series, was initially released by Bloomsbury in 1997.
title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

text: Jimmy Flynn, who uses the professional name James P. Flynn, appeared in many films shot in the New England area. James P. Flynn was cast as the judge in the Boston‑set movie Good Will Hunting (1997). He later acted in The Cider House Rules (1999) and in What’s the Worst That Could Happen? (2001). In 2008 he worked as a truck driver for movie‑production equipment during the filming of My Best Friend’s Girl. Boston actor Tom Kemp remarked that “The Departed wouldn’t be a Boston movie without me, a Wahlberg, and Jimmy Flynn from the teamsters.”
title: Jimmy Flynn

text: The first session of the Assam Association, convened in 1905, took place in Guwahati.
title: Tarun Ram Phukan

text: Accounts receivable represent a legally enforceable claim that a business holds for payment of goods supplied or services performed when customers have not yet paid. The information that creates each receivable normally originates from the invoices a company generates and sends to its clients, specifying the amounts due and the payment terms. These invoice‑based claims appear on the balance sheet as an asset and are part of the broader set of billing transactions that record what customers owe for ordered products or services.
title: Accounts receivable

text: When the First World War erupts, Fawcett travels to France to fight. In the brutal fighting at the Somme, Manley is killed in the trenches, and Fawcett later endures a brief period of blindness after a chlorine‑gas attack.
title: The Lost City of Z (film)

text: Hydrogen peroxide is produced inside the body as a fleeting by‑product of normal biochemical reactions. The antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase, which converts superoxide radicals into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide, is found in nearly all living cells; the peroxide that forms is then swiftly broken down by catalase into water and oxygen.
title: Hydrogen peroxide

text: The Data Protection Act 1998 (c 29) is legislation enacted by the United Kingdom Parliament to safeguard personal information that is kept on computers or within an organised paper filing system. It implements the EU Data Protection Directive of 1995, giving individuals legal rights to control data about themselves, while obliging anyone who holds personal data for non‑domestic purposes to comply with its provisions, subject to certain exemptions. The Act also sets out eight data‑protection principles to ensure that information is processed lawfully.
title: Data Protection Act 1998

text: The country song “Every Light in the House,” written by Kent Robbins, was recorded by Trace Adkins. It was issued in August 1996 as the second single from his debut album *Dreamin’ Out Loud* and became his first Top‑5 entry on the Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, peaking at number 3.
title: Every Light in the House

text: Lowe’s, whose Canadian headquarters are in Toronto, Ontario, launched its first three Canadian outlets on December 10 2007 in Hamilton, Brampton and Brantford. The following February it opened three additional stores in Toronto, East Gwillimbury, a second Brampton site and a new location in Maple (Vaughan). Since then the chain has continued building stores, bringing the Ontario count to 19, and has moved westward with locations in Calgary, Alberta, as well as stores in British Columbia, Manitoba and Saskatchewan. To date (2018) Lowe’s has **62** locations in Canada.
title: Lowe's

text: Mathematician John von Neumann distributed the paper titled *First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC* on June 30, 1945. In that document he described the architecture of a stored‑program computer, outlining the essential components that would later be recognized as the central processing unit. This design allowed programs to be kept in high‑speed memory rather than being hard‑wired, establishing the fundamental concept of the CPU.
title: Central processing unit

text: Saint Alphonsa, born Anna Muttathupadathu on 19 August 1910 and deceased on 28 July 1946, was an Indian religious sister and educator. Saint Alphonsa was the first Indian woman to be canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church, and she also became the first canonized saint of the Syro‑Malabar Catholic Church, an Eastern Catholic Church based in India. Her feast day is observed on 28 July.
title: Saint Alphonsa

text: The harp has long served as Ireland’s heraldic emblem.  In the 13th‑century French Wijnbergen Roll—one of the oldest medieval rolls of arms— the entry for the King of Ireland reads “D’azure a la harpe d’or” (blue with a golden harp), explicitly identifying the harp as the arms of Ireland.  This rare heraldic charge, linked historically to King David, appears only twice among the early rolls, underscoring its special association with Irish royalty and, ultimately, with the nation itself.
title: Coat of arms of Ireland

text: Keeley Clare Julia Hawes, the English actress born on 10 February 1976, portrays Detective Inspector Lindsay Denton in the second and third series of the television drama *Line of Duty* (2014–2016).
title: Keeley Hawes

text: Tyler Perry has announced that the film *A Madea Family Funeral* was released in 2018, introducing a new brother for Madea named Heathrow, who is also portrayed by Perry and is a Vietnam‑war veteran.
title: Madea

text: In September 19 and October 7 1777, the Battles of Saratoga represented the climax of the Saratoga campaign. The two engagements ended in a decisive victory for the Americans over the British in the American Revolutionary War. British General John Burgoyne had moved a large invasion army southward from Canada through the Champlain Valley, hoping to join forces with other British columns that never arrived, and he was ultimately surrounded by American forces in upstate New York. His attempts to break out in two small battles on the same ground, nine miles (14 km) south of Saratoga, New York, failed.
title: Battles of Saratoga

text: After finishing Chilton as valedictorian with a 4.2 GPA, Rory Gilmore enrolls at Yale University—her grandfather’s alma mater—beginning in season four. She lives in Durfee Hall during her freshman year, sharing a room with fellow Chilton graduate Paris Geller, among others. At the start of her sophomore year, both Rory and Paris move into Branford College, the same residential college where their grandfather once lived, and continue their studies there.
title: Rory Gilmore

text: The inaugural Indianapolis 500 was contested in 1911, and the race was won by Ray Harroun, who piloted the Marmon Wasp to victory.
title: List of Indianapolis 500 winners

text: In the tenth season of *Criminal Minds*, Jason Gideon is killed in the episode titled **"Nelson's Sparrow"**. In this installment, Gideon’s death occurs off‑screen when he is shot at close range by the serial killer Donnie Mallick (Arye Gross), prompting the BAU team to launch an investigation into his murder. The episode also features flashbacks to a younger Gideon working at the BAU in 1978, a role played by Ben Savage.
title: Jason Gideon

text: The spirit carries Scrooge through the bustling streets, revealing both celebrations and hardship, and as they move he scatters a little warmth from his torch. During the journey they encounter Scrooge’s nephew and the modest home of his clerk, Bob Cratchit, whose ailing son Tiny Tim draws Scrooge’s concern. The Ghost warns that, if the present conditions persist, the child will die, and he rebukes Scrooge’s earlier cruel remarks about the “surplus population,” urging him to reconsider his heartless outlook.
title: Ghost of Christmas Present

text: The Lupus Foundation of America, a national voluntary health organization headquartered in Washington, D.C., was established in 1977. It operates through a network of chapters, offices, and support groups across the United States, working to solve the mystery of lupus and to improve the quality of life for those affected through research, education, support, and advocacy.
title: Lupus Foundation of America

text: Kelly Reno, born on June 19 1966 in Pueblo, Colorado, is a former child actor. When she was eleven, she was chosen to portray Alec Ramsey—the young boy stranded on a deserted island with a horse—in the 1977 film *The Black Stallion*, which was adapted from Walter Farley’s novel.
title: Kelly Reno

text: Windows Media Player stores its native playlists in an XML‑based format whose file extension is Windows Playlist (WPL). This WPL extension is the default type the player uses for its own playlist files, in addition to supporting media formats such as WMV, WMA, and ASF.
title: Windows Media Player

text: Tom Stoppard’s absurdist, existentialist tragicomedy Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead—an expansion of the two minor courtiers from Shakespeare’s Hamlet—made its debut at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 1966. The play unfolds mainly “in the wings” of the original drama, interspersing brief appearances by Hamlet’s principal characters with the bewildered commentary of its two protagonists.
title: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead

text: In *A Madea Christmas*, Connor’s mother, Kim, appears alongside his father Buddy when the couple visits his home for the holidays. The role of Kim is performed by actress Kathy Najimy.
title: A Madea Christmas (film)

text: The novel *The Fault in Our Stars*, written by John Green and released in January 2012, follows the perspective of Hazel Grace Lancaster, a sixteen‑year‑old girl battling cancer. Pressured by her parents, Hazel attends a cancer support group, where she encounters and eventually falls for the seventeen‑year‑old Augustus Waters, an amputee and former basketball player. Their relationship develops into a romance, making Augustus Waters Hazel’s boyfriend in the story.
title: The Fault in Our Stars

text: On 10 June 1940, as the French government fled to Bordeaux amid the German invasion and proclaimed Paris an open city, Mussolini decided that the conflict would soon conclude and announced Italy’s entry into the war, declaring war on both Britain and France.
title: Military history of Italy during World War II

text: Michael Christopher McDowell (born December 21, 1984) is an American professional stock‑car racing driver who currently competes full‑time in the Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series, piloting the No. 95 Chevrolet SS for Leavine Family Racing.
title: Michael McDowell (racing driver)

text: Omar Khayyam (born 18 May 1048, died 4 December 1131) was a Persian scholar celebrated for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy and poetry. His lifetime places his death in the year 1131 CE, and his work earned him a reputation as a leading Islamic intellectual of his era.
title: Omar Khayyam

text: Scott Hudson arrives as a freshman at J.P. Zenger High, where he and his three best friends—Mitch, Patrick, and Kyle—discover that high school is a very different world from middle school. The school’s intimidating upperclassmen, the demanding honors and college‑prep classes, and the complex social scene all unfold on the J.P. Zenger High campus, providing the backdrop for Scott’s attempts to fit in, win the attention of his old kindergarten classmate Julia Baskins, and cope with the many challenges of his first year.
title: Sleeping Freshmen Never Lie

text: The song “How Do You Do It?” was written by songwriter Mitch Murray. He first offered the tune to Adam Faith and Brian Poole, both of whom turned it down. EMI producer George Martin later chose the piece for the Beatles, who recorded it in September 1962 but decided not to issue it as their debut single, preferring “Love Me Do.” The Beatles’ version eventually surfaced on the 1995 Anthology 1 compilation.
title: How Do You Do It?

text: Seattle Slew, the American Thoroughbred foaled on February 15, 1974, achieved the Triple Crown in 1977, becoming the tenth horse to do so. He remains the only Triple Crown winner who entered the series without any prior defeats. That same year he was honored as Horse of the Year and had already earned champion titles at ages two, three, and four. In the Blood‑Horse magazine’s list of the Top 100 U.S. Racehorses of the 20th Century, Seattle Slew was ranked ninth.
title: Seattle Slew

text: The 2014 Rose Bowl took place on January 1, 2014 at the Rose Bowl stadium in Pasadena, California. In this centennial edition of the game, the Big Ten champion Michigan State Spartans faced the Pac‑12 champion Stanford Cardinal, who entered as the defending Rose Bowl winners.
title: 2014 Rose Bowl

text: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles debuted in 1984, when Mirage Studios published the original comic book in Dover, New Hampshire. The creators self‑financed the first single‑issue release, intending it as a parody of several popular early‑1980s comics. Since that initial 1984 appearance, the TMNT series has been issued in multiple formats by various publishers.
title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles

text: In the season seven premiere, the team learns that Emily Prentiss is still alive. The episode shows Morgan capturing Doyle while Emily returns to the BAU to help locate the kidnapper of Doyle’s son. The discovery of Prentiss’s survival prompts a heated response from the judiciary panel, which had been pursuing disciplinary action for the team’s earlier retaliation. Section Chief Erin Strauss later explains that the panel, influenced by Prentiss’s defense, has decided to lift the suspensions, though the BAU will remain under close scrutiny. Reid, still upset by the presumed death, initially refuses to speak with her, but by the end of “Proof” they reconcile. Additionally, the premiere reveals that Garcia has been caring for Prentiss’s cat, Sergio, and jokes about needing visitation rights.
title: Emily Prentiss

text: The site where the English later established Jamestown was empty of permanent residents; the immediate area of the island was uninhabited when the colonists arrived. Shortly after landing on May 14, the newcomers faced attacks from nearby Paspahegh Indians, but the settlement itself had no native population living there beforehand.
title: History of Jamestown, Virginia (1607–99)

text: After Zedekiah’s revolt and his alliance with Pharaoh Hophra, the Babylonian monarch Nebuchadnezzar returned, defeated the Egyptian forces and laid siege to Jerusalem. In 587 BCE the siege concluded with the demolition of the city wall and the destruction of the First Temple, actions carried out by Nebuchadnezzar. He seized Zedekiah and his sons, put the sons to death before their father, blinded Zedekiah and led him, together with many other inhabitants, away to Babylon. Judah was then reorganized as the Babylonian province of Yehud, ending its independence and resulting in the exile of its people to Babylon.
title: Babylonian captivity

text: After smoking marijuana together and seeing a White Castle advertisement, Harold and Kumar decide to go get hamburgers. Their first stop is a former White Castle in New Brunswick, now operating as “Burger Shack.” While searching for a real White Castle, they discover that another White Castle is in Cherry Hill.
title: Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle

text: In the United Kingdom, the Child Benefit system was inaugurated in 1975 when the Child Benefit Bill—presented by Barbara Castle—established a universal payment for each child, marking the first occasion that a benefit was paid for the first child. This new scheme replaced the earlier family allowance and, like its predecessor, was not means‑tested.
title: Child benefits in the United Kingdom

text: When the command economies of Eastern Europe started shifting toward market‑based systems, the most immediate consequence was a rise in inequality of opportunity. In these transition economies, inequality of opportunity was noticeably higher than in many Western European developed economies, with the greatest levels observed in the Balkans and Central Asia.
title: Transition economy

text: Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory situated on the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, is the focus of an ongoing dispute between Spain and the United Kingdom. The territory was seized by British forces in 1704 during the War of the Spanish Succession and was formally ceded to the British Crown forever by the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713. Spain has repeatedly sought to reclaim it, launching sieges in 1727 and again from 1779 to 1783. Subsequent agreements, including the 1729 treaty signed in Seville and the 1783 Treaty of Paris, reaffirmed British sovereignty over Gibraltar.
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: Spain and the United Kingdom remain at odds over the status of Gibraltar. The Spanish position, first formalised under General Franco’s regime and continued by later democratic governments, seeks to reclaim the territory. In contrast, the inhabitants of Gibraltar reject any Spanish claim; no local party or pressure group advocates unification with Spain. A 2002 referendum saw the Gibraltarians vote against a joint‑sovereignty proposal that the two governments claimed to have reached broad agreement on. The British government has made clear that it will not enter into any sovereignty deal without the explicit consent of Gibraltar’s government and its people, and it now refuses to discuss the matter without that approval.
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: Britain’s Gibraltar Constitution Order 2006 created a governmental framework in which the Governor of Gibraltar oversees external affairs, defence, internal security and certain public‑office appointments, while the elected Government of Gibraltar handles all remaining matters. The United Kingdom argues that, as a United Nations‑recognised overseas territory, Gibraltar enjoys the individual and collective rights set out in that constitution, including the right of self‑determination. Spain, however, challenges the legality of the constitution and maintains that it does not alter Gibraltar’s status as a British colony, insisting that only the United Kingdom is authorised to discuss Gibraltar issues on the international stage. Consequently, Spain and the United Kingdom are in a dispute over Gibraltar.
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: Thomas Mundy Peterson (October 6, 1824 – February 4, 1904) of Perth Amboy, New Jersey became the first African‑American to register and cast a vote after the recently ratified 15th Amendment, doing so on March 31, 1870.
title: Thomas Mundy Peterson

text: David Akers tied the NFL’s longest‑field‑goal record by booting a 63‑yard kick on September 9, 2012, when he struck the ball off the crossbar against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
title: David Akers

text: John Calipari (born February 10, 1959) is an American basketball coach who has served as the head coach of the University of Kentucky men’s basketball team since 2009, leading the Wildcats to the NCAA Championship in 2012. He has been honored as Naismith College Coach of the Year three times (1996, 2008, and 2015) and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2015.
title: John Calipari

text: The dermis lies between the epidermis and the subcutaneous tissue, forming the deeper component of the cutis. Its most superficial portion, called the papillary region, is located adjacent to the epidermis, whereas the deeper, thicker portion is the reticular dermis.
title: Dermis

text: Real Madrid C.F. has achieved the greatest success in the European Cup, having lifted the trophy a total of twelve times, which remains a record. The club won the inaugural edition of the competition and is the only side to secure five consecutive titles in its first five seasons.
title: Real Madrid C.F. in international football competitions

text: The kudzu vine first entered the United States when it was imported from Japan for display at the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia in 1876.
