It later appeared in the Southeast at the 1883 New Orleans Exposition, after which it was marketed as an ornamental shade plant and subsequently used for erosion control and as high‑protein cattle fodder.
title: Kudzu in the United States

text: Actress Darlene Cates (born Rita Darlene Guthrie on December 13, 1947 and deceased March 26, 2017) is most noted for playing the title character’s housebound mother in the 1993 film What’s Eating Gilbert Grape.
title: Darlene Cates

text: The fourth season was commissioned as a double block of twenty episodes, divided into two ten‑episode segments; the second segment began airing on November 30, 2016.
title: Vikings (season 4)

text: When two or more players finish a Premier League season with the same highest goal total, the Golden Boot is not given to a single individual; instead the honour is awarded jointly. The award was therefore **shared** in the 1997‑98 and 1998‑99 campaigns, when three players each scored 18 goals, and again in 2010‑11 when Dimitar Berbatov and Carlos Tevez both netted 20 goals, resulting in a tie for the prize.
title: Premier League Golden Boot

text: In the movie *The Silence of the Lambs*, the antagonist is the character Buffalo Bill, a role famously portrayed by actor Ted Levine.
title: Ted Levine

text: Puente Hills Mall, a major regional shopping center in the City of Industry, California, was used as the filming location for the fictional Twin Pines (later renamed Lone Pine) Mall in the 1985 movie *Back to the Future* starring Michael J. Fox and Christopher Lloyd.
title: Puente Hills Mall

text:
Blood volume

In a typical adult human, the total amount of blood circulating in the body is approximately 5 liters. Generally, females possess a slightly lower blood volume than males, and the kidneys play a key role in regulating this volume.
title: Blood volume

text: In the musical episode, Sweet asks Buffy what she thinks about life, and Buffy replies with a bleak line that becomes the song **“Something to Sing About.”** When the rest of the Scooby gang arrives, Buffy confesses that Willow had taken her from heaven, delivering this revelation during the number “Something to Sing About.”
title: Once More, with Feeling (Buffy the Vampire Slayer)

text: The first Jnanpith Award was conferred in 1965 on G. Sankara Kurup, a poet who wrote in Malayalam, in recognition of his 1950 poetry collection *Odakkuzhal* (The Bamboo Flute). The honour at that time comprised a citation plaque, a cash prize of ₹1 lakh and a bronze replica of the goddess Saraswati.
title: Jnanpith Award

text: In the season seven premiere, it is revealed that JJ has returned to the Behavioral Analysis Unit after completing training to become a full‑time profiler, taking over the role that had previously been split between Hotch and Garcia as Media Liaison.
title: Jennifer Jareau

text: Gestalt psychology, also known as gestaltism, emerged as a philosophy of mind within the Berlin School of experimental psychology. It aims to uncover the laws that enable people to form and sustain meaningful perceptions in an apparently chaotic world. The core idea is that the mind automatically creates a global whole, driven by self‑organizing tendencies. Although the physiological mechanisms underlying Gestalt theory are poorly defined and lack strong empirical support, critics argue that the theory describes the end results of perception without explaining the processes that produce them. A 2016 special issue of *Vision Research* on Gestalt perception observed that, despite studying the same phenomena as early Gestaltists, contemporary work shows little theoretical coherence, suggesting that the original unified vision of experimental psychology has faded.
title: Gestalt psychology

text: Long John Silver tells Jim that he once served **in the Royal Navy**, and it was during that service—specifically under the “immortal Hawke”—that he lost his leg. His left leg was cut off near the hip, leaving him to rely on a crutch that he maneuvers with surprising dexterity.
title: Long John Silver

text: In the 2011 NBA Finals, the Western Conference champion Dallas Mavericks defeated the Eastern Conference champion Miami Heat, winning the series four games to two to secure the franchise’s first NBA championship.
title: 2011 NBA Finals

text: Sneaky Pete is an American crime‑drama series created by David Shore and Bryan Cranston. The show follows former inmate Marius Josipović, a role played by Giovanni Ribisi, who assumes the identity of his cell‑mate Pete Murphy in order to escape his troubled past. The ensemble also features Marin Ireland, Shane McRae, Libe Barer, Michael Drayer, Peter Gerety, and Margo Martindale. Its pilot aired on August 7, 2015, and a full series order followed in September. Shore left the production in early 2016 and was succeeded by Graham Yost, who served as executive producer and showrunner for the remaining nine episodes. The first season was released in its entirety on Amazon Video on January 13, 2017. Amazon announced a second‑season renewal on January 19, 2017, and that season premiered on March 9, 2018.
title: Sneaky Pete

text: Development of the Percy Jackson series began when Rick Riordan created a story about a boy traveling across the United States to retrieve Zeus’s lightning‑bolt. After his son Haley suggested turning that tale into a novel, Riordan wrote it over the next year, publishing it under the title **The Lightning Thief**. This book launched the Percy Jackson series.
title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians

text: In the Percy Jackson & the Olympians series, the opening novel is **The Lightning Thief**, which was first published on July 1, 2005.
title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians

text: “Only in My Dreams” is the debut single of American singer‑songwriter‑actress Debbie Gibson. The track was first issued as a maxi‑single on December 16, 1986 (Atlantic DM 86744) and later appeared in a remixed version in February 1987. Gibson wrote the song herself in 1984, two years before it was recorded. Produced by Fred Zarr and engineered by Don Feinberg for BiZarr Music, Inc., the dance‑pop recording was mixed by “Little” Louie Vega and mastered by Herb “Pump” Powers, eventually reaching number four on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in the summer of 1987. Douglas Breitbart served as executive producer for the release.
title: Only in My Dreams

text: Alabama, often called the Yellowhammer State and the “Heart of Dixie,” designates Montgomery as its capital city. The state’s largest population center is Birmingham, while Huntsville covers the greatest land area, and Mobile holds the distinction of being the oldest city, founded in 1702.
title: Alabama

text: The first reliable documentation of coffee being brewed and consumed dates to the 15th century, when Sufi monasteries in Yemen were already preparing the drink.
title: History of coffee

text: The first reliable documentation of coffee being prepared as a drink comes from the middle of the 15th century, when it was known within the Sufi monasteries of Yemen.
title: History of coffee

text: Tim Hortons first entered the United States in 1981, when the chain opened two locations in Deerfield Beach and Pompano Beach, Florida; those initial stores later proved unsuccessful and were closed.
title: Tim Hortons

text: The Spanish effort to subjugate the Inca Empire was spearheaded by the conquistador Francisco Pizarro. In 1532 he commanded roughly 180 Spanish soldiers together with native allies, and their forces seized the Sapa Inca Atahualpa during the Battle of Cajamarca. This initial victory set off a protracted series of campaigns that continued for decades, ultimately culminating in the Spanish conquest of the empire in 1572 and the establishment of the Viceroyalty of Peru.
title: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire

text: The opening theme used in the English‑language broadcast of the first season of the Pokémon television series was performed by American vocalist **Jason Paige**. Born on January 6, 1969, Paige is an actor, writer, record producer, and singer, but he is most widely recognized for providing that iconic Pokémon theme song.
title: Jason Paige

text: Sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka) are an anadromous Pacific salmon species that inhabit the Northern Pacific Ocean and the rivers that drain into it.
title: Sockeye salmon

text: In 1969, President Richard Nixon responded to the growing press corps at the White House by covering the indoor swimming pool—originally installed by the March of Dimes for Franklin D. Roosevelt—and converting the area into press offices and a lounge that could also serve as a briefing room.
title: James S. Brady Press Briefing Room

text: Before Islam reached the region, Persia’s prevailing faith was the Zoroastrian religion; the Arab conquest that terminated the Sasanian Empire in 651 later triggered its decline.
title: Muslim conquest of Persia

text: In a flat‑wick kerosene lamp the fuel is drawn from the tank into the wick by capillary action, which pulls the oil upward so that it can be vaporized and burned. The lamp consists of a fuel reservoir attached to a burner, and a glass chimney that protects the flame and creates a draft for clean combustion. The wick’s ability to lift the kerosene through capillary action is what enables the lamp to produce a steady, smokeless light.
title: Kerosene lamp

text: Proinsulin is converted into active insulin through a post translational modification that occurs only in the beta cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans. While passing through the Golgi apparatus, the precursor’s C‑peptide is removed by two endoproteases: the type‑I enzymes PC1 and PC3 sever the connection between the C‑peptide and the B chain, and the type‑II enzyme PC2 cleaves the bond linking the C‑peptide to the A chain. After this processing, the resulting mature insulin is stored as a Zn²⁺‑stabilized hexamer in secretory vesicles until it is secreted.
title: Proinsulin

text: The sweet flavor that we experience in fruit is caused by fructose, or fruit sugar, a simple ketonic monosaccharide that accumulates in the tissues of many plants. This sugar is commonly found in the flesh of tree and vine fruits, berries, flowers and even some root vegetables, where it contributes the characteristic sweetness. In nature it often occurs together with glucose, forming the disaccharide sucrose, but the individual fructose molecule itself is highly soluble and markedly sweet, making it the primary source of fruit’s sugary taste.
title: Fructose

text: Wonder Woman (2017) became available on Blu‑ray, Blu‑ray 3D, 4K Ultra‑HD Blu‑ray and DVD on September 19, 2017. The film had previously been released in Digital HD on August 29, 2017.
title: Wonder Woman (2017 film)

text: The Confederation Bridge (French: Pont de la Confédération) spans the Abegweit Passage of the Northumberland Strait, linking Prince Edward Island with mainland New Brunswick, Canada. Construction proceeded from October 1993 until May 1997, at a cost of C$1.3 billion, and the bridge was opened on 31 May 1997. The structure is 12.9-kilometre long.
title: Confederation Bridge

text: British‑American relations, commonly called Anglo‑American relations, have evolved through early conflicts and commercial rivalry into a close partnership. In fact, the two nations have acted as military allies from 1940 onward, establishing the so‑called “Special Relationship” and later cooperating as partners within NATO. Since 1940 the United Kingdom and the United States have maintained this enduring alliance.
title: United Kingdom–United States relations

text: The James Bond movie *The Man with the Golden Gun* uses a title song that was sung by Lulu. The piece was composed by John Barry with lyrics by Don Black. Although Alice Cooper had submitted his own track for the film, the producers ultimately chose Lulu’s recording as the official theme.
title: The Man with the Golden Gun (soundtrack)

text: The type I error rate, also known as the significance level and symbolized by the Greek letter α (alpha), represents the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true. In practice, researchers frequently set this significance level at 0.05, which means that the chance of incorrectly rejecting the null hypothesis is 5%.
title: Type I and type II errors

text: Loihi (also spelled Lōʻihi) is an active submarine volcano situated roughly 35 km (22 mi) southeast of the island of Hawaii. As the newest member of the Hawaiian‑Emperor seamount chain, it is a deep‑water preshield volcano that, like the other Hawaiian islands, was formed from the Hawaii hotspot.
title: Lōʻihi Seamount

text: Reconstruction of the temple was carried out by Herod, who launched a large‑scale enlargement of the Temple Mount while religious worship and temple rituals continued throughout the building work.
title: Second Temple

text: Nathan Hale (June 6, 1755 – September 22, 1776) served as a soldier and spy for the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War. He volunteered for an intelligence‑gathering mission in New York City, was captured by British forces, and was executed, making him a notable American who was put to death for espionage in that war.
title: Nathan Hale

text: “Suddenly,” the love‑theme track from the 1980 film Xanadu, appears on the movie’s soundtrack album. The recording is a duet, featuring Olivia Newton‑John together with Cliff Richard. The accompanying video shows the two singers performing the song from a penthouse setting.
title: Suddenly (Olivia Newton-John and Cliff Richard song)

text: The role of Command Sergeant Major of the Army passed to Daniel A. Dailey on 30 January 2015, when he took over the post from his predecessor, Raymond F. Chandler III.
title: Sergeant Major of the Army

title: The Windmills of Your Mind

title: Heaven (Los Lonely Boys song)

text: The Organ Mountains form a rugged range situated in southern New Mexico, part of the Southwestern United States. Designated as the Organ Mountains‑Desert Peaks National Monument on May 21 2014, the range lies about 10 miles (16 km) east of Las Cruces within Doña Ana County.
title: Organ Mountains (New Mexico)

text: Kate Warne (1833 – January 28, 1868) was hired by the Pinkerton Detective Agency in 1856, becoming the agency’s first female detective and the United States’ first woman to serve in that role.
title: Kate Warne

text: In mathematics and logical argumentation, a symbol formed by three dots arranged in an upright triangle is called the therefore sign. Represented by the character ∴, this sign is placed before a statement that follows as a logical consequence, such as the conclusion of a syllogism. It is encoded as U+2234 (HTML ∴) and can be entered in Microsoft Office by holding the ALT key and typing 8756. While it is not typical in formal prose, the therefore sign is common in mathematical shorthand and is paired with its counterpart, the because sign (∵).
title: Therefore sign

text: The World Economic Forum’s yearly meeting is convened each January in the Swiss mountain resort of Davos, situated in the Graubünden canton of the eastern Alps.
title: World Economic Forum

text: The World Economic Forum’s annual gathering was convened in Davos.
title: World Economic Forum

text: Gareth Barry became the all‑time leader in Premier League appearances when he took part in his 633rd match on 25 September 2017, a 2‑0 loss for West Bromwich Albion at Arsenal. This performance broke Ryan Giggs’ previous record of 632 appearances, which had stood since 14 May 2011. Prior to Giggs, the appearance record had been held by David James (572 matches) and before him by Gary Speed, the first player to reach 500 Premier League games.
title: List of Premier League players with 500 or more appearances

text: The IEEE 802.11a amendment specifies an OFDM‑based physical layer that works in the 5 GHz band while keeping the original 802.11 data‑link protocol and frame format. Its highest achievable net data rate is 54 Mbit/s, before the addition of error‑correction coding.
title: IEEE 802.11

text: A substitute good is a product that can be used instead of another. In economic analysis, such goods are seen as comparable by consumers, so that an increase in the quantity of one tends to lessen the desire for the other. Formally, when the price of good X rises, the demand for its substitute, good Y, goes up, reflecting the interchangeable nature of the two items.
title: Substitute good

title: Eric van der Woodsen

Davis—who was serving as pastor of New Birth Birmingham in Alabama—would become the senior pastor of New Birth Missionary Baptist Church in Lithonia, while continuing his leadership at the Birmingham church.

text: The film Proof of Life is primarily set in the Republic of Tecala, a fictional South American nation. This country has long been embroiled in an internal conflict between its government forces and the Liberation Army of Tecala (ELT), a guerrilla group that was once backed by the Soviet Union but turned to kidnapping for ransom after the USSR’s collapse in 1991. Although the map shown in the movie resembles Ecuador—featuring places such as Quito, the eastern jungle, and the Andean city of Baños de Agua Santa—the story’s location remains the Republic of Tecala.

text: G. Sankara Kurup (3 June 1901 – 2 February 1978), popularly known as Mahakavi G, was the inaugural recipient of India’s highest literary honour, the Jnanpith Award, when he received it in 1965 for his poetry collection *Odakkuzhal*. text: Cadbury, the British confectionery giant now wholly owned by Mondelez International, conducts its operations in more than 50 countries worldwide, distributing its well‑known chocolates and sweets across this extensive market.
title: Cadbury

title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961

text: My Country My Life is an autobiographical book by L. K. Advani. The former Deputy Prime Minister of India, who later served as Leader of the Opposition in the 15th Lok Sabha, saw the volume released on 19 March 2008 in a ceremony officiated by Abdul Kalam, the eleventh President of India. The memoir stretches across 1,040 pages, chronicling Advani’s personal journey and key episodes in Indian politics and history from the early 1900s onward. It swiftly became a bestseller in the non‑fiction category, with the publisher reporting sales of over one million copies.
title: My Country My Life

text: On 27 February 1844 the Dominican Republic secured its independence from Haiti, ending a 22‑year stretch during which the whole island of Hispaniola had been ruled by the Haitian government. Before that, the former Captaincy General of Santo Domingo had proclaimed the Republic of Spanish Haiti in 1821, only to be annexed by Haiti a year later.
title: Dominican War of Independence

text: “Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair” is a mid‑19th‑century parlor song that was written by Stephen Foster. The piece was issued by the New York publisher Firth, Pond & Co. in 1854, and Foster composed it while thinking of his estranged wife, Jane McDowell, with the lyrics hinting at a lasting separation.
title: Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair

text: The Bob & Tom Show was launched at **WFBQ in Indianapolis, Indiana** on March 7, 1983, when founders Bob Kevoian and Tom Griswold first aired the program on the local station before it entered national syndication.
title: The Bob & Tom Show

text: The frontal lobe enables people to anticipate the future consequences of their current actions, to weigh moral choices between good and bad (or better and best), to suppress socially inappropriate responses, and to judge similarities and differences among objects or events. These capabilities together support complex thinking.
title: Frontal lobe

text: The championship match of the 2015–16 UEFA Champions League was staged on 28 May 2016 at the San Siro in Milan. The final pitted two clubs from the same Spanish city—Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid—in a repeat of the 2014 showdown. After a 1‑1 stalemate persisted through regular time and extra time, the contest was settled by a penalty shoot‑out, with Real Madrid triumphing 5‑3 to secure a record‑extending eleventh European title.
title: 2016 UEFA Champions League Final

text: The Irish group The Boomtown Rats issued the track “I Don’t Like Mondays,” which climbed to the top of the UK Singles Chart and held the number‑one position for four weeks during the summer of 1979. This chart performance confirms that the single was released in 1979.
title: I Don't Like Mondays

text: The flag of Uruguay features a series of horizontal bands that echo the original nine departments of the nation, a design inspired by the United States flag’s representation of its first thirteen colonies. While the initial 1828 version displayed nine light‑blue stripes, the number was later reduced to four in 1830 to improve visibility from a distance. Dominating the upper left corner, the Sun of May is a symbolic element that stands for the May Revolution of 1810; according to historian Diego Abad de Santillán, this stylized sun also alludes to Inti, the Inca sun deity. Similar suns appear on the Argentine flag and Bolivia’s coat of arms.
title: Flag of Uruguay

text: Brant David Daugherty (born August 20, 1985) is an American actor who is best recognized for his recurring role as Noel Kahn on the teen‑drama series Pretty Little Liars. In 2013 he also appeared in a recurring capacity as Brian on the long‑running NBC daytime soap Days of Our Lives.
title: Brant Daugherty

text: The split of Korea into northern and southern zones occurred in 1945, following the end of World II and the conclusion of Japan’s 35‑year rule over the peninsula. Afterward, the United States and the Soviet Union each took control of a part of the country, establishing their boundary along the 38th parallel.
title: Division of Korea

text: In 1945 the Korean peninsula was split into two occupation zones, creating a northern area under Soviet control and a southern area under American control. This division was codified in General Order No. 1, which received approval on 17 August 1945, officially establishing the separate northern and southern zones.
title: Division of Korea

text: The Constitution’s Origination Clause stipulates that any legislation that involves raising revenue must begin in the House of Representatives. Although the clause is aimed at tax bills, the same rule has been applied to appropriation bills, which also start in the House. Consequently, the authority to draft and introduce appropriation bills is exercised under Congress’s power of raising revenue.
title: Appropriation bill

text: Apoptosis is a tightly regulated form of programmed cell death that, once initiated, cannot be stopped. It can be launched through two distinct routes. The intrinsic route is activated when a cell detects internal stress and decides to self‑destruct. The extrinsic route, however, is triggered by external cues: the cell receives signals from other cells, prompting it to undergo apoptosis. Both pathways converge on the activation of initiator caspases, which then activate executioner caspases that degrade cellular proteins and complete the death process.
title: Apoptosis

text: According to traditional Indian folklore, the area now called Delhi was originally the splendid city of Indraprastha, which was founded as a capital by the Pandavas around 3500 BC.
title: History of Delhi

text: Patriot Games makes clear that Jack Ryan’s home is Baltimore, Maryland, the city where he was born in 1950 to Emmet William Ryan, a homicide lieutenant with the Baltimore City Police Department, and his wife Catherine Burke Ryan, a nurse.
title: Jack Ryan (character)

text: The concept of the objective correlative in literary theory is most closely linked to the poet and critic T.S. Eliot. Eliot, who was part of the New Critics, set out the idea in his essay “Hamlet and His Problems,” later included in *The Sacred Wood: Essays on Poetry and Criticism*. In that piece he contrasts Shakespeare’s handling of Hamlet’s emotions with the effective use of an objective correlative in the depiction of Lady Macbeth, arguing that a character’s feelings should be evoked through external objects, actions, or circumstances rather than being directly described. This formalist approach ties external evidence to internal feeling in order to achieve artistic inevitability.
title: Objective correlative

text: In the system of biological classification, the highest rank is the domain, sometimes called a superkingdom or empire. Carl Woese’s three‑domain model, introduced in 1990, divides all living things into Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya. The first two domains consist of prokaryotic microorganisms—single‑celled organisms whose cells lack a nucleus. By contrast, every organism whose cells contain a nucleus and membrane‑bound organelles, as well as all multicellular forms, is placed in the domain **Eukarya**. Because humans are multicellular beings with nucleated cells, they are members of the domain Eukarya.
title: Domain (biology)

text: Jurassic World Evolution, a business‑simulation video game developed and published by Frontier Developments and based on the 2015 film Jurassic World, is slated to launch on June 12, 2018, for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.
title: Jurassic World Evolution

text: The death penalty was reinstated in Oregon in 1984 when Measure 6 amended the state constitution to again make capital punishment legal; that same year, Measure 7 created a separate sentencing hearing before a jury for aggravated‑murder cases.
title: Capital punishment in Oregon

text: The Chandrabhaga (also known as the Chenab and called Askni in Vedic texts) is the largest river in Himachal Pradesh in terms of water volume. It is created when its two source streams, the Chandra and the Bhaga, join together at Tandi, in Lahaul. From that confluence the river runs about 122 kilometres, draining an area of roughly 7,500 square kilometres before it leaves Himachal and enters Kashmir. The Chandra flows across the barren tribal lands before reaching the meeting point.
title: Rivers in Himachal Pradesh

text: The American Civil War, which raged across the United States between 1861 and 1865, pitted the nationalists of the Union—who affirmed their loyalty to the U.S. Constitution—against the secessionist forces of the Confederate States that sought to expand slavery.
title: American Civil War

text: In the 18th Dynasty of Egypt’s New Kingdom, the ruler originally called Amenhotep IV adopted the name Akhenaten to venerate the deity called the Aten, a solar manifestation of the god Ra. Akhenaten instituted the sole worship of the Aten, a reform that many scholars view as the earliest recorded instance of monotheism. His wife, Queen Nefertiti, likewise performed rites devoted to the Aten, reinforcing its central role in their religious transformation.
title: New Kingdom of Egypt

text: Although movable‑type printing began earlier in East Asia, the technology arrived in Europe in the mid‑15th century. Around 1450, the German inventor Johannes Gutenberg introduced a metal movable‑type printing press, developing a casting technique that used a lead‑tin‑antimony alloy together with a matrix and hand mould. In Germany, the first book printed with this movable‑type system is traditionally attributed to Johannes Gutenberg.
title: Movable type

text: Johannes Gutenberg of Mainz, Germany is recognized as the pioneer who first created a metal movable‑type printing system in Europe, known as the printing press.  A goldsmith by training, he drew on his experience cutting punches for coin moulds and, between 1436 and 1450, devised the hardware and casting methods needed to produce letters from matrices.  His chief innovation, the hand mould, provided a practical way to duplicate letter punches in the large numbers required to print entire books, thereby making movable‑type printing a viable enterprise.
title: Movable type

text:
Cell damage  
When a cell is unable to undergo regeneration, the organism compensates by substituting it with stromal connective tissue, thereby preserving the function of the affected tissue or organ. The stromal compartment consists of supportive cells that underlie the parenchymal elements of any organ; among the most prevalent stromal cell types are fibroblasts, immune cells, pericytes, and other inflammatory cells.
title: Cell damage

text: Sedimentary rock forms when material that has accumulated on Earth’s surface is buried and compacted together. Although it makes up only a small proportion of the planet’s crust, this rock type covers roughly three‑quarters of the continental land area.
title: Earth

title: Tablets of Stone

text: The Right to Buy programme was launched when the Housing Act was passed in 1980, shortly after Margaret Thatcher became Prime Minister in May 1979.
title: Right to Buy

text: Laura Jane Haddock, an English actress born on 21 August 1985, is known for playing the role of Meredith Quill in the Marvel film Guardians of the Galaxy and its sequel, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2.
title: Laura Haddock

title: Jonathan Cheban

text: In 1912 the province of Bihar and Orissa was created, separating Bihar from Bengal. At the same time, sections of the Chota Nagpur Division were transferred into this new province, marking the 1912 re‑organisation.
title: Chota Nagpur Division

text: Trigger points are found exclusively in muscles. They develop as a localized contraction of a small group of muscle fibers within a larger muscle or muscle bundle. This contraction can pull on the tendons and ligaments attached to the muscle, sometimes causing deep joint pain even in areas that contain no muscle tissue. The integrated hypothesis proposes that an excessive release of acetylcholine leads to sustained depolarization of those fibers, creating an abnormal biochemical environment with elevated acetylcholine, noradrenaline, serotonin and a lower pH. The continuous sarcomere contraction compresses the local blood supply, restricting energy delivery and generating sensitizing substances that activate nearby nociceptive nerves, producing localized pain at the neuromuscular junction. When trigger points are present in muscles, they are often accompanied by pain and weakness in the associated structures, following specific nerve pathways that have been mapped for diagnostic purposes.
title: Myofascial trigger point

text: The inaugural 2007 ICC World Twenty20 was staged in South Africa from 11 to 24 September 2007, featuring twelve sides – the ten Test‑playing nations together with Kenya and Scotland, the finalists of the 2007 WCL Division One tournament. After a thirteen‑day series of matches, India emerged as champions, defeating Pakistan in the final.
title: 2007 ICC World Twenty20

text: India won the toss and elected to bat on a pitch that was thought to favour the batters. Throughout the 20‑over innings the Pakistani bowlers, led by Umar Gul who removed both Yuvraj Singh and Mahendra Singh Dhoni, kept the run‑rate down and saw India finish on 157/5. Pakistan completed the fielding effort by delivering the very last over of India’s innings. Consequently, Pakistan bowled the final over of the 2007 World Twenty20, a match that India ultimately won.
title: 2007 ICC World Twenty20

text: The Philadelphia Eagles were founded in 1933. Throughout their history the team has made three Super Bowl appearances; after losing the first two, they finally won the championship in 2018. title: America's Next Top Model (cycle 8)

text: The British Indian Association, founded on 31 October 1851, was the first political society created under British rule in India. Its formation marked a major development in 19th‑century India, signalling that Indians could now organize collectively and could no longer be ignored.
title: British Indian Association

text: The Parlement de Bretagne, the administrative and judicial centre of Brittany, is regarded as the most famous 17th‑century building in Rennes. After a disastrous fire in 1994—possibly sparked by a protester’s flare—it was rebuilt and now houses the Rennes Court of Appeal. The surrounding plaza is designed in a classical architectural style.
title: Rennes

text: The narrative opens with Charlie, a quiet and sensitive fifteen‑year‑old, who begins writing letters about his life to an unknown recipient. He selects this person because he has heard they are nice and believes they will not judge him. In his letters, Charlie recounts his first year of high school while confronting two traumatic events from his past: the suicide of his only middle‑school friend, Michael Dobson, a year earlier, and the death of his beloved aunt, Helen, during his early childhood.
title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower

text: Novak Djokovic secured the men’s singles championship at the 2015 Australian Open, defeating Andy Murray in the final with a score of 7–6 (7–5), 6–7 (4–7), 6–3, 6–0.
title: 2015 Australian Open – Men's Singles

text: Matthew Gregory Wise (born 15 May 1966) is an English actor and producer who portrayed John Willoughby in the film version of *Sense and Sensibility*.
title: Greg Wise

text: The music video for One Direction’s “What Makes You Beautiful,” directed by John Urbano, was filmed on a beach in Malibu, California. It premiered on YouTube on August 19, 2011 and has since amassed over 940 million views. The clip earned the group three MTV Video Music Awards at the 2012 ceremony and was performed live on several television shows, award events, and during the Up All Night, Take Me Home, Where We Are, and On the Road Again tours.
title: What Makes You Beautiful

text: The video for One Direction’s “What Makes You Beautiful” was filmed during a two‑day shoot in July 2011. Its opening sequence places the group on a beach in Malibu, California, where they are shown hanging out and later joining a few girls for the rest of the song. The beach setting in Malibu, California is intercut with scenes of the band driving an orange camper‑van, establishing the location for the entire clip.
title: What Makes You Beautiful

text: Michelangelo, the celebrated 16th‑century Italian artist, created the renowned sculpture known as the Pietà and, in the same period, painted the Genesis scenes on the ceiling of Rome’s Sistine Chapel. His prolific output in painting, sculpture, and architecture, together with a wealth of surviving letters and sketches, makes him the best‑documented artist of his century.
title: Michelangelo

text: In *Boy Meets World*, Cory’s elder sibling is Eric Randall Matthews, a character who begins the series as a smooth‑talking, popular teen and later evolves into a more eccentric figure. The role of Eric, the older brother of Cory, Morgan and Joshua, is performed by Will Friedle. During the fourth season Eric takes a gap year after failing to gain admission to his chosen college.
title: List of Boy Meets World characters

text: The Tenth Amendment, adopted on December 15, 1791 as part of the Bill of Rights, embodies the principle of federalism by limiting the national government to the authorities expressly granted in the Constitution. It declares that any powers not specifically delegated to the federal government are retained by the states or the people.
title: Tenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

text: The Eagle Scout rank, introduced by the Boy Scouts of America in 1911, remains the organization’s highest honor. To earn it, a Scout must acquire at least 21 merit badges, live by the Scout Oath and Law, and complete a substantial service project that they plan, organize, lead, and manage, all before turning 18. Recipients receive a distinctive medal and badge, and they may later add Eagle Palms for further service, leadership, and merit‑badge achievements. Over the years, many well‑known Americans have attained Eagle Scout status; among them are astronaut Neil Armstrong, filmmaker Michael Moore, television host Mike Rowe, director Steven Spielberg, former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg, former Secretary of Defense Robert Gates, and President Gerald Ford.
title: Boy Scouts of America

text: President Gerald Ford, a former Boy Scout, once remarked, “I can say without hesitation, because of Scouting principles, I know I was a better athlete, I was a better naval officer, I was a better congressman, and I was a better prepared President.”
title: Boy Scouts of America

text: The Bronx, the northernmost of New York City’s five boroughs, sits directly north and east of Manhattan. The two landmasses are divided by the Harlem River, which forms the water boundary between the Bronx and Manhattan Island.
title: The Bronx

text: The Bronx is bounded on its southwestern edge by a waterway that runs between the borough and Manhattan Island. This channel is the Harlem River, which forms the natural separation between the Bronx and the island of Manhattan.
title: The Bronx

text: The red wolf (Canis rufus), also called the Florida black wolf or Mississippi Valley wolf, is a canid whose natural range is the southeastern United States. It displays a reddish‑tawny coat and is morphologically intermediate between the coyote and the gray wolf. Classified as a federally listed endangered species in the United States, it has been listed by the IUCN as critically endangered since 1996 and is regarded as the rarest of the wolf species worldwide.
title: Red wolf

text: The organism commonly referred to as E. coli is formally named **Escherichia coli**. It is a Gram‑negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod‑shaped coliform bacterium of the genus *Escherichia* that normally resides in the lower intestine of warm‑blooded animals. Most strains are harmless and even beneficial—producing vitamin K₂ and helping prevent colonisation by pathogenic microbes—though some serotypes can cause serious food‑borne illness and have prompted product recalls. The bacterium is shed in fecal matter, where it can multiply rapidly in fresh feces under aerobic conditions for about three days before its numbers slowly decline.
title: Escherichia coli

text: The actress Doreen Mantle (born 1926 in South Africa) is most widely recognised for playing the role of Jean Warboys—commonly called Mrs Warboys—in the television series *One Foot in the Grave*, which ran from 1990 to 2000.
title: Doreen Mantle

text: The series is widely recognized for its medieval realism, with the world crafted to evoke a historical period rather than a contemporary fantasy setting. George R.R. Martin deliberately emphasized battles, political intrigue, and character-driven drama over overt magic, aiming to make the story feel more like historical fiction. This approach reinforces the medieval atmosphere that defines the show's time setting.
title: Game of Thrones

text: The farcical black comedy *Arsenic and Old Lace* follows the Brewster family—descendants of Mayflower pilgrims who have become a troupe of unhinged murderers. Its protagonist, drama critic Mortimer Brewster, must contend with his homicidal relatives and the local police while wrestling with his promise to marry his beloved. All of the chaotic events unfold in Brooklyn, New York, where Mortimer tries to keep his family’s deadly secrets hidden.
title: Arsenic and Old Lace (play)

text: Only a single bowler has ever taken a hat‑trick in both innings of the same Test match. In the opening fixture of the 1912 Triangular Tournament, played at Old Trafford, Manchester, Australia faced South Africa on 28 May 1912. In that game the leg spinner Jimmy Matthews claimed a three‑wicket haul in South Africa’s first innings and repeated the feat in the second innings, completing each hat‑trick by dismissing Tommy Ward.
title: List of Test cricket hat-tricks

text: Along Came a Spider, released in 2001, is an American neo‑noir psychological thriller directed by Lee Tamahori. The film serves as a sequel to the 1997 movie Kiss the Girls, and it continues the story of detective Alex Cross. Morgan Freeman reprises his role as Alex Cross in this installment. The screenplay, written by Marc Moss, adapts James Patterson’s 1993 novel of the same name, although several major plot elements from the book were omitted. While critics gave the movie mixed to negative reviews, it performed well at the box office.
title: Along Came a Spider (film)

text: David Ben-Gurion, the head of the Yishuv, was the first individual to affix his signature to the Israeli Declaration of Independence. The document was intended to be signed by all 37 members of Moetzet HaAm, but twelve could not attend—eleven were trapped in besieged Jerusalem and one was abroad. The remaining 25 signatories present signed in alphabetical order, with spaces left for those absent. Subsequent signatories included Eliyahu Dobkin, Meir Vilner, and Zerach Warhaftig, whose placement sparked speculation that Vilner’s name had been isolated, a claim Warhaftig later denied. Two women, Golda Meir (Meyerson/Myerson) and Rachel Cohen‑Kagan, also signed the declaration.
title: Israeli Declaration of Independence

text: In 1869 the first functional periodic table was introduced by the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev. While his formulation incorporated earlier insights from scientists such as Antoine‑Laurent de Lavoisier and John Newlands, Mendeleev is widely regarded as the sole creator of the modern periodic arrangement.
title: History of the periodic table

text: Mason Alan Dinehart (born April 30, 1936), who has also been credited as Mason Alan Dinehart III, Alan Dinehart III, or Mase Dinehart, is an American businessman and former actor. He is most noted for playing a young Bat Masterson in thirty‑four episodes of the ABC/Desilu television series *The Life and Legend of Wyatt Earp*, which aired between 1955 and 1959.
title: Mason Alan Dinehart

text: The stability, security and predictability offered by British law and administration allowed Hong Kong to develop into a centre for international trade. In its early years the colony’s finances were heavily supported by opium revenues, which remained a major source of government income until the Japanese occupation in 1941. While the largest enterprises were run by British, American and other expatriates, the construction of the new port city relied largely on Chinese labor.
title: British Hong Kong

text: Chymotrypsin is a serine protease that operates in the digestive systems of many organisms, where it catalyzes the hydrolytic cleavage of peptide bonds. By providing a catalytic environment, it speeds up the otherwise very slow hydrolysis of these bonds, targeting sequences that have tryptophan, tyrosine, phenylalanine, or leucine on the N‑terminal side of the bond.
title: Chymotrypsin

text: Based on an inscription discovered in an interior chamber that identifies the work gang and mentions the Fourth‑Dynasty Pharaoh Khufu, scholars conclude that the Great Pyramid of Giza was erected as a tomb during a 20-year period, with construction finishing around 2560 BC.
title: Great Pyramid of Giza

text: The Cosby Show was an American sitcom starring Bill Cosby that ran on NBC from September 20, 1984, through April 30, 1992. Its storyline follows the Huxtable family, an upper‑middle‑class African‑American household that lives in Brooklyn, New York.
title: The Cosby Show

text: In the television series *The Cosby Show*, the Huxtable family is portrayed as living in a brownstone situated in Brooklyn, New York.
title: The Cosby Show

text: Christmas, although now observed as a Christian holiday, originally began as a celebration of the winter solstice, emerging from pre‑Christian festivals that pagan peoples marked at that time of year.
title: Christmas

text: The Beer Hall Putsch—also called the Munich Putsch—was a failed coup launched by Adolf Hitler, Generalquartiermeister Erich Ludendorff and other Kampfbund leaders. Their aim was to seize power in Munich, Bavaria, during the night of 8–9 November 1923. Approximately two thousand Nazi supporters marched into the centre of the city, where they clashed with police forces, leading to casualties on both sides. The event is historically recorded as having taken place in Munich, Bavaria.
title: Beer Hall Putsch

text: The dance series The Next Step received a renewal for a sixth season comprising 26 episodes, and that season is scheduled to debut in 2018.
title: List of The Next Step episodes

text: According to the record, the Republic of Korea has hosted the Olympic Games on two occasions, marking notable milestones in the nation’s sporting history.
title: South Korea at the Olympics

text: Panzerkampfwagen VIII Maus was a German super‑heavy tank finished in late 1944. It is recognized as the heaviest fully enclosed armoured fighting vehicle ever built, which makes it the largest tank used during World II. Although five were ordered, only two hulls and one turret were completed before advancing Soviet forces captured the testing grounds.
title: Panzer VIII Maus

text: Rolling Stone writer Greg Tate praised Chris Cornell’s track “Can't Change Me,” calling it a richly melodic pop‑rock ballad. He highlighted the song’s lyric, “She’s going to change the world / But she can’t change me,” noting how it reveals Cornell’s yearning to be heard as an openly wounded yet unapologetically grandiose rock vocalist.
title: Can't Change Me

text: According to historical records, the Dome of the Rock was first completed in 691 CE under the patronage of Umayyad Caliph Abd al‑Malik during the Second Fitna. It was erected on the former location of the Roman temple of Jupiter Capitolinus, which itself had been built over the Second Jewish Temple that was destroyed in the Roman siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE. The original dome collapsed in 1015 and was rebuilt between 1022 and 1023. Today the monument is regarded as one of the oldest surviving examples of Islamic architecture.
title: Dome of the Rock

text: In 1492, Christopher Columbus departed from Spain on his first expedition, commanding the Niña, the Pinta, and the flagship Santa María in search of a direct passage to Asia. On 12 October of that year he reached an island in the Bahamas, claimed it for Spain, and then visited a number of additional Bahamian islands. From there he sailed onward to the island now called Cuba and subsequently continued to Hispaniola.
title: History of the Bahamas

text: Mary Elizabeth Patterson (November 22, 1874 – January 31, 1966) was an American actress who worked in theatre, film, and television. Toward the end of her career she achieved broad fame by playing the elderly neighbor Matilda Trumbull on the television comedy series I Love Lucy.
title: Elizabeth Patterson (actress)

text: In the mid‑nineteenth century, the city of New Orleans was plagued by waste from its slaughterhouses, and about a mile and a half upstream roughly one thousand butchers who processed more than three hundred thousand animals each year lived in New Orleans.
title: Slaughter-House Cases

text: The Qing emperors were descendants of the Aisin Gioro clan, a Jurchen family whose roots lay in Manchuria. In the late sixteenth century the clan’s leader Nurhaci began consolidating the Jurchen tribes into a single entity, later renamed the Manchus, and organized them into the Banner system that also incorporated Han Chinese and Mongol elements. This Manchu lineage formed the basis of the dynasty that would later become known as the Qing.
title: Qing dynasty

text: The weapon most often associated with the Grim Reaper is a scythe. In both ancient Greek mythology and later artistic depictions, the figure of the Grim Reaper is regularly shown holding this curved cutting tool, just as the Titan Cronus is portrayed with a scythe in classical imagery. This association links the grim figure to the same implement that appears in Roman and Greek sources, where the scythe—known in Latin as the falx foenaria—served as a symbol of harvest and death.
title: Scythe

text: Captain Phasma, a fictional figure introduced in the 2015 movie *Star Wars: The Force Awakens*—the opening entry of the sequel trilogy—is portrayed by Gwendoline Christie. In the film, she commands the First Order’s stormtrooper forces, and Christie reprises the role in the subsequent sequel, *Star Wars: The Last Jedi* (2017). The character also appears in the prequel anthology *Before the Awakening*.
title: Captain Phasma

text: In the season’s finale, after a series of group numbers and solo reprises, the results were revealed during the last hour of the show. Emma finished in fourth place, Tate took third, J.T. was the runner‑up, and Kida won the $250,000 top prize and will appear on the cover of Dance Spirit magazine.
title: So You Think You Can Dance: The Next Generation (U.S. TV series)

text: Salisbury steak is prepared from ground beef combined with a variety of other ingredients and is commonly served with gravy or a brown sauce. In contrast, hamburger steak is a similar preparation, but the two dishes differ in ingredients.
title: Salisbury steak

text: A subdural hematoma is a collection of blood that gathers between the inner layer of the dura mater and the arachnoid mater. It most often follows trauma that tears the bridging veins which traverse the subdural space, allowing blood to leak into this compartment. This bleeding can raise intracranial pressure and compress the underlying brain tissue. When the condition is acute, it can be life‑threatening, whereas chronic cases generally have a better prognosis if treated appropriately.
title: Subdural hematoma

text: Thank You for Your Service is a 2017 American biographical war drama directed by Jason Hall and adapted from David Finkel’s 2013 nonfiction book. The story follows soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, 16th Infantry Regiment as they return to the vicinity of Fort Riley, Kansas after a 15‑month deployment in Iraq, depicting their battle with post‑traumatic stress disorder while trying to readjust to civilian life.
title: Thank You for Your Service (2017 film)

text: After a grueling fifteen‑month tour of duty in Iraq, decorated soldier Adam Schumann (Miles Teller) makes his way back to his family’s home in Kansas, where his wife Saskia (Haley Bennett) awaits with their two young children—a daughter and an infant son born while he was still overseas. Struggling with PTSD, Adam experiences nightmares and flashbacks, prompting his wife to urge him to seek assistance from the overtaxed Department of Veterans Affairs. He also finds support from two fellow Iraq veterans who live nearby: Solo Aeiti, an American Samoan (Beulah Koale), and Billy Waller (Joe Cole), the latter of whom tragically ends his own life after a personal crisis.
title: Thank You for Your Service (2017 film)

text: The Indian action‑comedy released in 2014 and directed by Prabhu Deva is titled **Action Jackson**. The film stars Ajay Devgn, who plays two characters, and pairs him with Sonakshi Sinha as one of the lead actresses. Supporting roles include Yami Gautam, Manasvi Mamgai, and Kunaal Roy Kapur, while Anandaraj portrays the chief villain. Produced by Gordhan Tanwani and Sunil Lulla, the movie premiered on 5 December 2014.
title: Action Jackson (2014 film)

text: The ancient Chinese umbrella, known by the character 傘 (sǎn), was originally made by fastening large leaves to rib‑like supports, giving it a shape much like today’s parasol. Though it also served as a status symbol—sometimes being carried before the emperor during hunts—its practical function in that context was a defense against rain rather than the sun. This early design later spread to Japan, Persia, and the Western world via trade routes.
title: Umbrella

text: Henrik Ibsen’s three‑act drama, first published in December 1879 and premiered at the Royal Theatre in Copenhagen, unfolds in a small Norwegian community of the same era. The play is set in a Norwegian town circa 1879.
title: A Doll's House

text: In the third season of HBO’s *Game of Thrones*, Diana Rigg was cast as Lady Olenna Tyrell, the sharp‑tongued matriarch known as the “Queen of Thorns” and the grandmother of the series regular Margaery Tyrell. Rigg continued to appear as Olenna in subsequent seasons, earning Emmy nominations for her guest‑acting performances.
title: Diana Rigg

text: Epithelium is one of the four fundamental animal tissue types. It lines the outer surfaces of organs and blood vessels, and it also coats the inner surfaces of cavities within many internal organs, serving as the innermost layer of cells in those regions.
title: Epithelium

text: The Democratic Party’s modern‑liberal philosophy stresses the pursuit of social and economic equality, endorsing a welfare‑state approach that seeks to level both societal and financial opportunities for Americans.
title: Democratic Party (United States)

text: Sofia serves as the capital and the most populous city of Bulgaria. Situated at the base of Vitosha Mountain in the western region of the nation, it lies near the centre of the Balkan peninsula, roughly equidistant between the Black Sea and the Adriatic Sea and closest to the Aegean Sea. The city itself is home to about 1.3 million residents, while its metropolitan area contains roughly 1.7 million people.
title: Sofia

text: Human heart development begins with the appearance of two endocardial tubes that fuse to form the primitive heart tube. This tube then loops and septates, giving rise to the four chambers and paired arterial trunks of the adult heart. As the first functional organ in vertebrate embryos, the human heart starts beating on its own, contracting spontaneously by week 4 of development.
title: Heart development

text: Mahatma Gandhi was the proponent of the Basic Education concept in India. He outlined its pedagogic aims as both broad and specific. The broad aims encompassed lifelong learning, social development and holistic education, while the specific aims focused on craft work, use of the native language, co‑education, village community involvement, hygiene through the “Programme of Safai,” and the teaching of reading and writing.
title: Basic education

text: Howard Ellsworth Rollins Jr. (October 17, 1950 – December 8, 1996) was an American stage, film, and television actor. In addition to his work in productions such as *King* and *Ragtime*, he is especially remembered for playing the detective Virgil Tibbs on the crime drama *In the Heat of the Night*.
title: Howard Rollins

text: The 2010 post‑apocalyptic neo‑Western *The Book of Eli* began principal photography in February 2009, and the production was carried out in New Mexico.
title: The Book of Eli

text: The San Juan Mountains constitute a lofty, rugged section of the Rocky Mountains that stretches across southwestern Colorado and reaches into northwestern New Mexico. This range is noted for its mineral‑rich geology and historic mining towns.
title: San Juan Mountains

text: Star Wars: From the Adventures of Luke Skywalker is the novelization of the 1977 Star Wars film. Though the book bears George Lucas’s name, it was actually written by Alan Dean Foster and released by Ballantine Books on 12 November 1976—several months before the movie’s theatrical debut. In later printings the title was changed to Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope to match the retroactive episode subtitles added to the film series.
title: Star Wars: From the Adventures of Luke Skywalker

text: The initial published incarnation of Star Wars was the novelization titled *Star Wars: From the Adventures of Luke Skywalker*. Ballantine Books issued this book in the United States in December 1976, a full six months before the film’s theatrical premiere in 1977. The same novelization was later released in the United Kingdom by Sphere Books.
title: Star Wars: From the Adventures of Luke Skywalker

text: Sir Alex Ferguson remains the longest‑serving manager in the history of Manchester United, having led the club for more than 26 years. In that period he accumulated an unrivalled trophy haul: 13 Premier League titles, five FA Cups, four League Cups, ten Community Shields, two UEFA Champions League trophies, plus wins in the UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup, UEFA Super Cup, Intercontinental Cup and FIFA Club World Cup.
title: List of Manchester United F.C. managers

text: In human reproduction, the fertilized ovum typically implants in the uterine lining roughly **around 9 days after ovulation**, although the timing can vary anywhere from about 6 to 12 days.
title: Implantation (human embryo)

text: The 21st FIFA World Cup, set for 14 June to 15 July 2018, will be staged in Russia after the country won the hosting rights on 2 December 2010. Most of the stadiums are located in the European portion of Russia, west of the Ural Mountains, to keep travel times reasonable.
title: 2018 FIFA World Cup

text: The game of Mexican Train is normally played with a double‑twelve set of dominoes, which is marketed as the standard set for the game and can accommodate up to eight players. Although other domino sets are sometimes used, A double-twelve set remains the common choice for playing Mexican Train.
title: Mexican Train

text: After its 1992 expansion into Hungary and Slovenia, Red Bull reached the United States by launching in California in 1997.
title: Red Bull

text: The Adelaide Crows did not reach another AFL Grand Final after their 1998 appearance until they returned in 2017. In that season the team entered the finals as the clear favourites, dispatched Greater Western Sydney and Geelong by large margins, and earned a spot in the Grand Final, where they were ultimately beaten by Richmond. Consequently, the last time the Crows contested a Grand Final was in 2017.
title: Adelaide Football Club

text: We Are the World, recorded in 1985 by the supergroup United Support of Artists (USA) for Africa, was written by Michael Jackson and Lionel Richie, arranged by Michael Omartian, and produced by Quincy Jones.
title: We Are the World

text: Tatsumi, the brown‑haired swordsman who is taken in by Night Raid, ultimately meets his end in the anime; after defeating Shikoutazer he dies in episode 24.
title: List of Akame ga Kill! characters

text: The Los Angeles Dodgers and the New York Yankees have long been one of baseball’s most celebrated cross‑coast rivalries, facing each other in the World Series more often than any other pair of National and American League clubs. Although the two franchises first clashed when the Dodgers were still based in Brooklyn, the rivalry persisted after the Dodgers moved to Los Angeles in 1958, symbolizing the competition between the nation’s two largest cities. Despite meeting eleven times in the Fall Classic, the Yankees and Dodgers have not met in the World Series since 1981. The two teams would not play one another again in any regular‑season or postseason game until a three‑game interleague series in 2004, but their matchups continue to draw large crowds.
title: Dodgers–Yankees rivalry

text: Tinker Air Force Base, initially known as the Midwest Air Depot, is named in honor of Oklahoma native Major General Clarence L. Tinker, the first Native American to achieve the rank of Major General.
title: Tinker Air Force Base

text: “Help Me Make It Through the Night” is a country‑music ballad that first appeared on the 1970 album *Kristofferson*. The song was written and composed by Kris Kristofferson, who also performed the original recording. Later that same year Sammi Smith released her own version on the album *Help Me Make It Through the Night*; Smith’s cover became the most commercially successful and widely recognized rendition in the United States, topping the country singles chart and reaching number eight on the pop chart.
title: Help Me Make It Through the Night

text: Mother's Day (2016) is set in Atlanta, where a collection of seemingly unrelated characters confront their relationships with their mothers as the holiday approaches. The film follows Sandy, a divorced mother of two, her ex‑husband’s new wife, and other intertwined storylines that all unfold against the backdrop of the city.
title: Mother's Day (2016 film)

text: Principal photography for the 2016 film *Mother’s Day* began on August 18, 2015, in Atlanta, Georgia. Although Julia Roberts required only four days to shoot her scenes, she was compensated with a $3 million salary.
title: Mother's Day (2016 film)

text: The forum started as the G6 in 1975, grew to the G7 when Canada joined in 1976, and then expanded to incorporate Russia in 1997; the year after, the enlarged coalition was renamed the G8.
title: Group of Eight

text: Lana Del Rey performed a somber, sinister rendition of “Once Upon a Dream,” which is used at the conclusion of the 2014 film Maleficent. Earlier versions of the song had been recorded by the American girl group No Secrets for a 2003 DVD release and by Emily Osment for the 2008 Platinum Edition of the movie, and it also appeared on the Princess Disneymania compilation.
title: Once Upon a Dream (Sleeping Beauty song)

text: In the series premiere “Days Gone Bye,” former sheriff’s deputy Rick Grimes is searching an abandoned convenience store for supplies when he sees a little girl who is, in fact, a walker. The walker is identified as Addy Miller, and when she charges at him, Rick shoots her in the head, killing her.
title: Days Gone Bye (The Walking Dead)

text: In “Baby,” the track’s upbeat R&B production gives way after the second verse to a rap segment performed by Ludacris, who delivers a brief recollection of his own teenage romance.
title: Baby (Justin Bieber song)

text: The Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) is a multidisciplinary institute that was created by the Department of Science and Technology of the Government of India to commemorate the birth centenary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. The centre’s campus is situated in Jakkur, Bangalore, India.
title: Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research

text: In the United States, a general election may be held at any level of government—city, county, congressional district, or state—whenever at least two parties vie for an office. These elections are scheduled to occur **every two to six years**, depending on the term length of the position being filled; most offices carry a four‑year term. The regular cycle includes the presidential election, and the timetable also allows for special elections that fill vacancies caused by death, resignation, or other premature departures. Although the U.S. system does not permit the calling of early elections, the Senate’s rotation means that roughly one‑third of its seats are contested at two‑year intervals, coinciding with the general election schedule.
title: General election

text: In Conan the Destroyer, the queen’s niece named Jehnna—identified in the story as a virgin who is meant to restore the jeweled horn of the dreaming god Dagoth—is portrayed by Olivia d'Abo.
title: Conan the Destroyer

text: Sweet Caroline has been part of the Boston Red Sox’s Fenway Park experience since at least 1997, when it first began to be played at the stadium. Since 2002, the song has been played during the middle of the eighth inning of every game.
title: Sweet Caroline

text: Habib (Arabic: حبيب, also transliterated as Habeeb) is an Arabic masculine given name—and at times a surname—that translates to the word "beloved". The name enjoys broad popularity throughout the Muslim world, particularly in the Middle East and Africa, and it is also borne by individuals of other faiths.
title: Habib

text: David Joseph Madden (December 17, 1931 – January 16, 2014) was a Canadian‑born American actor who is most remembered for his role as Reuben Kincaid, the manager of the musical family in the 1970s sitcom *The Partridge Family*.
title: Dave Madden

text: After the loss of the Thirteen Colonies in 1783, the British government looked for a new site for penal transportation and turned to the newly discovered lands of Australia. In 1770 the explorer James Cook reached the eastern coast, claimed the continent for Britain and named it New South Wales. Acting on botanist Joseph Banks’s advice, the first convoy of convicts set sail in 1787, arrived at Botany Bay in 1788 and founded a settlement that continued to receive convicts until 1840. Through this penal colony and the later Australian colonies, the British Empire controlled the entire continent of Australia.
title: British Empire

text: The lower chamber of Pennsylvania’s General Assembly is composed of 203 members, each chosen from a single‑member district to serve a two‑year term.
title: Pennsylvania House of Representatives

text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 was crafted to extend the right to be served in public places—hotels, restaurants, theaters, retail stores and similar establishments—to all Americans, and it also sought to strengthen protections for the right to vote.
title: Civil Rights Act of 1964

text: The American R&B group Boyz II Men recorded the single “End of the Road” for the Boomerang soundtrack, and the track was issued in 1992; it was written and produced by Kenneth “Babyface” Edmonds, L.A. Reid and Daryl Simmons.
title: End of the Road

text: Electromyography (EMG) is an electro‑diagnostic technique that evaluates and records the electrical activity of skeletal muscles. An electromyograph produces an electromyogram by sensing the electric potential generated by muscle cells when they are activated either electrically or neurologically. By analyzing these signals, clinicians can assess activation levels, recruitment patterns, and other aspects of muscle biomechanics.
title: Electromyography

text: The season known as autumn—called fall in American and Canadian English—is one of the four temperate seasons. It signals the change from summer to winter, arriving in September in the Northern Hemisphere or in March in the Southern Hemisphere, when daylight hours noticeably shrink and temperatures drop. A hallmark of this time of year is the shedding of leaves from deciduous trees.
title: Autumn

text: Before the sixteenth century the season was commonly called “harvest,” a term that still survives in other West Germanic languages. As populations shifted from rural labor to urban life, “harvest” narrowed in meaning to refer solely to the act of reaping. In that same era the names autumn and fall began to replace “harvest” as the word for the season.
title: Autumn

text: Fayetteville, North Carolina—located in the Sandhills of the western Coastal Plain along the Cape Fear River—has been honored three times with the National Civic League’s All‑America City Award and ranks as the sixth‑largest city in the state. While the 2010 census recorded 200,564 residents, later estimates show that the city’s population was 204,408 in 2013.
title: Fayetteville, North Carolina

text: “Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology), released as the second single from Marvin Gaye’s 1971 album *What’s Going On*, is celebrated as one of popular music’s most poignant anthems of sorrow regarding the environment. Written solely by Gaye, the track features his piano playing, strings arranged by Paul Riser and David Van De Pitte, multi‑tracked vocals by Gaye and The Andantes, instrumental support from The Funk Brothers, and a lead saxophone solo by Wild Bill Moore. It reached number 4 on Billboard’s Pop Singles chart and topped the R&B Singles chart for two weeks in August 1971, while also appearing on the Adult Contemporary and Canadian charts.
title: Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology)

text: After the 1981 Lord Howe Island Amendment Act established a Permanent Park Preserve on the island’s north and south ends, the island was listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1982.
title: Lord Howe Island

text: In the women's singles final of the 2017 Wimbledon Championships, Garbiñe Muguruza secured her second Grand Slam singles title by beating Venus Williams 7–5, 6–0. Her victory made her the second Spanish woman ever to win the Wimbledon singles crown, following Conchita Martínez’s triumph in 1994, and marked the first time a player had defeated both Williams sisters in Grand Slam singles finals.
title: 2017 Wimbledon Championships – Women's Singles

text: The Federal Reserve’s Board of Governors, which serves as the system’s principal governing body, is composed of members who are appointed by the President of the United States and confirmed by the Senate, each serving a staggered 14‑year term.
title: Federal Reserve Board of Governors

text: Under the Banking Act of 1935, the seven individuals who serve on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors—including the Chairman and Vice Chairman—are appointed by the President from among the sitting Governors, a process designed to provide fair representation of the country’s financial, agricultural, industrial, commercial interests and geographic regions.
title: Federal Reserve Board of Governors

text: The predominant style of megalithic construction across Europe is the portal tomb, a stone chamber built from upright orthostats topped by one or more large flat capstones that form a roof. Although many of these monuments contain human remains, scholars still debate whether burial was their primary function. Archaeologists use the term the portal tomb even though a variety of local names exist—anta in Galicia and Portugal, stazzone in Sardinia, hunebed in the Netherlands, Hünengrab in Germany, dysse in Denmark, and cromlech in Wales. It is generally assumed that most of these structures were originally covered by earthen mounds.
title: Megalith

text: Home and Family, the two‑hour daily Hallmark series, is recorded a day in advance in Los Angeles, California. The production schedule was chosen to let actors avoid early‑morning call times, such as 4 a.m. The program focuses on light‑hearted entertainment and practical tips, steering clear of current events, politics, and even certain words like “breast.”
title: Home and Family

text: St. Louis has served as the home city for four National Football League (NFL) franchises.
title: Sports in St. Louis

text: In the 2017 US Open women's singles, **Sloane Stephens** claimed her first Grand Slam title, defeating Madison Keys in the final with a score of 6–3, 6–0. This all‑American final was the first of its kind at the US Open since 2002, and Stephens became the second unseeded woman in the Open era to win the tournament, after Kim Clijsters in 2009.
title: 2017 US Open – Women's Singles

text: Super Bowl rings are typically fashioned from yellow or white gold and set with diamonds, displaying the team’s name, logo, and the Super Bowl number—usually shown in Roman numerals. The league contributes up to $5,000 toward each ring for a maximum of 150 rings, with any additional expense covered by the winning franchise. Most rings are produced by the memorabilia company Jostens. In 2015, the rings for the New England Patriots reportedly cost $36,500 each, making them the most expensive rings Jostens has ever produced.
title: Super Bowl ring

text: In Hawthorne’s short story **My Kinsman, Major Molineux**, the central figure is a young traveler named Robin. Around the year 1732 Robin, a youth, arrives in Boston by ferry seeking his kinsman, the colonial official Major Molineux, who has promised him a job. He wanders the town looking for the major, encounters hostile townspeople, and eventually discovers that Molineux is being led through the streets in a tar‑and‑feathered mob. The youth’s name, Robin, is given explicitly as the protagonist of the tale.
title: My Kinsman, Major Molineux

text: The attack was carried out inside Theater 9 of the Century 16 multiplex (operated by Cinemark) at the Town Center at Aurora shopping mall, located at 14300 E. Alameda Avenue. Police reports state that the shooter purchased a ticket, entered the auditorium and took a seat in the front row. Roughly twenty minutes after the film began, he exited Theater 9 through an emergency door beside the screen, which opened onto a lightly used parking area at the rear of the complex, propping the door slightly ajar with a plastic table‑cloth holder. At the time of the incident, about 400 patrons were inside Theater 9.
title: 2012 Aurora shooting

text: The MercyMe single “I Can Only Imagine,” sometimes shortened to “Imagine,” was written and composed by the band’s lead vocalist Bart Millard. Inspired by the passing of Millard’s father, the song reflects on what it might be like to stand before God in Heaven. It originally appeared on MercyMe’s 1999 independent release *The Worship Project* and was later rerecorded for their 2001 major‑label debut *Almost There*, where it appears as the fifth track.
title: I Can Only Imagine (MercyMe song)

text: In 1989 the Hawke Labor Government started to phase in tuition charges for Australian university students, ending the era of fully free higher education. That year it introduced the Higher Education Contributions Scheme (HECS), under which every student was assessed a fee of $1,800 while the Commonwealth covered the remaining costs. Students could postpone payment, creating a HECS debt that would later be repaid through the tax system once their income passed a set threshold. This reform marked the transition from a completely free university system to one in which students contributed financially.
title: Tertiary education fees in Australia

text: The extended (director’s) edition of *The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring*, issued in November 2002 on VHS and DVD, has a total running time of 228 minutes.
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring

text: In contemporary U.S. military practice, the morning bugle call **Reveille** is sounded at sunrise (the exact hour differing among installations). On Army posts and Air Force bases, the call is either played alone or followed by the bugle call “To the Colors” precisely when the national flag is hoisted; at that moment all service members outdoors must come to attention and render a salute. While the flag is being raised, soldiers move to parade‑rest, hear Reveille, and then stand at attention to present arms. (Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard installations typically raise the flag at 0800 with “The Star‑Spangled Banner” or “To the Colors,” but the Army and Air Force tradition links the flag‑raising ceremony directly to Reveille.)
title: Reveille

text: Released in 1967, the song titled “I Dig Rock and Roll Music” was recorded by the American folk group Peter, Paul and Mary. It was written by Paul Stookey, James Mason, and Dave Dixon.
title: I Dig Rock and Roll Music

text: The third installment of The Lunar Chronicles is Cress, which was released on February 4, 2014.
title: The Lunar Chronicles

text: Although the series drew negative reviews, it consistently pulled in solid ratings, enabling it to reach the 100‑episode benchmark required for syndication over a span of seven seasons.
title: Rules of Engagement (TV series)

text: In the United States, the agency responsible for issuing both driver’s licenses and non‑driver identification cards is the Department of Motor Vehicles of the respective state, so a state‑issued ID can be obtained at each state’s DMV.
title: Identity documents in the United States

text: The Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) creates a federal tax that is levied on employers to help finance state workforce agencies. Under this law, employers are the party that must pay the unemployment taxes. They fulfill this obligation by filing an annual Form 940 with the Internal Revenue Service, and in certain situations they must also make installment payments during the tax year.
title: Federal Unemployment Tax Act

text: Carnival Glory is a cruise ship that belongs to the Conquest class and is operated by Carnival Cruise Line.
title: Carnival Glory

text: Washington state has three nuclear power plants; the category listing includes three pages, representing all three facilities, although the list may not reflect recent changes.
title: Category:Nuclear power plants in Washington (state)

text: In 1962 McDonald’s rolled out its now‑famous Golden Arches logo. A year later the chain celebrated selling its millionth hamburger and introduced Ronald McDonald, the red‑haired clown created to attract young customers.
title: History of McDonald's

text: Michael Casimir “Mike” Stivic is a fictional character from the 1970s American sitcom *All in the Family*. He appears as the live‑in son‑in‑law of the series’ main character, Archie Bunker, who often derisively calls him “Meathead.” Mike is married to Archie’s daughter Gloria, a role portrayed by Sally Struthers. Rob Reiner played the role of Michael Stivic throughout the series.
title: Michael Stivic

text: The 1979 composition “What I Like About You” was performed by the American rock group **The Romantics**. It was written by band members Wally Palmar, Mike Skill and drummer Jimmy Marinos, appeared on the group’s self‑titled debut album released in 1980, and was issued as a single. Marinos also handled lead vocals on the recording, and a music video for the song received heavy rotation on MTV during the early 1980s.
title: What I Like About You (song)

text: The vessel known as the Hector arrived at Pictou, Nova Scotia, in 1773, marking its role in the first major wave of Scottish settlement in the region. A replica of this historic ship now stands at the Hector Heritage Quay, a volunteer‑run heritage centre in Pictou.
title: Hector (ship)

text: The ship known as The Hector arrived at Pictou, Nova Scotia, in the year 1773, disembarking 189 settlers, the majority of whom originated from Lochbroom.
title: Hector (ship)

text: During the 2017 NCAA Division I Men’s Basketball Tournament, the Final Four featured North Carolina defeating Oregon, a return to the semifinals for the Tar Heels after their last appearance in 1939. In the other semifinal, Gonzaga beat South Carolina, giving both programs their first ever Final Four berth. In the championship game, North Carolina prevailed over Gonzaga, 71–65, to capture the national title.
title: 2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament

text: A cylinder is a solid that is enclosed by a curved cylindrical surface and two parallel planes. The flat sections where the curved surface meets each of those planes are the cylinder’s bases, which are congruent figures. All line segments that run from one plane to the other along the surface (the elements of the cylinder) have the same length. When these elements are perpendicular to the planes, the cylinder is right; otherwise it is oblique. If the bases are circular disks, the solid is a circular cylinder.
title: Cylinder

text: Since 1877, the Wimbledon Championships have been staged at the All England Club, which lies in the Wimbledon district of London, and the matches are contested on outdoor grass courts.
title: The Championships, Wimbledon

text: In a condenser, relatively cool water is circulated through the device so that it can condense the steam leaving the cylinders or turbines. Running cooling water through the condenser therefore serves to condense the steam, reducing back‑pressure and improving the system’s efficiency.
title: Cooling tower

text: Chromosomes can be observed with a light microscope only when a cell reaches the metaphase stage of division, when every chromosome lines up at the cell’s center in a tightly packed configuration. Before this point, each chromosome is duplicated during the S phase and the duplicate stays attached to the original at the centromere, creating an X‑shaped pair known as sister chromatids.
