During metaphase the paired structure is called a metaphase chromosome, and in this highly condensed form the chromosomes are most easily distinguished.
title: Chromosome

text: The American Western series *Bat Masterson* aired on NBC between 1958 and 1961, presenting a dramatized version of the real‑life marshal and gambler. In this program, the lead role of Bat Masterson was portrayed by Gene Barry.
title: Bat Masterson (TV series)

text: English singer‑songwriter Dido released “White Flag” as the lead single from her second studio album, Life for Rent, on 1 September 2003. The track became one of her signature songs and contributed to the album selling over ten million copies worldwide. “White Flag” was nominated for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance at the 46th Grammy Awards and won the Best British Single award at the 2004 Brit Awards.
title: White Flag (song)

text: In the comic‑country tale “One Piece at a Time,” the narrator and a plant colleague hatch a scheme to obtain a Cadillac by gradually pilfering its components from the assembly line. The singer pockets the tiny parts in his unusually large lunchbox, while the bigger sections are smuggled out in his coworker’s motorhome.
title: One Piece at a Time

text: The Canadian Pacific Railway, Canada’s first trans‑continental line, was constructed between 1881 and 1885, linking Eastern Canada with British Columbia and fulfilling the promise made to the province when it joined Confederation.
title: Canadian Pacific Railway

text: The song “Heart and Soul” was recorded by the British pop band T'Pau. Issued in 1987 as the group’s first single from their debut album Bridge of Spies, the track gained further exposure after featuring in a Pepe Jeans advertisement and subsequently rose to No. 4 on the singles charts in both the United Kingdom and the United States.
title: Heart and Soul (T'Pau song)

text: The German princes who held the right to elect the Holy Roman Emperor were known as prince-electors. These electors formed the electoral college of the Holy Roman Empire, a body responsible for choosing the empire’s ruler. Their official titles varied in different languages—Kurfürst in German, Kurfiřt in Czech, and Princeps Elector in Latin—but the English term “prince-electors” is commonly used to refer to them.
title: Prince-elector

text: "I Knew the Bride (When She Used to Rock 'n' Roll)" was penned by Nick Lowe, yet the song first gained prominence through a recording by Dave Edmunds. Edmunds included the track on his 1977 album *Get It*, and a subsequent live rendition appeared a year later on Nick Lowe’s *Live Stiffs Live* with his group Last Chicken in the Shop.
title: I Knew the Bride

text: The wireless operator Harold Bride, who was close enough to hear the musicians as the RMS Titanic went down, later recalled that the band’s last piece was the tune called "Autumn". His 1912 account, recorded in Walter Lord’s *A Night to Remember* and reported by the New York Times, is one of only two eyewitness statements from the deck. Although some survivors later claimed the hymn “Nearer, My God, to Thee” was played, Bride’s testimony specifically names the melody “Autumn”, a tune that was not listed in the White Star Line’s official songbook.
title: Legends and myths regarding RMS Titanic

text: Jesse Wesley Williams (born August 5, 1981) is an American actor who portrays Dr. Jackson Avery on the ABC television series Grey’s Anatomy.
title: Jesse Williams (actor)

text: The Menendez brothers were convicted of killing their parents and each received life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
title: Lyle and Erik Menendez

text: Julie Deborah Kavner (born September 7, 1950) is an American actress, voice actress, and comedian who supplies the voice for Marge Simpson on the animated television series *The Simpsons*. In addition to Marge, she also performs the voices of several other characters on the show, such as Jacqueline Bouvier and the twins Patty and Selma Bouvier.
title: Julie Kavner

text: The vascular cambium, also called the main cambium, wood cambium, or bifacial cambium, is a cylindrical layer of undifferentiated meristematic cells situated between the existing xylem and phloem in the stems and roots of many vascular plants. This tissue continuously divides, giving rise to new secondary vascular tissues. Specifically, The vascular cambium is the source of secondary xylem that forms inward toward the pith and secondary phloem that develops outward toward the bark. Unlike the mature xylem and phloem, the cambium itself does not conduct water, minerals, or nutrients.
title: Vascular cambium

text: After testing a speaker‑based ordering system, Smith partnered with entrepreneur Charles Woodrow Pappe to launch the inaugural Sonic Drive‑In franchise. The first location opened in Woodward, Oklahoma, in 1956, a deal sealed with nothing more than a handshake. This pioneering site paved the way for additional drive‑ins in Enid and Stillwater by 1958.
title: Sonic Drive-In

text: The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight is based at RAF Coningsby in Lincolnshire, where it is administratively assigned to No. 1 Group RAF.
title: Battle of Britain Memorial Flight

text: The track “Rock You Like a Hurricane” was performed by the German rock band Scorpions. It was issued as the lead single from their ninth studio album, Love at First Sting (1984). The music was composed by Rudolf Schenker, and the lyrics were written by vocalist Klaus Meine along with drummer Herman Rarebell. The song’s lyrics also reference the title of the album on which it originally appeared, Love at First Sting.
title: Rock You Like a Hurricane

text: Kansas’ men’s basketball program holds the Division I record for conference championships, having won a total of 61 titles. This achievement places the Jayhawks at the top of the list for the most conference championships in college basketball history.
title: Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball

text: The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH)—the body that establishes the criteria for measuring skyscrapers and publishes the ranking of the world’s highest completed structures—lists Burj Khalifa in Dubai as the tallest building, with a height of 828 m (2,717 ft).
title: List of tallest buildings

text: The track titled “Brother”—which includes the lyric “let me be your shelter”—was recorded and performed by the American Christian rock band Needtobreathe.
title: Brother (Needtobreathe song)

text: Just before President Obama’s 2014 State of the Union address, media reports highlighted the extreme concentration of wealth in the United States. They noted that the richest 1% of Americans owned about 40 % of the nation’s total wealth, whereas the bottom 80% possessed only roughly 7 %. Subsequent coverage added that the “richest 1 percent in the United States now own more additional income than the bottom 90 percent.” In other words, only 1% of the U.S. population controls a disproportionately large share of the country’s wealth.
title: Wealth inequality in the United States

text: In 2007, the wealthiest 1% of the United States population owned about 35 percent of the country’s total wealth, making this tiny share of people the primary controllers of national assets.
title: Wealth inequality in the United States

text: Western Australia supplied the vast majority of Australia’s iron ore, producing 474 million tonnes in 2011 – about 97 % of the country’s total output. The state also holds the world’s largest Economic Demonstrated Resources of iron ore, accounting for roughly 22 % of global reserves.
title: Iron ore mining in Western Australia

text: Iron ore deposits have long been identified in Australia, but large‑scale extraction only began after the federal government removed its export embargo in 1960. Although production was modest—under 10 million tonnes annually through the early 1960s—it surged dramatically in the following decades. By the mid‑1970s, output had climbed to about 100 million tonnes, with the bulk of that coming from Western Australia. After a slight dip in the 1980s, production rebounded, reaching 150 million tonnes nationwide by 1997 and 200 million tonnes by 2003. Thus, the primary source of Australian iron ore is Western Australia.
title: Iron ore mining in Western Australia

text: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is a 2017 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team of the same name. Produced by Marvel Studios and released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, it serves as the sequel to the 2014 movie Guardians of the Galaxy and marks the fifteenth entry in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The picture was written and directed by James Gunn and features an ensemble cast that includes Chris Pratt, Zoe Saldana, Dave Bautista, Vin Diesel, Bradley Cooper, Michael Rooker, Karen Gillan, Pom Klementieff, Elizabeth Debicki, Chris Sullivan, Sean Gunn, Sylvester Stallone, and Kurt Russell. In the story, the Guardians travel across the cosmos while helping Peter Quill uncover details about his mysterious parentage.
title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2

text: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 made its debut in Tokyo on April 10, 2017 and reached U.S. audiences on May 5, 2017, marking its release year as 2017.
title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2

text: The CW confirmed on May 8, 2014 that the fourth installment of *Hart of Dixie* would be produced as a ten‑episode season. This final season launched on November 15, 2014, and the series was later announced as cancelled on May 7, 2015.
title: Hart of Dixie (Season 4)

text: "Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon" was written by American musician Neil Diamond, whose 1967 recording for Bang Records reached No. 10 on the U.S. pop singles chart. The song later gained renewed prominence when it was included on the 1994 *Pulp Fiction* soundtrack, performed by the rock band Urge Overkill. Other artists who have recorded the track include Cliff Richard (1968), Jackie Edwards (1968), the Biddu Orchestra (1978), and 16 Volt (1998).
title: Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon

text: Although Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha acted as the temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly, the members subsequently chose Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the body’s first president. The assembly’s vice‑president was Harendra Coomar Mookerjee, a Christian from Bengal who had formerly served as vice‑chancellor of Calcutta University. Mookerjee also chaired the Minorities Committee and was later appointed governor of West Bengal after India became a republic. Jurist B. N. Rau served as the constitutional adviser, drafting the original version of the constitution and later becoming a judge at the Permanent Court of International Justice in The Hague.
title: Constituent Assembly of India

text: The series originated with the debut of its first movie, The Fast and the Furious, which was released in 2001.
title: The Fast and the Furious

text: Emma Pillsbury, the guidance counselor at William McKinley High, eventually reunites with glee club director Will Schuester after a period of separation. Their reconciliation culminates in a wedding that takes place in the season finale of the fourth season.
title: Emma Pillsbury

text: When the USS Maine (ACR‑1) exploded, it was anchored in Havana Harbor.
title: USS Maine (ACR-1)

text: The armored cruiser USS Maine (ACR‑1) was lying in Havana Harbor when, on the evening of 15 February 1898, she suddenly detonated and sank, killing the majority of her crew. The ship had been dispatched to safeguard American interests amid the Cuban revolt against Spain, but the explosion occurred without warning while she was anchored in that Cuban port.
title: USS Maine (ACR-1)

text: Anant Chaturdashi marks the conclusion of the Hindu celebration called Ganeshotsav, the festival devoted to the deity Ganesh. It occurs ten or eleven days after Ganesh Chaturthi, and on this final day every Ganesh idol that has been installed in homes and public spaces is carried in lively processions to a river, lake, or the sea for immersion. The idols are accompanied by music and dance as they are set afloat, symbolising Ganesh’s departure until his return the following year.
title: Anant Chaturdashi

text: A simple sentence contains just one clause. When two or more independent clauses are linked, the construction is a compound sentence. When a sentence includes at least one independent clause together with at least one dependent clause, it is called **A complex sentence**. Any collection of words that lacks an independent clause is regarded as an incomplete sentence, also known as a sentence fragment.
title: Sentence clause structure

text: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, usually shortened to The Wealth of Nations, is the seminal work of Scottish economist and moral philosopher Adam Smith. First issued in 1776, the volume delivers one of the earliest systematic accounts of what builds nations' wealth and continues to serve as a foundational text in classical economics. By analysing the economy at the dawn of the Industrial Revolution, Smith explores broad themes such as the division of labour, productivity, and free‑market principles.
title: The Wealth of Nations

text: Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a sovereign nation that includes the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania, and numerous smaller islands. It is the largest country in Oceania, ranking as the world’s sixth‑largest by total area. Its neighboring states are Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and East Timor to the north; the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu to the north‑east; and New Zealand to the south‑east. Canberra serves as the capital, and Sydney is its biggest urban area.
title: Australia

text: During the Hand of Thrawn Duology, Luke Skywalker—now a Jedi Master—reunites with Mara Jade, who has deepened her Force knowledge after studying at Luke’s Jedi Academy. He falls in love with Mara Jade, and the two eventually marry. Later, in Edge of Victory: Rebirth, their son is born and they name him Ben in honor of Obi‑Wan Kenobi’s pseudonym.
title: Luke Skywalker

text: Jack Barry, the creator of The Joker's Wild, was the show's original host and continued to present every version of the program until his death in May 1984.
title: The Joker's Wild

text: A toddler is defined as a child who is between 12 months and 36 months old. Once a child reaches 36 months, they are no longer considered a toddler. The toddler stage is marked by rapid cognitive, emotional, and social growth, and the term comes from “to toddle,” describing the unsteady walking typical of children in this age range.
title: Toddler

text: Ordeal by Innocence is a BBC drama presented in a three‑part format, first airing in April 2018. The series adapts Agatha Christie’s novel of the same title and follows the earlier English‑language filmed versions. Its cast includes Bill Nighy, Anna Chancellor, Alice Eve and Eleanor Tomlinson, among others.
title: Ordeal by Innocence (TV series)

text: In British English, “fancy dress” denotes a costume. A fancy dress party is a social event in which attendees put on a costume, the same concept that American English calls a costume party.
title: Costume party

text: The American historical‑fiction drama series *The Bastard Executioner*, created by Kurt Sutter and shown on FX from September 15 2015 through November 17 2015, was cancelled after just one season; FX announced the series’ end on November 18 2015, confirming that it ran for only a single season.
title: The Bastard Executioner

text: Jean Valjean set out for Montfermeil with the intention of rescuing Cosette, the eight‑year‑old daughter of Fantine, because he had promised to do so.
title: Jean Valjean

text: The Bantu Education Act of 1953 (later renamed the Black Education Act) was a South African segregation law that gave legal force to several elements of the apartheid system.  Its chief provision was **enforcing racially separated educational facilities**, a measure that extended to universities, which were designated “tribal,” and led most missionary schools to close when state support was withdrawn.
title: Bantu Education Act, 1953

text: From the 2014‑15 season onward the FA Cup’s free‑to‑air television rights moved back to BBC Sport after ITV’s contract ended. The BBC will show the final on BBC One, while BT Sport retains the pay‑TV coverage. Under this new deal the BBC will broadcast roughly the same number of matches as ITV previously did and will have the first pick for each round.
title: FA Cup

text: Howard University's 256‑acre campus, frequently referred to as “The Mecca,” is located in northwest Washington. The grounds span roughly 1.04 km² (0.400 sq mi). Following World War I, the university underwent major improvements, including new buildings designed under the direction of architect Albert Cassell. The combined value of Howard's buildings and plant is estimated at $567.6 million.
title: Howard University

text: The earliest covenant recorded in the Old Testament is the Noahic Covenant; unlike later agreements that focus mainly on the Israelites, this covenant extends its promise to all of humanity.
title: Covenant (biblical)

text: The Noahic Covenant (Genesis 9:8–17) extends to every human being and to all other living creatures. In this agreement God promises never again to destroy all life on the earth by flood, and He establishes the rainbow as the sign of the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature on the earth.
title: Covenant (biblical)

text: The Indian National Congress, founded in 1885, was the first modern nationalist movement to arise in the British Empire in Asia and Africa. Although it had been active since the late nineteenth century, it was after 1920 that the party, under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, became the principal leader of the Indian independence movement. At its peak the Congress counted more than 15 million members and drew over 70 million participants, eventually steering India to independence from Great Britain.
title: Indian National Congress

text: During World War II, Alan Turing served at the Government Code and Cypher School’s Bletchley Park centre, where he headed Hut 8, the unit tasked with deciphering German naval communications. He refined the pre‑war Polish bombe and introduced additional techniques that dramatically accelerated the process of determining the settings of the German Enigma machine. Turing’s work was instrumental in breaking the intercepted Enigma traffic, enabling the Allies to win critical engagements such as the Battle of the Atlantic.
title: Alan Turing

text: A foreign exchange option—often referred to as an FX option or currency option—is a derivative contract that grants the holder the right, but not the obligation, to exchange money denominated in one currency for money in another currency at a pre‑agreed exchange rate on a specified date.
title: Foreign exchange option

text: The Nigerian House of Representatives is composed of 360 members, each chosen from a single‑member constituency through a simple‑majority (first‑past‑the‑post) election, and they serve four‑year terms. The presiding officer of this chamber is the Speaker.
title: House of Representatives (Nigeria)

text: Daniel Francis Haggerty (November 19 1941 – January 15 2016) was an American performer best remembered for starring as the title character in the television series *The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams*. The actor who portrayed Grizzly Adams was "Dan" Haggerty.
title: Dan Haggerty

text: The 1963 hit single “Blame It on the Bossa Nova” was performed by **Eydie Gormé**. Written by lyricist Cynthia Weil and composer Barry Mann, the song rose to number 7 on Billboard’s Hot 100 in March 1963 and later peaked at number 23 on the UK singles chart.
title: Blame It on the Bossa Nova

text: Konakuppakatil Gopinathan Balakrishnan, born on 12 May 1945, held the position of Chief Justice of India and subsequently served as the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission of India.
title: K. G. Balakrishnan

text: The Los Angeles Lakers are a professional basketball franchise that competes in the NBA’s Western Conference Pacific Division and hosts its home games at the Staples Center in Los Angeles. Over the course of their history the club has amassed 16 league titles, with 11 of those victories occurring after the team moved to Los Angeles. Their most recent championship was in 2010.
title: Los Angeles Lakers

text: The Los Angeles Lakers’ early years featured Hall of Famers Elgin Baylor and Jerry West, and the team reached the NBA Finals six times during the 1960s, though each appearance ended in defeat to the Boston Celtics. After adding four‑time MVP Wilt Chamberlain in 1968, the Lakers finally broke through, winning their first championship in Los Angeles in 1972 under head coach Bill Sharman. Subsequent eras brought stars such as Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar, Magic Johnson, and James Worthy, with the “Showtime” squads of the 1980s capturing five titles, including the franchise’s inaugural Finals victory over the Celtics in 1985. The early 1990s were lean until Shaquille O’Neal and Kobe Bryant joined the roster in 1996, and under Hall of Fame coach Phil Jackson the team secured three straight championships from 2000 through 2002. After losses in the 2004 and 2008 Finals, the Lakers added two more rings by beating the Orlando Magic in 2009 and the Boston Celtics in 2010. **The most recent championship the Lakers won was in 2010.**
title: Los Angeles Lakers

text: American country singer Toby Keith wrote and performed the track “Should’ve Been a Cowboy.” The song was issued as his debut single on February 8 1993 and appeared on his self‑titled first album. By June 5 1993 it had risen to number one on both the U.S. Hot Country Songs chart and Canada’s RPM Country Tracks, and it also peaked at No. 93 on the Billboard Hot 100.
title: Should've Been a Cowboy

text: Georgia is organized into 159 counties, making it the state with the second‑greatest number of counties after Texas, which has 254. The Georgia State Constitution grants each of these 159 counties home‑rule powers to address purely local issues. In addition, the state contains eight consolidated city‑county governments, including Athens–Clarke County, Augusta–Richmond County, Columbus–Muscogee County, Georgetown–Quitman County, Statenville–Echols County, Macon–Bibb County, Cusseta–Chattahoochee County, and Preston‑Webster County.
title: List of counties in Georgia (U.S. state)

text: Matt Flinders, born Sylvan Louis Bonett around 1937 in Alexandria, Egypt, emerged as a popular singer and TV presenter in Australia in the late 1960s. In 1969 he released a cover of the song “Picking Up Pebbles,” which climbed into the top‑five of the charts. He followed that hit with a successful version of “Butterfly” in 1971 and later hosted his own ABC‑TV variety programmes, The Matt Flinders Show (1972) and Matt Flinders and Friends (1973).
title: Matt Flinders

text: Matt Flinders released the single “Picking Up Pebbles” in late 1969; the track was a cover of a 1968 song by UK artist Johnny Curtis (also known as Bobby Kerr) and reached No. 4 on the Go‑Set National Top 40 singles chart.
title: Matt Flinders

text: In contemporary Indian customs, a man who decides to wear a wedding ring places it on the left ring finger, even though men generally prefer to wear other rings on the right hand.
title: Ring finger

text: The English actor Bernard Hill (born 17 December 1944) portrayed King Théoden in Peter Jackson’s The Lord of the Rings film trilogy.
title: Bernard Hill

text: Australian actress Claire Rhiannon Holt (born 11 June 1988) is recognised for a number of TV and film roles; among them, she portrayed the character Emma in the series H2O: Just Add Water.
title: Claire Holt

text: The Spanish Steps—known in Italian as the Scalinata di Trinità dei Monti—are situated in Rome, Italy. They ascend a steep incline that links the lower Piazza di Spagna with the upper Piazza Trinità dei Monti, which is dominated by the Trinità dei Monti church at its summit.
title: Spanish Steps

text: Hydrogen bonds can form either between distinct molecules or within different regions of a single molecule, and their energies typically lie between roughly 1 kcal mol⁻¹ and 40 kcal mol⁻¹—stronger than van der Waals interactions but weaker than covalent or ionic bonds. Importantly, hydrogen bonding is not confined to water; it also occurs in inorganic molecules such as water and in organic macromolecules like DNA and proteins.
title: Hydrogen bond

text: The pop duo Boy Meets Girl released their song “Waiting for a Star to Fall” in 1988; the single became a global hit and is regarded as the group’s signature track.
title: Waiting for a Star to Fall

text: Skat is a three‑player trick‑taking card game that originated in Germany in the early nineteenth century. It is considered, together with Doppelkopf, one of the most widely played card games in Germany and the Silesian area.
title: Skat (card game)

text: Estimates of how common naturally blonde hair is differ, but the lowest figures indicate that roughly 2% of the world’s population has naturally blond hair. This rarity is especially evident in adulthood, where light‑blond hair is uncommon, while higher regional estimates—such as about 16% in the United States—reflect local variation.
title: Human hair color

text: The colony of Maryland was initially founded by the English, who arrived in substantial numbers in 1634 and established a permanent settlement. Their arrival marked the first European presence that created the lasting colony.
title: History of Maryland

text: Gary Player holds the record for the greatest number of Masters Tournament appearances, having played in 52 editions of the event.
title: Masters Tournament

text: During the era of nationwide alcohol prohibition, anyone who wanted to drink would slip into the hidden venues called **Speakeasies**, which had become extremely popular as the go‑to places for illicit drinking.
title: Prohibition in the United States

text: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe, often simply called The Fringe, is the world’s largest arts festival. Founded in 1947 as an alternative to the Edinburgh International Festival, it is held each August each year in Edinburgh, Scotland, featuring thousands of performances across hundreds of venues.
title: Edinburgh Festival Fringe

text: After fleeing her abusive husband and assuming the name Katie, the heroine settles in Southport, North Carolina. There she finds employment at a seafood restaurant, becomes friends with her neighbor Jo, and gets acquainted with Alex, the proprietor of the town’s general store.
title: Safe Haven (novel)

text: The expression “baby boomer” entered print for the first time in 1970, when an article in The Washington Post employed the term. The Oxford English Dictionary records this as the earliest known usage. The phrase grew out of earlier descriptions of the post‑World II surge in births, which journalists had labeled a “baby boom.”
title: Baby boomers

text: In the United States presidential election of 1928, which took place on Tuesday, November 6, the Republican candidate and then Secretary of Commerce, Herbert Hoover, won the presidency.
title: United States presidential election, 1928

text: In the tale “How the Grinch Stole Christmas!”, the Grinch lives in a cave on Mount Crumpit with only a single companion—a dog. This canine, called Max, is described as loyal despite being unloved by his master. When the Grinch hatches his plan to pilfer the Whos’ Christmas celebrations, he outfits Max in a reindeer costume and makes him pull the sleigh down the mountain toward Whoville.
title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas!

text: During the NFL Draft, representatives from each team are present to make the selections. At any given moment one franchise is “on the clock,” and that team must submit its pick within a prescribed time limit—10 minutes in the first round, 7 minutes in the second, 5 minutes from the third through the sixth, and 4 minutes for the seventh round and any compensatory picks. If a team fails to decide before its clock expires, it may still submit a choice later, but the next team on the clock can select first, potentially taking a player the earlier team was considering. This process shows that the players are chosen by each team.
title: National Football League Draft

text: The rear-view mirror (also written as rearview mirror) is a reflective device fitted in automobiles and other vehicles, allowing the driver to look backward through the vehicle’s rear window (rear windshield).
title: Rear-view mirror

text: In automobiles, the rear-view mirror is typically mounted on the upper part of the windshield using a double‑swivel bracket. This mounting lets the driver adjust the mirror’s height and viewing angle to suit any individual, and it can swing harmlessly out of the way if it is struck during a collision.
title: Rear-view mirror

text: Central Germany (German: Mitteldeutschland) is an economic and cultural region that lies within the nation of Germany. Its precise limits vary with context, but it is commonly understood to encompass parts of the federal states of Saxony, Thuringia and Saxony‑Anhalt, or, in a narrower sense, the Leipzig‑Halle metropolitan area.
title: Central Germany (cultural area)

text: In the United States, people who want to shoot at a public range generally do not have to obtain a firearms license or complete any extensive training beyond learning how the gun works (when it is rented) and becoming acquainted with the range’s safety rules. Typically, no license or advanced training beyond just firearm familiarization (for rentals) and range rules familiarization is usually required for using a shooting range in the United States; the only common requirement is that the shooter must be at least 18 or 21 years old (or be accompanied by a legal guardian) and must sign a liability waiver before shooting.
title: Shooting ranges in the United States

text: The Baca surname originates in New Mexico. Its earliest known ancestors, Cristóbal Baca (also recorded as Vaca) and his wife Ana Ortiz, arrived in 1600 to help reinforce the Spanish colonial province of Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico and established the family there, later relocating to Grants, New Mexico.
title: Baca family of New Mexico

text: The Baca surname is rooted in the region of New Mexico, where the family bearing this name has long been established. Although the name is sometimes linked to the Spanish phrase “Cabeza de Vaca,” its primary association and origin lie in New Mexico.
title: Baca family of New Mexico

text: Porter Airlines, a regional carrier headquartered in Toronto, conducts its operations out of Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport, the airport situated on the Toronto Islands in the city of Toronto, Ontario, Canada.
title: Porter Airlines

text: After the Judiciary Committee reports a Supreme Court nomination, the entire Senate votes on the candidate, and confirmation—or rejection—depends on **a simple majority vote**. Historically, the Senate has rarely turned down nominees; the most recent full‑Senate rejection occurred in 1987 when the body declined to confirm Robert Bork.
title: Appointment and confirmation to the Supreme Court of the United States

text: In 1921, Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize, and the citation highlighted his simple yet revolutionary proposal that light is emitted and absorbed as discrete quanta, rather than honoring his more mathematically demanding work on special and general relativity.
title: Wave–particle duality

text: Deposition, a specific kind of phase transition, is the thermodynamic process in which a gaseous substance converts directly into a solid without first passing through the liquid state. The opposite transformation is sublimation, and because of this relationship deposition is also referred to as desublimation.
title: Deposition (phase transition)

text: In chemistry, the term pH stands for the **potential of hydrogen**. It denotes a numerical scale that indicates how acidic or basic an aqueous solution is. The scale is derived from the base‑10 logarithm of the hydrogen‑ion activity (or concentration) in the solution. A pH value below 7 signals acidity, while a value above 7 indicates basicity. Pure water at 25 °C is neutral, registering a pH of 7.
title: pH

text: Alfred P. Aldrich, a politician from Barnwell, warned that if a Republican were elected president in 1860 South Carolina would have to withdraw from the Union. He claimed that secession was the only way for the state to preserve slavery and to curb the growing power of the anti‑slavery Republican Party, whose success he believed would lead to the destruction of the South.
title: South Carolina in the American Civil War

text: Folded mountain ranges, including those that dominate Pennsylvania and the towering Himalaya, develop where two tectonic plates are forced toward one another. This tectonic setting is a convergent plate boundary. When continental edges bearing thick accumulations of sedimentary rock collide, the stacked layers are compressed and crumple, much like a tablecloth being pushed across a surface, especially if a mechanically weak layer such as salt is present.
title: Fold mountains

text: The series of product‑tampering deaths known as the Chicago Tylenol murders unfolded in the Chicago metropolitan area in 1982, when a number of people died after ingesting Tylenol‑branded acetaminophen capsules that had been contaminated with potassium cyanide.
title: Chicago Tylenol murders

text: Vincent van Gogh’s collection titled *Sunflowers* (French: *Tournesols*) consists of two separate series of still‑life paintings. The first series was produced in Paris in 1887 and portrays the blossoms lying on the ground, while the second series, painted a year later in Arles, depicts a bouquet of sunflowers arranged in a vase. In van Gogh’s later thinking both groups were associated with his friend Paul Gauguin, who bought two of the Paris versions, and he later incorporated the works into his decorative scheme for the Yellow House in Arles.
title: Sunflowers (Van Gogh series)

text: The most recent Christmas Day on which snow fell in England was in 2009, when a white Christmas was reported in several areas of Britain. This event marked the first time the United Kingdom experienced a snowy Christmas since 2004.
title: White Christmas (weather)

text: Muhammad Ali, who was still using the name Cassius Clay at the time, earned the light‑heavyweight gold medal at the 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome when he was 18 years old.
title: Muhammad Ali

text: Castleford is a town located in the metropolitan borough of Wakefield in West Yorkshire, England. The River Aire flows through the town, meeting the River Calder to the north of its centre, and the Aire and Calder Navigation also runs nearby.
title: Castleford

text: The track titled “Only Love Can Break Your Heart” was written and originally performed by Neil Young. Over the years, numerous groups have recorded their own versions, such as Saint Etienne, who released a single cover in 1990.
title: Only Love Can Break Your Heart

text: During a visit to Sarajevo, Bosnia, Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria – the heir presumptive to the Austro‑Hungarian throne – and his wife Sophie, Duchess of Hohenberg, were fatally shot by Gavrilo Princip on 28 June 1914. The attack was carried out by a group of six conspirators coordinated by Danilo Ilić, and it set off a chain of events that led directly to the outbreak of the First World War.
title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria

text: In larger organisms the body’s low surface‑area‑to‑volume ratio means that organs must contain highly folded or branched structures—such as gills, pulmonary alveoli, and spongy mesophyll—to supply enough area for the exchange of gases. The quantity of surface provided by these convoluted regions directly determines the capacity for effective gas exchange. Consequently, the amount of surface area present in many types of organs is a critical factor in how well they can perform gas exchange.
title: Gas exchange

text: The earliest recorded case of a book being turned into a motion picture happened in 1924, when director Erich von Stroheim produced the film *Greed* as a literal adaptation of Frank Norris’s novel *McTeague*.
title: Film adaptation

text: Chyme, the semi‑fluid mixture of partially digested food produced in the stomach, exits the stomach by passing through the pyloric valve and enters the duodenum, the initial segment of the small intestine.
title: Chyme

text: Sedimentary rock forms an extensive veneer over the continents, covering roughly 73 % of the Earth’s current land surface. This widespread surface layer makes sedimentary rock the dominant type of rock on the planet’s exposed crust.
title: Sedimentary rock

text: In 1774, after the Boston Tea Party, the British Parliament enacted a group of punitive statutes that American Patriots referred to as **The Intolerable Acts**. These laws were designed to punish the Massachusetts colonists for their resistance. In Britain, the same legislation was known as the **Coercive Acts**.
title: Intolerable Acts

text: Zachary John Quinto (born June 2, 1977) is an American actor and film producer who portrays Spock in the rebooted Star Trek film series, beginning with the 2009 movie and continuing in its sequels, Star Trek Into Darkness (2013) and Star Trek Beyond (2016).
title: Zachary Quinto

text: The surname Taylor goes back to the Old French word tailleur, meaning “cutter” or “tailor.”  It began as a Norman occupational name in medieval France, later spreading to the British Isles.
title: Taylor (surname)

text: The Cleveland Cavaliers made their debut in the NBA Finals in 2007, which also marked LeBron James’s first appearance in the championship series. Game 1 of that series was the franchise’s inaugural Finals contest and the first such game for every Cavs player except reserve point guard Eric Snow. Opposing them, the San Antonio Spurs arrived with recent Finals experience, having reached the championship round three times in the previous eight seasons and winning each time. Led by Tim Duncan, Tony Parker and Manu Ginóbili, the Spurs captured the opening game, holding LeBron James to 14 points on 4‑of‑16 shooting.
title: 2007 NBA Finals

text: The track “Lotta Love”—which contains the lyric “It’s gonna take a lot of love”—was written and recorded by Neil Young, appearing on his 1978 album *Comes a Time*.
title: Lotta Love

text: In Disney’s 1995 animated feature *Pocahontas*, the role of English settler John Smith is voiced by Mel Gibson.
title: Pocahontas (1995 film)

text: During the Siege of Béxar, Mexican General Cos dispatched his officer **Sanchez Navarro** to the Alamo with orders to “go save those brave men… approach the enemy and obtain the best terms possible.”  Navarro obeyed, returned to the plaza, and announced the imminent surrender to the troops.  Although several officers protested, insisting that the Morelos Battalion had never surrendered, Navarro remained firm.  After a bugle call for a parley went unanswered, he raised a flag of truce at 7 a.m., effecting the surrender of the Mexican garrison to the Texian forces.
title: Siege of Béxar

text: In suspension‑bridge terminology, the distance measured between the two towers—i.e., the length of the roadway that is suspended between them—is called the span. This measurement is the primary way engineers compare the size of different suspension bridges.
title: List of longest suspension bridge spans

text: The initial screen version of Stephen King’s novel *It* was produced as a 1990 American supernatural‑horror drama miniseries. It was directed by Tommy Lee Wallace and adapted for television by Lawrence D. Cohen.
title: It (miniseries)

text: Following Doug Diemoz’s departure in April 2017, Crate & Barrel announced that Neela Montgomery would assume the position of chief executive officer.
title: Crate & Barrel

text: Texhoma is a town in Texas County, Oklahoma, United States, positioned directly on the Texas–Oklahoma state line. The border separates the Oklahoma side of the community from its twin, Texhoma, Texas, making the town a divided city that straddles both states. Its name is a blend of the two state names. The settlement originated when the Rock Island Railroad laid tracks through the area, and its local economy has long been based on ranching and livestock.
title: Texhoma, Oklahoma

text: Arousal regulation is the primary focus of the sport‑psychology sub‑field of performance enhancement. It involves attaining and maintaining an optimal level of cognitive and physiological activation so that athletes can maximize their performance. When activation becomes too high, athletes may use relaxation techniques such as progressive muscle relaxation, breathing exercises, or meditation; when activation is too low, energizing strategies like listening to music or receiving cueing can be employed. This regulation of arousal underpins the efforts to enhance athletic performance.
title: Sport psychology

text: The Quiet Man is set in the 1920s, when Sean Thornton—an Irish‑born American who grew up in Pittsburgh—travels back to Ireland to reclaim his family’s farm in Inisfree. There he meets the spirited Mary Kate Danaher, whose brother, the boisterous Squire “Red” Will Danaher, also covets the property. As local figures such as Father Lonergan and the matchmaker Michaleen Oge Flynn intervene, the story unfolds against the backdrop of this early‑twentieth‑century Irish community.
title: The Quiet Man

text: In the story “A Bend in the Road,” Jonah’s second‑grade teacher—once a resident of Baltimore who relocated to New Bern after a painful divorce—volunteers to tutor Jonah because she cannot have children herself. She is fond of both Miles and Jonah, and she often spends time with them. When she learns that her own brother, Brian, was Missy’s killer, she is devastated.
title: A Bend in the Road

text: At the start of the tale the murderer is unknown, prompting Miles to pursue Otis Timson after hearing that he bragged about Missy’s death. Later, Sarah’s brother, Brian, confides in her that he was the killer, explaining that the killing was accidental. When Sarah finally tells Miles, he reacts with anger and wants to punish Brian, but after hearing Brian’s version of events, Miles revisits the scene and begins to suspect the confession may be truthful. He follows Brian to a cemetery, extracts a promise from him to pursue something meaningful, and ultimately releases him. Brian later becomes an emergency‑room physician and has saved six lives.
title: A Bend in the Road

text: The one‑child policy was formally ended when China adopted a two‑child policy; the new legislation went into force on January 1, 2016, after the standing committee of the National People's Congress approved it on December 27, 2015. Earlier, on October 29, 2015, officials reported that the existing law would be revised to allow two children per family.
title: One-child policy

text: The 2017 ICC Champions Trophy, the eighth edition of the tournament featuring the eight highest‑ranked One Day International sides, took place in England and Wales between 1 June and 18 June 2017. In the final at The Oval, Pakistan secured its inaugural title, defeating India by 180 runs—a margin that remains the greatest run difference ever recorded in the final of an ICC ODI competition.
title: 2017 ICC Champions Trophy

text: The sixth and final season of the American drama series Nashville, which premiered on CMT on January 4, 2018, is composed of 16 episodes.
title: Nashville (season 6)

text: John Quincy Adams (July 11 1767 – February 23 1848) was an American statesman who held numerous positions—diplomat, minister, ambassador, treaty negotiator, United States Senator, and Representative from Massachusetts—and he served as the sixth President of the United States from 1825 to 1829.
title: John Quincy Adams

text: Beorn is the character in J. R. R. Tolkien’s novel *The Hobbit* who possesses the ability to change his shape into that of a great black bear. He is described as a “skin‑changer,” a man capable of assuming the bear’s form.
title: Beorn

text: Reba McEntire revealed on December 15, 2016 that she was preparing her first gospel album, *Sing It Now: Songs of Faith & Hope*. The double‑disc collection was issued by Nash Icon/Rockin’ R Records on **February 3, 2017**, and the record’s lead single—“Back to God”—was released alongside the album.
title: Reba McEntire

text: The doctrine known as **separationism** calls for a clear division between religious institutions and government authority. In contrast, the Supreme Court’s decision in Zorach v. Clauson upheld accommodationism, reasoning that the nation’s institutions presume a Supreme Being and that governmental acknowledgment of God does not amount to establishing a state church, illustrating that the principle of separation is not always applied in an absolute manner.
title: Separation of church and state in the United States

text: In the Alvin and the Chipmunks film series, which combines live‑action performances with computer‑generated animation, the role of David Seville is performed by actor Jason Lee. Although Ross Bagdasarian, Jr. does not provide any voices for the movies, the productions are created in partnership with Bagdasarian Productions, the company that holds the characters’ rights.
title: David Seville

text: The series culminates in a finale that centers on the revelation that Sam’s leaps are being guided by an unseen force; this concluding episode is titled **"Mirror Image"**. Throughout the show, each episode follows Sam’s reaction to a new leap, his collaboration with Al and Ziggy to resolve the situation, and typically ends with a cliffhanger that previews the next leap. In the final installment, the characters’ earlier speculation about random leaping gives way to the understanding that someone—or something—is directing Sam’s jumps, making “Mirror Image” the decisive episode that ties this theme together.
title: Quantum Leap

text: The informal gathering called the Tam‑Tams takes place every Sunday afternoon on the eastern side of Mount Royal Park (Fletcher’s Field) during the warmer months. Participants—including drummers, dancers, vendors and visitors—congregate in the open space, while nearby Jeanne‑Mance Park serves as the city’s main outdoor sporting area. Although the event is neither officially sanctioned nor sponsored, it consistently begins around 10:30am and continues until sunset.
title: Tam-Tams

text: The expression “train of thought” was first introduced in the 1651 work *Leviathan*, where Thomas Hobbes in his Leviathan elaborated the term (though his usage differed somewhat from later meanings).
title: Train of thought

text: Iodine (symbol I, atomic number 53) is a chemical element that appears in the periodic table as a member of the halogen group. It is the heaviest of the stable halogens. At standard temperature and pressure it is a lustrous, purple‑black solid that readily sublimes, producing a violet vapor. The element was first isolated by the French chemist Bernard Courtois in 1811 and received its name two years later from Joseph‑Louis Gay‑Lussac, who chose the Greek term ἰωδης meaning “violet‑coloured.”
title: Iodine

text: When the Hejaz and Nejd kingdoms were united, the new nation received the official Arabic name al‑Mamlakah al‑ʻArabīyah as‑Suʻūdīyah (المملكة العربية السعودية) by royal decree on 23 September 1932, issued by its founder Abdulaziz Al Saud (Ibn Saud). Although English speakers usually render this as “the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the literal translation of the Arabic title is “the Saudi Arab kingdom.”
title: Saudi Arabia

text: Archaeological research identifies the first known civilization as having arisen in the area of Mesopotamia, situated within the Fertile Crescent. Evidence places this society earlier than any other complex culture, so Mesopotamia is regarded as the oldest civilization recognized by scholars. Although later advanced societies later appeared independently in regions such as the Indo‑Gangetic Plain, the Yellow River basin, Mesoamerica, and the Andean coast, none of them predates the Mesopotamian civilization.
title: Cradle of civilization

text: The earliest known non‑nomadic agrarian societies arose in the river valley formed by the convergence of the Tigris and Euphrates. In **Mesopotamia**, this meeting of waters produced rich, irrigable soil and a dependable water supply, enabling the development of settled communities and the first cities such as Eridu and Ur. Because these river‑valley cultures represent the oldest known settled civilizations, the region of Mesopotamia is commonly referred to as the cradle of civilization and is regarded as the place where the oldest civilization known to humanity originated.
title: Cradle of civilization

text: The extensor pollicis longus tendon runs along the back of the forearm; it is located dorsally on the forearm. This tendon is part of the extensor pollicis longus muscle, a skeletal muscle that lies on the dorsal surface of the forearm in human anatomy.
title: Extensor pollicis longus muscle

text: The Boston mayoral election of 2017 was held on Tuesday, November 7, 2017, to select the city's chief executive. Incumbent Democratic mayor Marty J. Walsh won re‑election to a second term, defeating District 7 City Councilor Tito Jackson and the long‑shot challengers Robert Cappucci and Joseph Wiley.
title: Boston mayoral election, 2017

text: The earliest potter’s wheels—called tournettes or slow wheels—first appeared around 4500 BC. These devices were turned slowly by hand or foot while a pot was being coiled, and they were used in the Near East. Only a modest range of vessels could be formed on a tournette, suggesting that the technique was limited to a small number of potters. The introduction of the slow wheel increased the efficiency of hand‑powered pottery production.
title: Potter's wheel

text: Anatomy is the scientific discipline that investigates the structure of human body parts. Although the same term can be applied to the study of other animals, it is most commonly understood to refer to human anatomy. In contrast, the study of plant structure is called plant anatomy, and the word zootomy is occasionally used when focusing specifically on animal bodies.
title: Anatomy

text: Anatomy, also known as human anatomy, is the basic medical science that studies the structure of the body’s parts. It is introduced to medical students early in their training, and can be organized either by bodily regions such as the head and chest or by functional systems such as the nervous or respiratory systems. Mastery of anatomy is essential for physicians, especially surgeons and specialists in diagnostic areas like radiology.
title: Anatomy

text: In 1967, Celtic became the first British team to win the competition, overturning a 1‑0 deficit after a Sandro Mazzola penalty to defeat Internazionale 2‑1 at the Estádio Nacional in Lisbon, with goals supplied by Tommy Gemmell and Stevie Chalmers. Managed by Jock Stein, the squad—later celebrated as the Lisbon Lions—was distinctive because every player hailed from within 30 miles (48 km) of Celtic Park in Glasgow.
title: European Cup and UEFA Champions League history

text: The Rugrats cartoon wrapped up its twelve‑year broadcast on August 1, 2004, finishing with a total of 172 episodes that were organized into 9 seasons.
title: List of Rugrats episodes

text: The abbreviation “IB” that appears on the IB board expands to International Baccalaureate. This name refers to the worldwide educational foundation that was created in 1968 and is based in Geneva, Switzerland. It administers four programmes—Primary Years, Middle Years, Diploma and Career‑related—each designed for specific age groups, and schools must receive authorization from the International Baccalaureate to deliver them.
title: International Baccalaureate

text: The International Baccalaureate’s governing body—commonly called the IB board—is organized as a Board of Governors that may include anywhere from fifteen to twenty‑five members. These governors are chosen by the Board itself following recommendations from the governance committee and nominations submitted by the Heads Council, Regional Councils, and the Board. To promote a mix of gender, cultural, and geographic representation, only three positions are ex officio: the Director General (who does not vote), the chair of the Examining Board, and the chair of the Heads Council.
title: International Baccalaureate

text: On October 20, 1977, a Convair CV‑240 that had been chartered by the rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd ran out of fuel and crashed in Gillsburg, Mississippi. The accident occurred near the end of the aircraft’s journey from Greenville, South Carolina, to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and the charter had been arranged through L&J Company of Addison, Texas.
title: 1977 Convair CV-240 crash

text: Cristiano Ronaldo, after starting his senior career with Sporting CP, moved to Manchester United when he was 18 years old, in 2003. Following his transfer, he helped the club secure an FA Cup in his first season and later contributed to multiple Premier League titles, a UEFA Champions League victory, and a FIFA Club World Cup.
title: Cristiano Ronaldo

text: The NFL introduced its salary‑cap system beginning with the 1994 season, initially establishing the cap at $34.6 million per team.
title: Salary cap

text: On Freedom Day, 27 April 2000, South Africa unveiled the present national coat of arms, which replaced the earlier design that had been in use since 1910. The new emblem carries the motto ǃke e: ǀxarra ǁke in the Khoisan language of the ǀXam people, literally meaning “diverse people unite,” while the former Latin motto was Ex Unitate Vires (“From unity, strength”).
title: Coat of arms of South Africa

text: The woolly mammoth was a large, cold‑adapted proboscidean that roamed the mammoth steppe of northern Eurasia and North America during the last ice age. Adults reached shoulder heights of up to three metres and could weigh several metric tons, while newborn calves weighed around ninety kilograms. Its thick fur, short ears and tail, and massive curved tusks helped it survive the frigid climate. Like modern elephants, it used its trunk and tusks for manipulating objects and foraging. Examination of its feeding habits indicates that its diet consisted mainly of grass and sedges. The animal’s molars were replaced six times over its lifetime, supporting a herbivorous lifestyle that could sustain individuals for up to six decades.
title: Woolly mammoth

text: Studies of the intestinal remains of multiple woolly mammoths show that these Ice Age proboscideans survived chiefly on plant material, with their diet being dominated by grass and sedges. In addition to this primary intake, they also consumed a variety of other vegetation such as herbaceous and flowering plants, shrubs, mosses, and occasional tree matter, the exact mix varying by region. To sustain their massive bodies—an adult weighing around six tonnes—these animals likely spent many hours each day foraging, using the two‑fingered tip of their trunks to grasp short grasses and pull up tufts, as well as to pluck buds, flowers, leaves, and branches when available. Isotopic evidence further indicates a preference for C3 plants, distinguishing their feeding habits from those of contemporary herbivores like horses and rhinos.
title: Woolly mammoth

text: In the 2004 Rockstar North title Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, the hidden feature known as Hot Coffee is a normally inaccessible mini-game. Public awareness of this content grew after the 2005 Hot Coffee mod for the Windows version of the game was released, allowing players to access the mini‑game.
title: Hot Coffee mod

text: Mitosis is the cellular process that separates a single nucleus into two genetically identical daughter nuclei. The event proceeds through a series of stages—prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase—during which duplicated chromosomes condense and become linked to spindle fibers. These fibers draw one copy of each chromosome toward opposite poles of the cell, ultimately yielding two nuclei that contain the same genetic material. After the nuclei have formed, the cell may complete division by cytokinesis, producing two separate daughter cells. Errors in this sequence can lead to abnormal outcomes such as tripolar or multipolar mitosis, apoptosis, or mutations that may contribute to cancer.
title: Mitosis

text: The plan‑do‑check‑act (PDCA) model of performance improvement originates with W. Edwards Deming, who popularized the cycle and initially referred to it as the “Shewhart cycle.” Later in his career Deming revised the terminology to “Plan, Do, Study, Act” (PDSA) to stress analysis over mere inspection.
title: PDCA

text: Joseph Nye Welch (October 22, 1890 – October 6, 1960) was an American lawyer who served as chief counsel for the United States Army during the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations’ probe of alleged Communist activity, the Army–McCarthy hearings. In a famous confrontation with Senator Joseph McCarthy, Welch turned to the senator and asked, “Have you no sense of decency?” This exchange is regarded as a turning point in the history of McCarthyism.
title: Joseph N. Welch

text: De Beers once controlled up to nine‑tenths of the world’s rough‑diamond supply, but the market became more fragmented and competitive over time. As a result, its share of global rough diamonds dropped dramatically, reaching only 33% in 2013. This decline reflected the rise of alternative producers and greater market transparency.
title: De Beers

text: Shortly after her baby is born, Claire begins a romantic relationship with Alex Ryan, and Alex even makes plans to propose to her at an upcoming party. Later, while Claire, Tess and baby Charlotte are returning from town with party supplies, their Ute strikes a pothole, loses control and slides off a cliff, resulting in Claire’s death.
title: List of McLeod's Daughters characters

text: Located in Tarapur, Palghar, the Tarapur Atomic Power Station is India’s largest nuclear generating facility. Constructed under the 1963 123 Agreement between India, the United States and the IAEA, the plant first placed two boiling‑water reactors into commercial service on 28 October 1969, initially supplying 210 MW of electricity (later reduced to 160 MW because of technical issues). These reactors were the first of their kind in Asia. More recently, two 540 MW pressurised heavy‑water reactors were added, with Unit 4 entering commercial operation on 12 September 2005 and Unit 3 on 18 August 2006. The station’s primary output is Atomic Power for the national grid.
title: Tarapur Atomic Power Station

text: Most of Fender’s amplifier production was shifted to the Ensenada factory in Mexico in 1996, when the company moved the bulk of its amp manufacturing there. This relocation coincided with many of the Red Knob models being refitted with black control knobs and the earlier‑era “unscripted tailless” Fender logo. The Red Knob series, originally built from 1987 to 1993, used printed‑circuit‑board construction and featured high‑gain channels that differed from the classic Blackface and Silverface designs.
title: Fender amplifier

text: The Celsius temperature scale, which was reorganized by Jean‑Pierre Christin in 1743, defines the freezing point of water as 0 °C and assigns the boiling point of water at a pressure of one atmosphere the value 100 °C. This scale is the one commonly taught in schools today and is linked to the Kelvin scale through definitions based on absolute zero and the triple point of highly purified Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water.
title: Celsius

text: John Cooper Clarke, born on 25 January 1949, is an English performance poet who rose to prominence during the late‑1970s punk rock era and became known as a “punk poet.” He issued several albums in the late 1970s and early 1980s and continues to perform regularly.
title: John Cooper Clarke

text: Roxette, the Swedish pop‑rock duo comprising vocalist Marie Fredriksson and guitarist‑vocalist Per Gessle, recorded the ballad “It Must Have Been Love,” which rose to number one on the U.S. Hot 100 chart.
title: Roxette

text: The tibia and its companion, the fibula (commonly known as the calf bone), are both situated in the leg; the fibula rests on the outer side of the tibia, which together form the long bones of the lower limb.
title: Fibula

It was written in collaboration with songwriter Don Schlitz.
title: He Thinks He'll Keep Her

text: Joseph Sherrard Kearns (February 12, 1907 – February 17, 1962) was an American actor best known for portraying George Wilson—often referred to as Mr. Wilson—on the CBS television series *Dennis the Menace*, a part he played from 1959 until his death in 1962.

title: Breakup of Yugoslavia

text: George Warren Barnes (July 17, 1921 – September 5, 1977) was an American swing‑jazz guitarist. He first played an electric guitar in 1931, and on March 1, 1938 he made the earliest commercial recording that featured the electric guitar, recording with Big Bill Broonzy.
title: George Barnes (musician)

text: The currency used in South Korea is called the **won** (symbol ₩, ISO code KRW). It is issued by the Bank of Korea, which is headquartered in Seoul. One won is officially split into 100 jeon, although the jeon is no longer employed in everyday transactions and appears only in foreign‑exchange quotations.
title: South Korean won

text: Most of the ongoing star formation in the Milky Way occurs inside the dense portions of **molecular clouds in interstellar space**. These compact regions, frequently described as stellar nurseries, collapse under gravity and give rise to new stars. Consequently, research on the interstellar medium and giant molecular clouds concentrates on these locations as the principal sites where protostars and young stellar objects are produced.
title: Star formation

text: The King and I is a 1956 American musical film produced by 20th Century Fox. It was directed by Walter Lang and produced by Charles Brackett together with Darryl F. Zanuck. Ernest Lehman wrote the screenplay, adapting the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, which in turn was based on Margaret Landon’s novel *Anna and the King of Siam*—itself drawn from the memoirs of Anna Leonowens, the 19th‑century teacher to King Mongkut’s children. The movie features performances by Deborah Kerr and Yul Brynner.

title: Call Me by Your Name (film)

title: University of Michigan School of Public Health

title: I Don't Feel at Home in This World Anymore

title: Jacques Cartier

title: The Canterbury Tales

title: World's tallest thermometer

In addition to Bart, Cartwright supplies the voices for several other characters on the show, including Nelson Muntz, Ralph Wiggum, Todd Flanders, Kearney, and Database.

text: The analysis of long‑term technological waves identifies the current, fifth wave as being defined by the **digitization of social systems**. This latest phase follows earlier periods driven by water‑powered mechanization, steam power, electrification, and motorized automation, and it marks the newest transformative change in the U.S. economy.
title: Digital Revolution

text: Frederik Barth, in his review of the system of social stratification found in Pakistan, argued that the hierarchical, hereditary groups constitute castes.
title: Caste

text: The clash known as the Battle of Issus was fought on 5 November 333 BC in **southern Anatolia**. Alexander the Great’s Hellenic League met Darius III’s Achaemenid forces near the mouth of the Pinarus River close to the town of Issus, after the Macedonians had previously defeated the Persian satraps at the Granicus. Darius, having taken personal command and gathered reinforcements, attempted a surprise march behind the Greek advance, prompting Alexander to turn his army and engage the Persians at this location.
title: Battle of Issus

text: Long before the first rifting phase that began in the Early‑Middle Jurassic—about 175 million years ago— the area that would become North America was incorporated within the supercontinent Pangaea. This massive landmass later started to split, with the initial break‑up occurring as Pangaea rifted from the Tethys Ocean in the east toward the Pacific in the west.
title: Pangaea

text: The first observation of a cell dividing under a microscope was reported in 1835 by the German botanist Hugo von Mohl, who was examining the green alga *Cladophora glomerata*.
title: Cell division

title: Dirty Dancing

text: The Great Depression began in August 1929, and at that point the United States economy entered an economic recession. Although the nation’s gross domestic product declined for a couple of months before the Wall Street crash of October 1929, the recession signaled the start of a decade‑long era of soaring unemployment, falling farm incomes, deflation and stalled economic growth throughout the 1930s.
title: Great Depression in the United States

text: Aegisthus, the son of Thyestes and his own daughter Pelopia, exacted revenge on Atreus by killing him; in doing so he restored his father Thyestes to the throne of Mycenae, thereby helping his side recapture the city.
title: Agamemnon

text: J. Wellington “Wimpy,” the hamburger‑loving character from the Popeye cartoons, is the source of the famous line, “I’ll gladly pay you Tuesday for a hamburger today.” The expression first appeared in 1932 as part of Wimpy’s recurring gag in which he tries to convince other diners to cover his meal. Because of this habit, Wimpy’s catchphrase has become a shorthand for promising payment that is never fulfilled.
title: J. Wellington Wimpy

text: Tug of war was included as a team event in the Summer Olympic Games from the first appearance in 1900 up until the 1920 Games, after which it ceased to be part of the Olympic programme. During that period the competition was entered by clubs, and nations could field multiple clubs, allowing a single country to win several medals in a single Olympiad. The final Olympic appearance of tug of war therefore occurred in 1920.
title: Tug of war at the Summer Olympics

text: In Sunni Islamic tradition, the era during which the three Rightly Guided Caliphs—Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman ibn Affan—ruled is called the Rashidun. This term, also rendered as “the Rashidun Caliphs,” designates the early period of Islamic governance following the Prophet Muhammad’s death.
title: Rashidun

text: The Indian television drama *Ye Hai Mohabbatein* premiered on Star Plus on 3 December 2013. It was created by Ekta Kapoor and produced by her company Balaji Telefilms. The series features the lead actors Divyanka Tripathi and Karan Patel.

text: The black‑and‑white music video that accompanies “Brenda’s Got a Baby” visualizes the narrative spoken by Shakur. While the opening scenes feature Shakur himself, the character of Brenda is portrayed on screen by Ethel "Edy" Proctor.
title: Brenda's Got a Baby

text: Itai‑itai disease arose in Toyama Prefecture as a direct result of cadmium exposure. Beginning in the early 20th century, mining operations released large amounts of cadmium into the Jinzū River and its tributaries; the contaminated water was used for irrigation, drinking, washing and fishing. Residents who consumed the river water and the rice grown with it therefore ingested cadmium, and the resulting poisoning manifested as the painful, debilitating condition known as itai‑itai disease, first observed around 1912.
title: Itai-itai disease

text: For the Netflix film *When We First Met*, principal photography began in mid‑July 2016, and the production was shot in New Orleans.
title: When We First Met

text: A Walk to Remember is a novel authored by American writer Nicholas Sparks, first published in October 1999. Set in Beaufort, North Carolina during 1958–1959, it tells the story of two teenagers whose contrasting personalities bring them together in love. The book was later adapted into a film of the same name.
title: A Walk to Remember (novel)

text: During the Civil War, the political body called the Confederacy championed the doctrine of states’ rights, asserting that individual states should retain their sovereignty rather than be subordinate to a larger national government. This commitment to state sovereignty was a central element of the Southern “Cause,” which the Confederacy promoted throughout its existence.
title: Confederate States of America

text: The narrator explains that he is behind the wheel of a truck that once belonged to his brother, a soldier who was killed in action while serving in the United States Army. By driving the vehicle, he feels a connection to his brother and keeps his memory alive.

title: Canada small business tax rate

text: Michael Clarke Duncan, the American actor born on December 10, 1957, portrayed the gentle giant John Coffey in the 1999 film The Green Mile, a performance that garnered him an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.
title: Michael Clarke Duncan

text: Catch‑22 is a satirical novel written by American author Joseph Heller. He began drafting the work in 1953, and it was first released to the public in 1961. The book employs a distinctive non‑chronological third‑person omniscient narration, showing events through the eyes of various characters, with its separate storylines arranged out of sequence so that the timeline develops alongside the plot.
title: Catch-22

text: Buckingham Palace, the London residence of the British monarch, still showcases many early‑19th‑century interior designs, including bright scagliola and lapis accents suggested by Sir Charles Long. King Edward VII later introduced a Belle Époque cream‑and‑gold colour scheme, while several smaller reception rooms are furnished in a Chinese Regency style with pieces brought from the Royal Pavilion at Brighton and from Carlton House. The building contains **775 rooms**, and its garden is the largest private garden in London. The state rooms, used for official and ceremonial entertaining, are opened to the public each August and September and on selected days during winter and spring.
title: Buckingham Palace

text: Buckingham Palace encompasses a total of 775 rooms. These include 19 state rooms, 52 principal bedrooms, 188 staff bedrooms, 92 offices and 78 bathrooms, alongside facilities such as a post office, cinema, swimming pool, doctor's surgery and a jeweller’s workshop. The building spans 108 metres by 120 metres, rises 24 metres high and provides over 77,000 m² (830,000 sq ft) of floor space.
title: Buckingham Palace

text: Timothy McGee first showed up as a guest in eight episodes of NCIS’s inaugural season. In season two he was promoted to the regular cast, with his name appearing in the opening credits.
title: Timothy McGee

text: Microfilaments are a component of the cytoskeleton that consist of actin, the most abundant protein found in cells. These actin‑based filaments play a key role in processes such as muscle contraction, where myosin motors generate force by pulling on parallel actin filaments within each muscle cell. The presence of calcium ions triggers regulatory proteins (tropomyosin and troponin) to permit the interaction between actin and myosin, leading to coordinated shortening of the muscle fiber.
title: Cytoskeleton

text: The tradition of delivering an opposition response to the State of the Union address began in 1966, when Republican U.S. Senator Everett Dirksen of Illinois and Representative Gerald Ford of Michigan appeared on television to reply to President Lyndon Johnson’s speech. Since then, the format has changed—ranging from a 45‑minute prerecorded program in 1970 to a live call‑in show in 1972 where congressmen answered unscripted questions—and, beginning in the late 1980s, it has typically taken the form of a televised speech delivered shortly after the President’s address.
title: Response to the State of the Union address

text: In 2018 the United States counted a total of 5,534 registered hospitals. This figure includes the nation’s community hospitals—non‑federal, short‑term general or specialty facilities—as well as privately owned for‑profit and government‑run institutions.
title: Health care in the United States

text: Dalveer Bhandari, born on 1 October 1947, is an Indian jurist who has served as a judge of the Supreme Court of India and currently sits as a member of the International Court of Justice.
title: Dalveer Bhandari

text: Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan (born 7 August 1925) is an Indian geneticist who played a pivotal role in the nation’s Green Revolution—a programme that introduced high‑yielding wheat and rice varieties to the fields of small‑holder farmers. Owing to his leadership in developing and promoting these crops, he is widely known as the Indian Father of the Green Revolution. He later founded and chairs the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and promotes sustainable agriculture and food security.
title: M. S. Swaminathan

text: The track titled “Say You Won’t Let Go” was performed by the British singer‑songwriter James Arthur. It was released as a digital download in the United Kingdom on 9 September 2016 through Columbia Records, acting as the lead single from his second studio album, Back from the Edge (2016). The single rose to number one on the UK Singles Chart, where it remained for three weeks, and also topped the charts in Australia, New Zealand, Sweden and the Republic of Ireland, while in the United States it peaked at number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100.
title: Say You Won't Let Go

text: In the event of a disaster, the **management team** assumes responsibility for overseeing and monitoring the recovery of the affected location. It coordinates the overall response, evaluates the incident, activates the recovery plan, and maintains communication with the various team leaders. By documenting progress and ensuring that recovery activities remain on schedule, the management team serves as the primary entity that watches the recovery process.
title: Disaster recovery plan

text: The synthesis of new DNA from an existing template occurs at defined sites in the genome known as **origins of replication**. At each origin the double‑stranded DNA is opened, creating replication forks that extend outward in both directions. Enzymes such as DNA polymerase then add nucleotides complementary to each template strand, enabling the formation of new DNA molecules.
title: DNA replication

text: Merry Clayton, an American soul and gospel singer born on December 25, 1948, performed a duet with Mick Jagger on the Rolling Stones song “Gimme Shelter.”
title: Merry Clayton

text: During the series Tony eventually makes amends with Michelle and gets back together with her. title: Tony Stonem

text: The pop song “Sugar, Sugar,” written by Jeff Barry and Andy Kim, was first recorded by the virtual group the Archies. Their rendition climbed to number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in 1969, where it stayed for four weeks, and also led the UK Singles chart for eight weeks that same year. The track saw a resurgence in 1970 when rhythm‑and‑blues singer Wilson Pickett returned it to the charts.
title: Sugar, Sugar

text: In the climax of *You Get Me*, Tyler finds Ali tied to the ceiling, frees her, and the two make their way out of the house together. When Holly confronts them at gunpoint, Tyler tells her that he loves Ali and never will love her. After a brief struggle, Holly is wounded and falls into the pool, while Gil and Ali stay with Tyler as they wait for the police to arrive. Consequently, Tyler ends up with Ali.
