He is shown having a good time with Ali at the party, making it clear that Tyler ends up with Ali. Lydia also appears in the scene, but the focus is on Tyler and Ali’s budding relationship.
title: You Get Me (film)

text: "Holiday Road" debuted as a single in 1983, written and recorded by Fleetwood Mac guitarist Lindsey Buckingham for the 1983 film *National Lampoon’s Vacation*. The song later appeared in the series’ sequels and, despite peaking at No. 82 on the Billboard Hot 100, has become one of Buckingham’s most recognizable tracks.
title: Holiday Road

text: Glycogen and amylopectin are both polymeric carbohydrates built from repeated units of the simple sugar glucose. Each molecule consists of long chains in which glucose residues are linked together, giving the two substances their characteristic structure and function.
title: Glycogen

text: During the Swadeshi era, the revolutionary Bengali newspaper Jugantar (also called Jugantar Patrika) was edited by **Bhupendranath Dutt**. He held the editorship until his arrest in 1907, after which the paper, which had once enjoyed a readership of about 20,000, faced repeated prosecutions by the British Indian government and was eventually forced to close in 1908.
title: Jugantar Patrika

text: Indoor toilets began as a luxury for the wealthy and only slowly reached ordinary households. Up through the 1890s, building codes in London did not obligate working‑class homes to provide indoor facilities, and even into the early twentieth century some houses were constructed with a toilet for the owners upstairs and a separate outhouse for servants. In certain cases, toilets were installed inside the structure but could be accessed only from the outside. After World War I, all new housing in London and its suburbs was built with indoor toilets, indicating the moment when indoor toilets became common.
title: Toilet (room)

text: According to Article 1, Section 7 of the Constitution, the President is the official who may either sign a bill, turning it into law, or refuse to sign it and return it unsigned—an action that constitutes a constitutional veto. The President must state any objections in writing, and Congress must then consider those objections and reconsider the legislation.
title: Veto

text: The narrative of the Book of Esther unfolds in the ancient kingdom of Persia, where the Hebrew heroine—originally named Hadassah and later called Esther—rises to become queen and prevents a planned extermination of her people.
title: Book of Esther

text: India’s land frontiers are limited to just seven neighboring countries; it does not share a land border with Sri Lanka.
title: Borders of India

text: The collapse of Youngstown’s steel mills began on September 19, 1977, a day that locals later dubbed “Black Monday.” That date marked the start of a wave of plant shutdowns and massive layoffs that would continue through the early 1980s, reshaping the city’s economy.
title: Economy of Youngstown, Ohio

text: Automobile drivetrains contain two principal locations where a simple gear train is employed. The first is the transmission, which houses several gear sets that can be shifted to provide a broad range of vehicle speeds. The second is the differential, which includes the final‑drive gearing that further reduces speed to the wheels and also contains gear arrangements that split torque equally while allowing the wheels to rotate at different speeds when turning. In some designs the transmission and final drive are linked by a driveshaft; in others they are integrated into a single transaxle. The gear ratios selected for the transmission and final drive significantly affect vehicle performance.
title: Gear train

text: Malcolm in the Middle centers on the chaotic household of a gifted teenager and his relatives. In the show, the mother Lois is portrayed by Jane Kaczmarek, and the father Hal is played by **Bryan Cranston**. The series also stars Frankie Muniz as Malcolm, Christopher Kennedy Masterson as the eldest brother Francis, Justin Berfield as the older sibling Reese, Erik Per Sullivan as the younger brother Dewey, and later adds a baby brother, Jamie.
title: Malcolm in the Middle

text: The television comedy *Malcolm in the Middle* follows the chaotic life of Malcolm and his family. The show’s parents are Lois, portrayed by Jane Kaczmarek, and their husband Hal, who is portrayed by **Bryan Cranston**. Malcolm, the third‑born son, lives with his brothers Reese (Justin Berfield), Dewey (Erik Per Sullivan) and later Jamie (James and Lukas Rodriguez), while the eldest sibling Francis (Christopher Masterson) attends military school. The series initially focuses on Malcolm’s teenage challenges before expanding to explore the broader family and their acquaintances.
title: Malcolm in the Middle

text: According to World Series records, **the New York Yankees** have won the most championships, securing 27 titles in 40 appearances. For comparison, the franchise that began as the Philadelphia Athletics and later became the Kansas City and Oakland Athletics has captured 9 titles from 14 trips to the Series, while the Boston Red Sox have earned 8 victories in 12 appearances. In the National League, the St. Louis Cardinals have appeared 19 times and won 11, the Giants (both New York and San Francisco) have played in 20 Series and won 8, the Dodgers (Brooklyn and Los Angeles) have made 19 appearances with 6 wins, and the Cincinnati Reds have participated 9 times, winning 5.
title: World Series

text: During production of the film *Into the Woods*, the singing was performed by the cast. Before filming began, the actors underwent six weeks of rehearsals on a soundstage, after which they each recorded their vocal parts at Angel Recording Studios in August while Stephen Sondheim was present. Over ninety percent of the vocal tracks in the finished movie come from those studio recordings, with the remaining portions captured on location or on set.
title: Into the Woods (film)

text: Most of the musical numbers in the film were performed by the cast, who recorded the majority of the songs in advance. Music producer Mike Higham, who had previously collaborated with Stephen Sondheim on *Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street*, captured the score with the London Symphony Orchestra and the London Philharmonic. Music supervisor and conductor Paul Gemignani coached the actors on vocal delivery, guiding them through live on‑set performances, playback of pre‑recorded studio tracks, and accompaniment by a live studio orchestra. Jonathan Tunick provided the orchestration for Sondheim’s original compositions, while specific adjustments—such as lowering the key of “Hello, Little Girl” for Johnny Depp’s voice—were made during production. text: In the fetus, the ductus arteriosus—also called the ductus Botalli—connects the main pulmonary artery to the proximal descending aorta, permitting most right‑ventricular blood to bypass the fluid‑filled, non‑functioning lungs. At birth, this vessel normally closes and thereafter becomes the ligamentum arteriosum. The fetal circulation also includes two additional shunts, the ductus venosus and the foramen ovale.
title: Ductus arteriosus

text: The ulnar nerve travels in close proximity to the ulna bone and, lacking muscular or bony protection, is especially prone to injury. Striking the area commonly referred to as the “funny bone” therefore compresses the ulnar nerve.
title: Ulnar nerve

text: When the “funny bone” is hit, the impact actually compresses the ulnar nerve against the medial epicondyle of the humerus. The ulnar nerve becomes trapped between the bone and the skin at this spot, producing the characteristic electric‑shock sensation. The ulnar nerve is therefore the structure that is compressed when the funny bone is struck.
title: Ulnar nerve

text: The aorta is the principal systemic artery. In humans it receives blood straight from the left ventricle of the heart through the aortic valve and then distributes that blood throughout the body. As it descends, the aorta gives rise to successive branches that become progressively smaller, eventually forming arterioles that feed capillary networks. The first off‑shoots of the aorta are the coronary arteries, which supply the heart muscle itself, followed by the branches of the aortic arch—the brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, and the left subclavian artery.
title: Artery

text: Animals that carry out most of their activity during the twilight periods—that is, at dawn and at dusk—are classified as **Crepuscular**. This activity pattern is set apart from diurnal behavior, which occurs in full daylight, and nocturnal behavior, which takes place in the dark of night. The label is somewhat flexible, because some Crepuscular animals may also be active on moonlit evenings or when the sky is overcast. For more precise distinctions, the terms *matutinal* and *vespertine* are used for species that are active only before sunrise or only after sunset, respectively.
title: Crepuscular

text: The word used to describe animals that are most active during the twilight periods of dawn and dusk is **Crepuscular**. Many well‑known mammals follow this pattern, including several bat species, hamsters, housecats, stray dogs, rabbits, ferrets, guinea pigs and rats. Other examples of crepuscular mammals are jaguars, ocelots, bobcats, strepsirrhine primates, red pandas, bears, deer, moose, sitatunga, capybaras, chinchillas, the common mouse, skunks, Australian wombats, wallabies, quolls, possums, marsupial gliders, tenrecids, spotted hyenas and African wild dogs.
title: Crepuscular

text: Neuropsychology is a branch of psychology that investigates how the brain’s structure and its functional activity are linked to specific mental processes and observable behaviours.  As an experimental discipline, it seeks to explain how variations in brain functioning shape cognition and conduct, and it is also involved in diagnosing and treating the behavioural and cognitive consequences of neurological disorders.  In contrast to classical psychology, which often treats mental phenomena separately from biology, neuropsychology places the nervous system—especially the brain—at the centre of its inquiry, sharing concerns with fields such as neuropsychiatry and behavioural neurology.
title: Neuropsychology

text: Neuropsychology is a branch of psychology that concentrates on the brain and the nervous system as the biological basis of mental processes. It employs experimental‑psychology methods to reveal how neural structures give rise to cognitive functions, typically by testing healthy human participants in laboratory environments, though some investigators also use animal models. For example, because visual input presented to a particular visual field is preferentially processed by the opposite cortical hemisphere, neuropsychologists can draw direct connections between specific neuroanatomy and psychological performance.
title: Neuropsychology

text: During World War I the German Empire belonged to the Central Powers and fought the Allied nations on both the eastern and western fronts. text: Spinal fusion—also referred to as spondylodesis or spondylosyndesis—is a neurosurgical or orthopedic operation that **joins two or more vertebrae**. The surgery can be carried out at any region of the spine, whether cervical, thoracic, or lumbar, and it eliminates movement between the fused segments. Various fusion techniques are employed, each using a bone graft taken from the patient (autograft), a donor (allograft), or a synthetic substitute to encourage the bones to heal together. Frequently, additional hardware such as screws, plates, or cages is implanted to keep the vertebrae aligned while the graft solidifies the connection.
title: Spinal fusion

text: In the United States a yellow sign that shows a speed—such as “35 mph”—is used to convey an advisory speed limit. title: Advisory speed limit

text: In today’s monetary system the instrument that functions as the medium of exchange is fiat money.  Critics contend that this fiat money does not meet the traditional criteria for a proper medium of exchange because its value is free‑floating: its market price shifts whenever the supply of money is altered relative to the economy’s demand.  As the supply of fiat money expands beyond what the economy needs, the basket of goods and services to which it is linked shrinks, reducing its purchasing power and preventing it from serving as a stable unit or standard measure of wealth.  Consequently, manipulators can influence prices, undermining the reliability of value‑related economic data.  Nonetheless, proponents such as Chartalists argue that the ability to adjust the value of fiat money can be advantageous, allowing fiscal stimulus to be deployed more readily during economic crises.
title: Medium of exchange

text: The silk floss tree (Ceiba speciosa) is widely planted in South Africa, where it is valued for its ornamental appearance. Its trunk and branches are covered in sharp prickles, so safety buffer zones are required around the trunk to protect people and domestic animals from injury.
title: Ceiba speciosa

text: The nuclear model of the atom was devised by Ernest Rutherford. He directed the famous Geiger–Marsden experiment in 1909, and after his 1911 analysis concluded that J. J. Thomson’s plum‑pudding picture was wrong. Rutherford’s revised model introduced a very small, highly charged central region that holds the bulk of the atom’s mass, a region later identified as the nucleus.
title: Rutherford model

text: The Electronic Fund Transfer Act, which defines consumer protections and the obligations of all parties involved in electronic money transfers, was enacted after Congress approved it and President Jimmy Carter signed it into law in 1978.
title: Electronic Fund Transfer Act

text: Nicholas "Nick" Bakay, born October 8 1959, is an American actor and voice actor who supplies the voice for Salem Saberhagen, the talking cat featured in the television series *Sabrina the Teenage Witch* and its animated continuation. His career also includes voice work as Norbert Beaver on *The Angry Beavers* and appearances such as playing Karl on the Fox series *’Til Death*, where he also served as a producer.
title: Nick Bakay

text: June Gable (born June 5, 1945) is an American character actress who is perhaps best known for playing Joey Tribbiani’s agent, Estelle Leonard, on the NBC sitcom *Friends*. She has also earned a Tony Award nomination for her work on Broadway.
title: June Gable

text: The inaugural series of *The Great British Bake Off* premiered on BBC Two on 17 August 2010, featuring ten home bakers who faced three weekly challenges in different UK locations. Each episode concluded with one or more contestants being eliminated, and the competition culminated in a final bake‑off that determined the series champion. The competition was won by **Edd Kimber**.
title: The Great British Bake Off (series 1)

text: Barry Bonds holds the Major League Baseball home run record with 762. He overtook Hank Aaron—who remains second with 755—on August 7, 2007. The sole other player to reach the 700‑home‑run milestone is Babe Ruth, who finished with 714. Only a handful of hitters have amassed 600 or more homers: Alex Rodriguez (696), Willie Mays (660), Ken Griffey Jr. (630), Albert Pujols (614), Jim Thome (612) and Sammy Sosa (609).
title: List of Major League Baseball career home run leaders

text: Arnold Schoenberg introduced a new compositional approach that replaces the traditional harmonic system with a series of twelve pitch classes, each related only to the others. This “Method of Composing with Twelve Notes related only to one another,” later known as twelve‑note serialism or dodecaphony, represents a clear break from conventional harmony.
title: Serialism

text: In the first quarter of 2015, 294 million domain names were registered worldwide. A large share of them belong to the com top‑level domain, which held 115.6 million names as of 21 December 2014, including millions of business, entertainment, finance and sports sites. Importantly, as of July 2012 the com TLD had more registrations than all of the ccTLDs combined.
title: Domain name

text: Veronica is a female given name that originates from the Latin transliteration of the Greek name Berenice. The Greek form, which stems from the Macedonian version of the Athenian names Φερενίκη (Phereníkē) or Φερονίκη (Pheroníkē), merges the verb φέρειν (phérein, “to bring”) with the noun νίκη (níkê, “victory”). As a result, the name means “she who brings victory.” The name was popular among the royal dynasties of the Hellenistic world—most notably the Ptolemies of Egypt and the Seleucids of Asia—and later became well‑known through the Christian Saint Veronica and her veil. Common pet forms include Ronnie, Roni, the German Frony, and the Russian diminutive Nika.
title: Veronica (name)

text: Kraków first assumed the role of capital of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland in 1038, beginning a long period during which the city served as the nation’s principal seat of power.
title: Kraków

text: In the year 1038, Kraków was established as the seat of the Polish government, thereby becoming the capital of Poland.
title: Kraków

text: The name of Huevos Rancheros’ 1996 album *Get Outta Dodge* points to the expression “Get out of Dodge,” a line that was originally spoken on the drama series Gunsmoke, where heroes would tell villains to leave Dodge City, Kansas.
title: Get Outta Dodge

text: In the climactic bout of *Real Steel*, the two robots trade blows for four intense rounds, with Atom repeatedly rising after being knocked down. Although Zeus is driven to the edge of defeat—once even stumbling to the floor—the match goes the distance. When the judges announce their decision, they award the win to Zeus, leaving the technologically superior machine as the victor of the final fight.
title: Real Steel

text: The track titled “December, 1963 (Oh, What a Night)” was recorded by the Four Seasons. It was written by the group’s original keyboard player Bob Gaudio and his future wife Judy Parker, produced by Gaudio, and later included on the Four Seasons’ 1975 album *Who Loves You*.
title: December, 1963 (Oh, What a Night)

text: Sophia Akuffo was sworn in as Ghana’s Chief Justice by President Akufo‑Addo on 19 June 2017, succeeding Georgina Wood, the nation’s first female chief justice.
title: Chief Justice of Ghana

text: On 24 August 2007, the portion of Highway 401 extending from Glen Miller Road in Trenton to the junction with the Don Valley Parkway and Highway 404 in Toronto was officially named the Highway of Heroes, a route used by funeral convoys carrying fallen Canadian Forces personnel from CFB Trenton to the coroner’s office in Toronto.
title: Ontario Highway 401

text: Jack Nicklaus holds the record for the most Masters victories, winning the tournament six times during his career. He also remains the oldest champion, having secured the green jacket at age 46 years 82 days in 1986. In addition, Nicklaus shares the record for most consecutive Masters wins (two) with Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods. Woods was the youngest winner at 21 years 104 days in 1997 and set the widest margin of victory and the lowest winning score that year, a total later matched by Jordan Spieth in 2015.
title: List of Masters Tournament champions

text: Barbara Park’s children’s series Junie B. Jones, illustrated by Denise Brunkus and released by Random House, launched in 1992. The opening book, Junie B. Jones and the Stupid Smelly Bus, introduces an almost six‑year‑old starting her first day of kindergarten.
title: Junie B. Jones

text: The debut Junie B. Jones novel was released by Random House in 1992, launching a series that would later grow to include twenty‑eight additional titles—twenty‑seven core books plus a journal—and has been translated into Spanish and French.
title: Junie B. Jones

text: The thirteenth installment of the reality competition series America’s Got Talent is slated to premiere on May 29, 2018 on NBC. The judging panel—Howie Mandel, Mel B, Heidi Klum and Simon Cowell—will return for their ninth, sixth, sixth and third seasons respectively, while Tyra Banks comes back as host for a second year. The live performances will again be staged at the Dolby Theatre, and the show continues to be co‑produced by FremantleMedia North America and Simon Cowell’s Syco Entertainment.
title: America's Got Talent (season 13)

text: During the American Civil War the Confederacy built a pioneering under‑sea vessel that would become known as the H. L. Hunley. This craft bore the name of its creator, Horace Lawson Hunley, who designed and constructed the submarine that later sank the Union warship USS Housatonic. The vessel’s brief service illustrated both the promise and the peril of early submarine warfare.
title: H. L. Hunley (submarine)

text: On November 7, 2017, the Virginia gubernatorial contest ended with Democratic nominee Ralph Northam defeating Republican Ed Gillespie, achieving the widest Democratic victory margin since 1985. Consequently, Northam will assume office as the Commonwealth’s 73rd governor on January 13, 2018. Voter turnout reached 47 percent, the highest level for a Virginia governor’s race in the past twenty years.
title: Virginia gubernatorial election, 2017

text: In the 1858 contest for the United States Senate seat from Illinois, the state legislature—whose districts had been drawn to benefit the Democratic Party—voted 54 to 46 to retain Stephen A. Douglas. Although Abraham Lincoln’s Republican ticket won a narrow popular‑vote majority of 50.6 percent, the legislative count returned Douglas to the Senate.
title: Lincoln–Douglas debates

text: The University of Wisconsin–Madison is a public research university that is situated in Madison, Wisconsin, United States.
title: University of Wisconsin–Madison

text: The formal signing of the United States Declaration of Independence was carried out chiefly on August 2, 1776, inside the Pennsylvania State House (today called Independence Hall) in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. At that time, the 56 delegates of the Second Continental Congress, representing the thirteen former colonies that had proclaimed themselves the “United States of America,” affixed their signatures to the document that Congress had previously adopted on July 4, 1776. Their names were listed by state, with President of the Continental Congress John Hancock appearing separately.
title: Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence

text: Henry Purcell (c. 10 September 1659 – 21 November 1695) was an English composer whose work blended Italian and French influences into a distinctly English style of Baroque music. Music historians generally regard Henry Purcell as the greatest English composer of the Baroque period, noting that no other native‑born English composer achieved comparable fame until the twentieth century.
title: Henry Purcell

text: Armed hostilities began in 1775. In 1776, the Second Continental Congress declared a new, independent nation: the United States of America. Led by General George Washington, the young country eventually won the Revolutionary War with substantial French assistance. The 1783 peace treaty granted the United States territory east of the Mississippi River, except for Canada and Florida. Although the Articles of Confederation created a central government, it proved ineffective because it could not levy taxes and lacked an executive officer. A convention in 1787 drafted a new Constitution that was adopted in 1789, and a Bill of Rights was added in 1791. Washington became the first president, with Alexander Hamilton as his chief adviser, establishing a stronger federal government. Later, the 1803 Louisiana Purchase doubled the nation’s size, and the War of 1812 further solidified national pride.
title: History of the United States

text: In 1776, and more precisely on July 4, 1776, the Second Continental Congress gathered in Philadelphia and adopted the Declaration of Independence, formally proclaiming the United States of America as an independent nation. This day is commemorated each year as the nation’s birthday.
title: History of the United States

text: In Sherman Alexie’s *The Absolutely True Diary of a Part‑Time Indian*, narrator Arnold “Junior” Spirit reveals early that he dreams of becoming a cartoonist, hoping that success will lift him out of the poverty and abuse that dominate reservation life. As the narrative unfolds, Junior repeatedly confronts the reservation’s scarcity of opportunity and education, leading him to the conviction that any genuine chance for a better future must be sought elsewhere. He explicitly states that hope is found off the rez, looking to the world beyond the reservation as the place where his aspirations might finally be realized.
title: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian

text: After a brief separation, Eric discovers that Donna has left town with Michael for California. Determined, he follows her, and the two quickly make up, resuming their romance. Their bond deepens to the point where Eric awkwardly proposes to Donna atop the water tower, and the couple becomes engaged. Despite doubts from friends and family, Eric and Donna stay together, remaining engaged through the later seasons of the show.
title: Eric Forman

text: Following his departure at the start of the eighth season, Eric spends a month teaching in Africa before returning home on New Year's Eve. He uses the holiday to make peace with Donna, rekindling their romance and planning to continue his teaching career alongside her. Consequently, Eric ends up with Donna.
title: Eric Forman

text: The Megaphone Trophy, which Notre Dame captured with a 38‑18 victory on September 23, 2017, will stay in its possession until the rivalry is renewed in 2026, the year the two teams are slated to meet again.
title: Michigan State–Notre Dame football rivalry

text: The iconic theme music for the television series *Mission: Impossible* (1966–1973) was written and composed by Argentine composer Lalo Schifrin. Since its debut, the piece has been reused in later *Mission: Impossible* TV revivals, films, and video games, and the 1960s version is often cited as one of television’s greatest theme tunes.
title: Theme from Mission: Impossible

text: Sex and the City is a television series that takes place in New York City; the show’s narrative and production are both rooted in that city, providing the backdrop for the lives of its four main female characters.
title: Sex and the City

text: The Ranjit Sagar Dam—also called the Thein Dam—is a hydro‑electric facility erected by the Government of Punjab on the Ravi River, straddling the border between the Indian states of Jammu and Kashmir and Punjab. The reservoir lies predominantly in Jammu and Kashmir (about 60 %) while the dam structure itself is situated near Pathankot in Punjab’s Pathankot district and also touches Kathua district in Jammu and Kashmir. The site is part of the Shah pur Kandi township. Feasibility work began in 1953, geotechnical investigations continued through 1980, construction started in 1981, the generators were commissioned in 2000, and the project was completed in March 2001.
title: Ranjit Sagar Dam

text: The NBA’s Most Valuable Player record shows that Kareem Abdul-Jabbar holds the top spot, having been named MVP six times—the highest total for any player who later entered the Hall of Fame. In contrast, both Bill Russell and Michael Jordan received the award five times, and Wilt Chamberlain together with LeBron James each earned it four times. Other multiple‑time winners include Moses Malone, Larry Bird and Magic Johnson with three MVPs each, and several players such as Bob Pettit, Karl Malone, Tim Duncan, Steve Nash and Stephen Curry who have won it twice. Only two rookies—Wilt Chamberlain in the 1959‑60 season and Wes Unseld in 1968‑69—have ever captured the MVP honor.
title: NBA Most Valuable Player Award

text: The Lincoln Highway was among the earliest coast‑to‑coast automobile routes in the United States. Conceived in 1912 by Indiana entrepreneur Carl G. Fisher and formally dedicated on October 31, 1913, the road began at Times Square in New York City and extended westward across the nation. Its western terminus was Lincoln Park in San Francisco, marking the end of the transcontinental corridor that originally traversed thirteen states.
title: Lincoln Highway

text: In the unaired 28‑minute pilot of *Charmed*, the character of the youngest sister, Phoebe Halliwell, was originally cast with Lori Rom. After Rom departed the series, a new pilot was produced in which Alyssa Milano assumed the role of Phoebe.
title: Charmed

text: “Make You Feel My Love” is a composition authored by **Bob Dylan**, first appearing on his 1997 album *Time Out of Mind*. Although Dylan’s own recording was released later that same year, the song’s initial commercial debut was made by Billy Joel, who issued it under the title “To Make You Feel My Love.” Since then, the track has been covered by many performers—including Adele, Garth Brooks, Bryan Ferry, Kelly Clarkson and Ane Brun—and has enjoyed considerable commercial success.
title: Make You Feel My Love

text: Left Behind is a series of sixteen best‑selling religious novels written by Tim LaHaye and Jerry B. Jenkins. The books explore the Christian dispensationalist vision of the End Times, presenting a pre‑tribulation, premillennial interpretation of the biblical apocalypse. The narrative follows the Tribulation Force, an underground network of converts, as they battle the Global Community—a worldwide organization headed by Nicolae Carpathia, portrayed as the Antichrist. The series, whose opening volume bears the same title, was published between 1995 and 2007 by Tyndale House, a firm noted for its focus on dispensationalism.
title: Left Behind

text: The CW confirmed that the American supernatural drama *The Vampire Diaries* would receive an eighth and final season, later specifying that the concluding run would consist of 16 episodes. This final season began its broadcast on October 21, 2016 and finished on March 10, 2017.
title: The Vampire Diaries (season 8)

text: The debut single of American pop artist Britney Spears, titled “…Baby One More Time,” was composed by Max Martin. The track, produced by Martin together with Rami, was released in 1998 through Jive Records as the lead single for Spears’s 1999 self‑titled debut album. After submitting a demo that included an unused Toni Braxton song, Spears secured a multi‑album contract with Jive. Musically, the song blends teen pop and dance‑pop styles and expresses a young woman’s feelings following a breakup.
title: ...Baby One More Time (song)

text: In the sitcom Drake & Josh, the character Walter—Josh’s father and the stepfather of Drake and Megan, who works as a meteorologist for a local San Diego news program—is portrayed by Jonathan Goldstein.
title: List of Drake & Josh characters

text: Thomas “Tom” Hagen, a fictional character created by Mario Puzo for *The Godfather* novel and later featured in Francis Ford Coppola’s films *The Godfather* and *The Godfather Part II*, is brought to life on screen by actor Robert Duvall.
title: Tom Hagen

text: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (14 April 1891 – 6 December 1956), popularly known as Baba Saheb, was an Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer. He served as Independent India’s first law minister and is widely regarded as the father of the Indian Constitution, having been its principal architect. Ambedkar also inspired the Dalit Buddhist Movement and campaigned for the rights of women and labourers.
title: B. R. Ambedkar

text: Aluminum building wiring was briefly used for whole‑house circuits in Ontario during a time of high copper prices. Installation began in the early 1960s, but the practice was abandoned by the mid-1970s, after which revised manufacturing standards for both the wire and the connected devices were introduced to mitigate the problems that had arisen.
title: Aluminum building wiring

text: During season 7 of The Drew Carey Show, the recurring character Nikki—who had appeared intermittently since season 3 and was noted for her weight‑related storylines—made a comeback. The role of Nikki was played by actress Kate Walsh, who once more donned a fat suit for the part.
title: The Drew Carey Show

text: The inscription on the Statue of Liberty is the poem "The New Colossus". Written by Emma Lazarus in 1883, the verses were cast in bronze in 1903 and placed on a plaque mounted inside the lower level of the statue’s pedestal.
title: The New Colossus

text: In 1903 a plaque bearing the poem “The New Colossus” was affixed to the inner wall of the Statue of Liberty’s pedestal, making the inscription visible there.
title: The New Colossus

text: In the deleted scene from the “The Farm” episode of The Office, Dwight’s brother Jeb is portrayed by Thomas Middleditch. The same scene also features guest appearances by Majandra Delfino as Dwight’s sister Fannie, Blake Garrett Rosenthal as his nephew Cammy, Matt Jones as his cousin Zeke, and Tom Bower as his great‑uncle Heinrich.
