text: The 2017–18 NBA season, the league’s 72nd, started its regular schedule earlier than in previous years to reduce the number of back‑to‑back games. The opening night of the season took place on **October 17, 2017**, when the 2017 runners‑up Cleveland Cavaliers hosted the Boston Celtics at Quicken Loans Arena in Cleveland, Ohio.
title: 2017–18 NBA season

text: The Best Years of Our Lives, a 1946 American drama about three World II veterans returning to civilian life, was directed by William Wyler. The film also featured a cast that included Myrna Loy, Fredric March, Dana Andrews, Teresa Wright, Virginia Mayo, and Harold Russell. Samuel Goldwyn decided to produce the picture after reading a 1944 Time article on the challenges faced by returning servicemen, and he commissioned former war correspondent MacKinlay Kantor to create the original novella, later adapted into a screenplay by Robert E. Sherwood.
title: The Best Years of Our Lives

text: In the episode titled Kobol's Last Gleaming, Commander Adama assigns Boomer a mission to destroy the basestar orbiting Kobol. While aboard that basestar she encounters numerous other Number Eight copies identical to herself, and although she initially refuses to accept that she is a Cylon, the hidden programming later overtakes her after she returns to Galactica, prompting her to shoot Commander Adama. Thus, Boomer discovers she is a Cylon during Kobol's Last Gleaming.
title: Number Eight (Battlestar Galactica)

text: On Opening Day, April 9 1965, a packed crowd of 47,879 watched an exhibition match between the Houston Astros and the New York Yankees inside the newly completed Astrodome. The ceremony featured President Lyndon B. Johnson, First Lady Lady Bird Johnson, Texas Governor John Connally—who tossed the inaugural ball—and Houston Mayor Louie Welch. The Astros’ pitcher Dick “Turk” Farrell delivered the first pitch, and during the game Mickey Mantle recorded both the stadium’s first hit (a single) and its first home run. The Astros ultimately defeated the Yankees 2‑1 that evening.
title: Astrodome

text: Star Trek: Discovery made its initial television premiere on September 19, 2017, when the first episode was shown publicly, before the series began its regular broadcast on CBS and CBS All Access starting September 24.
title: Star Trek: Discovery

text: In the inaugural series of the UK game show Take Me Out, the couples who succeeded in the competition went on their date at the venue called “FERNANDO’S!” in Manchester. That location is, in fact, the Club Bijou on Chapel Street. The date’s outcome was then featured in the following week’s episode.
title: Take Me Out (UK game show)

text: In the fifth U.S. season of *Hell’s Kitchen*, Executive Chef Danny Veltri was declared the champion, receiving a sous‑chef position alongside Stephen Kalt at the Italian restaurant Fornelletto in the Borgata casino, Atlantic City, New Jersey, and a cash prize of $250,000.
title: Hell's Kitchen (U.S. season 5)

text: The Thrust SSC established the world land‑speed record on 15 October 1997 by attaining a top speed of 1,228 km/h (763 mph), becoming the first ground vehicle to officially surpass the sound barrier.
title: ThrustSSC

text: The Star, the 2017 animated feature from Columbia Pictures under Sony Pictures Entertainment, opened in U.S. theatres on November 17, 2017.
title: The Star (2017 film)

text: In the music video for Green Day’s “21 Guns,” the female lead—identified as Gloria—is portrayed by actress Lisa Stelly. The storyline shows Christian (played by Josh Boswell) and Gloria (Lisa Stelly) sheltering in a stark white room after a bank robbery, while police fire into the space. Despite the barrage of bullets, the couple remains unharmed, eventually embracing as the room darkens, echoing the cover art of *21st Century Breakdown*.
title: 21 Guns (song)

text: According to the series details, the new season of The Little Couple premiered on September 19, 2017.
title: The Little Couple

text: The nineteenth season of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit began airing on September 27, 2017.
title: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (season 19)

text: "How You Remind Me," a song by the Canadian rock band Nickelback, was released as the lead single from their third studio album *Silver Side Up* on August 21, 2001. A later “Gold Mix” version of the track removed the heavier guitars from the chorus for subsequent pressings. The song, written by lead vocalist and guitarist Chad Kroeger about his former girlfriend Jodi, is frequently cited as Nickelback’s signature tune and the record that propelled the band into mainstream recognition.
title: How You Remind Me

text: During the 1971 Indo‑Pakistani War, Pakistan’s head of state was President Yahya Khan. He authorized the deployment of the armed forces to East Pakistan, directing the predominantly West‑Pakistani military to quell dissent after the resignation of Lieutenant‑General Yaqub Ali Khan, the chief of staff of the Eastern command.
title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971

text: One More Light, the seventh studio album by the American rock band Linkin Park, was released on May 19, 2017 through Warner Bros. and the Machine Shop imprint. It later became the final Linkin Park record issued before lead vocalist Chester Bennington’s death on July 20, 2017.
title: One More Light

text: Actor Ted Levine gained fame for his breakout performance in the 1991 thriller *The Silence of the Lambs*, where he portrayed the film’s chief villain, the serial killer known as **Buffalo Bill**. Following that role he was often typecast in antagonistic parts before later moving into more sympathetic characters, such as a member of Al Pacino’s police unit in *Heat*, astronaut Alan Shepard in the HBO miniseries *From the Earth to the Moon*, and Sergeant Tanner, Paul Walker’s police superior, in *The Fast and the Furious*.
title: Ted Levine

text:
The Senate’s leadership was contested in June‑July 2009 when Democrats Hiram Monserrate and Pedro Espada Jr. joined the 30 Republican senators in a motion to remove Majority Leader Malcolm Smith and install Minority Leader Dean Skelos as the new leader. The proposal would also have split the temporary presidency from the majority leadership, a practice not seen since 1913. Because Lieutenant Governor David Paterson had become governor after Eliot Spitzer’s resignation, the Senate’s majority leaders—Bruno, Skelos and Smith—had been acting as lieutenant governors. The June 8 motion also sought to name Pedro Espada as Temporary President, which would have made him acting lieutenant governor, a move the Democrats later contested. Legal updates were posted by the Senate beginning June 11, 2009. The conflict ended on July 9, 2009, when Senator Espada announced his return to the Democratic caucus and his acceptance of the majority‑leader role; former Majority Leader Malcolm Smith became president pro tempore, and John Sampson was named Democratic conference leader with a future claim to the presidency.

After the 2010 elections gave Republicans control of the chamber, Dean Skelos of Long Island held both the Temporary President and Majority Leader positions until he resigned in May 2015 amid corruption allegations. The current majority leader, or president, is **John J. Flanagan**.
title: Majority Leader of the New York State Senate

text: Egyptologists hold that the Great Pyramid of Giza was erected as a tomb for the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh Khufu and that its construction spanned a 20-year period. The monument’s original height was about 280 Egyptian royal cubits (roughly 146.5 m), though erosion and the loss of its pyramidion have reduced it to the present 138.8 m. Each side of the base measured 440 cubits, or approximately 230.4 m, and the structure’s total mass is estimated at 5.9 million tonnes, giving it a volume of around 2.5 million cubic metres.
title: Great Pyramid of Giza

text: Dragon Ball Z was broadcast in Australia on the free‑to‑air commercial network Network Ten as part of the morning children’s program Cheez TV. The series originally aired in Fall 1998.
title: Dragon Ball Z

text: The City and Guilds of London Institute is an awarding organisation that maps its many accredited qualifications onto the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF). Its catalogue of regulated qualifications extends **entry level to level 7** on the RQF, with the majority of the offerings concentrated in the entry‑level to level‑3 range.
title: City and Guilds of London Institute

text: Follow the Leader, the third studio album from American nu‑metal band Korn, hit the market on August 18, 1998, through Immortal/Epic. Unlike their earlier releases, this record was not produced by Ross Robinson; the production duties were handled by Steve Thompson and Toby Wright.
title: Follow the Leader (Korn album)

text: Archaeologists have recovered small wheeled artifacts—identified as children’s toys—from Mexican archaeological sites that have been dated to about 1500 BC. These finds represent the earliest known introduction of the wheel in the Americas, although large‑scale use of wheels did not appear there until after European contact.
title: Wheel

text: According to David Ng of the Los Angeles Times, the architecture of the city plays a starring role in 500 Days of Summer. Although the story was initially set in San Francisco, the production was later relocated and the script rewritten to take advantage of Los Angeles, making the city the primary filming location. The movie 500 Days of Summer was filmed in Los Angeles. Several recognizable Los Angeles landmarks appear on screen, such as the Los Angeles Music Center with its Dorothy Chandler Pavilion, the towers of California Plaza, and the historic Fine Arts Building, which Tom shows to Summer while discussing its designers Walker and Eisen.
title: 500 Days of Summer

text: The 1964 single “The Birds and the Bees” was performed by Jewel Akens. Its lyrics riff on the well‑known “birds and the bees” expression that is commonly invoked when giving youngsters their first lesson in sex education. The record rose to international prominence in 1965, and its musical style evoked the 1950s honky‑tonk feel of hits like Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill” and Wilbert Harrison’s “Kansas City.”
title: The Birds and the Bees (Jewel Akens song)

text: The Bond film *From Russia with Love* uses a title song that is performed by Matt Monro. Monro’s vocal recording is heard in the movie both as source music on a radio and over the closing credits. The soundtrack also includes an instrumental version of the same melody, but the only sung rendition credited in the film is Monro’s.
title: From Russia with Love (soundtrack)

text: Thomas Rhett's third studio album, Life Changes, was released on September 8, 2017 through Valory Music Group. The record was co‑produced by Rhett together with Dann Huff, Jesse Frasure, Julian Bunetta, and Joe London, and it includes the hit singles “Craving You” (featuring Maren Morris) and “Unforgettable.” Upon release the album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 123,000 album‑equivalent units.
title: Life Changes (Thomas Rhett album)

text: The official music video for Panic! at the Disco’s “LA Devotee,” which premiered on September 22 2016, features actor Noah Schnapp—best known for his role in the Netflix series *Stranger Things*—as a central figure in the storyline. In the video, a young boy is strapped to a chair and forced to sing while bizarre, unsettling events unfold around him, with other characters appearing in cloaked attire. The visual narrative progresses through a series of surreal scenes, culminating in a tense confrontation that leaves the boy electrocuted and seizing, while the lead singer approaches menacingly.
title: LA Devotee

text: Kubo and the Two Strings opened in United States theaters on August 19, 2016, following an earlier screening at the Melbourne International Film Festival on August 13, 2016.
title: Kubo and the Two Strings

text: The 1973 “Battle of the Sexes” exhibition match was staged in the Houston Astrodome, pitting 55‑year‑old former champion Bobby Riggs against the 29‑year‑old Billie Jean King. In a three‑set contest, Billie Jean King emerged victorious, a result that drew an estimated 90 million viewers worldwide and marked a turning point for the public’s acceptance of women’s tennis.
title: Battle of the Sexes (tennis)

text: In 1534, following the formal union of the Duchy of Brittany with France, Jacques Cartier was introduced to King Francis I by the bishop Jean Le Veneur at the Manoir de Brion. Le Veneur highlighted Cartier’s earlier expeditions to Newfoundland and Brazil as proof of his ability to command ships on voyages of discovery in the New World.
title: Jacques Cartier

text: The movie’s soundtrack features songs penned by a range of writers—Dan Bern and Mike Viola (of the Candy Butchers) supplied most of the numbers, while Charlie Wadhams contributed “Let’s Duet,” Marshall Crenshaw wrote the title track, Van Dyke Parks created the 1960s‑style psychedelic piece “Black Sheep,” and Antonio Ortiz added “Take My Hand.” Critics praised the collection for its high‑quality parody of various musical eras, and it earned nominations for both a Grammy and a Golden Globe, as well as a Sierra Award for Best Song in a Motion Picture from the Las Vegas Film Critics Society. John C. Reilly sang on all the tracks and played guitar on most of them.
title: Walk Hard: The Dewey Cox Story

text: The eighth season of the CBS police procedural drama **Hawaii Five‑0** began its broadcast on September 29, 2017, launching the series’ 2017–18 television season.
title: Hawaii Five-0 (2010 TV series, season 8)

text: Prince Mohammad bin Salman earned his undergraduate law degree at King Saud University, where he completed a bachelor's program in legal studies.
title: Mohammad bin Salman

text: When Rod Temperton composed “Thriller,” he imagined a spoken‑word segment to close the track but was unsure who should deliver it. He decided the part should be voiced by a well‑known figure from horror films. Peggy Lipton, who was acquainted with the legendary actor, recommended him, and the actor consented to record the line. Consequently, the spoken vocal at the end of Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” was performed by Vincent Price.
title: Thriller (song)

text: Although the Word of Wisdom was originally presented as a set of health recommendations and explicitly stated that it was “not by commandment or constraint,” the policy shifted in February 1834 when Joseph Smith brought before the church’s high council a resolution declaring that any official member who had been properly taught the Word of Wisdom and then failed to obey it was unfit to hold a church office. The council accepted the resolution unanimously, making adherence to the Word of Wisdom effectively mandatory from that date.
title: Word of Wisdom

text: DreamWorks Dragons: Race to the Edge wrapped up with its sixth and final season, which was released on February 16, 2018.
title: List of DreamWorks Dragons episodes

text: In the “Call Me Maybe” music video, the handsome, tattoo‑covered neighbor that Carly (played by Jepsen) keeps spying on is identified as Holden Nowell. The clip opens with Holden Nowell working on his lawn when he notices her staring, prompting her to slip on her high heels and tumble below her window. Later, after a series of comedic mishaps—including falling from the hood of her car while trying to attract his attention—she finally meets him again as he helps her up and watches her band rehearse. The video also shows her discovering that Holden Nowell passes his own number to a male bandmate, indicating his lack of romantic interest in her.
title: Call Me Maybe

text: James Brown wrote and recorded the song “Papa’s Got a Brand New Bag.” Issued as a two‑part single in 1965, it became his first record to break into the Billboard Hot 100 Top Ten, peaking at number eight, and it ruled the R&B chart for eight weeks. The single also secured Brown his first Grammy Award, winning in the Best Rhythm & Blues Recording category.
title: Papa's Got a Brand New Bag

text: The seven‑layer OSI model of computer networking places the physical layer or layer 1 at the bottom, making it the first and lowest layer. This layer may be implemented by a PHY chip.
title: Physical layer

text: The Senior Open Championship—commonly known as The Senior Open—is a professional golf tournament for players aged 50 and over, organized by The R&A. Its prize fund is quoted in U.S. dollars and counts as official money on both the PGA Tour Champions and the European Senior Tour. The purse, which is fixed in United States dollars, was $2 million in 2011, with the winner taking home $315,600.
title: Senior Open Championship

text: The HBO drama *The Wire* employed the song “Way Down in the Hole” as its opening theme, but a different recording was chosen for each season. The series began with a version by The Blind Boys of Alabama, then used renditions by Tom Waits, The Neville Brothers, and DoMaJe. **Steve Earle** performed the version that was used as the theme for season 5. For season 4 a specially arranged recording was created by a group of Baltimore teenagers, and an extended Blind Boys of Alabama take appears during the montage in the series finale.
title: Way Down in the Hole

text: Historical research indicates that the Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence occurred on August 2, 1776, nearly a month after the Continental Congress had approved the final draft on July 4. This date is now accepted by most scholars, correcting the common belief that the signing took place on the adoption day.
title: Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence

text: The film The Mask introduces the gangster Dorian Tyrell, owner of the Coco Bongo nightclub who plots to overthrow his boss Niko; this character is portrayed by Peter Greene.
title: The Mask (film)

text: The expression first shows up in book six of the autobiography *Confessions* written by Jean-Jacques Rousseau. In that passage Rousseau recounts hearing a “great princess” utter the words while he, dressed too finely to enter a common bakery, sought bread to go with wine he had stolen. Although the remark is often linked to Queen Marie Antoinette, there is no record of her saying it; the phrase’s origin lies in Rousseau’s memoir, whose early books were composed in 1765 and later published in 1782.
title: Let them eat cake

text: At the Open University, module results can be graded on a pass/fail scale. A grade 3 pass is given when the student’s mark lies in the range **55–69%**. This grade is determined by taking the lower of the overall continuous‑assessment score (OCAS) and the overall examination score (OES).
title: Open University

text: EDF Energy, the United Kingdom’s integrated electricity and gas supplier, serves roughly 5.7 million customer accounts throughout the country.
title: EDF Energy

text: The August 21, 2017 solar eclipse’s total phase finished over the United States when the Moon’s shadow left the South Carolina shoreline at roughly 6:44 p.m. UTC, which is 2:44 p.m. EDT.
title: Solar eclipse of August 21, 2017

text: The Flash’s fourth season premiered on October 10, 2017, launching a 23‑episode run on The CW that will conclude on May 22, 2018.
title: The Flash (season 4)

text: On April 17, 1982 the Canada Act—officially the Constitution Act, 1982—was proclaimed, granting Canada full sovereignty and marking its complete independence from Great Britain. Although the monarch’s role as Canada’s head of state remained, the Act separated that position from the British Crown, confirming Canada as an autonomous nation.
title: Canada Act 1982

text: Jacob Marley, the first figure introduced in Charles Dickens’s *A Christmas Carol*, is noted to have passed away on December 24, 1836, which is seven years before the story’s setting on Christmas Eve 1843.
title: Jacob Marley

text: The film presents the events through the eyes of Paul Baumer, the student who leads his classmates to enlist; the story is told from his point of view, showing how his romantic ideals are quickly shattered by the harsh training under Sergeant Himmelstoss.
title: All Quiet on the Western Front (1930 film)

text: The opening ceremony for the 2018 Winter Olympics was conducted at the Pyeongchang Olympic Stadium in Pyeongchang, South Korea on 9 February 2018. The event commenced in the evening and concluded a little after two hours, with the Games being formally inaugurated by President Moon Jae‑in.
title: 2018 Winter Olympics opening ceremony

text: Rich Mullins wrote and recorded the contemporary worship song “Our God Is an Awesome God” for his 1988 album *Winds of Heaven, Stuff of Earth*. Released as the album’s lead single, the track quickly rose to the top of Christian radio and became one of Mullins’ signature songs.
title: Awesome God

text: In the 1969 film The Rose, Bette Midler portrays the character Mary Rose Foster, a celebrated rock‑and‑roll diva who is exhausted, lonely, and struggling with alcoholism and past drug use. Despite her fame, she feels insecure and longs for approval, prompting her to attempt a return to her hometown as a superstar. The story follows her turbulent relationships, including a romance with a limousine driver and the pressures that lead to a breakdown during a tour stop in Memphis.
title: The Rose (film)

text: Deadpool 2 is slated to open in United States theaters on May 18, 2018. A follow‑up film, Deadpool 3, is currently in development.
title: Deadpool 2

text: ‘Young and Beautiful’ is a track performed by **Lana Del Rey**, an American singer‑songwriter, created for the 2013 drama film *The Great Gatsby*. The single was issued on April 23 2013 through Interscope Records and serves as the lead song from the movie’s soundtrack. Lana Del Rey co‑wrote the composition with Rick Nowels, who also handled production. An orchestral version produced by Dan Heath appears on the deluxe edition of the soundtrack.
title: Young and Beautiful (Lana Del Rey song)

text: ‘A Thousand Years’ is a track performed by Christina Perri, an American singer‑songwriter who co‑wrote the song with David Hodges. It was included on the soundtrack for The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1 and released as the album’s second single, becoming available as a digital download worldwide on 18 October 2011. Perri later re‑recorded the piece with Steve Kazee for the sequel soundtrack, issuing it as “A Thousand Years, Pt. 2.”
title: A Thousand Years (Christina Perri song)

text: Charles Sherrington, the English neurophysiologist, introduced the word “synapse” in 1897 while contributing to Michael Foster’s Textbook of Physiology. He used the term to denote the junction where separate neurons exchange signals, establishing that neural communication occurs across a specialized connection rather than through a continuous fiber. Earlier, Santiago Ramón y Cajal had argued that neurons are discrete units, a view later incorporated into the neuron doctrine. The term itself, derived from the Greek synapsis (“conjunction”), was suggested by the classical scholar Arthur Woollgar Verrall.
title: Synapse

text: During a pep rally in the movie *Grease*, Kenickie proudly displays his beat‑up jalopy and declares that he has entered it in a “pinks” street race that is held at Thunder Road.
title: Grease (film)

text: George II (George Augustus; born 30 October 1683, died 25 October 1760) held the throne of Great Britain and Ireland from 11 June 1727 until his death. Since his reign spanned the whole year of 1756, the monarch of England in that year was George II.
title: George II of Great Britain

text: Principal photography for *The Book of Eli* commenced in February 2009, and the production filmed on location in New Mexico.
title: The Book of Eli

text: In March 1930, Cornelia Vanderbilt and her husband opened the Biltmore Estate to the public after the City of Asheville asked that the mansion become a tourist attraction to help revive the area during the Great Depression. The estate later closed during World War II, and in 1942 a convoy of trains brought 62 paintings and 17 sculptures from the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., to protect them from potential attacks. While the first‑floor Music Room remained unfinished and was used for storage, it housed works such as the Gilbert Stuart portrait of George Washington and pieces by Rembrandt, Raphael, and Anthony van Dyck until the threat diminished in 1944.
title: Biltmore Estate

text: The film *I Can Only Imagine* was released in the United States on March 16, 2018. It later grossed $80 million worldwide against a $7 million production budget, ranking as the third‑highest‑grossing music biopic ever in the United States. Critics were split, with some applauding its inspirational qualities while others described it as flat and formulaic.
title: I Can Only Imagine (film)

text: Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword is a stand‑alone expansion of the Mount & Blade series, created by Sich Studio and TaleWorlds and published in Europe by Paradox Interactive. Its narrative, drawn loosely from Henryk Sienkiewicz’s novel, follows Poland’s conflict with the Khmelnytsky Uprising in Ukraine, a war that unfolded in 1648-51.
title: Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword

text: The title track for the James Bond film *From Russia with Love* was recorded by vocalist Matt Monro, who performed the movie’s theme song.
title: From Russia with Love (soundtrack)

text: The novelty Christmas tune “I Want a Hippopotamus for Christmas” was written by John Rox and first recorded in 1953. The original version was performed by ten‑year‑old singer Gayla Peevey, and the single climbed to number 24 on Billboard’s pop chart that December.
title: I Want a Hippopotamus for Christmas

text: Zhu Di, who seized the Ming throne in 1402 and took the reign title Yongle Emperor, ordered the construction of the Forbidden City. After design work by a team of architects, the building project was launched in 1406, establishing Beijing as a secondary capital of the empire. The palace complex that emerged from this initiative would become known as the Forbidden City.
title: History of the Forbidden City

text: During production of the film **The Devil Wears Prada**, costume designer Patricia Field received a $100,000 budget that was supplemented by contributions from friends throughout the fashion industry, eventually leading to more than $1 million worth of clothing being used in the movie. While numerous designers helped behind the scenes, the only designer who actually appears on screen is **Valentino Garavani**. The single most expensive item featured is a $100,000 Fred Leighton necklace worn by Meryl Streep.
title: The Devil Wears Prada (film)

text: The ninth and final season of the animated series *Adventure Time* debuted on Cartoon Network on April 21, 2017. Produced by Cartoon Network Studios and Frederator Studios, this season continues to follow Finn, a human boy, and his magical‑shapeshifting adoptive brother Jake as they explore the post‑apocalyptic Land of Ooo alongside characters such as Princess Bubblegum, the Ice King, Marceline the Vampire Queen, Lumpy Space Princess, BMO, and Flame Princess. The series was slated to wrap up sometime in 2018.
title: Adventure Time (season 9)

text: The American period sitcom **That ’70s Show** premiered on the Fox network on **August 23, 1998**, beginning its original run that would continue until May 18, 2006. The series follows a group of teenage friends living in the fictional town of Point Place, Wisconsin, during the years 1976 to 1979.
title: That '70s Show

text: The Simon Commission’s arrival in India coincided with the tenure of Viceroy Lord Irwin. It was Lord Irwin who selected the members of the All‑India Committee for Cooperation with the Commission, establishing the body under the Council of India’s direction.
title: Simon Commission

text: Michael Jackson's 1982 single “Thriller” is featured on a number of his greatest‑hits compilations, including HIStory (1995), Number Ones (2003), The Essential Michael Jackson (2005) and Michael Jackson’s This Is It (2009), and it was later remixed for the Immortal album in 2011. The song has a voice‑over from actor Vincent Price.
title: Thriller (song)

text: In Roman mythology the deity who rules the underworld and is sometimes identified with the obscure god Orcus or with the Greek‑derived name Pluto is called **Dis Pater**. The name Dis Pater is commonly understood to mean “Rich Father” and is thought to be a direct translation of the Greek Plouton. Although the Greek name Pluto is occasionally used in Latin literature for the ruler of the dead, the traditional Roman counterpart of the underworld god is Dis Pater.
title: Pluto (mythology)

text: In popular depictions, the heavenly gates—often imagined as large golden, white, or wrought‑iron portals set among the clouds—are watched over by Saint Peter, the keeper of the keys to the kingdom. Those deemed unworthy are turned away and sent elsewhere, while in some portrayals Peter consults a book of names before opening the gate.
title: Pearly gates

text: Lost in Space (2018 TV series) is an American science‑fiction show that re‑imagines the 1965 series of the same name. The story follows a pioneering family of space colonists whose ship goes off course. Written by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless and produced by Legendary Television, Synthesis Entertainment, Clickety‑Clack Productions, and Applebox Entertainment, the ten‑episode series was overseen by showrunner Zack Estrin. Netflix made the series available to viewers on **April 13, 2018**.
title: Lost in Space (2018 TV series)

text: The 1971 single “How Can You Mend a Broken Heart” was performed by the Bee Gees. Written chiefly by Barry and Robin Gibb, it served as the lead and first single from the group’s 1971 album *Trafalgar*, and went on to become their first U.S. No. 1 hit, also topping the Cashbox chart for two weeks.
title: How Can You Mend a Broken Heart

text: The Second Continental Congress, meeting in Philadelphia’s State House, cast its vote to adopt the resolution for independence on July 2, 1776, and then publicly proclaimed the decision two days later when the Declaration of Independence was presented. Thomas Jefferson of Virginia authored the declaration, while John Adams led the pro‑adoption debates and John Hancock of Massachusetts served as president during those proceedings. The Congress continued to govern throughout the Revolutionary War, meeting at various locations until it transitioned into the Congress of the Confederation after the Articles of Confederation were ratified on March 1, 1781.
title: Continental Congress

text: Around c. 3000 BC the two kingdoms of Upper and Lower Egypt were first united, although each region kept its own royal regalia—the white hedjet crown for Upper Egypt and the red deshret crown for Lower Egypt. Consequently, pharaohs were styled as rulers of the Two Lands and wore the pschent, a double crown that combined the symbols of both realms. Ancient Egyptian tradition attributes this initial unification to the king known as Menes, who is now identified with Narmer; the Narmer Palette shows him wearing each crown in separate scenes, signifying his authority over both lands.
title: Upper and Lower Egypt

text: Construction of the new Tappan Zee Bridge began in 2013 under the direction of Tappan Zee Constructors. The north span opened to westbound traffic on August 26, 2017 and later to eastbound traffic on October 6, 2017. Following the opening, work started on demolishing the old bridge, and eastbound traffic will be moved onto the south span once it is finished. Both spans are expected to be in operation by June 15, 2018.
title: Tappan Zee Bridge (2017–present)

text: Athens rose to become the dominant economic power in Greece around the late 6th century BCE, a status that was reinforced by the discovery of several silver veins in the nearby mountains, which greatly increased its wealth. This prosperity enabled the city‑state to develop an efficient trading network with other Greek polities, moving large quantities of pottery and cooking utensils (over 80,000 amphorae and similar items have been uncovered in archaeological contexts around Athens). Marble and bronze artworks were also exchanged, though these luxury goods saw a major surge only after the Roman Republic’s rise, when Greek art heavily influenced Roman culture. Because of its poor soil, Athens began importing grain to meet its needs.
title: Economic history of Greece and the Greek world

text: The 1967 Walt Disney animated feature *The Jungle Book* contains the musical number “I Wan’na Be Like You.” Written by the Sherman brothers, the song is performed by Louis Prima.
title: I Wan'na Be like You (The Monkey Song)

text: Kidney transplantation is divided according to the origin of the donor organ, and when the kidney is obtained from a person who is still alive, it is described as a living‑donor transplantation.
title: Kidney transplantation

text: The earliest surviving written record that mentions a Chinese abacus dates to the 2nd century BC.
title: Abacus

text: Star Wars Battlefront II, the action‑shooter sequel in the Star Wars film franchise series, launched globally on November 17, 2017 for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Microsoft Windows.
title: Star Wars Battlefront II (2017 video game)

text: Ellen's Game of Games is an American television game show that made its debut on December 18, 2017. The series, hosted by Ellen DeGeneres with Stephen “tWitch” Boss as announcer, was ordered by NBC earlier that year and launched with a special preview episode on that same date.
title: Ellen's Game of Games

text: Season five of RWBY (Volume 5) launched on October 14, 2017, a release date that was initially announced at the RTX Austin 2017 event. New episodes are first made available to Rooster Teeth FIRST subscribers on Saturdays at 10 a.m. Central Time, then to all Rooster Teeth members the following Tuesday, and finally to the general public the subsequent Saturday.
title: List of RWBY episodes

text: Bruno, a nine‑year‑old boy, grows up in Berlin while World War II is raging. After his father is promoted following a visit by Adolf Hitler, the family is forced to move to a remote location the boy calls “Out‑With,” which is in fact the Auschwitz camp. From their new home Bruno observes a fenced camp where prisoners wear striped pajamas, and he eventually befriends a Jewish boy named Shmuel who lives on the other side of the fence.
title: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas

text: The Christmas carol “What Child Is This?” contains lyrics that were penned in 1865 by William Chatterton Dix. At that time Dix worked as a manager for an insurance company and was convalescing from a severe illness that sparked a spiritual renewal, prompting him to write a number of hymns, including the words to this carol, which was later paired with the traditional English folk tune “Greensleeves.” Although the piece was created in Great Britain, it is now more popular in the United States than in its country of origin.
title: What Child Is This?

text: During the lengthy casting process for the lead of Indiana Jones, George Lucas and Steven Spielberg ultimately chose actor Tom Selleck for the part. However, CBS would not release him from his contractual obligations on *Magnum, P.I.*, forcing him to turn down the role.
title: Indiana Jones

text: Consumers International notes that World Consumer Rights Day is observed on 15 March every year.
title: Consumers International

text: In the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man and Ireland, the confection formerly marketed as Marathon was rebranded as Snickers on 19 July 1990.
title: Snickers

text: Staind is an American rock band that formed in 1995. Among its original members were lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist Aaron Lewis, lead guitarist Mike Mushok, bassist and backing vocalist Johnny April, and drummer Jon Wysocki. Aaron Lewis has been the group's frontman since its inception.
title: Staind

text: The song “My Bucket’s Got a Hole in It” was originally credited to Clarence Williams, who obtained a copyright for it in 1933. It was Hank Williams’s recording for MGM that made the tune a hit, carrying it to the No. 4 spot on the country chart in 1949.
title: My Bucket's Got a Hole in It

text: In the series’ debut season, Kelly Taylor’s mother, Jackie, is played by actress Ann Gillespie. The storyline follows their strained relationship, which is highlighted throughout the early episodes.
title: Kelly Taylor (90210)

text: The 1956 single “Hallelujah I Love Her So” was written and recorded by American musician Ray Charles. Issued on the Atlantic label, the jazz‑ and rhythm‑and‑blues‑styled track was later included on his self‑titled debut album in 1957, also released by Atlantic, and it climbed to number five on the Billboard R&B chart. The composition is loosely based on Ike Turner’s 1953 song “Get It Over Baby.”
title: Hallelujah I Love Her So

text: The blues composition titled “Mean Old World” was recorded in 1942 by the American electric‑guitar blues musician T‑Bone Walker, whose rendition is regarded as one of the earliest significant electric‑guitar blues recordings.
title: Mean Old World

text: Following its premiere at the El Capitan Theatre on February 26, 2018, the live‑action version of *A Wrinkle in Time* entered Canadian theatres on March 9, 2018, where it was shown in Disney Digital 3‑D, Real D 3D, and IMAX formats.
title: A Wrinkle in Time (2018 film)

text: In the narrative of *The Deep End of the Ocean*, it is disclosed that at a Chicago reunion the celebrity alumna Cecil Lockhart kidnapped a boy named Ben, renamed him Sam, and raised him as her own child until she was later committed to a mental hospital. After Lockhart’s confinement, Sam was taken in by his adoptive father, the thoughtful and scholarly George Karras, and grew up in a house just two blocks from the Cappadora family.
title: The Deep End of the Ocean

text: The Assamese movie Mission China premiered on 8 September, playing in 55 theatres throughout Assam and additional locations such as Delhi, Bangalore, Pune and Mumbai. Its opening‑day net takings amounted to ₹ 39.97 lakh.
title: Mission China

text: The film’s principal theme, the piece titled “The Gael,” was composed by Scottish singer‑songwriter Dougie MacLean and originally appeared on his 1990 album *The Search*.
title: The Last of the Mohicans (soundtrack)

text: In the soundtrack for *The Last of the Mohicans*, tracks 1–9 were composed by Trevor Jones, while the principal theme was created by Dougie MacLean; tracks 10–15 were provided by Randy Edelman.
title: The Last of the Mohicans (soundtrack)

text: The G‑Wagen, officially known as the Mercedes‑Benz G‑Class, is a mid‑size, four‑wheel‑drive luxury SUV that is marketed and sold by Mercedes‑Benz. It is recognized for its boxy styling, body‑on‑frame construction, and the use of three fully locking differentials. Despite the introduction of newer models, the G‑Class remains in production and continues the long‑standing lineage of Mercedes‑Benz vehicles.
title: Mercedes-Benz G-Class

text: Principal photography for the movie began in January 2015 in New Zealand. Filming was carried out at several New Zealand sites, including the Bay of Plenty, Taupo, Wellington, Rotorua and later Tapanui, where the former Blue Mountain Lumber mill stood in for the film’s mill.
title: Pete's Dragon (2016 film)

text: In the 2000 Mexican presidential election, the Alliance for Change’s candidate Vicente Fox won the presidency, receiving 43.4 percent of the vote and becoming the first opposition victor since the Mexican Revolution.
title: Mexican general election, 2000

text: Hero Beauregard Fiennes‑Tiffin, an English actor born on 6 November 1997, portrays the eleven‑year‑old Tom Riddle—the young version of Lord Voldemort—in the sixth Harry Potter film, *Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince*.
title: Hero Fiennes-Tiffin

text: Clash Royale, the freemium mobile tower‑rush title created and published by Supercell, debuted worldwide on March 2, 2016, which is also the date it became available to players in the United States.
title: Clash Royale

text: After an initial soft‑launch in a handful of regions, Clash Royale received its worldwide rollout on March 2, 2016, which included its release in the United States.
title: Clash Royale

text: In Max Boyce’s celebrated poem “9 – 3,” which recounts Llanelli RFC’s triumph over the New Zealand All Blacks at Stradey Park, the match occurred on 31 October 1972. The game, attended by 26,000 spectators, finished 9‑3 to Llanelli, and the ensuing revelry was so massive that the town’s public houses ran out of alcoholic drinks – a night forever remembered as the day the pubs ran dry.
title: Llanelli RFC

text: AARP operates as a 501(c)(4) organization that lobbies on behalf of older Americans at both state and national levels. The group states that it is non‑partisan and does not support, oppose, or give money to any political candidates or parties. In 2006 the organization reported roughly $1 billion in revenue and allocated $23 million to lobbying activities. Recent initiatives have emphasized middle‑class security, and AARP also provides consumer information, volunteer opportunities, and hosts its annual National Event & Expo.
title: AARP

text: Middle‑earth: Shadow of Mordor, the open‑world action‑adventure developed by Monolith Productions and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, debuted on Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in September 2014, with the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 versions following in November 2014. It is the second Middle‑earth game to earn an ESRB Mature rating, after The Lord of the Rings: War in the North.
title: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor

text: In the movie *Kingsman: The Secret Service*, the character of Crown Princess Tilde of Sweden is portrayed by Hanna Alström.
title: Kingsman: The Secret Service

text: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was created in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. Its secretariat operates from Kathmandu, Nepal, and the body works to advance economic development and regional integration among its members.
title: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation

text: Seth MacFarlane provides the voice for Stewie Griffin on *Family Guy*; he also supplies the voices for the show’s other main characters, Peter and Brian Griffin.
title: List of Family Guy cast members

text: The Paraguayan guaraní, introduced after the 1943 law that replaced the peso at a 1‑to‑100 ratio, was later fixed to the U.S. dollar. Between 1960 and 1985, the guaraní was pegged at a rate of 126 PYG to 1 USD.
title: Paraguayan guaraní

text: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union in the referendum held on 23 June 2016, when 51.9 % of participating voters chose to exit the EU.
title: Brexit

text: "I'm Coming Out" is a track performed by American vocalist Diana Ross. The song was penned and produced by Chic’s Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers, and it was issued as the second single from Ross’s self‑titled tenth album, *Diana*. The single was released on **August 22, 1980**.
title: I'm Coming Out

text: In the TV adaptation of the comic series Preacher, the fearsome figure called the Saint of Killers is portrayed on screen by Graham McTavish.
title: Saint of Killers

text: Imagine Dragons is an American rock group that originates from Las Vegas, Nevada, and is composed of lead vocalist Dan Reynolds, lead guitarist Wayne Sermon, bassist‑keyboardist Ben McKee, and drummer Daniel Platzman. Their early breakthrough came with the single “It’s Time,” followed by the award‑winning debut album *Night Visions* (2012), which produced chart‑topping tracks such as “Radioactive” and “Demons.”
title: Imagine Dragons

text: Clifford the Big Red Dog, the American‑British educational animated series based on Norman Bridwell’s books, premiered on PBS Kids on September 4, 2000 and ran until February 25, 2003. A UK edition, re‑voiced with British actors, later started airing on BBC 2 on April 1, 2002.
title: Clifford the Big Red Dog (TV series)

text: Ain’t Living Long Like This is the first studio album released by American country‑music singer‑songwriter Rodney Crowell. Issued in 1978 on Warner Bros. Records, the record did not reach the Top Country Albums chart, and its singles—“Elvira,” “Baby Better Start Turnin’ ’Em Down,” and “(Now and Then, There’s) A Fool Such as I”—failed to break into the top‑40. Despite the modest commercial response, the album is widely regarded as one of Crowell’s most influential works, showcasing his songwriting skill and his ability to interpret both his own material and that of other writers. Several tracks were later covered by artists such as The Oak Ridge Boys and Alan Jackson, and a 2002 reissue enlarged the cover’s font for better legibility.
title: Ain't Living Long Like This

text: The Bell UH‑1 Iroquois acquired its famous “Huey” nickname because it was originally designated HU‑1; even after the official redesignation to UH‑1 in 1962, the original HU‑1 designation continues to be the source of the name.
title: Bell UH-1 Iroquois

text: The fourth installment of Fox’s musical comedy‑drama Glee was green‑lit on April 9, 2012, and its debut episode aired on September 13, 2012. This season was produced by 20th Century Fox Television, Ryan Murphy Television, and Brad Falchuk Teley‑Vision, with Dante Di Loreto, series co‑creators Ryan Murphy, Brad Falchuk and Ian Brennan serving as executive producers.
title: Glee (season 4)

text: The 1927 adventure novel The Treasure of the Sierra Madre (originally titled Der Schatz der Sierra Madre) was written by the bilingual German writer B. Traven, whose true identity has never been confirmed.
title: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre

text: In 1969, John McConnell designed a flag to mark the first Earth Day. The banner displays a dark‑blue field on which the iconic “Blue Marble” photograph of Earth, taken by NASA, is centered. The initial version was screen‑printed, using blue for both ocean and land and white for the clouds. McConnell subsequently offered his flag to the United Nations as a symbol for contemplation.
title: Flag of Earth

text: In the animated series *Over the Garden Wall*, the half‑brothers Wirt and Greg wander through the enigmatic forest called the Unknown. Along their journey they receive occasional assistance from a mysterious, elderly figure known as the Woodsman, who is voiced by Christopher Lloyd. The show also features the irritable bluebird Beatrice, voiced by Melanie Lynskey, who travels with the boys in search of Adelaide, a woman believed to be able to lift the curse on her family and guide the brothers home.
title: Over the Garden Wall

text: American Idol, the U.S. singing‑competition series created by Simon Fuller, was first broadcast on the Fox network beginning on June 11, 2002. After fifteen seasons, its original run concluded on April 7, 2016. (The show later returned on ABC in 2018.)
title: American Idol

text: The annual San Fermin festival in Pamplona, which features the famous running of the bulls, is held each year from 6–14 July. The first encierro occurs on 7 July, and a subsequent run is held every morning of the festival, each starting at 8 a.m. Participants must be at least 18 years old, run in the same direction as the bulls, avoid provoking them, and must not be under the influence of alcohol.
title: Running of the Bulls

text: The custom of setting up an entire evergreen tree for Christmas was unheard of in Britain until the turn of the 19th century. In 1800, George III’s German‑born consort, Charlotte of Mecklenburg‑Strelitz, displayed a Christmas tree at a party she organized for children, thereby bringing the tradition to the United Kingdom. At first the practice remained largely confined to the royal family.
title: Christmas tree

text: The Fox quiz series *Are You Smarter Than a 5th Grader?* began its run with a three‑day special that launched on **February 27, 2007**; the first two installments of that special were half‑hour episodes. Regular one‑hour episodes followed a few days later, and the show continued to air in subsequent seasons.
title: Are You Smarter than a 5th Grader? (U.S. game show)

text: The British mock‑documentary comedy *Come Fly with Me*, devised and performed by Matt Lucas and David Walliams and narrated by Lindsay Duncan, made its debut on BBC One and BBC One HD on 25 December 2010. The show parodies the style of UK aviation programmes such as *Airport* and *Airline*, following the antics at a fictional airport and its three imagined carriers: the budget airline FlyLo, the Irish low‑cost carrier Our Lady Air, and the major carrier Great British Air.
title: Come Fly with Me (2010 TV series)

text: After the TV movie *The Homecoming: A Christmas Story* aired on December 19, 1971, CBS ordered a regular series based on the same characters. The resulting series, called **The Waltons**, premiered on CBS in **September 1972** and continued for nine seasons.
title: The Waltons

text: “Things That Make You Go Hmmm…” is a track by the American dance act C+C Music Factory. It was issued as the third single from their album *Gonna Make You Sweat* and hit the market in June 1991. The release features a rap verse by Freedom Williams, who also appears in the accompanying music video. The song later sparked a recurring joke on *The Arsenio Hall Show*, where the host would humorously label various musings as “things that make you go hmmm…”.
title: Things That Make You Go Hmmm...

text: The track titled “If She Knew What She Wants” was written and performed by Jules Shear, appearing on his 1985 release *The Eternal Return*. A year later, The Bangles recorded their own version for the 1986 album *Different Light*.
title: If She Knew What She Wants

text: The 2018 World Men’s Curling Championship opened on March 31 and ran through April 8, 2018, with the competition staged at the Orleans Arena on the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise, Nevada, United States.
title: 2018 World Men's Curling Championship

text: The 2018 reboot of *Tomb Raider* stars Alicia Vikander as Lara Croft, anchoring the film’s cast. In addition to Vikander’s lead performance, the movie includes supporting roles for Dominic West, Walton Goggins, Daniel Wu and Kristin Scott Thomas.
title: Tomb Raider (film)

text: The practice of striking coins that displayed the issuer’s own name began with the Indo‑Greek kings. They were the earliest rulers to place their personal names on minted currency, a convention later adopted by other Indian dynasties such as the Satavahanas, who copied the method after defeating the Western Kshatrapas.
title: Satavahana dynasty

text: Nintendo Co., Ltd., the Japanese multinational renowned for its video‑game franchises, traces its origins to 23 September 1889, when Fusajiro Yamauchi founded the company as a producer of handcrafted hanafuda playing cards.
title: Nintendo

text: After the princely state of Hyderabad joined the Indian Union on 24 November 1949, the region was constituted as Hyderabad State, a state of independent India that existed from 1948 until it was reorganised in 1956.
title: Hyderabad State (1948–56)

text: Season two of *Jessica Jones* is slated to debut on March 8, 2018.
title: Jessica Jones (season 2)

text: Robbie Coltrane, the actor chosen by J. K. Rowling to portray the half‑giant Rubeus Hagrid in the Harry Potter films (2001–2011), is 6ft 1in tall; for certain shots an unnamed stand‑in of about 8 ft was used in his place.
title: Robbie Coltrane

text: On February 5, 2017, the Super Bowl LI halftime show was held at NRG Stadium in Houston, Texas. The performance was headlined by Lady Gaga, who presented a medley of her songs and included newer material from her most recent studio album, Joanne.
title: Super Bowl LI halftime show

text: During Super Bowl XXXVII, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were led on offense by quarterback Brad Johnson. Early in the game, a pass thrown by Johnson was intercepted by Raiders cornerback Charles Woodson, who returned the ball to the Buccaneers’ 36‑yard line, setting up a Raiders field‑goal attempt.
title: Super Bowl XXXVII

text: The Fate of the Furious opened in Indian theatres on April 12, 2017, as part of its simultaneous worldwide rollout across major markets.
title: The Fate of the Furious

text: The AMC Theaters website, posted on August 16, listed the opening of the third Jeepers Creepers film as September 26, 2017. Shortly thereafter, on August 29, selected cinemas began selling tickets and released the official poster, indicating that the movie would be shown for a single night. A later encore screening was added for October 4, and additional venues such as Marcus Theaters and Galaxy Theaters participated in the limited‑run event.
title: Jeepers Creepers 3

text: In an interview with Catalunya Ràdio, Lana Del Rey explained that her third extended play, *Paradise*, would include three new tracks: “I Sing the Body Electric,” “In the Land of Gods and Monsters,” and “Will You Still Love Me When I’m No Longer Young and Beautiful.” During the same broadcast she also performed the chorus of “Young and Beautiful.”
title: Young and Beautiful (Lana Del Rey song)

text: The lyric “Will you still love me when I’m no longer young and beautiful?” appears in the song “Young and Beautiful,” which is performed by Lana Del Rey. Her ethereal voice is layered over muted strings and programmed percussion, creating a nostalgic mood that echoes the 1920s setting of the novel that inspired the track. A remix by Cedric Gervais was released on October 11, 2013.
title: Young and Beautiful (Lana Del Rey song)

text: David McCallum portrays the NCIS medical examiner Dr. Donald “Ducky” Mallard in the American television series NCIS.
title: David McCallum

text: Amnesia: The Dark Descent was originally slated for an August 2010 launch, but the schedule was later shifted, and the game was ultimately released on 8 September 2010. The title reached Gold status on 27 August 2010, a demo became available on 3 September, and the full version became commercially available on the aforementioned 8 September 2010 date.
title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent

text: The country song “I Just Want to Dance with You,” penned by John Prine and Roger Cook, was recorded and released by American singer George Strait in April 1998 as the lead single from his album *One Step at a Time*. The single became his 34th Number One on Billboard’s Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart (now Hot Country Songs) and his 42nd overall Number One when all major trade charts are considered. (Prine’s own version had first appeared on his 1986 album *German Afternoons*.)
title: I Just Want to Dance with You

text: The inaugural Christmas cards were ordered by Sir Henry Cole. He engaged artist John Callcott Horsley to create the design, and the commission was made in London on 1 May 1843. The first issue featured a central illustration of three generations of a family raising a toast, flanked by charitable scenes of food and clothing being distributed to the poor. Two print runs totalling 2,050 cards were produced that year, each sold for a shilling.
title: Christmas card

text: The 1979 hit single titled “Just When I Needed You Most” was recorded by the American singer‑songwriter Randy VanWarmer.
title: Just When I Needed You Most

text: The European fairy tale known as Little Red Riding Hood was eventually set down in print, and one of the earliest and most celebrated literary versions was authored by Charles Perrault. His written rendition helped establish the story’s lasting form.
title: Little Red Riding Hood

text: The earliest known printed version of Little Red Riding Riding Hood, called *Le Petit Chaperon Rouge*, was published in 1697 as part of the collection *Tales of Mother Goose* (Histoires et contes du temps passé, avec des moralités). This inaugural French edition was authored by Charles Perrault, and it introduced the red hood while giving the tale a darker, more moralizing tone.
title: Little Red Riding Hood

text: “Put Your Hand in the Hand” is a gospel‑pop composition written by Gene MacLellan. The song was first released by Canadian vocalist Anne Murray on her third studio album, *Honey, Wheat and Laughter*.
title: Put Your Hand in the Hand

text: The music video for “Lips of an Angel,” which debuted in early 2007 under the direction of Shaun Silva, dramatizes the song’s storyline by centering on a midnight telephone conversation. In the video, the singer Austin Winkler speaks with his ex‑girlfriend, portrayed by actress Emmanuelle Chriqui.
title: Lips of an Angel

text: The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, popularly known as Rio+20, was hosted by Brazil in Rio de Janeiro during June 2012. The summit unfolded over ten days, running from 13 to 22 June 2012, and served as the third major international gathering on sustainable development, commemorating both the 20‑year anniversary of the 1992 Earth Summit and the 10th anniversary of the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development.
title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development

text: The duet “Does He Love You,” penned by Sandy Knox and Billy Stritch, was recorded by American country vocalists Reba McEntire and Linda Davis. Issued in August 1993 as the lead single from Reba’s Greatest Hits Volume Two, the song has become one of country music’s well‑known tracks about a love triangle.
title: Does He Love You

text: The Eurostar’s London terminus is St Pancras International, with additional British stops at Ebbsfleet International and Ashford International in Kent. In France, the service calls at Calais‑Fréthun and Lille‑Europe before reaching Paris‑Gare du Nord, while Belgian routes end at Brussels‑Midi/Zuid. Dutch services include a stop at Rotterdam Centraal before terminating at Amsterdam Centraal, and seasonal routes run to destinations such as Disneyland Paris, southern France and the French Alps.
title: Eurostar

text: Krypton‑85, which has a half‑life of 10.756 years, most often undergoes a beta‑particle emission. In this dominant decay mode the nucleus is converted into the stable, non‑radioactive isotope rubidium‑85. The beta particles released have a maximum energy of 687 keV (average 251 keV), and a much less frequent branch (0.43 %) involves a lower‑energy beta particle followed by a 514 keV gamma ray.
title: Krypton-85

text: The New Testament supplies four separate enumerations of the apostles—Mark 3:13‑19, Matthew 10:1‑4, Luke 6:12‑16, and Acts 1:13. In the passage Acts 1:13 the twelve disciples are specifically listed.
title: Apostles

text: The university takes its name from St. Ignatius of Loyola. His family’s heraldic crest—displayed on the lintel of the family home in Azpeitia, Spain—shows two wolves standing over a kettle, a symbol of the Loyola family’s generosity and prosperity. This coat‑of‑arms inspired the school’s mascot and is the source of the institution’s name.
title: Loyola University Chicago

text: Season 8 of the American comedy‑drama *Shameless* is set to return on November 5, 2017. The series, which adapts the award‑winning British show created by Paul Abbott, announced this twelfth‑episode season on December 19, 2016, a day after the finale of its seventh season.
title: Shameless (season 8)

text: Britain’s East India Company was created when Queen Elizabeth I granted it a Royal Charter on 31 December 1600, formally establishing the English trading venture in the Indies.
title: East India Company

text: Ajay Tyagi was named the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India on 10 January 2017, taking over from U K Sinha, and he formally assumed the chairmanship on 1 March 2017.
title: Securities and Exchange Board of India

text: Virgin Australia Airlines Pty Ltd, which started out as Virgin Blue, was founded in November 1999. The airline was launched by British entrepreneur Richard Branson together with former Virgin Blue chief executive Brett Godfrey, initially operating two aircraft on a single route.
title: Virgin Australia

text: In the movie *Little Shop of Horrors*, Seymour Krelborn works at Mushnik’s Flower Shop in a rundown New York City neighborhood. To boost sales, he displays an odd plant he had purchased from a Chinese flower shop during a solar eclipse. He names this strange specimen **Audrey II**, and it quickly becomes the shop’s attraction, eventually revealing a need for human blood to survive.
title: Little Shop of Horrors (film)

text: Since West Bengal’s establishment in 1947, the state has been led by eight chief ministers. The inaugural chief minister was Prafulla Chandra Ghosh of the Indian National Congress.
title: List of Chief Ministers of West Bengal

text: In the light‑independent reactions of photosynthesis, the first step is the fixation of atmospheric CO₂ by the enzyme RuBisCO. This enzyme attaches the carbon from CO₂ to a three‑carbon compound, producing 3‑phosphoglycerate as the initial stable product of carbon fixation.
title: C4 carbon fixation

text: Beryl Markham’s historic trans‑Atlantic attempt took place in early September 1936. She departed from Abingdon, England on 4 September 1936, and after a roughly 20‑hour nonstop flight she was forced to crash‑land at Baleine Cove on Cape Breton Island, Nova Scotia, becoming the first person to fly nonstop from England to North America westward.
title: Beryl Markham

text: The American rock band P.O.D. issued their song “Boom” as the third single from the album Satellite in May 2002. Although it did not achieve the same chart success as earlier singles, the track has been featured extensively in movies and television. A remix titled “Boom (The Crystal Method remix)” appeared on the remix collection Community Service and as a bonus track on the special‑edition re‑release of Satellite on August 27, 2002, while a limited‑edition gatefold picture disc of the single was also released in the United Kingdom.
title: Boom (P.O.D. song)

text: From Under the Cork Tree, the second studio album by American rock band Fall Out Boy, was issued on May 3, 2005 through Island Records, marking the group’s major‑label debut. The record’s music was written by lead vocalist and guitarist Patrick Stump, while all lyrics were supplied by bassist Pete Wentz, continuing the collaborative approach they used on their 2003 album Take This to Your Grave. Production was overseen by Neal Avron, and the release was supported by worldwide headline tours and festival appearances. A later reissue for the Black Clouds and Underdogs tour added new songs and remixes.
title: From Under the Cork Tree

text: Mount Ruapehu’s most recent eruption occurred on 25 September 2007, when a hydrothermal blast erupted at about 8:20 p.m. without warning. The explosion sent a rock crashing into the Dome Shelter near the crater, crushing the leg of William Pike, a 22‑year‑old primary‑school teacher, and triggering a rescue effort.
title: Mount Ruapehu

text: The transformation of the California Insurance Commissioner from a governor‑appointed role to an elected office occurred because voters approved Proposition 103 in 1988; that initiative paved the way for the creation of the elected commissioner position in 1991.
title: California Insurance Commissioner

text: The country song “Humble and Kind” was written by Lori McKenna. It debuted as the second single from Tim McGraw’s 14th studio album, *Damn Country Music*, when it was released on January 20, 2016. Later that year McKenna recorded her own version for her eighth album, *The Bird and the Rifle*, which arrived in July 2016. The track went on to win Best Country Song at the 59th Grammy Awards, Video of the Year at the 2016 CMT Music Awards, Song of the Year at the 2016 CMA Awards, and Country Song of the Year at the 2016 American Music Awards, and it achieved platinum certification while topping the country charts in both Canada and the United States.

text: Yo La Tengo’s fifteenth full‑length studio album, *There’s a Riot Going On*, was issued by Matador Records on March 16, 2018.
title: There's a Riot Going On

text: “Where Are Ü Now,” the collaborative track by Skrillex and Diplo (as Jack Ü) featuring Justin Bieber, was made public on February 27, 2015, the same day the duo’s debut album Skrillex and Diplo Present Jack Ü was released. The song later reached mainstream radio on April 21, 2015.
title: Where Are Ü Now

text: The pop single titled “Bobby’s Girl,” written by Gary Klein and Henry Hoffman, was recorded and released by the American teenage singer Marcie Blane.
title: Bobby's Girl (song)

text: In Poland the custom called prima aprilis—literally “1 April” in Latin—is a long‑standing day of jokes, hoaxes and playful deception. Although the whole day is filled with pranks, many Poles regard the celebration as officially ending at noon on April 1st; jokes made after that hour are generally considered inappropriate and not in good taste.
title: April Fools' Day

text: The command that forbids blasphemy—misusing or treating the name of the God of Israel disrespectfully or for evil purposes—is included among the Ten Commandments and is recorded in Exodus 20:7.
title: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain

text: In the 2014 dark‑fantasy film *Maleficent*, the closing scene includes a version of the classic Sleeping Beauty song “Once Upon a Dream.” That rendition was performed by American singer‑songwriter **Lana Del Rey**, who initially offered the track as a free digital download on January 26, 2014 before it became available for purchase on February 4.

text: The eighteenth season of *Law & Order: Special Victims Unit* premiered on NBC on Wednesday, September 21, 2016, and concluded with a two‑hour finale on Wednesday, May 24, 2017.
title: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit (season 18)

text: The eighth film in the Saw series, titled Jigsaw, started shooting in November 2016 and moved into post‑production the following January. It premiered in United States theaters on October 27, 2017, and ultimately grossed roughly $102.9 million worldwide.
title: Jigsaw (2017 film)

title: A Walk Among the Tombstones (film)

title: Benjamin Stone (Law & Order character)

text: According to 2012 data, the United States had 3.2 million people identified as farmers, ranchers, or other agricultural managers.
title: Agriculture in the United States

text: The Battle of Badr, a decisive early‑Islamic clash that took place in the Hejaz area of present‑day Saudi Arabia, occurred on 13 March 624 (corresponding to 17 Ramadan, 2 AH). It marked a turning point in Muhammad’s struggle against the Quraysh of Mecca and is remembered both as a victory attributed to divine aid in Islamic tradition and as a testament to Muhammad’s strategic skill in secular accounts.
title: Battle of Badr

text: Beginning in the 13th century, a body of German princes called the prince‑electors held the exclusive privilege of choosing the King of the Romans, who would subsequently be crowned by the Pope as Holy Roman Emperor. This electoral right continued into the early modern period; for example, Charles V was elected in 1519 and crowned in 1530, after which his successors were elected directly by the electoral college and styled “Elected Emperor of the Romans.” In practice, from 1440 onward almost every emperor—except Charles VII of the Wittelsbach line—came from the Austrian Habsburg dynasty, with the prince‑electors merely confirming the Habsburg succession.
title: Prince-elector

text: Geraldine Margaret Agnew‑Somerville (born 19 May 1967) is an Irish‑born actress who portrayed Lily Potter, the mother of Harry Potter, in the Harry Potter film series. In addition to this role, she is known for playing Detective Sergeant Jane Penhaligon in the television drama *Cracker* (1993–1995) and has appeared in films such as *Gosford Park* (2001), *My Week with Marilyn* (2011) and *Grace of Monaco* (2014).
title: Geraldine Somerville

text: The fourteenth entry in the Dark Parables series, Return of the Salt Princess, saw its beta version released in September 2017, coinciding with Blue Tea Games’ return to the franchise after 2014.
title: Dark Parables

text: The 2018 DreamWorks Animation series Trolls: The Beat Goes On!—which premiered on Netflix in January—features a new voice cast for its main characters. In this show, the role of Poppy is performed by Amanda Leighton.
title: Trolls: The Beat Goes On!

text: In the “Say You’ll Haunt Me” video, a 1972 Plymouth Barracuda pulls into a dimly lit alley before Corey Taylor is dragged from the trunk by his bandmates and taken upstairs. There he is strapped to a chair and questioned by a woman—Joanna Moskawa—who displays a clear hostility toward him. While this confrontation unfolds, ghostly silhouettes of the band appear in an abandoned warehouse, including a blindfolded Taylor. Later, a bald, suited figure in sunglasses enters, removes his glasses, and the blindfold is taken off, revealing the same woman from earlier. The climax shows the band leaving the woman bound as the screen fades to black with the question “What did you see?”—the entire scenario was part of a contest that included the code “I am you.”

text: The 2017 National Football League season, the league’s 98th, opened on September 7, 2017 with the Kansas City Chiefs defeating the defending Super Bowl LI champion New England Patriots. The campaign came to a close with Super Bowl LII, which was held on February 4, 2018 and pitted the NFC champion Philadelphia Eagles against the AFC champion New England Patriots.
title: 2017 NFL season

text: Alpha Centauri, the nearest stellar system to the Solar System, is situated at an approximate distance of 4.37 light‑years (about 1.34 parsecs) from the Sun. The system comprises three stars—Alpha Centauri A, Alpha Centauri B, which together form a binary pair, and the faint red dwarf Alpha Centauri C (Proxima Centauri)—but its defining characteristic for distance measurements is that it lies roughly 4.37 light‑years away from our Solar neighborhood.
title: Alpha Centauri

text: The mapmakers Martin Waldseemüller and Matthias Ringmann, aided by René II, Duke of Lorraine, added the name America to their new map because they were convinced that the newly identified continent had been discovered by Amerigo Vespucci.
title: Early world maps

title: Ric Flair

text: Mississippi’s catfish aquaculture industry supplies the bulk of the farm‑raised catfish that are eaten throughout the United States.
title: Mississippi

title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege

text: The Duluth Model is built on a feminist perspective that sees male violence in intimate relationships as a tool for exercising power and control, a concept visualized by the “Power and Control Wheel” that is often posted in participating sites. It argues that women and children are especially at risk because of broader social, economic, and political inequalities. Within this framework, the treatment of abusive men is centered on re‑education, with the goal of reshaping their attitudes and behaviors so they can adopt non‑violent conduct in any relationship.
title: Duluth model

text: The Wave Hill walk‑off came to an end when the Whitlam Labor government secured the return of part of the Vestey lease to the Gurindji people. The official hand‑over ceremony, which marked the conclusion of the protest, was held on 16 August 1975 at Kalkaringi.
title: Wave Hill walk-off

text: Published in 1989, the children’s picture book *We’re Going on a Bear Hunt* was authored by Michael Rosen and illustrated by Helen Oxenbury. The story has collected numerous awards and, in 2014, set a Guinness World Record for the “Largest Reading Lesson,” with 1,500 children attending in person and another 30,000 listening online.
title: We're Going on a Bear Hunt

text: The Taming of the Shrew was already being performed prior to June 1592.  Scholars note that the anonymous comedy A Knack to Know a Knave, which premiered at The Rose on 10 June 1592, contains several passages that are also found in The Shrew, as well as material unique to Shakespeare’s version.  Because the later play borrows from The Shrew, the latter must have been on the stage before the June 1592 debut of A Knack.  This internal evidence, together with contemporary references, places the first performances of The Shrew earlier than that date.
title: The Taming of the Shrew

text: The current Prime Minister of India is Narendra Modi, who has headed the BJP‑led National Democratic Alliance government since 26 May 2014, making it the country’s first non‑Congress single‑party majority administration.
title: List of Prime Ministers of India

text: The fifth installment of the American police drama Chicago P.D. premiered on September 27, 2017, and this season also included the series’ 100th episode.
title: Chicago P.D. (season 5)

text: Shakespeare’s Sonnet 116 is widely regarded as one of his most celebrated love poems. In this sonnet the poet describes love as an immutable force that does not change even when circumstances shift. Critics such as Hilton Landry note that, although the poem is praised for its universal significance, its meaning is tied to its place within a specific sequence of sonnets. Others, like Carol Thomas Neely, point out that the sonnet belongs to a distinct trio (Sonnets 94, 116, 129) that presents a detached view of love. Despite differing interpretations, the central idea that true love remains constant is a defining feature of Sonnet 116.
title: Sonnet 116

text: The Bureau of Land Management, a division of the United States Department of the Interior, is responsible for administering more than 247.3 million acres of public land throughout the United States, a tract that represents roughly one‑eighth of the nation’s total land area.
title: Bureau of Land Management
